149. 陆氏宗祠

Lu's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
湖北省重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
黄石市下陆区东方山路东方山风景区
类型 Type
祭祀性建筑·砖石石混合结构
看点 Highlights
整体格局石雕檐垛陆迥弘化禅寺
中文 Chinese

陆氏宗祠坐落于三楚佛教胜地东方山上的弘化禅寺内，宗祠的修建与两个人有十分密切的关系。陆迥，字伯高，唐代名相陆贽之弟，生于唐元宗八年（720），曾任朝廷五马大夫。后辞官归田，于东方山放牧安度晚年。

804年，高僧智印云游至东方山，得陆迥赐基建寺，两人交往甚密，结为方外之交。812年，智印圆寂，其骨被安放于东方山上的多宝塔中。陆迥去世后，其后人为了纪念陆迥与智印的友谊，在多宝塔中供奉陆迥的塑像。

北宋中期（1100），陆迥后裔为方便祭祀，在祖师殿后修建宗祠，命名'大士阁'。阁内正中供奉陆迥的沉香木雕像。明神宗万历三十一年（1603），'大士阁'毁于火灾。万历三十四年（1606），陆氏后裔集资在'大士阁'的废墟重修陆氏宗祠。

其后，陆氏宗祠又历经三毁三建。现存宗祠面宽28米，进深16米，属砖、石、木混合结构。大门后退半间，檐下设四柱三间牌楼，两侧各立一精美石鼓。大殿内16根木柱落地，三神龛皆雕龙刻凤。

两侧为汉白玉圆门，圆门上方刻有篆体'腊梅''秋菊'。通过圆门可进入两侧厢房。屋顶12座檐垛，青砖布瓦，屋檐山脊耸立，显示出陆氏宗祠的气势恢宏。与大雄宝殿和祖师塔殿并称为东方山三大建筑。

English 英文

Lu's Ancestral Hall is located inside Honghua Chan Temple on Dongfang Mountain, a famous Buddhist site of Three Chu. The construction of the ancestral hall is closely related to two people. Lu Jiong, courtesy name Bogao, younger brother of the famous Tang prime minister Lu Zhi, was born in the 8th year of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang (720), and once served as Wuma Grand Master of the court. Later he resigned and returned to farming, spending his later years herding on Dongfang Mountain. In 804, the eminent monk Zhiyin traveled to Dongfang Mountain and received land from Lu Jiong to build a temple; the two had close interactions and became friends beyond worldly affairs. In 812, Zhiyin passed away, and his relics were placed in the Duobao Pagoda on Dongfang Mountain. After Lu Jiong's death, his descendants, to commemorate the friendship between Lu Jiong and Zhiyin, enshrined a statue of Lu Jiong in the Duobao Pagoda. In the mid-Northern Song (1100), Lu Jiong's descendants, for the convenience of sacrifice, built an ancestral hall behind the Patriarch Hall, named 'Dashi Pavilion.' In the center of the pavilion is enshrined the agarwood statue of Lu Jiong. In the 31st year of Wanli, Ming Shenzong (1603), the 'Dashi Pavilion' was destroyed by fire. In the 34th year of Wanli (1606), Lu's descendants raised funds to rebuild Lu's Ancestral Hall on the ruins of the 'Dashi Pavilion.' Thereafter, Lu's Ancestral Hall underwent three destructions and three reconstructions. The existing ancestral hall is 28 meters wide and 16 meters deep, belonging to a brick-stone-wood composite structure. The main gate recedes half a bay, with a four-column three-bay memorial archway under the eaves, and an exquisite stone drum on each side. In the main hall, 16 wooden columns reach the ground, and the three shrines are all carved with dragons and phoenixes. On both sides are white marble round doors, with seal-script 'Winter Plum' and 'Autumn Chrysanthemum' carved above the round doors. Through the round doors one can enter the side wing rooms. The roof has 12 eave垛, with gray brick and tile, and the eaves and ridges stand tall, showing the grand momentum of Lu's Ancestral Hall. Together with the Mahavira Hall and the Patriarch Pagoda Hall, they are called the Three Great Buildings of Dongfang Mountain.

150. 水南湾民居

Vernacular Dwellings in Shuinanwan
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
黄石市大冶市大箕铺镇
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
木雕石雕砖雕曹氏家族一进九重门
中文 Chinese

水南湾村子坐北朝南，背依青山前临碧水。始建于明末清初。据曹氏家谱载，曹氏家族于明万历年间（1573-1620）由江西瑞昌迁居至水南湾，其后百余位工匠耗时13年，修建了这片气势恢宏的徽派建筑。村头一八字形门楼为主要出入口，门楼上书'水南湾'三字。

由八字形门楼而入，迎面为一水质清澈的大池塘，塘后为打谷场，其后为宗祠。宗祠前殿面阔七间，明间、次间后退半间，四柱立于檐下，一人高的石鼓立于大门两侧的石墩之上，雕刻有瑞兽卷云，工艺精湛，十分华丽。

以祠堂九如堂为中轴线，宅院向两侧扩展，依山就势、逐级而建，对称布局，宅院呈'目'字形，一进九重门，共有36个天井、72个槛窗，可容纳2000余人居住。其主次分明，院落之间多用天井、走廊和装饰华丽的垂花门分隔。

堂屋、正屋、厢房、耳房错落有致，通常由大门进去，一进三、四幢，或更多幢，每幢之间都设一天井。故2000人虽同居一室，各家各户又独成体系。建筑内大量使用砖雕、木雕、石雕。

木雕以浮雕、镂空雕为主，题材多为日常生活、花鸟鱼虫，取意吉祥，多用于梁枋、栏杆、窗棂、桌椅等处，尤以窗棂为最，窗户以透花雕为主。石雕主要用在础石、门当、石鼓、窗户等处，构思十分巧妙，其中石窗'福鹿寿'，外表看为一'福'字，其实却是由一鹿、一鹤构成。

砖雕多为如意龙凤纹，呈四边形、六边形及扇形，分布于门洞上方，起到装饰墙面、通风换气的作用。

English 英文

Shuinanwan Village faces south, backed by green mountains and fronted by clear water. It was first built in the late Ming and early Qing. According to the Cao family genealogy, the Cao family moved from Ruichang, Jiangxi to Shuinanwan during the Wanli period of the Ming (1573-1620), and thereafter over a hundred craftsmen took 13 years to build this grand Hui-style architectural complex. An eight-character-shaped gate tower at the village head is the main entrance, with the three characters 'Shuinanwan' written on the gate tower. Entering through the eight-character gate tower, facing you is a large pond with clear water; behind the pond is a threshing ground, and behind that is the ancestral hall. The front hall of the ancestral hall is seven bays wide, with the central and secondary bays receding half a bay; four columns stand under the eaves, and one-person-high stone drums stand on the stone piers on both sides of the main gate, carved with auspicious beasts and scrolling clouds, with exquisite craftsmanship, very gorgeous. Taking the ancestral hall Jiurutang as the central axis, the residences expand to both sides, built according to the mountain terrain and逐级, with symmetric layout; the residential complex is in the shape of the character '目' (eye), with one entry and nine layers of gates, a total of 36 courtyards (tianjing) and 72 lattice windows, capable of accommodating over 2,000 people. The primary and secondary are distinct, and between courtyards are mostly separated by courtyards, corridors, and gorgeously decorated pendant gate towers. The main halls, principal rooms, wing rooms, and side rooms are well-arranged; usually entering through the main gate, there are three, four, or more buildings, with a courtyard set between each building. Therefore, although 2,000 people live together in one complex, each household is an independent system. The building extensively uses brick carvings, wood carvings, and stone carvings. Wood carvings are mainly relief and openwork, with themes mostly of daily life, flowers, birds, fish, and insects, taking auspicious meanings, mostly used on beams, railings, window lattices, tables and chairs, especially window lattices; windows are mainly openwork carvings. Stone carvings are mainly used on base stones, door ornaments, stone drums, windows, etc., with very ingenious构思; among them, the stone window 'Fortune Deer Longevity' appears as a 'Fu' (fortune) character from the outside, but is actually composed of a deer and a crane. Brick carvings are mostly ruyi dragon-phoenix patterns, in quadrilateral, hexagonal, and fan shapes, distributed above door openings, serving to decorate walls and ventilate.

151. 胡家大院

Hu Family's Residential Complex
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
黄石市大冶市灵乡镇长坪胡村新屋
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
木雕石雕嘉庆十一年一进八重
中文 Chinese

胡家大院始建于清嘉庆十一年（1806），据胡家后人介绍，胡家大院的始祖为胡启旦，生于康熙年间，靠贩卖茶叶发家，当时胡家大院建有12幢房屋，分与三子九孙居住。由于战火、'文革'的破坏，胡家大院大部分已损坏或坍塌，仅保存有少部分建筑。胡家大院四合院式布局，一进八重，重重相连，占地数十亩。

每一重老屋，又由正屋、横屋、照壁、戏楼、隔楼及高深的围墙构成。均为单檐硬山灰瓦顶，砖木结构，梁架形式多样，设封火山墙。

正屋坐北朝南，中间是厅堂，靠天井连接两边数量不等的厢房，偏房、厢房一般为二层楼，然后又与其他的厅堂相连，呈对称状依次排开。院内门、窗、梁上依然还保存了大量完好的木雕，大多为人物、飞龙、花鸟等吉祥物，柱础亦饰有各式纹样，十分精美。

English 英文

Hu Family's Residential Complex was first built in the 11th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1806). According to Hu family descendants, the始祖 of the complex was Hu Qidan, born during the Kangxi period, who made his fortune by selling tea. At that time, the complex had 12 buildings, divided among three sons and nine grandchildren for residence. Due to the destruction of wars and the Cultural Revolution, most of the complex has been damaged or collapsed, with only a small part of the buildings preserved. The complex has a courtyard layout, with one entry and eight layers, connected layer by layer, covering dozens of mu. Each old house is further composed of a principal room, horizontal room, screen wall, stage, partition building, and high deep enclosure walls. All are single-eave gable gray-tile roofs, brick-wood structure, with diverse beam frame forms and fire-sealing gable walls. The principal room faces south, with the main hall in the middle, connected to unequal numbers of wing rooms on both sides by courtyards; the side rooms and wing rooms are generally two-story, then connected to other halls, arranged symmetrically in sequence. On the doors, windows, and beams in the courtyard, a large number of well-preserved wood carvings still remain, mostly auspicious objects such as figures, flying dragons, flowers, and birds; the column bases are also decorated with various patterns, very exquisite.

152. 邹氏宗祠

Zou's Ancestral Hall

整体格局前殿戏楼中殿女儿楼后殿祖堂
中文 Chinese

据《邹氏宗谱》记载，邹氏宗祠始建于明朝洪武五年（1372），清康熙九年（1672）扩建，顺治九年（1652）重建。

宗祠坐东朝西，四合院式布局，面阔26米，进深60米，硬山青瓦顶，砖木结构，抬梁式构架。由前殿戏楼、中殿女儿楼、内殿中堂和后殿祖堂四部分组成。

English 英文

According to the 'Zou Family Genealogy,' Zou's Ancestral Hall was first built in the 5th year of Hongwu, Ming (1372), expanded in the 9th year of Kangxi, Qing (1672), and rebuilt in the 9th year of Shunzhi (1652). The ancestral hall faces west, with a courtyard layout, 26 meters wide and 60 meters deep, with a gable gray-tile roof, brick-wood structure, and post-and-lintel frame. It consists of four parts: the front hall stage, the middle hall daughter tower, the inner hall central hall, and the rear hall ancestral hall.

153. 龙港革命旧址

Historic Site of Longgang Revolution
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
黄石市阳新县龙港镇
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
古镇格局龙港红军街70余处革命旧址小汉口
中文 Chinese

龙港镇是一个历史古镇，位于阳新县西南部，得名于龙港河，兴于埠头。据《阳新县志》载，古镇始建于元末，明代称龙川市，清光绪十一年（1855）在此设龙港巡检司，改称龙港市。清末民初，龙港街形成了拥有300余家商号、作坊的'小汉口'。

1929年至1930年，红五军先后进驻龙港，开创鄂东南革命根据地，此间龙港成为湘鄂赣苏区鄂东南革命根据地政治、经济、文化中心。

现为龙港古镇第四批（2009年）国家级历史文化名镇，主体格局包括四处历史建筑群，涵括国家级文物保护单位16处、省级文物保护单位22处、市县级文物保护单位3处，建筑总面积4.8万平方米。其中，最具有代表性的为龙港革命老街，又称龙港红军街。

这里保存有彭德怀旧居、中共鄂东南特委、鄂东南苏维埃政府、鄂东南工农兵银行、彭杨学校、列宁学校、红军后方医院等革命旧址70余处，其中12处集中在老街中段。老街全长800余米，宽5米，青石板路面，街道蜿蜒曲折，保存基本完好。

街道两旁建筑为大多为二层单檐砖木结构瓦房，一进多重，多建于清末，有江南古风。店铺前均砌有二级石台阶，红漆店面门板。

English 英文

Longgang Town is a historical ancient town, located in the southwest of Yangxin County, named after the Longgang River and prospering at the wharf. According to the 'Yangxin County Annals,' the ancient town was first built at the end of the Yuan, called Longchuan City in the Ming, and in the 11th year of Guangxu, Qing (1855), the Longgang Inspection Office was established here, renamed Longgang City. In the late Qing and early Republican periods, Longgang Street formed a 'Little Hankou' with over 300 commercial firms and workshops. From 1929 to 1930, the Fifth Red Army successively stationed in Longgang, establishing the Southeastern Hubei Revolutionary Base Area; during this period, Longgang became the political, economic, and cultural center of the Southeastern Hubei Revolutionary Base Area of the Hunan-Hubei-Jiangxi Soviet Area. It is now the fourth batch (2009) of national historical and cultural towns for Longgang Ancient Town. The main pattern includes four historical building complexes, encompassing 16 national cultural heritage protection units, 22 provincial cultural heritage protection units, and 3 municipal/county cultural heritage protection units, with a total building area of 48,000 square meters. Among them, the most representative is the Longgang Revolutionary Old Street, also called Longgang Red Army Street. Here are preserved over 70 revolutionary historic sites such as Peng Dehuai's former residence, the Southeastern Hubei Special Committee of the CPC, the Southeastern Hubei Soviet Government, the Southeastern Hubei Workers-Peasants-Soldiers Bank, Peng-Yang School, Lenin School, and the Red Army Rear Hospital, of which 12 are concentrated in the middle section of the old street. The old street has a total length of over 800 meters and a width of 5 meters, with bluestone slab pavement; the street winds and twists, basically well preserved. The buildings on both sides of the street are mostly two-story single-eave brick-wood structure tile houses, with multiple sections per entry, mostly built in the late Qing, with Jiangnan ancient style. In front of the shops are all built with two-level stone steps, and red-lacquered storefront door panels.

154. 李蘅石故居及李氏祠堂

Former Residence of Li Hengshi and Li's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清
地址 Address
黄石市阳新县浮屠镇玉堍村
类型 Type
居住、祭祀建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
木雕石雕光禄大夫李氏宗祠
中文 Chinese

玉堍村位于黄姑山脚下，属阳新县浮屠镇，村落内保存有较多的明清特色民居。其中较为出名的是清代光禄大夫李蘅石告老还乡的居所，亦称'李氏官厅''光禄大夫宅'，以及李氏宗祠。李蘅石（1838-1922），原名均善，字守吾，号子吾，曾游太学，任县丞。

后投左宗棠部，1879年出使俄国，据理力争收复伊犁，被钦赏二品封典，授新疆按察使，诰授光禄大夫，故旧居又称'光禄大夫宅'。

李蘅石故居始建于光绪三十一年（1905），坐东朝西，建筑面积1380平方米，由过堂、正堂、祖堂等主体建筑组成，并建有供管家、佣人、厨师用的次间。

过堂为硬山式，面阔五间，进深三间，中央明间后退半间形成门廊，门楣上方为楷书'光禄大夫'石刻匾额。两根立柱以支撑檐口，一柱双料，立柱下部为一人高石制大花瓶柱，上部木制。

正堂与祖堂均面阔五间，进深五间，开间宽阔，以间距对称的木柱为支撑，横梁为大小一致的匀称弧形木料，雕刻精美的格扇门分隔房间，宽敞通透。檐下均施平綦天花，中间有方形和八角形藻井。所有房间都设阁楼，阁楼作寻杖栏杆围合，彼此贯通。

距李蘅石故居百余米的地方，是光绪二十六年（1900）由李蘅石捐建的李氏宗祠。宗祠为三进四合院，占地1650平方米，主体建筑由戏台、看台、正堂、过堂、祖堂构成。

宗祠入口上部的墙体高出檐口，与两侧山面云墙组成'山'字形轮廓，正面有四柱三间牌坊式正门，其下是石制门框，上刻'李氏宗祠'四字，正立面未设窗洞以突出主入口。

门背面为戏台，单檐歇山顶，平面大致呈方形，面阔进深约5米，石柱将戏台抬起，供人穿行。两侧原为连接前后两进的双层连廊，现已毁。戏台对面为体量高大的厅堂，面阔三间，进深七间，高约8米，与故居一样，开间宽阔。

檐下做平綦天花，遮盖屋架构造。厅堂正中为斗八藻井，内绘太极八卦图。李氏宗祠的装饰装修比较丰富。戏台额枋上雕有精美的云龙交织图，屏风饰以书法字画；后院厢房的隔扇，格心为冰裂纹样，根板绘以不同瓶花；石柱础上的雕饰以动物花鸟为主，雕工细腻，构思巧妙。

English 英文

Yutu Village is located at the foot of Huanggu Mountain, under Futu Town, Yangxin County; the village preserves many Ming-Qing characteristic vernacular dwellings. Among them, the more famous is the residence where Li Hengshi, the Guanglu Grand Master of the Qing, returned to his hometown in old age, also called 'Li's Official Hall' and 'Guanglu Grand Master Residence,' as well as Li's Ancestral Hall. Li Hengshi (1838-1922), original name Junshan, courtesy name Shouwu, art name Ziwu, once studied at the Imperial Academy and served as county assistant. Later he joined Zuo Zongtang's department, and in 1879 was sent as envoy to Russia, arguing strongly to recover Ili, was imperially awarded the second-rank canon, appointed as Xinjiang Surveillance Commissioner, and conferred as Guanglu Grand Master; hence the former residence is also called 'Guanglu Grand Master Residence.' Li Hengshi's former residence was first built in the 31st year of Guangxu (1905), facing west, with a building area of 1,380 square meters, composed of main buildings such as the passage hall, main hall, and ancestral hall, and also built with secondary rooms for the housekeeper, servants, and cooks. The passage hall is gable style, five bays wide and three bays deep, with the central bay receding half a bay to form a porch; above the lintel is a stone plaque in regular script 'Guanglu Grand Master.' Two columns support the eaves, one column with double materials; the lower part of the column is a one-person-high stone large vase column, and the upper part is wooden. Both the main hall and ancestral hall are five bays wide and five bays deep, with wide bays, supported by symmetrically spaced wooden columns; the crossbeams are uniformly sized and proportioned curved wood, with exquisitely carved lattice doors separating rooms, spacious and transparent. Under the eaves are all flat coffered ceilings, with square and octagonal caissons in the middle. All rooms have attics, and the attics are enclosed by handrail railings, connected to each other. More than a hundred meters from Li Hengshi's former residence is Li's Ancestral Hall, donated and built by Li Hengshi in the 26th year of Guangxu (1900). The ancestral hall is a three-entry courtyard, covering 1,650 square meters; the main buildings consist of a stage, viewing stands, main hall, passage hall, and ancestral hall. The wall above the entrance of the ancestral hall is higher than the eaves, forming a 'mountain'-shaped outline with the cloud gable walls on both sides; the front has a four-column three-bay memorial-arch-style main gate, below which is a stone door frame engraved with the four characters 'Li's Ancestral Hall'; the front facade has no window openings to highlight the main entrance. The back of the gate is the stage, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, roughly square in plan, about 5 meters wide and deep; stone columns lift the stage for people to pass through. On both sides were originally two-story corridors connecting the front and rear sections, now destroyed. Opposite the stage is a large-scale hall, three bays wide and seven bays deep, about 8 meters high, like the former residence with wide bays. Under the eaves are flat coffered ceilings, covering the roof frame structure. In the center of the hall is an octagonal caisson, painted with a Taiji Eight Trigrams diagram. The decoration and furnishing of Li's Ancestral Hall are relatively rich. The stage architrave is carved with an exquisite interwoven cloud-dragon pattern, and the screen is decorated with calligraphy and paintings; the partitions of the backyard wing rooms have ice-crack pattern lattice hearts, and the root boards are painted with different vase flowers; the carvings on the stone column bases are mainly animals, flowers, and birds, with delicate carving and ingenious构思.

155. 泉山画屋

Quanshanhuawu (Residence)

看点 Highlights
木雕石雕百门大屋嘉庆十二年
中文 Chinese

泉山画屋又称花屋，由舒氏先人舒善炽于清嘉庆十二年（1807）建造，占地面积约1000平方米，一进三重，四合院式布局，房舍70余间，天井10个，大、小门100扇，故又称'百门大屋'。

前堂、过厅、祖堂均面阔五间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶。门、窗、梁、柱上均有人物山水、花鸟鱼虫、亭台楼阁等多种图案的木雕、石雕构件，运用镂雕、浮雕等技法，既有刀法细腻的工笔，又有粗犷的大写意，皆逼真传神，栩栩如生。

English 英文

Quanshanhuawu, also called Flower House, was built by Shu's ancestor Shu Shanchi in the 12th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1807), covering about 1,000 square meters, with one entry and three sections, a courtyard layout, over 70 rooms, 10 courtyards (tianjing), and 100 large and small doors, hence also called 'Hundred-Door Great House.' The front hall, passage hall, and ancestral hall are all five bays wide, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs. On the doors, windows, beams, and columns are wood-carved and stone-carved components with various patterns such as figures and landscapes, flowers, birds, fish, and insects, pavilions and terraces, using techniques such as openwork carving and relief carving; there are both delicate brushwork with fine knife work and rough freehand brushwork, all realistic and vivid, lifelike.

156. 宝塔村文峰塔

Wenfeng Pagoda in Baota Village
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
黄石市阳新县兴国镇宝塔村
类型 Type
古塔·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
地标建筑六角七层阁楼式空心砖塔嘉庆二十四年日本侵略军炮击
中文 Chinese

文峰塔坐落于宝塔湖横泊洲的土岗上，背向网湖，南临富河，北近银山。塔建于清嘉庆二十四年（1819），由兴国州文人学子募款捐资兴建，为富河上往来船舶航行的标志。民国二十七年（1938）曾遭日本侵略军炮击，塔身二、三层东南面塔壁被击破，但塔仍巍然屹立。

1986年重修，复原如初。文峰塔为六角七层阁楼式空心砖塔，高21米，塔基周长33.6米，塔身自下而上递减，底座由大青条石相错砌成，二至七层为砖砌。

一层正门上方嵌石匾，阴刻楷书'文峰塔'，以上各层分别刻有牌匾'引虹''凌云''凝霞''御风''重光'，四、五层背面门额篆有'浴日''揽月'牌匾。每层交错设两扇拱券门及两个壁龛。各层皆有砖叠涩砌成的挑檐，檐角为石雕鱼尾，檐下刻有装饰图案。塔内有旋转阶梯，可拾级而上至顶层。

塔顶为铁铸塔刹。

English 英文

Wenfeng Pagoda is located on the earth mound of Hengbo Zhou in Baota Lake, with its back to Wang Lake, facing Fu River to the south, and near Yin Mountain to the north. The pagoda was built in the 24th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1819), funded and built by scholars and students of Xingguo Prefecture, serving as a navigation marker for ships traveling on the Fu River. In the 27th year of the Republic (1938), it was shelled by the Japanese invading army; the southeast pagoda walls of the second and third stories were broken, but the pagoda still stood majestically. It was rebuilt in 1986, restored to its original state. Wenfeng Pagoda is a hexagonal seven-story multi-eaved hollow brick pagoda, 21 meters high, with a pagoda base perimeter of 33.6 meters; the pagoda body tapers from bottom to top, with the base built of large bluestone slabs staggered, and the second to seventh stories brick-built. Above the main gate of the first story is embedded a stone plaque, yin-carved in regular script 'Wenfeng Pagoda'; above each story are respectively carved plaques 'Yin Hong' (Guiding Rainbow), 'Ling Yun' (Reaching the Clouds), 'Ning Xia' (Condensing Rosy Clouds), 'Yu Feng' (Riding the Wind), 'Chong Guang' (Restoring Light); on the back door lintels of the fourth and fifth stories are seal-script plaques 'Yu Ri' (Bathing in the Sun) and 'Lan Yue' (Embracing the Moon). Each story alternately sets two arched doors and two wall niches. Each story has projecting eaves built with brick corbelling, with the eave corners as stone-carved fish tails, and decorative patterns carved under the eaves. Inside the pagoda are spiral stairs, which can be climbed step by step to the top story. The pagoda top is an iron-cast pagoda finial.

157. 李清塔

Liqing Pagoda
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位

地标建筑八角七层阁楼式实心砖石塔道光二十一年冲天凤
中文 Chinese

李清塔建于清道光二十一年（1841），为八角七层阁楼式实心砖石塔，通高24米。一、二层为石砌，不设门窗，三至七层为砖砌。塔顶以石板铺盖，塔刹为石雕宝珠。石雕塔檐，檐角装鱼尾。据族谱记载，古塔为当时李清村族长李之德提议建造。

一说是因为李清村坐落于笔架山下，但空有笔架而无笔难出大人物，于是在笔架山下修一宝塔，象征毛笔搁在笔架上。另一说是古时曾有一只凤栖落于此地，为守住此凤而修塔镇守。塔旁有一座名为'冲天凤'的青山，山中有一种似凤冠的岩石，栩栩如生。

English 英文

Liqing Pagoda was built in the 21st year of Daoguang, Qing (1841), an octagonal seven-story multi-eaved solid brick-stone pagoda, with a total height of 24 meters. The first and second stories are stone-built, without doors or windows; the third to seventh stories are brick-built. The pagoda top is covered with stone slabs, and the pagoda finial is a stone-carved precious pearl. The stone-carved pagoda eaves have fish tails installed at the eave corners. According to genealogy records, the ancient pagoda was proposed and built by Li Zhide, the clan head of Liqing Village at that time. One theory is that because Liqing Village is located at the foot of Bijia (Pen Rack) Mountain, but having only a pen rack without a pen makes it difficult to produce important figures, so a pagoda was built at the foot of Bijia Mountain, symbolizing a brush placed on the pen rack. Another theory is that in ancient times a phoenix once perched here, and to guard this phoenix a pagoda was built to suppress and guard it. Beside the pagoda is a green mountain named 'Chongtian Feng' (Soaring Phoenix), and in the mountain there is a rock resembling a phoenix crown, lifelike.

Liang's Ancestral Hall

梁氏宗祠建于清康熙三十七年（1698），由清朝二品大臣梁勇孟主持修建，此后历有扩建，光绪二十三年（1898）形成现有规模。宗祠坐北朝南，前有案山，背靠祖山，前后分为三进，中轴对称布局，建筑面积达2400多平方米。

主要由大门、前厅、戏楼、享堂、过厅、拜殿及左右廊庑组成。梁氏宗祠的入口为八字如意门，抱鼓石分立两侧，面阔三间，明间为主入口，两边各有一次入口。门楣上方为楷书'梁氏宗祠'石雕匾额，四周镶嵌有人物...

English 英文

Liang's Ancestral Hall was built in the 37th year of Kangxi, Qing (1698), presided over by Liang Yongmeng, a second-rank minister of the Qing dynasty, and has since been expanded several times, reaching its current scale in the 23rd year of Guangxu (1898). The ancestral hall faces south, with an anshan (document mountain) in front and backed by the ancestral mountain, divided into three sections front to back, with a central axis symmetric layout, and a building area of over 2,400 square meters. It is mainly composed of the main gate, front hall, stage, worship hall, passage hall, offering hall, and left and right corridors. The entrance of Liang's Ancestral Hall is an eight-character ruyi gate, with drum-holding stones standing separately on both sides, three bays wide, with the central bay as the main entrance and one secondary entrance on each side. Above the lintel is a stone-carved plaque in regular script 'Liang's Ancestral Hall,' surrounded by inlaid figures...

Wu's Ancestral Hall

黄石市阳新县王英镇伍家祠村

看点 Highlights
木雕石雕梁柱体系渔樵耕读滚龙硬山式
中文 Chinese

伍氏宗祠始建于清顺治年间，祠堂规模宏大，坐南朝北，前后分为三进，总占地面积达到2400多平方米，有戏台、拜殿、抱厅、祖堂殿。

伍家祠第一进为门楼，由三座牌楼组成，正中牌楼为四柱三楼，门楣上书'伍氏宗祠'，匾额下端雕刻有'渔樵耕读'灰塑及彩绘，墙顶正中有一造型独特的金属器物，据称为伍氏宗族所崇尚的一种图腾。大门两侧各立一面精美的石鼓，给宗祠增添了几丝威严之感；

两侧门楼为两柱三楼，门框上施灰塑及彩绘。进入正门为一狭长天井，两侧设小门可进入观戏场。天井背后是一个平面为'山'字形的戏台，分为前后台，后台与两侧的廊屋相连。戏台为单檐歇山顶，檐角上翘，给人以轻盈之感。

横梁上刻有精美人物浮雕，上为云龙交织石雕，十分精致，堪称精品。戏台对面为拜殿，殿前供奉有伍子胥金身塑像。拜殿与抱厅围绕一方天井修建。拜殿为滚龙硬山式，两端山墙墀头装饰从人物、花草、瑞器到倒爬狮共五层，皆为砖雕，精致鲜活。

殿内有九个天花藻井，藻井内施大量如意斗拱，绘龙、蝠等吉祥图案。跨空...

English 英文

Wu's Ancestral Hall was first built during the Shunzhi period of the Qing. The ancestral hall is large in scale, facing north, divided into three sections front to back, with a total area of over 2,400 square meters, including a stage, worship hall, embrace hall, and ancestral hall. The first entry of Wu's Ancestral Hall is a gate tower, composed of three memorial archways; the central archway is four columns and three stories, with the lintel inscribed 'Wu's Ancestral Hall,' and below the plaque are carved 'fisherman, woodcutter, farmer, scholar' gray plaster sculptures and paintings; in the center of the wall top is a uniquely shaped metal object, said to be a totem revered by the Wu clan. On both sides of the main gate stand an exquisite stone drum each, adding a sense of majesty to the ancestral hall; the side gate towers are two columns and three stories, with gray plaster sculptures and paintings on the door frames. Entering the main gate is a long and narrow courtyard (tianjing), with small doors on both sides leading to the theater viewing area. Behind the courtyard is a stage with a 'mountain'-shaped plan, divided into front and back stages, with the back stage connected to the corridor rooms on both sides. The stage has a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, with upturned eave corners, giving a sense of lightness. The crossbeams are carved with exquisite figure reliefs, above which are interwoven cloud-dragon stone carvings, very exquisite, worthy of being called masterpieces. Opposite the stage is the worship hall, in front of which is enshrined a gilded statue of Wu Zixu. The worship hall and embrace hall are built around a square courtyard. The worship hall is a rolling-dragon gable style, with the gable wall chi heads on both ends decorated with five layers from figures, flowers and plants, auspicious vessels to inverted climbing lions, all brick carvings, exquisite and vivid. Inside the hall are nine ceiling caissons, with a large number of ruyi bracket sets inside the caissons, painted with auspicious patterns such as dragons and bats. Spanning...

Mansion of Chen Guangheng the State Preceptor

中文 Chinese

陈宅建于清道光二十六年（1846），为清咸丰帝老师陈光亨辞官归故里后的宅第，据传是咸丰帝特拨国库银两为其修建的，属于'官宅'或'官厅'，故当地人称这座颇具规模的宅第为'国师府'或'国师堂'。

宅第为一进三重合院式住宅，建筑面积350平方米，以现存规模来看，纵深三进，横向四路，可确定的有大小房间超过159间、天井22口。主入口墙后退三开间的宽度，檐下四根立柱支撑屋檐，两侧外墙砌为八字形。

屋架为穿斗式和抬梁式结合，兼有硬山搁檩的做法。从残存的木构件上精美的雕刻，正厅天井的石栏板上的精美石雕与转角处栩栩如生的小狮子望柱头，以及正门口雕有狮、象的抱鼓石，可见此宅装饰之精美。

English 英文

Chen's residence was built in the 26th year of Daoguang, Qing (1846), the residence of Chen Guangheng, teacher of Emperor Xianfeng of the Qing, after he resigned and returned to his hometown. It is said that Emperor Xianfeng specially allocated national treasury silver to build it, belonging to an 'official residence' or 'official hall,' hence locals call this quite large-scale residence 'State Preceptor's Mansion' or 'State Preceptor's Hall.' The residence is a one-entry three-section courtyard-type residence, with a building area of 350 square meters. Judging from the existing scale, it is three sections deep and four routes wide, with determinable large and small rooms exceeding 159 and 22 courtyards (tianjing). The main entrance wall recedes by the width of three bays, with four columns under the eaves supporting the eave, and the exterior walls on both sides are built in an eight-character shape. The roof frame combines column-and-tie and post-and-lintel styles, with the practice of gable wall resting purlins. From the exquisite carvings on the remaining wooden components, the fine stone carvings on the stone parapet of the main hall courtyard and the lifelike small lion capitals at the corners, as well as the drum-holding stones carved with lions and elephants at the main entrance, one can see the exquisiteness of this residence's decoration.

First built during the Kangxi period. The building area is about 800 square meters. Single-eave gable gray-tile roof, brick-wood structure. The door plaque reads 'Luoyang Shize' (Luoyang World Grace); legend has it that the Jia clan here originated from Luoyang, Henan, as a branch of Jia Yi, a Western Han statesman; to让 descendants remember the family's ancestral home, they used the ancestor's place of residence as the door plaque inscription.

Built from the late Qing to the Republican period; because there is copper ore here and they are all descendants of the Chen family, it is called 'Tongwanchen' (Copper Bay Chen). It preserves dozens of ancient vernacular dwellings such as 'Huashan Qixiu' (Huashan Opening Talent), 'Qingshui Yangying' (Clear Water Raising Talent), and 'Xiuyu Lushan' (Talent Nurtured by Lushan). The forms are basically the same, with a courtyard layout, mostly three bays wide, brick-wood structure. The principal house faces north from the south, toward the village entrance, built by the Chen ancestors in ancient times for entertaining guests, also serving as an ancestral hall. On the hillside at the village entrance is a Fushen (Fortune God) Temple, said to have a history of over 400 years.

Sizhou Temple is located on an open mountain land on the west side of Luojia Mountain, first built in the Tang dynasty. According to the Yangxin County Annals: in 903 AD, Lord Luoguan built Sizhou Temple at Luojia Mountain in Dongyuan; the temple was destroyed in the Yuan, and during the Xuande period of the Ming, Shandong monk Xidao came here to rebuild it. Now only half of the main hall remains, as well as the side hall Wusheng Palace and Guanyin Hall. There were originally multiple stone pagodas beside Sizhou Temple, now only one remains, with a gourd-shaped pagoda top.

167. 鄂州观音阁

Guanyin Pavilion in Ezhou
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
元、明、清
地址 Address
鄂州市鄂城区小东门外长江中
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
元代石刻碑刻湖心景观龙蟠矶小蓬莱
中文 Chinese

鄂州观音阁又称龙蟠矶寺，位于鄂州市城区小东门外长江江心龙蟠矶之上。据旧《武昌县志》载：'龙蟠矶去岸不盈一里，隆起于江中，周围七十丈。冬出夏没，相传有龙蟠于此石，积日方去，石势蜿蜒如龙，因名。

'始建于元至正五年（1345），为元代蒙古族人监邑铁山所建。明、清、民国多次重建、维修。观音阁以条石垒成，红石青砖砌筑阁身，与阁下龙蟠矶巧妙地融为一体。

建筑面积约400平方米，总体为一进纵向三栋，由祖师殿、观音殿、老君殿三殿，及纯阳楼、观澜亭等组成。其中纯阳楼和观澜亭为明嘉靖六年（1527）增建，其余建筑皆为1954年重修。

祖师殿为观音阁第一进殿，即前殿，砖木结构，面阔三间。正门牌坊匾额上有石刻'龙蟠晓渡'四字门额，出自清代官文，下刻嵌'小蓬莱'三字门额。殿内脊梁上悬挂相传能镇压水势的儒教神祗东方朔，故又名东方朔殿。

观音殿即中殿，位于祖师殿的后端，砖木结构，屋面铺小布瓦，抬梁式大木构架。门两侧设有神台，右侧台上供奉观音雕像，左侧台上雕像已毁；殿内正中偏后设有木雕神龛，龛中供奉有青石阴刻观音大士站像，上方悬挂'普度众生'匾额，是一座佛教殿堂。

老君殿，即后殿，面阔三间，进深一间，砖木结构，抬梁式大木构架，硬山式屋面，前檐建有一支香轩廊；殿中设有三个牌坊式神龛，龛内供奉有太上老君、玉帝、王母神像；龛上悬挂'紫气东来'四字匾额；

龛前左右二山墙柱间刻有八仙图案及其生平小传石刻碑。阁内保留有较多的石刻及碑刻。其中元代的莲花纹刻石古井圈为阁内最早的石刻。碑刻有明代诗人王廷陈的《龙蟠矶》诗三首，刘养微的《龙蟠矶短歌》，光绪年间的《维修观音阁记》《功德碑》题刻等。

阁之外墙西壁刻有辛亥革命遗老朱维昌于民国二十一年（1932）所书'观音阁'三字。相传，龙蟠矶上原有两个凹口，为'神鳖'的两只巨眼，巨眼时刻注视着江面，使得观音阁能随潮涨潮落，并且两只眼一只注出江，一只出盐。

后来有一个贪心的道士为了多取油盐，将凹口凿大，却不料将神鳖两眼戳瞎了，不但不能出油盐，观音阁也不能随潮涨潮落了，此后常常被江水冲刷。石墙边上的几棵古树，原已枯萎多年，近几年竟又萌发新芽，死而复生。

在观音殿与老君殿之间的天井旁有古水井一口，传井中江水可通江海，自古清水见底，水位高出江水数尺。神鳖眼、老树和古井，被称做观音阁'三趣'。

English 英文

Ezhou Guanyin Pavilion, also called Longpanji Temple, is located on Longpan (Dragon Coiling) Rock in the middle of the Yangtze River, outside Xiaodong Gate of Ezhou city proper. According to the old 'Wuchang County Annals': 'Longpan Rock is less than one li from the shore, rising in the river, with a circumference of seventy zhang. It emerges in winter and submerges in summer; legend has it that a dragon coiled on this rock for days before leaving, and the rock's shape winds like a dragon, hence the name.' It was first built in the 5th year of Zhizheng, Yuan (1345), by Tieshan, a Mongol supervisor of the Yuan dynasty. It was rebuilt and repaired many times in the Ming, Qing, and Republican periods. Guanyin Pavilion is built with dressed stone, and the pavilion body is built with red stone and gray brick, ingeniously integrated with the Longpan Rock below. The building area is about 400 square meters, overall one entry with three longitudinal buildings, composed of three halls: the Patriarch Hall, Guanyin Hall, and Laojun Hall, as well as the Chunyang Tower and Guanlan Pavilion. Among them, the Chunyang Tower and Guanlan Pavilion were added in the 6th year of Jiajing, Ming (1527), and the remaining buildings were all rebuilt in 1954. The Patriarch Hall is the first entry hall of Guanyin Pavilion, i.e., the front hall, brick-wood structure, three bays wide. On the main gate memorial archway plaque is a stone-carved 'Longpan Xiaodu' (Dragon Coiling Morning Ferry) four-character lintel, from Qing official Guan Wen, with a 'Xiao Penglai' (Little Penglai) three-character lintel carved and embedded below. On the interior ridge beam hangs the Confucian deity Dongfang Shuo, said to be able to suppress water forces, hence also called Dongfang Shuo Hall. The Guanyin Hall is the middle hall, located at the rear of the Patriarch Hall, brick-wood structure, with small tile roofing and post-and-lintel large wooden frame. On both sides of the door are deity platforms; the right platform enshrines a Guanyin statue, and the statue on the left platform has been destroyed; in the center rear of the hall is a wooden carved shrine, in which is enshrined a bluestone yin-carved standing statue of Guanyin Bodhisattva, with a 'Universal Salvation' plaque hanging above; it is a Buddhist hall. The Laojun Hall, i.e., the rear hall, is three bays wide and one bay deep, brick-wood structure, post-and-lintel large wooden frame, gable roof, with a one-incense porch built under the front eave; in the hall are three memorial-arch-style shrines, in which are enshrined statues of the Supreme Lord Laozi, Jade Emperor, and Queen Mother; above the shrines hangs a 'Purple Qi Comes from the East' four-character plaque; between the two gable wall columns in front of the shrines are carved Eight Immortals patterns and their biographical stone-carved steles. The pavilion preserves many stone carvings and steles. Among them, the Yuan dynasty lotus-pattern carved stone ancient well ring is the earliest stone carving in the pavilion. The steles include three poems 'Longpan Rock' by Ming poet Wang Tingchen, 'Short Song of Longpan Rock' by Liu Yangwei, and inscriptions such as 'Record of Repairing Guanyin Pavilion' and 'Merit Stele' from the Guangxu period. On the west wall of the pavilion's exterior wall is carved the three characters 'Guanyin Pavilion' written by Zhu Weichang, a leftover of the 1911 Revolution, in the 21st year of the Republic (1932). Legend has it that there were originally two concave openings on Longpan Rock, the two giant eyes of a 'divine turtle,' which watched the river surface at all times, enabling Guanyin Pavilion to rise and fall with the tides; and one eye注出 river water and one produced salt. Later, a greedy Taoist, to get more oil and salt, chiseled the concave openings larger, but unexpectedly blinded the divine turtle's two eyes; not only could it no longer produce oil and salt, but Guanyin Pavilion could also no longer rise and fall with the tides, and has since often been scoured by the river. Several ancient trees on the edge of the stone wall, originally withered for many years, have in recent years unexpectedly sprouted new buds, coming back to life. Beside the courtyard between the Guanyin Hall and Laojun Hall is an ancient water well; legend has it that the well water connects to the river and sea, has been clear to the bottom since ancient times, and its water level is several feet higher than the river water. The divine turtle eyes, old trees, and ancient well are called the 'Three Delights' of Guanyin Pavilion.

吕洞宾歇山式屋面上下两层
中文 Chinese

纯阳楼位于观音阁西南，面向南方江岸，建于祖师殿和老君殿相接的南山墙外，砖木结构，面阔三间，进深一间，歇山式屋面，上有小布瓦，吻、脊、翼角错落有致。四壁设格扇。楼分为上下两层，一楼设有斋厨，二楼供中厅奉吕洞宾的卧像。

English 英文

Chunyang Tower is located southwest of Guanyin Pavilion, facing the south river bank, built outside the south gable wall where the Patriarch Hall and Laojun Hall connect, brick-wood structure, three bays wide and one bay deep, with a hip-and-gable roof, small tiles on top, with ornaments, ridges, and wing corners arranged in a picturesque disorder. Lattice partitions are set on all four walls. The tower is divided into upper and lower floors; the first floor has a vegetarian kitchen, and the second floor has a central hall enshrining the reclining statue of Lü Dongbin.

中文 Chinese

文峰塔，又名文星塔，因处古武昌城南门外，文星路中段，故俗称南门塔。文峰塔是鄂州市现存的唯一古塔，始建于明嘉靖二十一年（1542），后废。清康熙七年（1668）易地在'距旧址六十步'处重建，距今已450余年。

文峰塔为八角攒尖顶五层楼阁式塔，由塔基、塔身和塔座三部分组成。塔基为两层青石基座，南面设踏跺上下，四周围有汉白玉栏杆。塔身为砖砌，每层结构不尽相同。塔四壁间或设门、壁龛。塔内室平面八边形，中央有一立柱，直通塔顶。其内壁设砖砌楼梯，可攀至顶层。

塔身一层南面设拱券门，可进入塔内，其上二层南面镶置石碑，阴刻楷书'文峰'二字；西北面镶嵌一青石文物保护标志碑。塔刹为铁铸，高1.8米。刹座为两个覆钵相扣，上安三层相轮，再上为葫芦刹顶。

English 英文

Wenfeng Pagoda, also called Wenxing Pagoda, because it is located outside the south gate of ancient Wuchang City, in the middle section of Wenxing Road, is commonly called the South Gate Pagoda. Wenfeng Pagoda is the only ancient pagoda existing in Ezhou City, first built in the 21st year of Jiajing, Ming (1542), later abandoned. In the 7th year of Kangxi, Qing (1668), it was rebuilt at a different location 'sixty paces from the old site,' over 450 years ago. Wenfeng Pagoda is an octagonal pyramidal-roof five-story multi-eaved pagoda, composed of three parts: pagoda base, pagoda body, and pagoda seat. The pagoda base is a two-layer bluestone pedestal, with steps on the south side for going up and down, surrounded by white marble railings. The pagoda body is brick-built, with the structure of each story not entirely the same. The pagoda walls alternately set doors and wall niches. The interior chamber of the pagoda has an octagonal plan, with a central column reaching straight to the top. Its inner wall has brick-built stairs, which can be climbed to the top story. On the south side of the first story of the pagoda body is an arched door, allowing entry into the pagoda; on the south side of the second story above is inlaid a stone stele, yin-carved in regular script with the two characters 'Wenfeng'; on the northwest side is inlaid a bluestone cultural heritage protection marker stele. The pagoda finial is iron-cast, 1.8 meters high. The finial base is two inverted alms bowls扣 together, with three-tiered相轮 installed above, and then a gourd finial top on top.

庾亮楼原为吴王孙权安乐宫之端门门楼，后因西晋大将庾亮镇守鄂州时常登台观月而得名。始建于三国时期，明洪武初年（1368）、清康熙九年（1670）、乾隆二十七年（1762）、均多次维修、重建，现存古楼是民国年间在原基复建的。

庾亮楼坐落在巨石砌成的、如一堵城墙跨街而立的城台的门洞正上方，圆拱门头上刻有'庾楼'二字。坐北朝南，面阔、进深三间，单檐四面坡式灰瓦顶，砖木结构。以前东侧有放置更鼓的亭台，西侧有倒映日月和滴水计时的水池，现已毁去无存。

English 英文

Yuliang Tower was originally the Duanmen gate tower of Sun Quan's Anle Palace of Wu, later named because Yu Liang, a general of the Western Jin, often ascended the tower to view the moon when guarding Ezhou. It was first built during the Three Kingdoms period, and was repaired and rebuilt multiple times in the early Hongwu period of Ming (1368), the 9th year of Kangxi, Qing (1670), and the 27th year of Qianlong (1762); the existing ancient tower was rebuilt on the original foundation during the Republican period. Yuliang Tower sits directly above the gate opening of a city platform built of giant stones, standing across the street like a city wall; on the round arch gate head are carved the two characters 'Yu Lou.' Facing south, three bays wide and three bays deep, with a single-eave four-sided pitched gray-tile roof, brick-wood structure. Formerly on the east side there was a pavilion for placing the night watchman's drum, and on the west side there was a pool for reflecting the sun and moon and for water-clock timekeeping, now destroyed and no longer existing.

Located in Yangjiajingwan, Sanshan Village, Dushan Town, Ezhou City, the original construction date is unknown; it was destroyed by flood in the 29th year of Daoguang, Qing (1849), and rebuilt in the 8th year of Xianfeng (1858). 中文 Chinese

古灵泉寺又名圆通寺、资福寺、西山寺，位于鄂州西山的青龙、白虎二峰之间，为中国佛教净土宗的发祥地。相传晋代陶侃由武昌（今鄂州市）太守升迁为广州刺史时，于海中捞得文殊师利金佛像，遂送往武昌寒溪寺中供奉。

后转任江州刺史时，曾派人将金佛像运上船送往浔阳，不料途中风起而舟覆，因此作罢。时荆楚之人作歌谣：'陶惟剑椎，像以神标。云翔泥宿，邈何遥遥，可以诚致，难以力招。'后来，文殊菩萨托梦给当时的佛教领袖慧远高僧，称武昌西山为清凉福地，是'清净乐土'。

慧远于江边祈祷，终请回金佛，便在吴王孙权避暑宫故墟卓锡，修建寺庙，开创'净土法门'。及至唐会昌年间，武宗灭佛，...

English 英文

Gulingquan Temple, also called Yuantong Temple, Zifu Temple, and Xishan Temple, is located between the Qinglong (Blue Dragon) and Baihu (White Tiger) peaks of Xishan (West Mountain) in Ezhou, and is the birthplace of the Pure Land school of Chinese Buddhism. Legend has it that when Tao Kan of the Jin dynasty was promoted from governor of Wuchang (present-day Ezhou) to governor of Guangzhou, he fished up a golden statue of Manjushri Bodhisattva from the sea and sent it to be enshrined in Hanxi Temple in Wuchang. Later, when he was transferred to governor of Jiangzhou, he sent people to transport the golden statue by boat to Xunyang, but unexpectedly the wind rose and the boat capsized midway, so the matter was abandoned. At that time, people of Jingchu made a ballad: 'Tao only has sword and hammer, the statue is marked by divinity. It soars in clouds and dwells in mud, so distant and remote; it can be reached by sincerity, difficult to招 by force.' Later, Manjushri Bodhisattva appeared in a dream to the then Buddhist leader, the eminent monk Huiyuan, saying that Xishan in Wuchang was a cool and blissful land, a 'pure and happy land.' Huiyuan prayed by the river and finally invited back the golden Buddha, then established his dwelling at the ruins of Sun Quan's summer palace of King Wu of Wu, built a temple, and founded the 'Pure Land Dharma Gate.' By the Huichang period of the Tang, when Wuzong destroyed Buddhism, ...

174. 东山宝塔

Dongshan Pagoda
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
宋、清
地址 Address
荆门市东宝区东宝山太平顶
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
拱券门小圆窗八角七级南宋绍兴元年
中文 Chinese

东山宝塔是一座砖石结构的楼阁式塔，八角七级，高近30米。其中五层以下为南宋绍兴元年（1131）的遗构，六层以上的部分在乾隆四十九年（1784）的一场暴雨中倾坍，第二年重建，嘉庆年间又两次重修。虽然经过若干次大规模维修，但塔的基址一直未变。

塔基为石砌须弥座，各角雕刻托塔力士一尊。首层塔身的下半段亦为石砌，以上的塔身全部为砖砌。塔身每层用三层砖叠涩出檐，二至六层每层间隔开拱券门，七层则间隔开小圆窗。一层西北开一个拱券门，上有一块石匾，书'长林头角'四字。进门后可以沿石阶盘旋登上塔顶。

荆门有句俗语，叫'立了东山塔，长林生头角'，是说东山宝塔的创立是荆门当时称为长林县一桩值得骄傲的事。以往认为，东山宝塔始建于隋开皇十二年（592），由天台山国清寺高僧智禅师创建，其依据是乾隆年间成书的《荆门州志》。

但近年在塔身二级发现的一块元代碑刻上，明确记载着：'东山七级宝塔，乃宋僧宗愍之所建也。'目前看来，这两则史料各自都有一定的疑点，要确定宝塔的始建年代还需要更多的证据。

English 英文

Dongshan Pagoda is a brick-stone structure multi-eaved pagoda, octagonal with seven stories, nearly 30 meters high. The part below the fifth story is a surviving structure from the 1st year of Shaoxing, Southern Song (1131); the part above the sixth story collapsed in a heavy rain in the 49th year of Qianlong (1784), was rebuilt the following year, and was repaired twice during the Jiaqing period. Although it has undergone several large-scale repairs, the pagoda's foundation site has remained unchanged. The pagoda base is a stone-built Sumeru pedestal, with each corner carved with a pagoda-supporting strongman. The lower half of the first-story pagoda body is also stone-built, and the pagoda body above is all brick-built. Each story of the pagoda body uses three layers of brick corbelling to project the eaves; from the second to the sixth story, each story alternately opens arched doors; the seventh story alternately opens small round windows. On the northwest of the first story is an arched door, with a stone plaque above it inscribed with the four characters 'Changlin Toujiao' (Changlin Produces Horns). After entering the door, one can spiral up to the top along stone steps. There is a saying in Jingmen: 'When the Dongshan Pagoda was erected, Changlin grew horns,' meaning that the founding of Dongshan Pagoda was a matter of pride for what was then called Changlin County in Jingmen. Previously it was believed that Dongshan Pagoda was first built in the 12th year of Kaihuang, Sui (592), founded by the eminent monk Zhi Chan Master of Guoqing Temple on Tiantai Mountain, based on the 'Jingmen Prefecture Annals' compiled during the Qianlong period. However, in recent years, a Yuan dynasty stele discovered on the second story of the pagoda body clearly records: 'The seven-story Dongshan Pagoda was built by the Song monk Zongmin.' At present, both historical records have certain doubts, and more evidence is needed to determine the original construction date of the pagoda.

白云楼又称白云观，坐落在荆门城区青龙山西麓，相传吕洞宾曾驾白云来此，因而得名。乾隆五十一年（1786）始建，历时8年完工，嘉庆同治年间维修。

整个建筑群坐西朝东，占地面积约1.2万平方米，中轴线上有山门、白云楼、三清殿、会仙桥和纯阳殿等，其中最重要的建筑为白云楼。白云楼位于白云洞之上。相传东汉张角创立太平道，其信徒曾在此习诵太平经。

根据碑刻记载，白云洞在嘉庆年间定型，洞内共有三间，正中的石墙将洞一分为二，中间开拱券门，后室左侧辟'斜月'洞。白云洞的立面由须弥座台基、台身和平盘檐三部分组成。须弥座上方有方形的倚柱，将立面分为三间。

明间开半圆形拱券门，券顶有月梁形额枋，枋上置石匾，石刻'卧云'两个大字。两次间中央各有一个镂空团龙云纹石雕，线条流畅，工艺精湛。倚柱之上有一层贯通三间的云纹雕饰，其上为糙砥石和平盘檐口。洞顶的石砌高台称为'斯台'，也叫读书台，南、西、北...

English 英文

Baiyun Tower, also called Baiyun Temple, is located at the western foot of Qinglong Mountain in Jingmen city proper; legend has it that Lü Dongbin once rode white clouds to come here, hence the name. It was first built in the 51st year of Qianlong (1786), completed after 8 years, and repaired during the Jiaqing and Tongzhi periods. The entire building complex faces east, covering about 12,000 square meters; on the central axis are the mountain gate, Baiyun Tower, Sanqing Hall, Huixian Bridge, and Chunyang Hall, among which the most important building is Baiyun Tower. Baiyun Tower is located above Baiyun Cave. Legend has it that Zhang Jiao of the Eastern Han founded the Taiping Dao, and its followers once practiced and recited the Taiping Jing here. According to stele records, Baiyun Cave took shape during the Jiaqing period; there are three rooms inside the cave, with a stone wall in the center dividing the cave into two, an arched door in the middle, and a 'Slanting Moon' cave opened on the left side of the rear chamber. The facade of Baiyun Cave consists of three parts: the Sumeru pedestal base, the pedestal body, and the flat eave. Above the Sumeru pedestal are square pilasters, dividing the facade into three bays. The central bay opens a semicircular arched door, with a moon-beam-shaped lintel above the arch, and a stone plaque placed on the lintel, stone-carved with the two large characters 'Woyun' (Reclining Cloud). In the center of each of the two secondary bays is an openwork carved coiled-dragon cloud-pattern stone carving, with smooth lines and exquisite craftsmanship. Above the pilasters is a layer of cloud-pattern carvings贯通 the three bays, above which are rough ground stones and flat eave openings. The stone-built high platform at the top of the cave is called 'Si Tai' (This Platform), also called the Reading Platform, with south, west, and north...

176. 龙泉书院

Longquan Academy
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty

中轴对称布局特色展馆景色育德、洗心、东山草堂
中文 Chinese

龙泉书院的前身是一座书塾，其年代可以上溯到南宋绍兴年间，明代中叶经历了一次重建。清乾隆十九年（1754），荆门知州舒成龙在书塾旧址上重建书院，并在书院西边开凿泉眼，以'龙泉'为书院命名。

龙泉书院依山势而建，中轴对称布局，规模一度很大，有育德、洗心、东山草堂'三堂'，春华、秋实'两馆'，敬业、乐群'两斋'，尺木、文明'两楼'和寄畅、会心'两轩'，形成三条并列的轴线。现仅存文明楼、洗心亭和白鹤亭。

文明楼建于清光绪三十二年（1906），坐北朝南，面临文明湖。当时清政府下令'立停科举以广学校'，荆门州牧筹资兴建新校舍，修建文明楼，蕴含振兴教育、传播文明之意。建筑为二层单檐庑殿顶，屋顶坡度平缓，蔚然有古风，而翼角翘起，又不失南方建筑的灵动之气。

面阔七间，进深四间，抬梁式屋架，两侧各有一耳房。下层为砖墙砌筑，前壁无门，开有六扇窗；上层则有外廊环绕，木槅扇装修，凭栏可以眺...

English 英文

The predecessor of Longquan Academy was a private school, whose history can be traced back to the Shaoxing period of the Southern Song, and it underwent a reconstruction in the mid-Ming. In the 19th year of Qianlong, Qing (1754), Shu Chenglong, the prefect of Jingmen, rebuilt the academy on the old site of the private school, and dug a spring west of the academy, naming the academy 'Longquan' (Dragon Spring). Longquan Academy is built according to the mountain terrain, with a central axis symmetric layout; its scale was once very large, with 'three halls' of Yude (Nurturing Virtue), Xixin (Washing the Heart), and Dongshan Thatched Hall; 'two libraries' of Chunhua (Spring Flowers) and Qiushi (Autumn Fruits); 'two studios' of Jingye (Dedicated to Work) and Lequn (Joy in Community); 'two towers' of Chimu (Ruler Wood) and Wenming (Civilization); and 'two pavilions' of Jichang (Sending Joy) and Huixin (Meeting the Heart), forming three parallel axes. Now only the Wenming Tower, Xixin Pavilion, and Baihe Pavilion remain. Wenming Tower was built in the 32nd year of Guangxu, Qing (1906), facing south, facing Wenming Lake. At that time, the Qing government ordered to 'immediately stop the imperial examination to expand schools,' and the Jingmen prefect raised funds to build new school buildings and construct Wenming Tower, containing the meaning of revitalizing education and spreading civilization. The building is a two-story single-eave hip roof, with a gentle roof slope, majestic with ancient style, while the wing corners are upturned, not lacking the nimble air of southern architecture. Seven bays wide and four bays deep, with a post-and-lintel roof frame, and one ear room on each side. The lower floor is built with brick walls, with no door on the front wall and six windows opened; the upper floor has an exterior corridor surrounding it, decorated with wooden lattice partitions, from which one can lean on the railing to overlook...

蔡氏节孝坊建于清乾隆十一年（1746），是本乡监生廖世熏为其母蔡氏所建，第二年完工。这座石坊采用青石雕刻，平面为'一'字形，四柱三间仿木结构，正中石匾书'旌表儒士廖恺发妻蔡氏节孝'，背面书'闺中完人'。方柱上部及额枋浮雕人物和吉祥图案。

English 英文

Cai's Chastity and Piety Memorial Archway was built in the 11th year of Qianlong, Qing (1746), by Liao Shixun, a provincial student of this township, for his mother, née Cai, and completed the following year. This stone archway is carved from bluestone, with a '一'-shaped plan, four columns and three bays in imitation-wood structure; the central stone plaque is inscribed with 'Commending the Chastity and Filial Piety of Cai, Wife of Confucian Scholar Liao Kaifa,' and the back is inscribed with 'Perfect Woman in the Boudoir.' The upper parts of the square columns and the architraves are relief-carved with figures and auspicious patterns.

中文 Chinese

显陵是明世宗嘉靖皇帝的生身父亲兴献王和王妃蒋氏的合葬墓，是中国历史上一座独具特色的帝王陵。明正德十六年（1521），明武宗朱厚照无嗣崩殂，据太祖朱元璋'兄终弟及'的遗训，袭封为兴王不久的朱厚熜被迎往北京继承皇位，改年号为嘉靖，即明世宗。

嘉靖皇帝登基后的第一件事就是追封自己的父亲为皇帝，但大臣们认为新帝应追认他的叔叔孝宗为父皇，并称他的亲生父亲为'皇叔'。为此君臣双方各执一词，争论激烈，随之又产生一系列关于皇位正统和皇室利益的争执，直到嘉靖皇帝执政的中期，世宗统治彻底稳固，这些争执才平息下来。

史学家称这件事为'大礼仪'事件，它对整个明代中叶的社会思想和信仰都有着重大的影响，也在很大程度上决定了后来的北京城的面貌。

皇考之争是'大礼仪'事件中嘉靖皇帝取得的首个胜利：嘉靖三年（1524），世宗为生父母上尊号'皇考恭睿献皇帝''章圣慈仁皇太后'，改称孝宗为'皇伯考'，生父为'皇考'，而显陵的改建便是这次胜利的战利品。

显陵始建于明正德十四年（1519），最初按照藩王陵寝的规格修造，嘉靖三年以帝陵规制改建，至嘉靖十九年（1540）最终建成。陵区总面积约50万平方米，有外罗城、紫禁城两层城墙环绕。

外罗城高6米，长4730米，轮廓似一个细长的宝瓶，宝瓶底部的新红门是神道的起点，门前左右竖立一对汉白玉下马碑，上刻'官员人等至此下马'。

新红门内不远是旧红门，两道门都是砖石砌筑的无梁殿，单檐歇山琉璃屋顶，但两门之间的神道并没有笔直沿轴线伸出，而是向东倾斜了一定的角度。从新红门到祾恩门，神道上布置了御碑亭、棂星门和十二对石像生，伴随蜿蜒的九曲河，还设置了五道御桥和内外明塘。

棂星门由三间单门双柱冲天式石牌坊组成，通过影壁墙相连，中间的牌坊高于两侧。六根方柱柱顶各置独角神兽一只，额枋上雕刻云纹和火焰宝珠。棂星门内的神道弯曲如龙形，两侧石像生有狮子、獬...

English 英文

Xianling is the joint tomb of Xingxian King, the biological father of Emperor Jiajing of the Ming, and his consort née Jiang, and is a unique imperial mausoleum in Chinese history. In the 16th year of Zhengde, Ming (1521), Emperor Wuzong Zhu Houzhao died without an heir; according to the behest of Emperor Taizu Zhu Yuanzhang that 'when an elder brother dies without an heir, the younger brother succeeds,' Zhu Houcong, who had not long succeeded as the Xing King, was welcomed to Beijing to inherit the throne, changing the reign title to Jiajing, i.e., Emperor Shizong of Ming. The first thing Emperor Jiajing did after ascending the throne was to posthumously enfeoff his father as emperor, but the ministers believed that the new emperor should recognize his uncle, Emperor Xiaozong, as his imperial father, and call his biological father 'Imperial Uncle.' For this, the ruler and ministers each held their own views, arguing fiercely, followed by a series of disputes over imperial orthodoxy and imperial family interests, which did not subside until the mid-term of Emperor Jiajing's reign, when Shizong's rule was completely consolidated. Historians call this event the 'Great Rites Controversy,' which had a major impact on social thought and beliefs throughout the mid-Ming, and also largely determined the later appearance of Beijing. The dispute over the imperial father was the first victory Emperor Jiajing achieved in the 'Great Rites Controversy': in the 3rd year of Jiajing (1524), Shizong bestowed the honorific titles 'Imperial Father Gongrui Xian Emperor' and 'Empress Dowager Zhangsheng Ciren' on his biological parents, renamed Xiaozong as 'Imperial Uncle Father,' and his biological father as 'Imperial Father'; the reconstruction of Xianling was the spoils of this victory. Xianling was first built in the 14th year of Zhengde, Ming (1519), originally built according to the specifications of a prince's mausoleum; in the 3rd year of Jiajing it was reconstructed according to imperial mausoleum regulations, and was finally completed in the 19th year of Jiajing (1540). The total area of the mausoleum area is about 500,000 square meters, surrounded by two layers of city walls: the outer Luocheng and the Forbidden City. The outer Luocheng is 6 meters high and 4,730 meters long, with an outline resembling a slender treasure vase; the New Red Gate at the bottom of the treasure vase is the starting point of the spirit way, with a pair of white marble dismount steles erected on the left and right in front of the gate, inscribed with 'Officials and others dismount here.' Not far inside the New Red Gate is the Old Red Gate; both gates are brick-stone beamless halls with single-eave hip-and-gable glazed tile roofs, but the spirit way between the two gates does not extend straight along the axis, but tilts eastward at a certain angle. From the New Red Gate to the Ling'en Gate, the spirit way is arranged with imperial stele pavilions, a Lingxing Gate, and twelve pairs of stone statues; along with the winding Nine-Bend River, five imperial bridges and inner and outer bright ponds are also set. The Lingxing Gate consists of three single-door double-column sky-reaching stone archways, connected by screen walls, with the central archway higher than the sides. Each of the six square column tops is placed with a one-horned divine beast, and the architraves are carved with cloud patterns and flaming pearls. The spirit way inside the Lingxing Gate bends like a dragon, with stone statues on both sides including lions, xiezhi...

179. 元佑宫

Yuanyou Palace
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明
地址 Address
钟祥市元佑宫路
类型 Type
宗教建筑·石、砖木结构
看点 Highlights
琉璃照壁元佑宝殿抬梁结构嘉靖皇帝登基后三大工程
中文 Chinese

元佑宫是嘉靖皇帝登基后，在钟祥继兴王宫、显陵之后的第三大工程。始建于嘉靖二十八年（1549），历时十年建成，是供皇帝返乡、皇室宗亲和州府官员朝奉显陵或举行其他大型的祭祀活动时，斋戒、焚香、祷告的场所。清顺治、康熙、乾隆和同治年间多次维修。

元佑宫坐北朝南，中轴线上依次有照壁、宫门、元佑宝殿、降祥殿和三洞阁；宫门两侧则有钟鼓楼，宣法、衍真二配殿和左右厢房，还有一座敕御碑。四周红色围墙，墙外环绕以水，水面有堤有桥。

如今两座木枋中的保祚枋已不复存在，降祥殿仅剩遗址，三洞阁在遗址上重新建造，其他主要的建筑则基本保持了原貌。元佑宫的琉璃琼花照壁可以分为须弥座、壁身和壁顶三部分。须弥座较低，壁身中央的盒子很大。盒子中的琉璃缠枝花卉为青黄二色，四角类似，以外的部分为红色抹灰。

壁身之上额枋、斗拱、椽子等构件，均用琉璃构件忠实地模仿木结构。斗拱五踩单抄单昂，出耍头。壁顶为简化处理的歇山顶，正脊两段有吻兽，垂脊下端有角兽，做法非常规整。

宫门为一座三间单檐硬山屋顶的砖木混合建筑，明间开圆拱券门，两次间为圆拱券窗，拱券均以白色石材砌筑。上有精细的纹饰雕刻。宫门的材质与配色与照壁类似，也是黄绿色琉璃瓦和仿木构件，红色抹灰。明间门上'元佑宫门'四字为嘉靖朝晚期的宰相严嵩所题。

元佑宝殿是元佑宫中最重要的建筑，面阔七间，单檐歇山琉璃瓦屋顶，前有月台，正面除两尽间外均有门窗隔扇。斗拱为五踩单抄单昂，与粗大的额枋相比，斗拱的用材非常小。抬梁式结构，梁架非常简洁，室内装饰也相对较少。

整个元佑宫与荆楚建筑的风格有很大不同，而是呈现出显著的北方官式建筑特点，是嘉靖时期湖北皇家道教建筑的重要标本。

English 英文

Yuanyou Palace was the third major project in Zhongxiang after the Xingwang Palace and Xianling, after Emperor Jiajing ascended the throne. First built in the 28th year of Jiajing (1549), completed after ten years, it was a place for fasting, burning incense, and praying when the emperor returned to his hometown, imperial clan members and prefectural officials paid homage to Xianling or held other large sacrificial activities. It was repaired many times during the Shunzhi, Kangxi, Qianlong, and Tongzhi periods of the Qing. Yuanyou Palace faces south, with on the central axis依次 a screen wall, palace gate, Yuanyou Precious Hall, Jiangxiang Hall, and Sandong Pavilion; on both sides of the palace gate are bell and drum towers, the two side halls of Xuanfa and Yanzhen, and left and right wing rooms, as well as an imperial stele. Surrounded by red walls, with water环绕 outside the walls, and the water surface has dikes and bridges. Today, the Baozuo Fang among the two wooden fang no longer exists, the Jiangxiang Hall only remains as ruins, the Sandong Pavilion was rebuilt on the ruins, and the other main buildings basically maintain their original appearance. The glazed floral screen wall of Yuanyou Palace can be divided into three parts: the Sumeru pedestal, wall body, and wall top. The Sumeru pedestal is relatively low, and the box in the center of the wall body is very large. The glazed scrolling branch flowers in the box are blue and yellow, with the four corners similar, and the parts outside are red plaster. Above the wall body, components such as architraves, bracket sets, and rafters all use glazed components to faithfully imitate wooden structures. The bracket sets are five-step single-copy single-ang, with a耍头. The wall top is a simplified hip-and-gable roof, with吻兽 at both ends of the main ridge and horn beasts at the lower ends of the vertical ridges, with very regular workmanship. The palace gate is a three-bay single-eave gable roof brick-wood composite building, with a round arch door in the central bay and round arch windows in the two secondary bays; the arches are all built with white stone. There are fine pattern carvings above. The material and color scheme of the palace gate are similar to the screen wall, also yellow-green glazed tiles and imitation-wood components, with red plaster. The four characters 'Yuanyou Palace Gate' on the central bay door were inscribed by Yan Song, the prime minister in the late Jiajing period. The Yuanyou Precious Hall is the most important building in Yuanyou Palace, seven bays wide, with a single-eave hip-and-gable glazed tile roof, a platform in front, and except for the two end bays, the front has doors and windows with lattice partitions. The bracket sets are five-step single-copy single-ang; compared with the粗大 architraves, the materials used for the bracket sets are very small. The post-and-lintel structure has a very simple beam frame, and the interior decoration is relatively less. The entire Yuanyou Palace is quite different from the Jingchu architectural style, but instead presents significant northern official-style architectural characteristics, and is an important specimen of Hubei royal Taoist architecture during the Jiajing period.

180. 钟祥文风塔

Wenfeng Pagoda in Zhongxiang
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明
地址 Address
钟祥市城东龙山
类型 Type
古塔·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
地标性建筑覆钵式实心砖塔白乳高僧塔二十一层相轮
中文 Chinese

钟祥文风塔原名白乳高僧塔，位于钟祥市区东侧的龙山之上，是一座覆钵式实心砖塔，也称为喇嘛塔，明洪武二十三年（1390）建成。塔高近22米，通身雪白，由塔基、塔身、相轮、宝盖和塔刹五部分组成。塔基为八边形，分为上下两段，砖叠涩逐层收缩。

塔身为一个瘦长的覆钵，正面开辟佛龛，内供菩萨。塔身之上是多达二十一层的相轮，比常见的十三层相轮要多出七层；各层之间距离较远，自下而上依次减小，轮廓反倒有点像汉传佛教的密檐式塔。在第二层相轮下面四面还开辟小龛。

宝盖部分是三层铜制圆盘，四面悬挂风铃，其上的塔刹一柱嵌三'元'字，寓意'三元及第'。文风塔比例修长，与人们所熟悉的喇嘛塔形象有很大的不同，与北京白塔寺的白塔、五台山塔院寺的白塔相比，显得高耸、纤细、秀美。

根据民国时期的《钟祥县志》记载，唐末黄巢起义时，曾在此处的弥勒院杀一高僧，流出的是乳白色的血液，于是'巢异之，邦人敬礼，累土为浮图'。后来白乳高僧塔几度兴废，到元朝末年彻底变成了一堆废墟。

明洪武二十二年（1389），钟祥官员和乡贤重建此塔，改弥勒院为报恩寺，白乳高僧塔为文风塔，以祈求钟祥千年文风鼎盛，人才辈出。邑人唐志淳撰文记载了重建的过程，并记述道'塔中藏古佛像一，辟支佛舍利二，柏达师舍利二十，碧峰师灵骨一'。关于此塔，民间还有一个有趣的传闻。

据说清乾隆年间，塔刹歪斜，城中匠人攀上塔顶将其摆正，满城欢庆，府衙对出了上联'文风塔儿斜指头捶红日'，一时间无人能对出下联。后来兵部左侍郎李潢回乡，在塔下游玩赏景时看了上联，遥望小东门城墙对出了下联：'城墙垛子倒长牙齿啃青天'。时至今日，这副对联依然是人们津津乐道的趣谈。

English 英文

Zhongxiang Wenfeng Pagoda, originally named the White Milk Eminent Monk Pagoda, is located on Longshan (Dragon Mountain) east of Zhongxiang city proper. It is a stupa-style solid brick pagoda, also called a Lama pagoda, completed in the 23rd year of Hongwu, Ming (1390). The pagoda is nearly 22 meters high, entirely snow-white, composed of five parts: pagoda base, pagoda body,相轮 (harmika rings), precious canopy, and pagoda finial. The pagoda base is octagonal, divided into upper and lower sections, with brick corbelling contracting layer by layer. The pagoda body is a slender stupa, with a Buddhist niche opened on the front, enshrining a Bodhisattva inside. Above the pagoda body are as many as twenty-one layers of相轮, seven more than the common thirteen-layer相轮; the distance between each layer is relatively far, decreasing sequentially from bottom to top, and the轮廓 is somewhat like the dense-eave pagoda of Han Chinese Buddhism. Below the second layer of相轮, small niches are also opened on all four sides. The precious canopy part is three layers of copper discs, with wind chimes hanging on all four sides; the pagoda finial above has one column embedded with three 'Yuan' characters,寓意 'Sanyuan Jidi' (First place in all three imperial examinations). Wenfeng Pagoda has a slender proportion, very different from the familiar image of a Lama pagoda; compared with the White Pagoda of Baita Temple in Beijing and the White Pagoda of Tayuan Temple on Wutai Mountain, it appears tall, slender, and graceful. According to the 'Zhongxiang County Annals' of the Republican period, during the Huang Chao Uprising at the end of the Tang, an eminent monk was killed here at the Maitreya Courtyard, and what flowed out was milky white blood; hence 'Huang Chao was surprised by it, and the local people paid respects, piling earth into a stupa.' Later, the White Milk Eminent Monk Pagoda rose and fell several times, and by the end of the Yuan dynasty it had completely become a pile of ruins. In the 22nd year of Hongwu, Ming (1389), Zhongxiang officials and local worthies rebuilt this pagoda, changing the Maitreya Courtyard to Bao'en Temple and the White Milk Eminent Monk Pagoda to Wenfeng Pagoda, to pray that Zhongxiang's literary style would thrive for a thousand years and talents would emerge in large numbers. Local Tang Zhichun wrote an article recording the reconstruction process, and noted that 'inside the pagoda are hidden one ancient Buddha statue, two Pratyekabuddha relics, twenty relics of Master Bida, and one spiritual bone of Master Bifeng.' Regarding this pagoda, there is also an interesting folk rumor. It is said that during the Qianlong period of the Qing, the pagoda finial was tilted; a craftsman in the city climbed to the top of the pagoda to straighten it, and the whole city celebrated. The prefectural yamen came up with the first half of a couplet: 'Wenfeng Pagoda tilts its finger and pounds the red sun,' and for a time no one could match the second half. Later, Li Huang, the Left Vice Minister of War, returned to his hometown; while sightseeing below the pagoda he saw the first half, and looking at the Small East Gate city wall in the distance, he matched the second half: 'The city wall battlements grow teeth backwards and gnaw the blue sky.' To this day, this couplet is still an interesting topic people enjoy talking about.

181. 兴王府凤翔宫

Fengxiang Palace of Prince Xing's Mansion
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明
地址 Address
钟祥市王府大道
类型 Type
王府建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
平面布局嘉靖皇帝出生地大礼仪之争单檐歇山建筑
中文 Chinese

兴王府是明世宗嘉靖皇帝的出生地，也是他的父亲兴献王朱祐杬的府邸。兴建于明弘治四年（1491），三年后朱祐杬从北京出发，就藩湖广安陆州，即今天的钟祥。1519年薨逝，谥号为'献'；1521年，袭封为兴王不久的朱厚熜被迎往北京继承皇位。

他即位后便开始整修父亲的陵墓，并对王府'重加修饰，其制俱视帝都宫阙'；嘉靖十八年（1539），又增建了世子府，使兴王宫成为一组不同于普通藩王府的宏大复杂的建筑群。根据《兴都志》记载，兴王府'矩式之祥，深严之秘，创以藩府之制，饰以天子之规，内外合一，先后相辉，实海内所创见者焉'！

兴王府原占地面积约3万平方米，坐北朝南，分为东侧的世子府和西侧的旧王府两个区域，二者各自独立又相互关联。原有龙飞殿、隆庆殿、卿云宫、凤翔宫、御书斋、荷花池等，大部分毁于明末兵燹，清乾隆年间部分重修，现仅存凤翔宫。

凤翔宫为一座单檐歇山建筑，面阔五间，进深三间，抬梁式构架，青绿色琉璃瓦屋面。正中三间出前廊，隔扇装修。凤翔宫前原有一个椭圆形荷花池，东侧还有一组御书斋，现已无存。

兴王府的兴衰是明代'大礼仪'之争的重要见证，也是与世界文化遗产明显陵相辅相成的重要实物资料。

English 英文

Xingwang Mansion was the birthplace of Emperor Shizong Jiajing of the Ming, and also the mansion of his father, Xingxian King Zhu Youyuan. It was first built in the 4th year of Hongzhi, Ming (1491); three years later, Zhu Youyuan departed from Beijing to take up his fief at Anlu Prefecture in Hunan, i.e., present-day Zhongxiang. He died in 1519, with the posthumous title 'Xian'; in 1521, Zhu Houcong, who had not long succeeded as the Xing King, was welcomed to Beijing to inherit the throne. After his accession, he began to renovate his father's mausoleum and 'heavily decorate the prince's mansion, with its system all following the imperial palace of the capital'; in the 18th year of Jiajing (1539), he also added the Shizi (Heir Apparent) Mansion, making the Xingwang Palace a grand and complex architectural group different from ordinary prince's mansions. According to the 'Xingdu Annals,' Xingwang Mansion had 'the auspiciousness of its standard form, the profundity and strictness of its secrets, created with the system of a prince's mansion, decorated with the regulations of the Son of Heaven, inner and outer united, front and back shining together, truly something unprecedented within the seas'! Xingwang Mansion originally covered about 30,000 square meters, facing south, divided into two areas: the Shizi Mansion on the east and the old prince's mansion on the west, each independent yet interconnected. It originally had the Longfei Hall, Longqing Hall, Qingyun Palace, Fengxiang Palace, Imperial Study, Lotus Pond, etc., most of which were destroyed by war at the end of the Ming; partially rebuilt during the Qianlong period of the Qing, now only the Fengxiang Palace remains. Fengxiang Palace is a single-eave hip-and-gable building, five bays wide and three bays deep, with a post-and-lintel frame and a blue-green glazed tile roof. The central three bays project a front porch, with lattice partition decoration. In front of Fengxiang Palace there was originally an oval lotus pond, and on the east side there was also a group of Imperial Study, now no longer existing. The rise and fall of Xingwang Mansion is an important witness to the 'Great Rites Controversy' of the Ming, and is also important physical material complementary to the World Cultural Heritage Xianling Tombs of the Ming Dynasty.

浮雕曾省吾六柱三间五楼恩荣
中文 Chinese

少司马坊是明万历年间的兵部侍郎曾省吾于万历九年（1581）主持建造的，采用青灰石，通高11米，宽近10米，六柱三间五楼，明间为一字形，两侧为八字形。明间两柱前后各有一对石狮子，两侧的四根则各有抱鼓石。正中檐下悬一块'恩荣'竖匾，其下为'少司马'石匾。

每间的额枋都遍布各种吉祥纹样的镂空浮雕，有二龙戏珠、凤凰、牡丹、松鹤、麒麟、鲤鱼等，镂空极深，图案富有动感，整座牌坊显得玲珑通透又不失宏伟壮丽。'少司马'是兵部侍郎的别称，表明建造石坊时主人的身份。

据《钟祥县志》记载，曾省吾是明湖广承天府钟祥县人，生于嘉靖十一年（1532），嘉靖三十五年（1556）中进士，万历三年（1575）任兵部侍郎，后升任工部尚书、加封太子太保。

万历十年（1582），首辅张居正病故，一批曾受他重用、拥护改革和变法的大臣受到牵连，其中就包括曾省吾。万历皇帝先是勒令曾省吾退休，美其名曰'致仕'，随后很快下旨查抄其房屋田产，并削去官籍，将其发回原籍为民，永不叙用。

曾家原本是钟祥名门望族，曾省吾的曾祖父、祖父和父亲都曾被封为光禄大夫，曾祖母、祖母和母亲诰封一品太夫人。钟祥的察院街从前曾有两座牌坊，一为'两朝纶命'，一为'父子进士'，所标榜的就是曾氏一门四代的荣耀。而在少司马坊以东，原来还有一座'大司空坊'，是曾省吾任工部尚书时所立。

经历了漫长的时光，世事变幻，如今幸存下来的只有这座少司马坊了。2010年之前，少司马坊耸立在钟祥市城区兰台山的右侧。随着城市发展，牌坊周边的环境越来越拥挤混乱。配合钟祥新博物馆的建设，钟祥市对少司马坊进行了整体搬迁。

尽管在搬迁过程中遇到了不少困难、牌坊甚至还受到了损坏，但经过热爱文物的钟祥市民的共同努力，迁至新址的少司马坊重新屹立于莫愁湖畔，恢复了往昔的风光，也依然寄托着人们对于这位被冤屈的一代能臣深深的敬意。

English 英文

Shaosima Memorial Archway was presided over and built by Zeng Shengwu, the Minister of War during the Wanli period of the Ming, in the 9th year of Wanli (1581), using blue-gray stone, with a total height of 11 meters and a width of nearly 10 meters, six columns and three bays with five stories, the central bay in a '一' shape and the two sides in an 'eight' shape. In front of and behind the two columns of the central bay are each a pair of stone lions, and the four columns on the sides each have drum-holding stones. Under the central eave hangs a vertical 'Enrong' (Imperial Grace) plaque, below which is the 'Shaosima' (Junior Minister of War) stone plaque. The architraves of each bay are covered with openwork relief carvings of various auspicious patterns, including two dragons playing with a pearl, phoenix, peony, pine and crane, qilin, carp, etc., with extremely deep openwork, and the patterns are full of movement; the entire archway appears exquisite and transparent yet without losing its grandeur and magnificence. 'Shaosima' is another name for the Vice Minister of War, indicating the identity of the owner when the stone archway was built. According to the 'Zhongxiang County Annals,' Zeng Shengwu was a native of Zhongxiang County, Cheng天府, Huguang, Ming, born in the 11th year of Jiajing (1532), passed the jinshi examination in the 35th year of Jiajing (1556), served as Vice Minister of War in the 3rd year of Wanli (1575), and was later promoted to Minister of Works and conferred the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. In the 10th year of Wanli (1582), after the death of the Senior Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng, a group of ministers who had been重用 by him and supported reform and变法 were implicated, including Zeng Shengwu. Emperor Wanli first ordered Zeng Shengwu to retire, euphemistically calling it 'zhishi' (returning office), and then soon issued an edict to confiscate his houses and land, strip him of his official rank, and send him back to his hometown as a commoner, never to be employed again. The Zeng family was originally a prominent clan in Zhongxiang; Zeng Shengwu's great-grandfather, grandfather, and father were all conferred the title of Guanglu Grand Master, and his great-grandmother, grandmother, and mother were conferred the title of First Rank Grand Lady. There were once two archways on Chayuan Street in Zhongxiang, one called 'Liangchao Lunming' (Edicts of Two Reigns) and one called 'Fuzi Jinshi' (Father and Son Jinshi), which advertised the glory of four generations of the Zeng family. East of Shaosima Archway, there was originally a 'Dasikong Archway,' erected when Zeng Shengwu served as Minister of Works. After a long time and changing world events, the only surviving archway today is this Shaosima Archway. Before 2010, Shaosima Archway stood on the right side of Lantai Mountain in the urban area of Zhongxiang City. With urban development, the environment around the archway became increasingly crowded and chaotic. In conjunction with the construction of the new Zhongxiang Museum, Zhongxiang City carried out an overall relocation of Shaosima Archway. Although many difficulties were encountered during the relocation process and the archway was even damaged, through the joint efforts of Zhongxiang citizens who love cultural relics, the relocated Shaosima Archway stands again by Mochou Lake, restoring its former scenery, and still寄托s people's deep respect for this wronged capable minister of a generation.

中文 Chinese

石牌镇位于钟祥市西南，汉江西岸，是钟祥历史最为悠久的古镇。在古镇的西侧现保存有一处汉代荆城遗址，属于湖北省重点文物保护单位，三国时关羽曾在这里屯兵，而这座古城也是今天石牌镇的前身。

明末清初时，这里因为临近汉江，依托汉水便利的交通条件，逐渐发展成一个繁华的区域中心，而'石牌'一名就源于岸边的一块石头牌坊。当时往来船只均以此牌坊为标记，停靠装卸货物，牌坊边也有不少茶肆客栈供往来商旅歇脚，'石牌'这个名称也随着商人的脚步逐渐传播开来。

石牌老镇区现有的道路骨架基本保持了明清时期的格局，主要的道路有东西相连的山街、上正街、集街，南北相接的西街与北门街，二者纵横交错呈十字形，而整个镇区的形态被当地人称为'凤凰展翅'，故石牌也有'凤台'之称。古镇的西、南、北三面过去有土城墙环绕，东面则以汉水为天然屏障。

在每条街巷的入口和交会处都有用于安全防卫的关卡——闸门，夜里和遇到外敌入侵时便关闭各门。因此，古镇的格局有'十街三巷十八门'的说法，具有平原地区城镇的防卫式格局。闸门均为砖砌拱券门，每一座都有自...

English 英文

Shipai Town is located southwest of Zhongxiang City, on the west bank of the Han River, and is the oldest ancient town in Zhongxiang. On the west side of the ancient town, a Han dynasty Jing City site is now preserved, belonging to a Hubei Provincial Key Cultural Heritage Protection Unit; during the Three Kingdoms period, Guan Yu once stationed troops here, and this ancient city is also the predecessor of today's Shipai Town. At the end of the Ming and beginning of the Qing, because it was close to the Han River and relied on the convenient transportation conditions of the Han River, it gradually developed into a prosperous regional center, and the name 'Shipai' (Stone Archway) originated from a stone archway on the bank. At that time, passing ships all used this archway as a marker to dock and load/unload goods, and there were also many tea houses and inns by the archway for passing merchants and travelers to rest; the name 'Shipai' gradually spread with the footsteps of merchants. The existing road framework of the old Shipai town area basically maintains the pattern of the Ming and Qing periods; the main roads are the east-west connected Shan Street, Shangzheng Street, and Ji Street, and the north-south connected West Street and North Gate Street, which crisscross in a cross shape. The shape of the entire town area is called by locals 'Phoenix Spreading Wings,' hence Shipai is also called 'Fengtai' (Phoenix Platform). In the past, the west, south, and north sides of the ancient town were surrounded by earthen city walls, and the east side used the Han River as a natural barrier. At the entrances and intersections of each street and alley, there were checkpoints for security and defense—gate doors, which were closed at night and when encountering foreign enemy invasion. Therefore, the pattern of the ancient town has the saying 'ten streets, three alleys, eighteen gates,' with a defensive town pattern typical of plain areas. The gate doors are all brick-built arch doors, each with its own...

184. 兰台书院

Lantai Academy
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清
地址 Address
钟祥市石城中路兰台中学内
类型 Type
教育建筑·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
平面格局环境宋玉阳春白雪杨炳
中文 Chinese

兰台书院所在的地方为古兰台山，相传是战国时期楚王兰台宫的所在，宋玉曾在这里作《风赋》《对楚王问》，诞生了'阳春白雪''曲高和寡'等著名的成语，至今兰台东侧仍有宋玉井。历代诗人创作了大量以兰台为吟咏对象的怀古诗，如李白《寄上吴王其三》：'襄王怜宋玉，愿入兰台宫。

'张九龄《登古阳云台》：'楚国兹故都，兰台有余址。'还有李商隐的《楚宫》《石城》等。到了明朝嘉靖年间，作为皇帝故土的钟祥更名为兴都，受皇帝南巡的影响，大江南北的文人墨客纷至沓来，'兰台午风'被列入郢中八景，备受推崇。而现存的这座兰台书院和钟祥兰台中学，就是这里文脉的延续。

书院的前身是清代探花杨炳的故宅。杨炳是雍正年间一位优秀的教育大臣，经他考试录取的考生，很多都成为优秀的人才。后杨炳因思念老母，辞官回乡，在兰台东侧隐居二十余年。

乾隆十五年（1750），由安陆府官员集资募捐，在杨炳故宅背后的兰台山上修建了几个四合院，取名为'兰台书院'，作为本府学署的训导署和士子们以文相会的场所。书院在乾隆、道光和咸丰年间曾三次修整。

清末停止科举后，安陆府在兰台书院创办了安陆府师范学堂，即今天钟祥一中（兰台中学）的前身。书院坐北朝南，两进四合院，有前厅、后堂和厢房，单檐硬山灰瓦屋顶，前厅和后堂均面阔九间，进深一间。

整个书院位于兰台山之上，视野开阔，远眺江山，令人心旷神怡，情趣飞扬。

English 英文

The place where Lantai Academy is located is ancient Lantai Mountain; legend has it that it was the site of the King of Chu's Lantai Palace during the Warring States period, where Song Yu once wrote 'Ode to the Wind' and 'Reply to the King of Chu's Questions,' giving birth to famous idioms such as 'Spring Snow' (highbrow art) and 'too highbrow to be popular.' To this day, there is still a Song Yu Well on the east side of Lantai. Poets of past dynasties created a large number of historical poems with Lantai as the subject of chanting, such as Li Bai's 'To the King of Wu, No.3': 'King Xiang pitied Song Yu, wishing to enter the Lantai Palace.' Zhang Jiuling's 'Climbing the Ancient Yangyun Terrace': 'Chu State's former capital here, Lantai has remaining foundations.' And Li Shangyin's 'Chu Palace' and 'Stone City,' etc. By the Jiajing period of the Ming, Zhongxiang, as the emperor's hometown, was renamed Xingdu (Capital of Rise); influenced by the emperor's southern tour, literati and scholars from all over the country flocked here, and 'Lantai Noon Wind' was listed among the Eight Scenes of Yingzhong, highly esteemed. The existing Lantai Academy and Zhongxiang Lantai Middle School are the continuation of the cultural lineage here. The predecessor of the academy was the former residence of Yang Bing, a Qing dynasty tanhua (third-place jinshi). Yang Bing was an outstanding educational minister during the Yongzheng period; many of the candidates he examined and admitted became excellent talents. Later, Yang Bing, missing his elderly mother, resigned and returned to his hometown, living in seclusion on the east side of Lantai for more than twenty years. In the 15th year of Qianlong (1750), officials of Anlu Prefecture raised funds and donations to build several courtyards on Lantai Mountain behind Yang Bing's former residence, naming it 'Lantai Academy,' serving as the instruction office of the prefectural school and a place for scholars to meet through literature. The academy was renovated three times during the Qianlong, Daoguang, and Xianfeng periods. After the imperial examination was abolished at the end of the Qing, Anlu Prefecture founded the Anlu Prefecture Normal School at Lantai Academy, the predecessor of today's Zhongxiang No.1 Middle School (Lantai Middle School). The academy faces south, with two courtyards, having a front hall, rear hall, and wing rooms, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs; both the front hall and rear hall are nine bays wide and one bay deep. The entire academy is located on Lantai Mountain, with a broad view; looking far at the rivers and mountains, it makes one feel relaxed and joyful, with emotions soaring.

中文 Chinese

建于宣统元年（1909），为旌表儒士魏元善妻常氏所建，是荆门年代最晚的牌坊。它的结构与少司马坊类似，六柱三间五楼，明间一字形，两侧八字形。青灰石仿木结构，共有三层檐楼，层层交错，轮廓非常丰富。明间有三层额枋，每层都有精美的雕刻，上面两层为人物故事，最下层为双龙戏珠。

最下方的石匾上阴刻'节孝可风'四个大字。柱脚用石狮、石象作倚柱石。

English 英文

Built in the 1st year of Xuantong (1909), to commend Chang, wife of Confucian scholar Wei Yuanshan, it is the latest-dated memorial archway in Jingmen. Its structure is similar to Shaosima Archway: six columns, three bays, five stories, with the central bay in a '一' shape and the two sides in an 'eight' shape. Blue-gray stone imitation-wood structure, with three layers of eave towers,交错 layer by layer, with a very rich轮廓. The central bay has three layers of architraves, each with exquisite carvings; the upper two layers are figure stories, and the lowest layer is two dragons playing with a pearl. On the lowest stone plaque, the four large characters 'Jie Xiao Ke Feng' (Chastity and Piety Worthy of Emulation) are incised. The column bases use stone lions and stone elephants as column-holding stones.

186. 京山吴湾民居

Vernacular Dwellings in Wuwan
级别 Level
