看点 Highlights
烽火山墙平面格局豫鄂边区委员会新四军第五师
中文 Chinese

吴湾民居建造于清末，坐南朝北，由两栋并连的天井院组成，公共的墙被打通后连为一体。西边的宅院有两间门屋、三间正房和两间厢房围绕着天井，门屋有前廊，木质门窗；正房屋顶高于厢房。正房明间为堂屋，两侧为卧室，屋顶均用小青瓦。

东边的天井院正房与西边一样，但门屋没有外廊，门窗均为石材，山墙升起做成马头墙式的封火墙。这处宅院四面环山，地势险要，不远处的鸳鸯溪是当地主要的水源。

1940年10月至1942年9月，鄂豫边区委员会和新四军第五师曾在这里驻扎，并改小焕岭为小花岭，寓意抗战之花漫山遍岭。其中堂屋作为领导人的办公室，两间厢房则为卫兵室和传达室。

English 英文

Wuwan Dwellings were built at the end of the Qing, facing south, composed of two connected courtyard houses, with the common wall打通后 connected as one. The western courtyard has two gate rooms, three principal rooms, and two wing rooms surrounding the courtyard; the gate rooms have front porches with wooden doors and windows; the principal room roof is higher than the wing rooms. The central bay of the principal room is the main hall, with bedrooms on both sides, and the roofs all use small gray tiles. The principal room of the eastern courtyard is the same as the western one, but the gate room has no exterior porch, the doors and windows are all stone, and the gable walls rise to form horse-head-wall-style fire-sealing walls. This courtyard is surrounded by mountains on all sides, with a strategic terrain; the nearby Yuanyang Stream is the main local water source. From October 1940 to September 1942, the Hubei-Henan Border Region Committee and the Fifth Division of the New Fourth Army were stationed here, and renamed Xiaohuanling to Xiaohualing, meaning the flowers of the war of resistance spread all over the mountains and ridges. Among them, the main hall served as the leaders' office, and the two wing rooms served as the guard room and communication room.

187. 京山牛车垱民居

Vernacular Dwellings in Nuochedang
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清
地址 Address
京山县钱场镇西北约2公里吴家大湾
类型 Type
民居建筑·木结构
看点 Highlights
回字形天井木雕插梁式屋架精致雕刻装饰
中文 Chinese

这座民居的具体建造年代不详，大致在清末民初时期，由两个'回'字形的天井院串联而成。外墙用土坯砖，内部的门窗墙体则采用杉木，从外面看朴素无华，甚至觉得有些简陋，内部却非常舒适，华丽典雅。老屋坐西北朝东南，有两间门屋、三间正房和四间厢房。

屋架的加工十分讲究，明间是一种介于抬梁式和穿斗式之间的'插梁'式屋架，从明间的柱身上还伸出鱼尾型的斗拱，两山则为穿斗式屋架。屋顶均为双坡悬山，铺小青瓦，其中正房的屋顶要高于厢房。正房的后堂中设神龛，供奉祖先和'天地君亲师'牌位，左右两间为长辈的卧室；

厢房的前部用来储藏杂物，后部则是晚辈的居室。这种中轴对称、长幼有序的布置，符合儒家传统的礼制思想。这座建筑最有特点的是它精致的雕刻装饰，几乎所有的槅扇门窗和栏杆斜撑上都布满了吉祥寓意的纹样。特别是第二天井窗格中心的雕刻，有狮子、麒麟等瑞兽，也有麻姑献寿、天官赐福等神话传说。

而屋檐下的斜撑，繁复的缠枝花纹和镂空雕刻，体现了木工师傅精湛的技艺。站在天井中，光线从屋檐泻下，整座建筑给人一种静谧的美感，仿佛可以忘记时间的流逝。

English 英文

The specific construction date of this dwelling is unknown, roughly from the late Qing to early Republican period, composed of two '回'-shaped courtyards connected in series. The exterior walls use adobe bricks, while the interior doors, windows, and walls use Chinese fir; from the outside it looks plain and unadorned, even somewhat crude, but the interior is very comfortable, gorgeous and elegant. The old house faces southeast from northwest, with two gate rooms, three principal rooms, and four wing rooms. The processing of the roof frame is very particular; the central bay uses an 'inserted beam' roof frame, a type between the post-and-lintel and column-and-tie styles; from the column body of the central bay, fish-tail-shaped bracket sets also extend out, and the two gable sides use column-and-tie roof frames. The roofs are all double-slope overhanging gables, covered with small gray tiles, with the principal room roof higher than the wing rooms. In the rear hall of the principal room, a shrine is set up, enshrining ancestors and the 'Heaven-Earth-Monarch-Parent-Teacher' tablet; the left and right rooms are the bedrooms of the elders; the front part of the wing rooms is used for storing sundries, and the rear part is the living quarters of the younger generation. This centrally symmetric, orderly arrangement of elders and juniors conforms to traditional Confucian ritual thought. The most distinctive feature of this building is its exquisite carved decoration; almost all lattice doors, windows, and railing diagonal braces are covered with patterns of auspicious meaning. Especially the carving at the center of the second courtyard window lattice includes auspicious beasts such as lions and qilins, as well as mythological legends such as Magu Presenting Longevity and the Heavenly Official Bestowing Blessings. The diagonal braces under the eaves, with complex scrolling branch patterns and openwork carvings, reflect the exquisite craftsmanship of the carpenters. Standing in the courtyard, with light pouring down from the eaves, the entire building gives a sense of tranquil beauty, as if one could forget the passage of time.

188. 文笔峰塔

Wenbifeng Pagoda

类型 Type

拱券门圆窗旋转楼梯青云直上六角七层
中文 Chinese

这座楼阁式的风水塔建于清光绪五年（1879），3年后完工，六角七层，高约33米。塔的底层用青石砌筑，南侧开门，门额书'青云直上'四字。二至七层以大型条砖叠砌，每层设拱券门和小圆窗，各层、各面门窗交错相对。

塔身内部有125级台阶，可以旋转登至塔顶。整个塔身的轮廓笔直硬挺，具有典型的清代塔的特征。文笔峰塔建成后，周围又相继修建了勉园、水波凉亭和文昌阁，还有纪念明代京山经学家郝楚望的楚望楼等建筑。

English 英文

This multi-eaved fengshui pagoda was built in the 5th year of Guangxu, Qing (1879), completed 3 years later, hexagonal with seven stories, about 33 meters high. The bottom story of the pagoda is built with bluestone, with a door opened on the south side, and the door lintel inscribed with the four characters 'Qingyun Zhishang' (Rising Straight to the Blue Clouds). From the second to the seventh story, large brick strips are stacked, each story with arched doors and small round windows, with doors and windows on each story and each face交错 opposite. Inside the pagoda body, there are 125 steps, which can spiral up to the top of the pagoda. The outline of the entire pagoda body is straight and rigid, with typical characteristics of Qing dynasty pagodas. After Wenbifeng Pagoda was completed, Mian Garden, Water Wave Cool Pavilion, and Wenchang Pavilion were successively built around it, as well as buildings such as the Chuwang Tower commemorating Hao Chuwang, a Jingshan classics scholar of the Ming.

荆州市

Jingzhou
58 处

189. 荆州城墙/荆州古城

City Wall of Jingzhou / Jingzhou Ancient City
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
荆州市城历史文化旅游区
类型 Type
古城址·砖石结构、木结构
看点 Highlights
完好的明代府城墙独特藏兵洞延续时间长跨越朝代多砖城为主土垣为辅
中文 Chinese

荆州古城又名江陵城。是我国保存最为完好的明代府城墙之一，具有延续时间长、跨越朝代多、砖城为主、土垣为辅的特点。战国时，楚成王在今城东南隅兴建渚宫，为江陵建置之始，楚幽王在渚宫址上修筑郢都，基地为江边丘陵，故名江陵，此后两千年江陵城位置基本不变。

东汉及三国时期，蜀将关羽镇守荆州，在渚宫旧址西北筑土城。《水经注》载：（荆州）旧城关羽所筑。某北攻曹仁，吕蒙袭而据之。某曰：此城吾所筑，不可攻也，乃引而退。

关于关羽筑土城，有一段关羽'智斗九仙女'的传说：相传关羽镇守荆州，发动十万守城将士，挑土堆城，土地神上报天庭，王母娘娘派九仙女前去收回荆州为上天管辖的圣地，以免连年争夺，干戈不息，百姓涂炭。关羽提出与九仙女比赛筑城，以半夜鸡鸣为限，谁先筑成城墙，便拥有对城的管辖权。

九仙女仰仗仙法，以衣裙包土，兜土成墙，眼看将赢，关羽用芦苇扎垛，堵住缺口，很快筑成，同时，使人去鸡笼边拍簸箕学鸡叫，引发全城公鸡提早打鸣，九仙女听闻鸡叫，措手不及，黯然退去。

前来帮助筑城的张飞手拎两筐土赶来，听闻胜讯，喜不自胜，将土倒在城边，形成大土丘，后世称'张飞一担土'，宋代盛宏之《荆州记》对此有绘色的描述：'一峰回然，西映落月，远而望之，如画扇然。'故'张飞一担土'又名画扇峰。其上曾建有六角小亭，当时被誉为荆州城八景之一。

传说虽不足信，但三国之土城确得到今天考古之印证：1997年10月，考古工作者先后发现了隐身现砖墙内侧的宋代砖墙和已沉寂地下五代砖墙，以及叠压于现城墙之下的三国、两晋时期的土城墙。

由此可见，三国至五代、宋、明清，历代荆州城墙上下重叠，没有发生大的变动。东晋时，恒温督荆州，将汉东城与关羽所建西城连接起来，其间城垣并未拆除，形成了城中有隔墙的特殊格局。

五代后梁时期，南平王高季兴改筑砖城，《五代史》载：'季兴大筑重城，复建雄楚楼、望沙楼为扦蔽，执畚锸者十数万人，将校宾友皆负土相助。郭外五十里冢墓多发掘，取砖以甓城。工毕，阴惨之夜，常闻鬼泣，及见磷火焉。'此后宋、明、清多有记毁、重建、增建、改建及修葺。

现存城垣为清顺治年间依明城旧基所建，多有明代遗构。

由于荆州为中原通往岭南之要冲，为历朝重镇和兵家必争之地，荆州城墙的军事防御功能尤其得到历朝重视，围绕着攻城和守城，发生在荆州古城的厮杀征战几乎没有停止过，因此，荆州古城也留下许多历史故事，如春秋战国时期的吴王攻郢，如三国时刘备借荆州、大意失荆州等。

如今，彼时故事烟消云散，只留下'铁打荆州'美名。除了古城墙本身，荆州内外还留下许多与三国战争有关的遗迹、遗物。

如古城墙南门内侧的关庙，就曾是关羽镇守荆州时的府第，新南门边上的关羽祠、卸甲山，北城墙脚下的洗马池、得胜街、西城墙外面的点将台、拍马山、马跑泉等。

English 英文

Jingzhou Ancient City, also called Jiangling City, is one of the best-preserved Ming dynasty prefectural city walls in China, characterized by a long duration, spanning many dynasties, with brick walls as the main part and earthen walls as auxiliary. During the Warring States period, King Cheng of Chu built Zhugong in the southeastern corner of the present city, marking the beginning of Jiangling's establishment; King You of Chu built Yingdu on the site of Zhugong, with the base being a riverside hill, hence the name Jiangling. Thereafter, the location of Jiangling City remained basically unchanged for two thousand years. During the Eastern Han and Three Kingdoms periods, Shu general Guan Yu, guarding Jingzhou, built an earthen city northwest of the old Zhugong site. The 'Commentary on the Water Classic' records: The old city of (Jingzhou) was built by Guan Yu. When Guan Yu attacked Cao Ren to the north, Lü Meng seized and occupied it. Guan Yu said: This city was built by me, it cannot be attacked, so he withdrew. Regarding Guan Yu building the earthen city, there is a legend of Guan Yu 'outwitting the nine fairies': It is said that when Guan Yu guarded Jingzhou, he mobilized 100,000 defending soldiers to carry earth and pile up the city; the Earth God reported to Heaven, and the Queen Mother of the West sent nine fairies to take back Jingzhou as a holy land under Heaven's jurisdiction, to avoid years of contention and endless warfare causing suffering to the people. Guan Yu proposed to compete with the nine fairies in building the city, with the rooster crowing at midnight as the limit; whoever built the city wall first would have jurisdiction over the city. The nine fairies, relying on immortal magic, carried earth in their skirts and built walls, and were about to win. Guan Yu used reeds to tie battlements and block gaps, quickly completing the construction; at the same time, he had people pat winnowing baskets by the chicken coop to imitate rooster crowing, causing all roosters in the city to crow early. The nine fairies, hearing the rooster crow, were caught off guard and retreated dejectedly. Zhang Fei, who came to help build the city, arrived carrying two baskets of earth; hearing the news of victory, he was overjoyed and poured the earth by the city, forming a large earthen mound, later called 'Zhang Fei's Load of Earth.' Song dynasty Sheng Hongzhi's 'Records of Jingzhou' gives a vivid description: 'A peak rises abruptly, reflecting the setting moon to the west; viewed from afar, it is like a painted fan.' Hence 'Zhang Fei's Load of Earth' is also called Painted Fan Peak. A hexagonal small pavilion was once built on it, and at that time it was praised as one of the Eight Scenes of Jingzhou City. Although the legend is not credible, the earthen city of the Three Kingdoms has indeed been confirmed by archaeology today: In October 1997, archaeologists successively discovered Song dynasty brick walls hidden inside the present brick walls, Five Dynasties brick walls sunk underground, and Three Kingdoms and Two Jin dynasties earthen city walls叠压 under the present city wall. This shows that from the Three Kingdoms to the Five Dynasties, Song, Ming, and Qing, the Jingzhou city walls of successive dynasties overlapped vertically without major changes. During the Eastern Jin, Huan Wen, governor of Jingzhou, connected the Han eastern city with the western city built by Guan Yu, without demolishing the city walls between them, forming a special pattern of partition walls within the city. During the Later Liang of the Five Dynasties, Gao Jixing, King of Nanping, rebuilt the brick city; the 'History of the Five Dynasties' records: 'Jixing greatly built heavy walls, and rebuilt the Xiongchu Tower and Wangsha Tower as defenses; more than 100,000 people carried baskets and shovels, and generals, officials, and friends all helped carry earth. Tombs within fifty li outside the city were mostly excavated to take bricks for walling. When the work was completed, on gloomy nights, ghost crying was often heard, and will-o'-the-wisps were seen.' Thereafter, the Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties had many records of destruction, reconstruction, addition, alteration, and repair. The existing city wall was built during the Shunzhi period of the Qing on the old foundation of the Ming city, with many Ming remains. Because Jingzhou was a strategic passage from the Central Plains to Lingnan, an important town of successive dynasties and a contested place for military strategists, the military defense function of the Jingzhou city wall was especially valued by successive dynasties. Around attacking and defending the city, the bloody battles that took place in Jingzhou Ancient City almost never stopped; therefore, Jingzhou Ancient City also left many historical stories, such as King Wu attacking Ying during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, and Liu Bei borrowing Jingzhou and carelessly losing Jingzhou during the Three Kingdoms. Today, those stories have vanished like smoke, leaving only the reputation of 'Iron Jingzhou.' Besides the ancient city wall itself, many relics and remains related to the Three Kingdoms wars remain inside and outside Jingzhou. For example, the Guan Temple inside the south gate of the ancient city wall was once Guan Yu's mansion when he guarded Jingzhou; the Guan Yu Shrine and Xiejia Mountain by the new south gate, the Horse Washing Pool and Desheng Street at the foot of the north city wall, the General-Appointing Platform, Horse-Beating Mountain, and Horse-Running Spring outside the west city wall, etc.

190. 城墙及护城河

City Wall and Moat
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
荆州市荆州古城
类型 Type
古城址·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
不规则长方形周长11.28公里高8.83米糯米浆叠砌藏兵洞
中文 Chinese

荆州城墙平面呈不规则长方形，东西长而南北窄。

城垣周长11.28公里，高8.83米，城基条石垒筑，墙身用青砖石灰糯米浆叠砌，青砖铺面，古城墙上现存有上百处文字砖，记载了城砖的产地，来自鄂、豫、陕、湘、桂、黔、赣等地，最早的文字砖为南宋淳熙年间烧制，最晚的文字砖为民国二十六年（1937年）。

环城设有雉堞、敌楼、炮台、藏兵洞等设施。城垣内为土坡，无砖护面，外为护城河，宽10米－120米不等。河岸块石以铁件锚拉，城门设闸以拒洪水，城内下水道系统至今尚存。

English 英文

The Jingzhou city wall has an irregular rectangular plan, long east-west and narrow north-south. The city wall has a perimeter of 11.28 km and a height of 8.83 meters; the wall base is built with strip stones, and the wall body is叠砌 with blue bricks, lime, and glutinous rice mortar, with blue brick paving. On the ancient city wall, there are now over a hundred inscribed bricks recording the production places of the city bricks, from Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Jiangxi, etc.; the earliest inscribed bricks were fired during the Chunxi period of the Southern Song, and the latest inscribed bricks were from the 26th year of the Republic (1937). Around the city are facilities such as battlements, watchtowers, gun emplacements, and soldier-hiding caves. Inside the city wall is an earthen slope without brick facing, and outside is a moat, varying from 10 to 120 meters wide. The riverbank block stones are anchored with iron pieces, and the city gates are equipped with sluices to resist floods; the underground drainage system inside the city still exists today.

191. 瓮城、城门及城门楼

Wengcheng, City Gates and Gate Towers
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
荆州市荆州古城
类型 Type
古城址·砖石结构、木结构
看点 Highlights
六座城门六门均设瓮城藏兵洞大北门拱极门
中文 Chinese

荆州古城共有城门六座，东垣、北垣各2门，南垣、西垣各1门，六门均设瓮城，上有城楼、马步。20世纪50年代，为缓解城内交通，新开城门3座：新东门、新南门、新北门。新开的城门均无瓮城。大北门和东门是保存原有风貌较完整的两处城门。

六座城门、楼台、马道和瓮城的规制、大小、设置各具特色。其中，又以藏兵洞最为独特。荆州城墙共设有五座藏兵洞，有的单层，有的分上下两层，可容100多人，每层又有小藏兵洞，每个小洞可容2人，洞中均有射孔。

大北门明代称拱辰门，清代称拱极门，又名得胜门，因其北通中原，是仕宦进京调职之处，古人常在此远行相送，折柳相赠，故又称柳门，宋代苏轼《荆州十首》诗云：'柳门京国道，驱马及春阳。野火烧枯草，东风动绿芒。北行连许邓，南去极衡湘。楚镜横天下，怀王信弱王。'即咏此。

主城门洞高7米，宽4.8米，深15米。出城门洞高5.8米，宽4.6米，深10米；内外门相距32米，瓮城略呈半圆形。

内券门上方有乾隆年间荆州府知府张方理立一石匾，横书'拱极门'三字。城门上城楼名朝宗楼，为纪念唐代荆州长史韩朝宗而名，建于清道光十八年（1838），日寇入侵期间受到很大破坏，1981年按原样修复。

English 英文

Jingzhou Ancient City has a total of six city gates: two on the east wall, two on the north wall, one on the south wall, and one on the west wall; all six gates are equipped with wengcheng (outer defensive enclosures), with gate towers and horse ramps above. In the 1950s, to alleviate traffic inside the city, three new city gates were opened: New East Gate, New South Gate, and New North Gate. The newly opened gates have no wengcheng. The Great North Gate and East Gate are the two city gates that preserve their original style relatively completely. The regulations, sizes, and settings of the six city gates, towers, horse ramps, and wengcheng each have their own characteristics. Among them, the soldier-hiding caves are the most unique. The Jingzhou city wall has a total of five soldier-hiding caves, some single-story, some divided into upper and lower layers, capable of holding over 100 people; each layer also has small soldier-hiding caves, each small cave can hold 2 people, and there are shooting holes in the caves. The Great North Gate was called Gongchen Gate in the Ming and Gongji Gate in the Qing, also called Desheng Gate; because it connects to the Central Plains to the north and was the place where officials went to the capital for transfers, ancients often saw off travelers here, breaking willow branches as gifts, hence it is also called Liu Gate (Willow Gate). Song dynasty Su Shi's 'Ten Poems of Jingzhou' says: 'Liu Gate is the road to the capital, driving horses in the spring sun. Wildfires burn withered grass, east wind stirs green awns. Going north connects Xu and Deng, going south reaches Heng and Xiang. The Chu mirror spans the world, King Huai was indeed a weak king.' This is the chant. The main city gate tunnel is 7 meters high, 4.8 meters wide, and 15 meters deep. The outgoing city gate tunnel is 5.8 meters high, 4.6 meters wide, and 10 meters deep; the inner and outer gates are 32 meters apart, and the wengcheng is slightly semicircular. Above the inner arch gate is a stone plaque erected by Zhang Fangli, prefect of Jingzhou during the Qianlong period, horizontally inscribed with the three characters 'Gongji Gate.' The gate tower on the city gate is named Chaozong Tower, named to commemorate Han Chaozong, the Jingzhou Chief Clerk of the Tang; it was built in the 18th year of Daoguang, Qing (1838), was greatly damaged during the Japanese invasion, and was restored according to the original in 1981.

192. 玄妙观/元妙观

Xuanmiao Taoist Temple / Yuanmiao Taoist Temple
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
荆州市荆州区荆州北路34号
类型 Type
宗教建筑·木结构、砖石结构
看点 Highlights
高台建筑九老仙都宫碑记玉皇阁铜质宝顶三天门紫皇殿
中文 Chinese

玄妙观为明代道教宫观，坐落在荆州古城北部中段，小北门内西侧，北靠城垣内墙壁，南向城区新建的荆北路，为荆州道观之首。

元妙观始建于唐代开元年间（713-741），一说始建于唐贞观九年（635），原名已不可考，据《江陵志余》载，其基址'旧在府治西北'。宋真宗祥符二年（1009）诏天下府州县监建道观一所，以'天庆'为名，因此该建筑便改名为天庆观。

元代成宗大德年间，又诏天下诸路天庆观为玄妙观，元贞三年（1297），元成宗复改为玄妙观。元至元五年（1339），元顺帝封观内主持道人唐洞云为八仙之后的第九仙，将道观迁到现址，并赐额'九老仙都宫'，规模巨大，显赫一时。据载，建造此观共耗楮币三万九千四百余缗。

明正德年间，玄妙观遭到火焚，后道观一度改为书院，嘉靖年间复为观，清代增修，清康熙时为避康熙帝玄烨名讳，曾改名元妙观。晚清时道观已破败不堪，在清代王柏心的《元妙观》诗中是这样一片荒凉景象：'废坛犹下鹤，坏馆只啼乌。'民国时，道观附属建筑毁。

1983-1984年，道观全面维修。玄妙观坐北朝南，纵长178米，总面积约1.7万平方米。

明代鼎盛时，主体建筑有山门、四圣殿、三清殿、玉皇阁及建在高台上的三天门、玄武阁，呈纵轴线递次排列，台下东西两侧建圣母、梓潼二殿。现存建筑有山门、玉皇阁、三天门、紫皇殿（又名玄武阁、玄武殿）。

其中，玉皇阁为明万历年间重建，三天门面阔三间，进深三间，为1987年新建。紫皇殿为明嘉靖年间重建，清乾隆五十年（1785）及，1985年前后修缮。

山门重檐歇山式，面阔三间，进深三间，为1987年新建。三座建筑依主轴递次而立。以城垣高势为背景，筑起不同高程的台明，使单体建筑层层拔高。

这种平面布局方式与荆州三观的另外两座——太晖观、开元观基本相似：在中轴线上依次布置各种殿堂，最后置高台主殿，并都在高台置天门（元妙观——三天门，太晖观——朝圣门）。

荆州三观的这种平面布置方式与武当山道观一般在主要殿堂之后布置父母殿的做法有明显的不同。

English 英文

Xuanmiao Temple is a Ming dynasty Taoist temple, located in the middle of the northern part of Jingzhou Ancient City, west of inside the Small North Gate, with its north against the inner wall of the city wall, facing the newly built Jingzhou North Road in the city to the south, and is the foremost Taoist temple in Jingzhou. Yuanmiao Temple was first built during the Kaiyuan period of the Tang (713-741), one saying says it was first built in the 9th year of Zhenguan, Tang (635); its original name is no longer verifiable. According to the 'Remaining Records of Jiangling,' its site was 'formerly northwest of the prefectural government.' In the 2nd year of Xiangfu, Emperor Zhenzong of Song (1009), an edict ordered all prefectures, counties, and supervisors in the empire to build one Taoist temple, named 'Tianqing' (Heavenly Celebration), hence this building was renamed Tianqing Temple. During the Dade period of Emperor Chengzong of Yuan, another edict ordered all Tianqing Temples in the empire to be renamed Xuanmiao Temple; in the 3rd year of Yuanzhen (1297), Emperor Chengzong of Yuan changed it back to Xuanmiao Temple. In the 5th year of Zhiyuan, Yuan (1339), Emperor Shun of Yuan conferred on the temple's presiding Taoist Tang Dongyun the title of the Ninth Immortal after the Eight Immortals, moved the temple to its current site, and bestowed the plaque 'Jiulao Xiandu Palace' (Palace of the Nine Elders and Immortal Capital), with a huge scale, prominent for a time. According to records, building this temple consumed over 39,400 min of paper currency. During the Zhengde period of the Ming, Xuanmiao Temple was destroyed by fire; later the temple was once converted into an academy, restored as a temple during the Jiajing period, and expanded during the Qing. During the Kangxi period of the Qing, to avoid the given name of Emperor Kangxi (Xuanye), it was once renamed Yuanmiao Temple. By the late Qing, the temple had fallen into disrepair; in Qing dynasty Wang Baixin's poem 'Yuanmiao Temple,' it is such a desolate scene: 'Abandoned altars still have cranes descending, ruined halls only have crows crowing.' During the Republic, the temple's附属 buildings were destroyed. From 1983 to 1984, the temple was comprehensively repaired. Xuanmiao Temple faces south, with a longitudinal length of 178 meters and a total area of about 17,000 square meters. At its peak in the Ming, the main buildings included the mountain gate, Four Sages Hall, Sanqing Hall, Yuhuang Pavilion, and the Three Heavens Gate and Xuanwu Pavilion built on a high platform, arranged sequentially along the longitudinal axis; east and west of the platform below were built the Hall of the Holy Mother and the Hall of Zitong. The existing buildings include the mountain gate, Yuhuang Pavilion, Three Heavens Gate, and Zihuang Hall (also called Xuanwu Pavilion, Xuanwu Hall). Among them, Yuhuang Pavilion was rebuilt during the Wanli period of the Ming; the Three Heavens Gate, three bays wide and three bays deep, was newly built in 1987. Zihuang Hall was rebuilt during the Jiajing period of the Ming, and was repaired in the 50th year of Qianlong, Qing (1785) and around 1985. The mountain gate, with double-eave hip-and-gable roof, three bays wide and three bays deep, was newly built in 1987. The three buildings stand sequentially along the main axis. Against the high terrain of the city wall as a backdrop, platforms of different elevations were built, making the individual buildings rise layer by layer. This planar layout is basically similar to the other two of Jingzhou's Three Taoist Temples—Taihui Temple and Kaiyuan Temple: various halls are arranged sequentially on the central axis, with a high-platform main hall at the end, and a heaven gate is placed on the high platform (Yuanmiao Temple—Three Heavens Gate, Taihui Temple—Pilgrimage Gate). This planar arrangement of Jingzhou's Three Taoist Temples is明显 different from the practice of Wudang Mountain Taoist temples, which generally place the Parents Hall after the main halls.

193. 玉皇阁

Yuhuang Pavilion
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明
地址 Address
荆州市荆州区玄妙观内
类型 Type
宗教建筑·木结构
看点 Highlights
三重檐正方形平面12根檐柱铜质莲花宝座宝顶大明万历庚辰吉旦
中文 Chinese

玉皇阁始建于明嘉靖年间，万历十二年（1584）重建，位于观内中部、1米多高的高台上，台基长、宽各14米。玉皇阁平面为正方形，面阔、进深均为三间，略呈正方形，底层12根檐柱，室内四根金柱直通上层檐檐下，四壁砖墙封檐，下层设拱门。

屋顶为三重檐，自下而上由大而小，呈宝塔形，檐下施五栖重翘斗拱，抬梁式构架，四角攒尖黄色琉璃瓦顶，顶托铜质莲花宝座宝顶，上镌'大明万历庚辰吉旦'。

玉皇阁旁碑林内立有一高大的青石质石碑《九老仙都宫记》碑，此碑初立于元顺帝至正三年（1343），清代重立，20世纪90年代文物管理部门为之加修仿古碑屋加以保护。

石碑圆首方座，通高2.85米，宽1.45米，厚0.18米，碑身正面上方阴刻雷云纹，边框阴刻龙云图案，额阳刻篆书'九老仙都宫'，为赵期颐所篆，碑文为楷书阴刻，元代著名洞庭学士欧阳元所撰，元代书法家危素手书，字迹清晰，笔力遒劲。

碑文分正文和附录两部分，正文1033字，记九老仙都宫营建始末及玄妙观住持唐洞云的家世、生平事迹，描述当时的玄妙观主持道人唐洞云（道号元静真人）被元顺帝封为八仙之后的'第九仙'，附录镌于碑身正面左侧，记述重刻此碑的缘由，作者为宁远祖泽深。该碑的史料及艺术价值均弥足珍贵。

English 英文

Yuhuang Pavilion was first built during the Jiajing period of the Ming, rebuilt in the 12th year of Wanli (1584), located in the middle of the temple on a high platform over 1 meter high, with the platform base 14 meters long and wide. Yuhuang Pavilion has a square plan, three bays wide and three bays deep, slightly square; the bottom floor has 12 eave columns, and four interior golden columns extend straight up to under the upper eave; the four walls are brick walls sealing the eaves, and the lower floor has arched doors. The roof is triple-eaved, from bottom to top from large to small, in a pagoda shape; under the eaves are five-step double-upward bracket sets, with a post-and-lintel frame, four-corner pyramidal yellow glazed tile roof, topped with a copper lotus throne precious finial, inscribed with 'Auspicious Day of Gengchen, Wanli of the Great Ming.' In the stele forest beside Yuhuang Pavilion stands a tall bluestone stele, the 'Record of the Palace of the Nine Elders and Immortal Capital' stele. This stele was first erected in the 3rd year of Zhizheng, Emperor Shun of Yuan (1343), re-erected in the Qing, and in the 1990s the cultural relics management department added an antique stele house to protect it. The stele has a round head and square base, with a total height of 2.85 meters, width of 1.45 meters, and thickness of 0.18 meters; above the front of the stele body is incised cloud-thunder patterns, the border is incised with dragon-cloud patterns, the forehead is yang-carved with seal script 'Palace of the Nine Elders and Immortal Capital,' seal-carved by Zhao Qiyi; the stele text is in regular script incised, composed by the famous Yuan dynasty Dongting scholar Ouyang Yuan, and handwritten by the Yuan dynasty calligrapher Wei Su, with clear characters and vigorous brushwork. The stele text is divided into two parts: main text and appendix; the main text has 1,033 characters, recording the construction process of the Palace of the Nine Elders and Immortal Capital and the family background and life deeds of Tang Dongyun, the abbot of Xuanmiao Temple, describing that Tang Dongyun (Taoist name Yuanjing Zhenren), the presiding Taoist of Xuanmiao Temple at that time, was conferred by Emperor Shun of Yuan as the 'Ninth Immortal' after the Eight Immortals; the appendix is engraved on the left side of the front of the stele body, recording the reason for re-engraving this stele, authored by Ningyuan Zu Zeshen. The historical and artistic value of this stele is both precious.

Three Heavens Gate

牌坊式仿木砖结构重檐歇山顶三个圆形券门青石踏跺
中文 Chinese

玉皇阁后有高6.1米、边长10.2米的高台，高台四面环以围墙，由饰有石栏的24级阶梯上台，三天门和玄武阁即建于其上。三天门重建于清，为牌坊式仿木砖结构，重檐歇山顶。

面阔三间，进深一间，总面阔6.2米，总进深2米，中间歇山顶，两侧硬山顶，开三个圆形券门，各安两扇木板门。正中券门上方书'三天门'，下设长7.2米，宽2.17米青石踏跺。

English 英文

Behind Yuhuang Pavilion is a high platform 6.1 meters high with a side length of 10.2 meters; the high platform is surrounded by walls on all four sides, and one ascends the platform via 24 steps decorated with stone railings; the Three Heavens Gate and Xuanwu Pavilion are built on it. The Three Heavens Gate was rebuilt in the Qing, with a paifang-style imitation-wood brick structure and a double-eave hip-and-gable roof. Three bays wide and one bay deep, with a total width of 6.2 meters and total depth of 2 meters; the middle has a hip-and-gable roof, the two sides have gable roofs, with three round arch doors opened, each fitted with two wooden board doors. Above the central arch door is inscribed 'Three Heavens Gate,' below which is a bluestone stepping platform 7.2 meters long and 2.17 meters wide.

195. 紫皇殿/玄武殿

Zihuang Hall / Xuanwu Hall
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
荆州市荆州区玄妙观内
类型 Type
宗教建筑·木结构
看点 Highlights
重檐歇山顶庑殿顶推山颇有江汉地方特点1985年维修
中文 Chinese

紫皇殿面阔、进深均为三间，重檐歇山顶。因上檐只有一间，屋脊长度不够收山，因此屋顶梁架采用了庑殿顶推山的做法，颇有江汉地方特点。屋面原为黄、绿、灰筒板瓦，1985年维修时改换成清官式黄琉璃瓦。

紫皇殿整体建筑造型凝重，古朴典雅，其距离玉皇阁21米，建筑总高不过9米，在高台和背面城墙的衬托之下，更显出超乎尺寸的巍峨壮观。

English 英文

Zihuang Hall is three bays wide and three bays deep, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof. Because the upper eave has only one bay, the ridge length is not enough for mountain-retraction, so the roof beam frame adopts the practice of hip-roof mountain-pushing, quite characteristic of the Jianghan region. The roof was originally yellow, green, and gray cylindrical and plate tiles, replaced with Qing official-style yellow glazed tiles during the 1985 repair. The overall architectural form of Zihuang Hall is dignified, simple and elegant; it is 21 meters from Yuhuang Pavilion, with a total building height of no more than 9 meters, but against the backdrop of the high platform and the city wall behind it, it appears even more towering and magnificent beyond its dimensions.

196. 太晖观

Taihui Taoist Temple
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
荆州市荆秘路太晖村
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖石、木结构
看点 Highlights
砖石木雕石雕三象轴线布局小金顶僭越
中文 Chinese

和位于城内的玄妙观、开元观不同，太晖观位于荆州城西门外约1公里，太湖港北岸，太晖山上。荆州三观中，就建筑规模及建筑艺术水平而言，太晖观当居首位。太晖观祖师殿的石雕、木雕和砖雕，是荆州地上文物的精品。

太晖观始建于明朝，当时是仅次于武当山的道场。

据《江陵县志》载，'宋元时，曾有草殿'，明洪武二十六年（1393），朱元璋第十二子朱柏被封为湘王，就藩荆州，由于湘献王'尤善道家言，自号紫虚子'，于此量地造林，大兴土木，'易而新焉，明年落成'，据《江陵县志》记载，其时太晖观设有主体殿阁五座，偏殿、左右殿俱备，殿宇高大，规模宏伟。

殿内雕梁画栋，熠熠生辉，时人赞曰：'遍数琳宫，独此雄甲荆楚。'更有'小金顶''赛武当'的盛誉。后朱柏被卜告朝廷逾制，时人'僭越'使用石雕蟠龙柱，认其有谋反之心，朱柏被迫焚烧太晖观，并自焚而亡。

抛开历史恩怨，从另一个角度来看，太晖观的营建从一开始便工程浩大，等级甚高，既有宫殿建筑特点，又具有道观的建筑风格，在当时当地的建筑物中堪称上乘。正如清代沙市举人邓廷人所描述：'观桥上面人攘攘，太晖观上烛辉煌。'

English 英文

Unlike Xuanmiao Temple and Kaiyuan Temple located inside the city, Taihui Temple is located about 1 km outside the west gate of Jingzhou City, on the north bank of Taihu Port, on Taihui Mountain. Among Jingzhou's Three Taoist Temples, in terms of architectural scale and artistic level, Taihui Temple ranks first. The stone carvings, wood carvings, and brick carvings of the Founder Hall of Taihui Temple are fine examples of Jingzhou's above-ground cultural relics. Taihui Temple was first built in the Ming dynasty, and at that time it was a Taoist site second only to Wudang Mountain. According to the 'Jiangling County Annals,' 'during the Song and Yuan, there was once a thatched hall'; in the 26th year of Hongwu, Ming (1393), Zhu Bai, the 12th son of Zhu Yuanzhang, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Xiang and took up his fief in Jingzhou. Because Prince Xiangxian 'was especially fond of Taoist sayings and called himself Zixuzi,' he measured land and planted forests here, undertaking large-scale construction, 'renovating and renewing it, completed the following year.' According to the 'Jiangling County Annals,' at that time Taihui Temple had five main halls and pavilions, with side halls and left and right halls all complete; the halls were tall and the scale was magnificent. Inside the halls, carved beams and painted pillars shone brightly; contemporaries praised: 'Counting all the jade palaces, this one alone is the foremost in Jingchu.' It also had the reputation of 'Little Golden Summit' and 'Rivaling Wudang.' Later, Zhu Bai was reported to the court for exceeding regulations; contemporaries 'usurped' the use of stone-carved coiled-dragon columns, believing he had a rebellious heart; Zhu Bo was forced to burn Taihui Temple and died by self-immolation. Setting aside historical grievances, from another perspective, the construction of Taihui Temple was from the beginning a huge project with a very high grade, having both the characteristics of palace architecture and the architectural style of a Taoist temple, and was among the best in the buildings of that time and place. Just as described by Deng Tingren, a juren of Shashi in the Qing: 'On the temple bridge people bustle, on Taihui Temple candles shine brilliantly.'

中文 Chinese

山门位于中轴线前部，四柱三间两重楼，砖石结构。门上石匾楷书'太晖观'。面阔三间，12.5米，进深一间，5.6米，中楼高3.3米，为单檐歇山绿琉璃瓦顶；

边楼高2.6米，无梁架，各开一券门。中门门额嵌'太晖观'石匾。两侧接出八字形影壁。山门前曾有清水一泓，上有石桥3座。山门后有一小过殿，近年所建，现为售票处，或为四圣殿址。

English 英文

The mountain gate is located at the front of the central axis, with four columns, three bays, and two stories, of brick-stone structure. On the gate, a stone plaque is in regular script 'Taihui Temple.' Three bays wide, 12.5 meters, one bay deep, 5.6 meters; the central tower is 3.3 meters high, with a single-eave hip-and-gable green glazed tile roof; the side towers are 2.6 meters high, without beam frames, each opening an arch door. The central gate lintel is inlaid with the 'Taihui Temple' stone plaque. On both sides, eight-shaped screen walls extend out. In front of the mountain gate there was once a pool of clear water, with three stone bridges over it. Behind the mountain gate there is a small transitional hall, built in recent years, now serving as the ticket office, possibly the site of the Four Sages Hall.

仿汉双阙式建筑钟楼鼓楼单檐卷棚歇山绿琉璃瓦顶抬梁式构架
中文 Chinese

朝圣门、阙楼和祖师殿组团均位于中轴线后部，构筑于高约8米的崇台上，崇台为青石垒砌，台正面和两侧各有三道石梯。石雕望柱栏板，内容多为人物、花草、禽兽等图案，石栏柱顶雕兽头和金瓜，多已毁坏。高台两侧是阙楼，又称钟鼓楼，为仿汉双阙式建筑。

两座阙楼左、右对称，面阔、进深分别为3.06米和3米，高5.5米。单檐卷棚歇山绿琉璃瓦顶，抬梁式构架，四壁砖墙围砌。后与朝圣门紧连。

English 英文

The group of the Pilgrimage Gate, watchtowers, and Founder Hall are all located at the rear of the central axis, built on a high platform about 8 meters high; the high platform is built with bluestone, and there are three stone staircases on the front and both sides of the platform. The stone-carved baluster columns and panels mostly contain patterns of figures, flowers and plants, birds and beasts, etc.; the tops of the stone railing columns are carved with beast heads and golden melons, many of which have been destroyed. On both sides of the high platform are the watchtowers, also called bell and drum towers, which are imitation-Han double-watchtower architecture. The two watchtowers are left-right symmetric, with width and depth of 3.06 meters and 3 meters respectively, and a height of 5.5 meters. Single-eave rolling-roof hip-and-gable green glazed tile roof, with a post-and-lintel frame, surrounded by brick walls on all four sides. They are closely connected to the Pilgrimage Gate at the rear.

朝圣门位于阙楼后侧，通面阔三间，8.25米，进深一间，2.2米。抬梁式砖木构架，开三孔券门。明间为单檐歇山顶，黄琉璃瓦屋面，高6.2米；

English 英文

The Pilgrimage Gate is located behind the watchtowers, with a total width of three bays, 8.25 meters, and a depth of one bay, 2.2 meters. Post-and-lintel brick-wood frame, with three arch doors opened. The central bay has a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, with yellow glazed tile roofing, 6.2 meters high; the secondary bays have single-eave gable roofs, with gray cylindrical tile roofing, 4.8 meters high, with brick-carved bracket sets under the eaves.

200. 太晖观祖师殿

Founder Hall of Taihui Temple
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明-清
地址 Address
荆州市荆秘路太晖观内
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
重檐歇山顶黄色琉璃瓦屋面金殿小金顶透雕蟠龙石柱12根青石八角廊柱
中文 Chinese

祖师殿位于朝圣门北侧，重檐歇山顶，黄色琉璃瓦屋面，屋顶原覆盖有铜瓦，金光闪耀，曾有'金殿'、'赛武当''小金顶'之称，敢与武当、青城山的金顶相媲美。

而今仅能在大殿左侧墙上嵌的乾隆年间石碑碑文中得知，当时大殿有'旧铜瓦一千零六十八块，新铜瓦四百三十六块'，可遥想当时的金殿盛景。

祖师殿面阔、进深各三间，抬梁式木构架，主体构架均为楠木，比例适中，用材较合理，既接近明清官式营造的做法，又有地方的民间建筑特征。梁枋、挑檐、壁柱上饰有彩绘图案。

檐下置斗拱，正殿四周围廊均采用轩棚顶，廊下置有12根青石八角廊柱，其中正面4根和背面2根透雕蛟龙。柱面雕刻大型浮云蟠龙，每条蟠龙姿势各异，龙身鳞片清晰，龙头伸出柱面1尺左右，夭矫盘绕，凌空欲飞，形态逼真，雕刻刀法刚劲浑厚，饱满圆润。

另外6根为正八边形素面石柱。

English 英文

The Founder Hall is located north of the Pilgrimage Gate, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof and yellow glazed tile roofing. The roof was originally covered with copper tiles, shining with golden light, and was once called the 'Golden Hall,' 'Rivaling Wudang,' and 'Little Golden Summit,' daring to compare with the golden summits of Wudang and Qingcheng Mountain. Today, one can only learn from the Qianlong period stele inscription embedded in the wall on the left side of the main hall that at that time the main hall had '1,068 old copper tiles and 436 new copper tiles,' from which one can imagine the grand scene of the golden hall at that time. The Founder Hall is three bays wide and three bays deep, with a post-and-lintel wooden frame; the main frame is all made of nanmu, with moderate proportions and reasonable material use, both close to the official construction methods of the Ming and Qing and having local folk architectural characteristics. The beams, lintels, overhanging eaves, and engaged columns are decorated with painted patterns. Bracket sets are placed under the eaves; the surrounding corridor of the main hall all use a coffered ceiling, and under the corridor there are 12 bluestone octagonal corridor columns, of which 4 on the front and 2 on the back are openwork-carved with coiling dragons. The column surfaces are carved with large floating-cloud coiling dragons; each coiling dragon has a different posture, the dragon body scales are clear, and the dragon head extends about 1 chi (about 33 cm) out of the column surface, gracefully coiling, as if about to fly in the air, with a lifelike form; the carving knife technique is vigorous and rich, full and rounded. The other 6 columns are regular octagonal plain-faced stone columns.

201. 开元观

Kaiyuan Taoist Temple
级别 Level

看点 Highlights
轴线布局高台建筑石雕彩绘荆州三大道观之一唐开元年间建
中文 Chinese

与太晖观、玄妙观同为荆州三大道观之一的开元观，坐落在古城西门内侧。相传因奉唐明皇李隆基诏书而建。据《江陵县志·古迹》记载：'（开元观）在县治西，唐开元年间建。'又载：'开元二十九年，唐玄宗夜梦巨人，云：吾欲出，建道场。适闻荆州奏：地涌侯天尊像。诏立开元观。

历宋、元、明、清，皆有修葺。'新中国成立后，1952年、1955年、1984年也曾进行修缮，以及近年（2015年4月－9月）也在修缮中。

1958年起，在以开元观为主体的基地上逐渐兴建了荆州地区博物馆。现存开元观主体建筑为明代万历年间遗构，清代重修，整体呈现明清风格。

现总占地面积约5000平方米，现存7座建筑，中轴线上有一门三殿（山门、雷祖殿、三清殿、天门和祖师殿）为明清两代重建，坐北朝南，梯次排列；轴线两侧各有耳房一座，是近代所建的附属建筑。观内还存有元、明时期的碑刻、钟、炉等文物。

沿高台有砖砌帏城，内壁嵌石雕神将五百灵官。每位灵官高0.23米，宽0.19米，厚0.04米。青石和青白石浮雕而成，刀法圆润、线条如意、精致细腻，惟妙惟肖。

灵官的姿态各不相同，有的身着铠甲手握兵器，有的身作道服手持仙家之物，有的慈眉善目，有的庄重严肃，有的威武雄壮，为太晖观建筑艺术之精粹。殿后一泓清池，四周苍松翠柏。

English 英文

Kaiyuan Temple, one of Jingzhou's Three Great Taoist Temples along with Taihui Temple and Xuanmiao Temple, is located inside the west gate of the ancient city. Legend has it that it was built by imperial edict of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Li Longji. According to the 'Jiangling County Annals · Ancient Sites': '(Kaiyuan Temple) is west of the county government, built during the Kaiyuan period of the Tang.' It also records: 'In the 29th year of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong of Tang dreamed of a giant at night, saying: I wish to go out, build a Taoist ritual site. Just then came a report from Jingzhou: a statue of the Heavenly Venerable surged from the earth. An edict ordered the establishment of Kaiyuan Temple. Through the Song, Yuan, Ming, and Qing, it was all repaired.' After the founding of New China, repairs were also carried out in 1952, 1955, and 1984, as well as in recent years (April–September 2015). From 1958, on the site with Kaiyuan Temple as the main body, the Jingzhou Regional Museum was gradually built. The existing main buildings of Kaiyuan Temple are remains from the Wanli period of the Ming, rebuilt in the Qing, overall presenting a Ming-Qing style. The current total area is about 5,000 square meters, with 7 existing buildings; on the central axis there is one gate and three halls (Mountain Gate, Leizu Hall, Sanqing Hall, Heaven Gate and Founder Hall), rebuilt in the Ming and Qing dynasties, facing south, arranged in tiers; on each side of the axis there is one ear room, an附属 building built in modern times. Inside the temple there are also cultural relics such as steles, bells, and furnaces from the Yuan and Ming periods. Along the high platform there is a brick-built curtain wall, with the inner wall inlaid with stone-carved divine generals, the Five Hundred Lingguan. Each Lingguan is 0.23 meters high, 0.19 meters wide, and 0.04 meters thick. Relief-carved from bluestone and blue-white stone, with mellow knife technique, smooth lines, exquisite and delicate, lifelike. The postures of the Lingguan are all different: some wear armor and hold weapons, some wear Taoist robes and hold immortal objects, some have kind eyebrows and good eyes, some are solemn and serious, some are mighty and majestic, being the essence of Taihui Temple's architectural art. Behind the hall is a clear pool, surrounded by green pines and cypresses.

中文 Chinese

山门位于开元观南端，为木结构牌楼式建筑，四柱三门二重楼，面阔约10米，主楼为庑殿顶，次楼为悬山顶，皆覆琉璃瓦，檐下施斗拱，明间置六攒九踩斗拱，次间置四攒九踩斗拱。

每攒斗拱纵横各出四层翘、栱，另在45°方向挑出斜栱。山门中间为门道，两侧后掩为室，门两侧有八字影壁，门前立石雕蹲狮一对。山门整体上高宽比例舒适，檐角高低错落，造型庄重秀丽。

English 英文

The mountain gate is located at the southern end of Kaiyuan Temple, a wooden structure paifang-style building, with four columns, three doors, and two stories, about 10 meters wide; the main tower has a hip roof, the secondary towers have overhanging gable roofs, all covered with glazed tiles; bracket sets are placed under the eaves, with six clusters of nine-step bracket sets in the central bay and four clusters of nine-step bracket sets in the secondary bays. Each cluster of bracket sets projects four layers of upstands and arms both longitudinally and transversely, additionally projecting diagonal arms in the 45° direction. The middle of the mountain gate is the doorway, with the two sides enclosed as rooms behind; on both sides of the gate there are eight-shaped screen walls, and in front of the gate stands a pair of stone-carved crouching lions. The overall height-to-width ratio of the mountain gate is comfortable, with the eave corners staggered high and low, and the shape is dignified and graceful.

The Thunder God Hall is located on the north side of Kaiyuan Temple, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, three bays wide and three bays deep, with a post-and-lintel frame and no bracket sets. Surrounded by brick walls on all four sides. It was rebuilt in the 24th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1819). On the ridge purlin and lintels of the central bay there are paintings and ink-line inscriptions. 三清殿位于雷祖殿北侧20余米，建于高约1米的台基上，单檐歇山顶灰瓦顶，面阔五间，进深三间，前檐施五栖重斗拱，后檐及两侧均施三幅云衬托桃檐木桁，前壁设槅扇，内檐、梁架等构件，为明代建筑风格。

English 英文

The Sanqing Hall is located more than 20 meters north of the Leizu Hall, built on a platform about 1 meter high, with a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, five bays wide and three bays deep; the front eave has five-step double bracket sets, and the rear eave and both sides have three-cloud patterns supporting the overhanging eave wooden purlins; the front wall has lattice partitions, and the inner eaves, beam frames, and other components are in Ming architectural style. The Sanqing Hall enshrines the three highest deities in Taoism—the Primordial Heavenly Venerable, the Lingbao Heavenly Lord, and the Supreme Lord Laozi.

开元观后部建有3.3米崇台，下置一道20余级石阶。天门之前有一窄台面，使高台平面呈凸字形，崇台四周建有围廊，石阶两侧栏板雕刻禽兽、人物及几何图案。祖师殿与天门、耳房均建在崇台之上。

Before the Heaven Gate there is a narrow platform surface, making the high platform plan convex-shaped; around the high platform there are surrounding corridors, and the balustrade panels on both sides of the stone steps are carved with birds and beasts, figures, and geometric patterns. 206. 铁女寺

Tienü Temple (Iron Maiden Temple)
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
荆州市西城街道办事处铁女寺巷13号
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖石、木结构
看点 Highlights
历史传说大雄宝殿古钟铁女像铜像等文物铁女寺传说
中文 Chinese

铁女寺位于荆州古城北门附近，江陵中学西侧一条幽静的小巷内，该巷即以铁女寺命名。铁女寺始建于唐贞观年间，伴有一段动人的传说。相传唐代江陵府有冶铁监官孙坤，坐事陷狱冤死，孙氏有两女，痛父蒙冤，投告无门，投炉自焚，铸铁若人形。皇上闻奏，感其孝烈，昭赐立祠祭祀，号'铁女祠'。

这段故事经代代口耳相传，已然是扑朔迷离的一段公案，例如，孙坤到底是铁匠还是分管冶铁的官员，其冤死之因由何在，孙的女儿到底是两位还是三位，等等，已经无从考证。

然而今天的铁女寺，依旧在大殿中保存着两尊印证此段传说的重达千斤的人形铁铸造像，以及保持着荆州唯一一座尼众道场的独特身份，寺内红墙环抱，花木扶疏，满庭温馨，儒释共礼，香火游人不断，形成了独特的清幽雅致的铁女寺文化。

据《铁女寺志》载，最初落成时，'斯寺坐北朝南，占地三十有二公顷，（大雄宝殿）深五重，宽六舍……文武将相，迁客骚人多有朝礼，无不颂皇恩浩荡也……'此后，铁女寺几次毁损，又多次修缮重建。元朝末年，铁女寺坍塌荒废。

明朝洪武年间，朱元璋的第十四子——辽王朱植改藩荆州，在其所撰《铁女寺碑记》中载：'庙宇倾秃，周垣尽圮，赖先王从而耸之，尤大雄殿者为甚……'可见在明初初年就对铁女寺有过至少两次维修；

而另据《江陵县志》，明嘉靖三年（1524）和二十四年（1545），亦对大雄宝殿有两次维修。

20世纪，在寺院三代演灵、宽量、弘法住持苦心维持下，铁女寺先后历经日军侵华、'文革'动荡，门罗荆棘，破败不堪，20世纪六七十年代，寺庙先后被当地小学、中学使用，80年代，铁女寺还寺于尼，寺院修整一新，并先后寻回四尊明代铜佛以及3口古钟。

2002年冬，大雄宝殿东墙倒塌，木构架整体偏移，之后大殿进行了近年最大的一次修缮。

现铁女寺占地面积约4000平方米，主要建筑为晚清所建，中轴线上存山门、韦陀殿、大雄宝殿等建筑，还有弥陀殿、念佛堂、铁女殿、观音殿、斋堂、净塔园、藏经楼、龙井亭、智慧亭等建筑。

English 英文

Tienü Temple is located near the north gate of Jingzhou Ancient City, in a quiet alley west of Jiangling Middle School; the alley is named after Tienü Temple. Tienü Temple was first built during the Zhenguan period of the Tang, accompanied by a moving legend. Legend has it that during the Tang, there was an iron-smelting supervisor official named Sun Kun in Jiangling Prefecture, who was implicated in a case and died unjustly in prison; Sun had two daughters, pained by their father's wrongful death, with no way to appeal, they threw themselves into the furnace and self-immolated, casting iron into human form. When the emperor heard the report, moved by their filial piety and martyrdom, he bestowed an edict to establish a shrine for sacrifice, named 'Tienü Shrine' (Iron Maiden Shrine). This story, passed down orally from generation to generation, has become a confusing case; for example, whether Sun Kun was a blacksmith or an official in charge of iron smelting, what was the cause of his wrongful death, whether Sun's daughters were two or three, etc., can no longer be verified. However, today's Tienü Temple still preserves in the main hall two human-shaped iron cast statues weighing a thousand jin each that corroborate this legend, as well as maintaining the unique identity of the only nunnery in Jingzhou. Inside the temple, red walls surround it, flowers and trees are lush, the whole courtyard is warm, Confucianism and Buddhism are worshipped together, incense and visitors continue, forming a unique, quiet and elegant Tienü Temple culture. According to the 'Tienü Temple Annals,' when it was first completed, 'this temple faces south, covering thirty-two hectares, (the Mahavira Hall) is five bays deep and six bays wide... civil and military generals, exiled officials and poets all come to pay homage, none fail to praise the vast grace of the emperor...' Thereafter, Tienü Temple was destroyed several times and repaired and rebuilt many times. At the end of the Yuan, Tienü Temple collapsed and fell into disuse. During the Hongwu period of the Ming, Zhu Zhi, the 14th son of Zhu Yuanzhang—the Prince of Liao—changed his fief to Jingzhou; in his 'Record of the Tienü Temple Stele,' he wrote: 'The temple buildings were bare and collapsed, the surrounding walls were all ruined, relying on the former king to renovate them, especially the Mahavira Hall was the most...' It can be seen that in the early Ming, Tienü Temple was repaired at least twice; and according to the 'Jiangling County Annals,' in the 3rd year (1524) and 24th year (1545) of Jiajing, Ming, the Mahavira Hall was also repaired twice. In the 20th century, under the painstaking maintenance of three generations of abbots—Yanling, Kuanliang, and Hongfa—Tienü Temple successively experienced the Japanese invasion of China and the 'Cultural Revolution' turmoil, with thorns overgrowing the doors and in dilapidated condition; in the 1960s and 1970s, the temple was successively used by local primary and middle schools; in the 1980s, Tienü Temple was returned to the nuns, the temple was renovated anew, and four Ming dynasty copper Buddha statues and three ancient bells were successively recovered. In the winter of 2002, the east wall of the Mahavira Hall collapsed, the wooden frame shifted overall, after which the main hall underwent the largest repair in recent years. Currently, Tienü Temple covers an area of about 4,000 square meters; the main buildings were built in the late Qing, with the mountain gate, Weituo Hall, and Mahavira Hall existing on the central axis, as well as the Mituo Hall, Buddha Recitation Hall, Tienü Hall, Guanyin Hall, dining hall, Jingta Garden, Buddhist Scripture Library, Longjing Pavilion, and Wisdom Pavilion.

Mahavira Hall of Tienü Temple

单檐悬山灰瓦顶二铁女像明代铜佛5座血书《妙法莲花经》
中文 Chinese

唐代的铁女寺大殿'高五丈，深九丈，面宽六间，金丝楠木凡四十八根撑立其间……雕梁画栋，极尽威雄矣'。（《铁女寺志》）今天的大雄宝殿已不复此威雄，仅面阔三间，进深三间，单檐悬山灰瓦顶，前壁满设槅扇门。

其中，铜像铸于明弘治年间，分别为释迦牟尼佛、文殊菩萨、普贤菩萨、观音菩萨、韦驮菩萨，佛身最大的高1.7米，最小的高1.4米，均为红铜铸成。

English 英文

The Tang dynasty Tienü Temple main hall was 'five zhang high, nine zhang deep, six bays wide, with forty-eight golden nanmu columns supporting it... carved beams and painted pillars, extremely majestic.' ('Tienü Temple Annals') Today's Mahavira Hall no longer has such majesty, being only three bays wide and three bays deep, with a single-eave overhanging gable gray-tile roof, and the front wall fully fitted with lattice doors. The two iron maiden statues are placed inside the Mahavira Hall, 90 cm and 137 cm high respectively, with blurred forms, as if sitting or standing. The temple also enshrines 60 relics, one copy of the 'Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma' written in blood, and five copper statues, all precious cultural relics. Among them, the copper statues were cast during the Hongzhi period of the Ming, respectively Shakyamuni Buddha, Manjushri Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Guanyin Bodhisattva, and Weituo Bodhisattva; the largest Buddha body is 1.7 meters high, the smallest is 1.4 meters high, all cast from red copper.

210. 荆州文庙

Temple of Confucius in Jingzhou
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
荆州市西城街道办事处荆中路西段南侧，荆州中路185号
类型 Type
礼制建筑·砖石、木结构
看点 Highlights
藻井彩绘荆州古代崇文尊孔的标志性建筑荆州城区明清古建筑典范
中文 Chinese

荆州文庙是荆州古代崇文尊孔的标志性建筑，也是荆州城区明清古建筑典范和重要的实物例证。荆州文庙原为江陵县文庙，始建于唐代，时有兴废。元代以沙市为江陵县治，县学随之迁往沙市。

明洪武年间，由沙市迁往荆州城内东北隅，清康熙六十年（1721）迁于今址，雍正三年（1725）告成，'时殿、庑、门、楹俱全'。乾隆九年（1744）、嘉庆元年（1796）先后两次扩建修缮，殿阁堂亭，表坊泮池，石桥墉墙。

先后建成的建筑包括：大成殿、两庑戟门、名宦祠、乡贤祠、崇圣祠、尊经阁、棂星门及两旁石牌坊、明伦堂、奎文阁（又名文明阁）、节孝祠、内室（包括更衣所、刑牲处、祭品乐器库）、碑亭等，是一处规模显赫的建筑群。

可惜1940年日本侵略军侵占荆州时，庙内建筑多被焚毁，直到1949年前，仅存府围残缺的泮池、三桥、大成殿、棂星门及两侧石牌坊等建筑。

新中国成立后，在此地先后设江陵师范附属小学、荆州师范专科学校附属中学、荆州市实验中学，大成殿成为学校老师办公之地，1953年翻修大成殿等建筑。

'文革'时期，大成殿作为学校办公之用，进行过两次翻修，因缺乏保护意识，大成殿内部结构和外部风貌受到一定的破坏。今天的荆州文庙仅存大成殿和棂星门。2004年文物部门对文庙进行了测绘和修缮。

现荆州文庙占地面积约1.8万平方米，坐北朝南，中轴对称布局。

English 英文

Jingzhou Temple of Confucius is a landmark building of ancient Jingzhou's respect for literature and Confucius, and also an important physical example and model of Ming-Qing ancient architecture in the Jingzhou urban area. Jingzhou Temple of Confucius was originally the Jiangling County Temple of Confucius, first built in the Tang, with periods of prosperity and abandonment. In the Yuan, Shashi was made the county seat of Jiangling, and the county school moved to Shashi accordingly. During the Hongwu period of the Ming, it moved from Shashi to the northeast corner inside Jingzhou City; in the 60th year of Kangxi, Qing (1721), it moved to its current site, and was completed in the 3rd year of Yongzheng (1725), 'at that time halls, side rooms, doors, and pillars were all complete.' In the 9th year of Qianlong (1744) and the 1st year of Jiaqing (1796), it was expanded and repaired twice successively, with halls, pavilions, memorial archways, and the Pan Pond, stone bridges, and walls. The successively built buildings included: the Mahavira Hall (Dacheng Hall), two side wings, Halberd Gate, Hall of Famous Officials, Hall of Local Worthies, Hall of the Sages' Ancestors, Scripture-Preserving Pavilion, Lingxing Gate and stone archways on both sides, Minglun Hall, Kuiwen Pavilion (also called Wenming Pavilion), Chastity and Filial Piety Shrine, inner rooms (including changing rooms, animal-slaughtering place, sacrificial vessel and instrument storehouse), stele pavilions, etc., a building complex of prominent scale. Unfortunately, when the Japanese invading army occupied Jingzhou in 1940, most of the buildings in the temple were burned down; by 1949, only buildings such as the incomplete Pan Pond with surrounding walls, three bridges, Dacheng Hall, Lingxing Gate, and stone archways on both sides remained. After the founding of New China, the Jiangling Normal Affiliated Primary School, Jingzhou Normal College Affiliated Middle School, and Jingzhou Experimental Middle School were successively established here; the Dacheng Hall became the office place for school teachers, and in 1953 the Dacheng Hall and other buildings were renovated. During the 'Cultural Revolution' period, the Dacheng Hall, used as school office space, underwent two renovations; due to lack of conservation awareness, the internal structure and external appearance of the Dacheng Hall suffered certain damage. Today's Jingzhou Temple of Confucius only retains the Dacheng Hall and Lingxing Gate. In 2004, the cultural relics department surveyed and repaired the Temple of Confucius. Currently, Jingzhou Temple of Confucius covers an area of about 18,000 square meters, facing south, with a central axis symmetric layout.

211. 荆州文庙棂星门

Lingxing Gate of Jingzhou Temple of Confucius

中文 Chinese

棂星门是进入文庙的起点，位于文庙前部，建于光绪二十二年（1896），至今保存完好。全门皆石结构，三门四柱，宽9.9米，高6.65米。

中额枋题刻光绪皇帝御书楷体'棂星门'三字，并饰有浮雕六幅，背面刻题记'大清光绪二十二岁次丙申六月吉日重建'，柱下端前后有石雕抱鼓石，柱顶部雕金瓜。

English 英文

The Lingxing Gate is the starting point for entering the Temple of Confucius, located at the front of the temple, built in the 22nd year of Guangxu (1896), and still well preserved today. The entire gate is of stone structure, with three doors and four columns, 9.9 meters wide and 6.65 meters high. The central architrave is inscribed with the three characters 'Lingxing Gate' in regular script personally written by Emperor Guangxu, and decorated with six relief carvings; the back is inscribed with the record 'Rebuilt on an auspicious day in the sixth month of the 22nd year of Guangxu, Great Qing, corresponding to the year Bingshen'; at the lower end of the columns, front and back, there are stone-carved drum-holding stones, and the tops of the columns are carved with golden melons.

中文 Chinese

按江陵地区风俗，进棂星门，过大成门，遇泮池，上建三座石拱桥，中间一桥桥面石刻龙凤，只有中状元回乡祭祖拜孔，才能踏龙凤而过，谓之'三桥不流水'。经这一系列仪式，方可达到大成殿。

English 英文

According to the customs of the Jiangling region, after entering the Lingxing Gate, passing through the Dacheng Gate, and encountering the Pan Pond, three stone arch bridges are built over it; the bridge deck of the middle bridge is stone-carved with dragons and phoenixes, and only those who achieved the first place in the imperial examination and returned home to sacrifice to ancestors and worship Confucius could step on the dragons and phoenixes to cross, called 'three bridges with no flowing water.' After this series of rituals, one could reach the Dacheng Hall.

中文 Chinese

荆州南门天主教堂又名真福童贞玛利亚教堂、大经堂，是荆州近代史上最早的西方中世纪小教堂，也是目前荆州唯一保存较完整，且仍在使用的欧式教堂建筑。南门天主堂位于荆州城南门外东堤街，而南门外一带可以说是天主教在荆州城的发源地。

早在清顺治十八年（1661），法籍耶稣会士穆迪我（Jac Motel）来荆州传教，在荆州城南门外建起县内第一座教堂。

1870年，湖北传教区划分成三个教区，西南部教区由董文芳神父（FY.Alexius Filippi.O.F.M）主管，董神父上任后，在今日的荆州老南门外东堤街买下民房一栋，...

English 英文

Jingzhou South Gate Catholic Church, also called the Church of the Blessed Virgin Mary and the Great Church, is the earliest Western medieval chapel in modern Jingzhou history, and is also the only relatively well-preserved European-style church building in Jingzhou that is still in use today. The South Gate Catholic Church is located on Dongdi Street outside the south gate of Jingzhou City, and the area outside the south gate can be said to be the birthplace of Catholicism in Jingzhou City. As early as the 18th year of Shunzhi, Qing (1661), French Jesuit Jacques Motel came to Jingzhou to preach and built the first church in the county outside the south gate of Jingzhou City. In 1870, the Hubei mission area was divided into three dioceses, and the southwestern diocese was administered by Father Alexius Filippi (O.F.M.); after taking office, Father Dong bought a civilian house on Dongdi Street outside the old south gate of today's Jingzhou, ...

214. 荆州城区民居

Vernacular Dwellings in Jingzhou City
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代、近代
地址 Address
分布于荆州市荆州区三义街、得胜街、民主街、冠带巷、繁荣街、宾兴街、荆中路等
类型 Type
民居建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
传统格局整体风貌三义街得胜街前店后宅式多为一至两层
中文 Chinese

荆州城区的传统民居多分布在古城的历史风貌保护街区内，重要的有三义街、得胜街、胜利街等。三义街直通大北门，取刘、关、张桃园三结义之意，曾经是城北的重要商品集散地，有过相当长的繁荣期。

地段内的道路以宽3—6米的三义街为主，辅以仅宽1—1.5米的王家巷、观音庵巷等。其中民居多为晚清及民国建筑，在三义街北段的历史街区核心保护区，清末的民居建筑约占三成，以临街的院落为主。

具有一些共同特征：多为一至两层，前店后宅式，砖木结构，建筑多为一进等。从三义街出大北门过得胜桥即得胜街。得胜街传说是关羽北攻樊城得胜归来而名，其与三义街是荆州历史风貌保存完好的两条街道，一条在城内，一条在城外，连为一体。

得胜街整体风貌较差，大部分为现代建筑及仿古建筑，街道宽度为4—6米。

English 英文

The traditional dwellings in the Jingzhou urban area are mostly distributed in the historical style protection blocks of the ancient city, with important ones including Sanyi Street, Desheng Street, Shengli Street, etc. Sanyi Street leads directly to the Great North Gate, taking the meaning of the Oath of the Peach Garden by Liu, Guan, and Zhang; it was once an important commodity distribution center in the north of the city, with a fairly long period of prosperity. The roads in the area are mainly Sanyi Street, 3–6 meters wide, supplemented by Wangjia Lane and Guanyin'an Lane, only 1–1.5 meters wide. Among them, the dwellings are mostly late Qing and Republican-era buildings; in the core protection area of the historical block at the northern section of Sanyi Street, late Qing residential buildings account for about 30%, mainly street-facing courtyards. They have some common characteristics: mostly one to two stories, front-shop-back-dwelling style, brick-wood structure, and the buildings are mostly one-entry etc. From Sanyi Street, exiting the Great North Gate and crossing the Desheng Bridge leads to Desheng Street. Desheng Street is legendarily named after Guan Yu's victorious return from the northern attack on Fancheng; it and Sanyi Street are the two streets in Jingzhou with well-preserved historical styles, one inside the city and one outside, connected as one. The overall style of Desheng Street is relatively poor, with most being modern and antique-style buildings, and the street width is 4–6 meters.

215. 梅槐桥

Meihuai Bridge
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty

地址 Address
荆州市荆州区梅槐村梅槐桥路
类型 Type
桥梁·石结构
看点 Highlights
历史传说生动石雕荆州72古石桥中仅存的一座始建于明代
中文 Chinese

梅槐桥位于荆州城西约15公里处的梅槐村，为荆州72古石桥中仅存的一座。桥东西向跨太湖港河，南通荆江大堤，始建于明代。相传此地本无桥，旧时有梅槐合生，乡人以为吉兆，始架木桥以连湖港两岸。

桥成树茂，时有暗香浮动、絮花飘飞，故留梅槐之名至今，又作梅回桥。又有一说此地与东晋权臣桓玄被诛之地——枚回洲相接，故桥又名枚回桥。清代康熙年间乡乡郑维周等募资重修，改木为石，同治年间重修，见《荆州府志》：'国朝康熙四十九年，因木桥朽坏，郑维周等聚资改建石桥，后圮。

同治十三年官民捐资迁地重建。'2011年又集资大修，补齐了缺失的构件及石雕，并立碑于其前。

English 英文

Meihuai Bridge is located in Meihuai Village, about 15 km west of Jingzhou City, and is the only surviving one among Jingzhou's 72 ancient stone bridges. The bridge spans the Taihu Port River east-west, connecting to the Jingjiang Dike to the south, and was first built in the Ming. Legend has it that there was originally no bridge here; in old times, plum and pagoda trees grew together, and the villagers regarded it as an auspicious sign, so they began to build a wooden bridge to connect the two sides of the lake port. After the bridge was completed, the trees flourished, with faint fragrance floating and catkin flowers flying from time to time, hence the name Meihuai (Plum-Pagoda) retained to this day, also called Meihui Bridge. Another saying is that this place is connected to Meihui Isle, the place where Huan Xuan, a powerful minister of the Eastern Jin, was executed, hence the bridge is also called Meihui Bridge. During the Kangxi period of the Qing, local Zheng Weizhou and others raised funds to rebuild it, changing wood to stone; it was rebuilt during the Tongzhi period, as seen in the 'Jingzhou Prefecture Annals': 'In the 49th year of Kangxi of the current dynasty, because the wooden bridge was decayed and damaged, Zheng Weizhou and others pooled funds to rebuild it as a stone bridge, which later collapsed. In the 13th year of Tongzhi, officials and people donated funds to relocate and rebuild it.' In 2011, funds were raised again for a major repair,补齐 the missing components and stone carvings, and a stele was erected in front of it.

216. 荆州万寿宝塔

Wanshou Pagoda in Jingzhou
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明代
地址 Address
荆州市沙市区荆堤路99号
类型 Type
古塔·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
特色砖雕汉白玉佛像接引塔嘉靖二十七年建塔身陷入堤面之下
中文 Chinese

万寿宝塔亦名接引塔，位于沙市区荆江大堤万寿园内，古观音矶头畔。观音矶始建于南宋，因建有观音寺而得名，又因矶身伸入江心，形如象鼻而名象鼻矶。

荆江大堤为国家一级确保堤防，自古以来都受到当权者高度关注，万寿宝塔迎江稳坐矶头，是临江观水的绝佳处所，而茫茫江心，宝塔岿然，亦为江边胜景，也是沙市的标志性建筑。万寿宝塔始建于嘉靖二十七年（1548），历时四载建成。

明代第七代辽王朱宪爝藩封荆州，尊嫡母毛太妃之命，建此塔为嘉靖皇帝祈寿，据《鼎建万寿宝塔记》碑文：'祝延圣天子万万寿，用敷锡余福以庇下民。'故命名'万寿宝塔'。清康熙、乾隆、嘉庆、道光年间均有修缮。

1949年后，随着长江水位增高，荆江大堤泥沙沉积，大堤堤面也逐步加高，古塔逐渐陷入堤面之下。1952年加固荆江大堤时，为保证宝塔安全度汛，塔座正面仅留下6米多长的坡形通道，以供游客登塔参观。

目前，塔基距地面以下7米，堤面以上的塔高约20米。'文革'中，万寿宝塔四周墙内外镶嵌的汉白玉佛像和大部分砖雕佛像被砸毁。塔身墙面被水泥封涂，宝塔遭受极大损害。1984年、1988年、2003年又对宝塔进行了维修。

English 英文

Wanshou Pagoda, also called Jieyin Pagoda, is located in Wanshou Garden on the Jingjiang Dike in Shashi District, by the ancient Guanyin Jetty. Guanyin Jetty was first built in the Southern Song, named after the Guanyin Temple built there, and also called Xiangbi (Elephant Trunk) Jetty because the jetty body extends into the river center, shaped like an elephant trunk. The Jingjiang Dike is a national first-class guaranteed dike, and has received high attention from those in power since ancient times; Wanshou Pagoda sits firmly at the jetty head facing the river, an excellent place to view the river, and in the vast river center, the pagoda stands firm, also a riverside scenic spot and a landmark building of Shashi. Wanshou Pagoda was first built in the 27th year of Jiajing (1548), completed after four years. The seventh-generation Prince of Liao of the Ming, Zhu Xianjue, was enfeoffed in Jingzhou; by the order of his嫡母, the Dowager Consort Mao, he built this pagoda to pray for longevity for Emperor Jiajing. According to the inscription of the 'Record of the Establishment of Wanshou Pagoda': 'Praying for the Holy Son of Heaven's ten-thousand-year longevity, using it to bestow remaining blessings to protect the people below.' Hence it was named 'Wanshou Pagoda' (Longevity Pagoda). It was repaired during the Kangxi, Qianlong, Jiaqing, and Daoguang periods of the Qing. After 1949, as the Yangtze River water level rose and sediment deposited on the Jingjiang Dike, the dike surface was gradually raised, and the ancient pagoda gradually sank below the dike surface. When reinforcing the Jingjiang Dike in 1952, to ensure the pagoda's safety during flood season, only a slope-shaped passage over 6 meters long was left in front of the pagoda base for tourists to climb the pagoda. Currently, the pagoda base is 7 meters below the ground, and the pagoda height above the dike surface is about 20 meters. During the 'Cultural Revolution,' the white marble Buddha statues inlaid inside and outside the surrounding walls of Wanshou Pagoda and most of the brick-carved Buddha statues were smashed. The pagoda body wall surface was sealed and painted with cement, and the pagoda suffered great damage. In 1984, 1988, and 2003, the pagoda was repaired again.

217. 川主宫戏楼

Theater in Chuanzhu Shrine
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代（1986年搬迁）
地址 Address
荆州市沙市区碧波路17号
类型 Type
娱乐建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
特色砖雕藻井四川帮的帮会会馆清乾嘉年间蜀英会馆
中文 Chinese

川主宫坐落在荆州市沙市区江津湖畔。江津即沙市的古称，自汉代开通至沙洋的大漕河后，江津成为江南数省向洛阳进贡财物和运送漕粮的枢纽，发展为著名的商业要地。

明清时期，沙市已成为湖北仅次于汉口的重要市场，各省市客商先后在沙市组织行帮，形成了著名的'十三帮'，而各帮除举办各种帮会活动之外，也多建以会馆、书院或寺院，作为喝酒、唱戏等各种帮会活动的载体。

如十三帮总会馆的旃檀庵、山陕帮的金龙寺、安徽帮的泾太会馆、四川帮的川主宫、湖南帮的禹王宫、浙江帮的孤魂会馆、黄州帮的帝王宫、广东帮的广东会馆、福建帮的天后宫、河南帮的中州会馆、汉阳帮的晴川书院、武昌帮的鄂城书院、江西帮的万寿宫、南京帮的金陵会馆、以及作为各省钱铺公馆的财神殿等。

至明朝末年，沙市的商业氛围已经非常浓厚，清人刘献廷所著《广阳杂记》中如是描述：'沙市明末极盛，列巷九十九条，每行占一巷，舟车辐凑，繁盛甲宇内。

'这种盛况一直持续了整个清代，刊印于光绪年间的《通商各关关华洋贸易总册》下卷中《光绪二十二年沙市口华洋贸易情形论略》曾有描述：'转奂巍然，足称美备。即其经费之充裕，可知其商务之殷繁，且其款项均由捐集而来，亦足知善贾者之多财矣。

'川主宫是四川帮的帮会会馆，而在沙市的川人更是早在宋代便已成规模，南宋乾道六年（1170）陆游到沙市日记记载：'十七日，日入后，迁行李过嘉州赵青船、盖入峡船也。沙市堤上居者，大抵皆蜀人也；不然、则与蜀人为婚姻者也。

'据《重修川主宫碑记》记载，川主宫始建于清乾嘉年间，系在滨江港口原杨泗庙旧址兴建而成，为四川商帮集资兴建，又称'蜀英会馆'。宫内正殿供奉三国时期蜀汉国主刘备，因而得名'川主宫'。川主宫戏楼是诸多会馆戏楼中最为有名的一座，宽阔高大，雕梁画栋，装饰富丽，也...

English 英文

Chuanzhu Shrine is located by Jiangjin Lake in Shashi District, Jingzhou City. Jiangjin is the ancient name of Shashi; since the Han dynasty opened the Great Canal River to Shayang, Jiangjin became a hub for several southern provinces to pay tribute goods to Luoyang and transport tribute grain, developing into a famous commercial hub. During the Ming and Qing, Shashi had become an important market in Hubei second only to Hankou; merchants from various provinces and cities successively organized trade guilds in Shashi, forming the famous 'Thirteen Guilds.' Besides holding various guild activities, each guild mostly built guildhalls, academies, or temples as venues for drinking, opera performances, and other guild activities. For example, the Zhantan Nunnery of the Thirteen Guilds General Guildhall, the Jinlong Temple of the Shan-Shaan Guild, the Jingtai Guildhall of the Anhui Guild, the Chuanzhu Shrine of the Sichuan Guild, the Yuwang Palace of the Hunan Guild, the Guhun Guildhall of the Zhejiang Guild, the Diwang Palace of the Huangzhou Guild, the Guangdong Guildhall of the Guangdong Guild, the Tianhou Palace of the Fujian Guild, the Zhongzhou Guildhall of the Henan Guild, the Qingchuan Academy of the Hanyang Guild, the Echeng Academy of the Wuchang Guild, the Wanshou Palace of the Jiangxi Guild, the Jinling Guildhall of the Nanjing Guild, and the God of Wealth Hall as the money-shop mansion of various provinces, etc. By the end of the Ming, Shashi's commercial atmosphere was already very strong; in the 'Guangyang Miscellaneous Records' written by Qing dynasty Liu Xianting, it is described as: 'Shashi was extremely prosperous at the end of the Ming, with ninety-nine lanes, each trade occupying one lane; boats and carts converged, its prosperity unmatched in the empire.' This grand situation lasted throughout the entire Qing. In the second volume of the 'General Records of Chinese and Foreign Trade at Various Treaty Ports' printed during the Guangxu period, the 'Brief Discussion on the Situation of Chinese and Foreign Trade at Shashi Port in the 22nd Year of Guangxu' once described: 'The turnover is magnificent, sufficient to be called excellent. From the abundance of its funds, one can know the prosperity of its commerce, and since its funds are all raised by donations, one can also know the wealth of good merchants.' Chuanzhu Shrine is the guildhall of the Sichuan Guild, and the Sichuan people in Shashi had already reached a scale as early as the Song dynasty; in the 6th year of Qiandao, Southern Song (1170), Lu You recorded in his Shashi diary: 'On the 17th, after sunset, I moved my luggage onto the Zhao Qing boat of Jiazhou, which is a boat entering the gorges. Most of the people living on the Shashi dike are Shu (Sichuan) people; otherwise, they are those married to Shu people.' According to the 'Record of the Rebuilding of Chuanzhu Shrine,' Chuanzhu Shrine was first built during the Qianlong-Jiaqing period of the Qing, constructed on the former site of the Yangsi Temple at the riverside port, built with funds raised by Sichuan merchant guilds, also called 'Shuying Guildhall.' The main hall inside enshrines Liu Bei, the ruler of Shu Han during the Three Kingdoms, hence the name 'Chuanzhu Shrine' (Sichuan Lord Shrine). The Chuanzhu Shrine Theater is the most famous one among many guildhall theaters, broad and tall, with carved beams and painted pillars, richly decorated, also...

218. 章华寺

Zhanghua Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
荆州市沙市区太师渊路西段北侧
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖石、木结构
看点 Highlights
楚梅唐杏沉香古井石碑古刻楚灵王章华台旧址元泰定二年建
中文 Chinese

章华寺位于荆州市沙市区东北隅太师渊路北侧，东北邻太师渊公园，地处高阜，视野开阔。章华寺原名章台寺，得名于传此地为楚灵王六年（公元前535年）所建之章华台旧址，据寺碑记载：'章华古台，楚灵王故宫旧址也。

'章华台俗称'细腰宫'，即'楚王好细腰，宫中多饿死'的楚灵王所建之离宫。然而关于章华台的位置的推测，众说纷纭，绝不仅此一处。从史料、传说和考古来看，有沙市说（即沙市章华寺所在），监利说，潜江说，武汉说，商水说，等等。

据考古学界的逐年探索，对沙市之章华寺所在，或认为楚离宫故址豫章台所在。在唐代诗人韦庄《楚行吟》中如此描述：'章华台下草如烟，故郢城头月似弦。惆怅楚宫云雨后，露啼花笑一千年。'宋代苏轼则如此描述：'池空野迥楼阁小，唯有深竹藏狐狸。

'可见至少在唐代，章华寺所在高台已湮灭成遗址，一派荒芜景象，或因此被当时文人附会成楚灵王'楚宫云雨'之处，当时已有僧人在此结茅静修，植下银杏树。据寺内碑文记载，元泰定二年（1325），高僧悟开禅师募化十年，在宋代草庐僧寮的基础上，大兴土木，始建为寺，名章台寺。

元天历二年（1329），元文宗图帖睦尔曾亲临寺。到至正十四年（1354）悟开祖师参禅圆寂时，章台寺已达七殿九阁的规模，弟子遍天下。

English 英文

Zhanghua Temple is located on the north side of Taishiyuan Road in the northeast corner of Shashi District, Jingzhou City, adjacent to Taishiyuan Park to the northeast, situated on a high mound with a broad view. Zhanghua Temple was originally named Zhangtai Temple, named after the legend that this place is the former site of Zhanghua Terrace built in the 6th year of King Ling of Chu (535 BC). According to the temple stele records: 'Zhanghua Ancient Terrace is the former site of King Ling of Chu's palace.' Zhanghua Terrace is commonly called 'Slim Waist Palace,' i.e., the detached palace built by King Ling of Chu, of whom it is said 'the King of Chu loved slim waists, and many in the palace starved to death.' However, speculations about the location of Zhanghua Terrace are varied, certainly not limited to this one place. From historical materials, legends, and archaeology, there are the Shashi theory (i.e., where Zhanghua Temple in Shashi is located), the Jianli theory, the Qianjiang theory, the Wuhan theory, the Shangshui theory, etc. According to the year-by-year exploration of the archaeological community, the location of Zhanghua Temple in Shashi is considered by some to be the site of Yuzhang Terrace, the former site of the Chu detached palace. In Tang dynasty poet Wei Zhuang's 'Chanting of a Journey to Chu,' it is described as: 'Below Zhanghua Terrace, grass is like smoke; above the old Ying city head, the moon is like a string. Melancholy after the cloud and rain of the Chu palace, dew cries and flowers laugh for a thousand years.' Song dynasty Su Shi described it as: 'The pool is empty, the wilderness vast, the pavilions small; only deep bamboo hides foxes.' It can be seen that at least in the Tang, the high terrace where Zhanghua Temple is located had been annihilated into ruins, a scene of desolation, and perhaps because of this it was associated by literati of the time as the place of King Ling of Chu's 'cloud and rain of the Chu palace'; at that time there were already monks building thatched huts for quiet cultivation here, planting ginkgo trees. According to inscriptions inside the temple, in the 2nd year of Taiding, Yuan (1325), the eminent monk Wukai Chan Master spent ten years alms-raising, and on the basis of Song dynasty thatched huts and monk quarters, undertook large-scale construction, first building it as a temple, named Zhangtai Temple. In the 2nd year of Tianli, Yuan (1329), Emperor Wenzong of Yuan, Tugh Temür, once personally visited the temple. By the 14th year of Zhizheng (1354), when the founding master Wukai passed away in meditation, Zhangtai Temple had reached the scale of seven halls and nine pavilions, with disciples all over the world.

219. 春秋阁

Chunqiu Pavilion
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
荆州市沙市区公园路1号中山公园内
类型 Type
娱乐建筑·木、石结构
看点 Highlights
精美彩绘石雕关羽读《春秋》嘉庆十一年建戏楼形式
中文 Chinese

春秋阁位于荆州市沙市中山公园内，建于嘉庆十一年（1806），原位于荆州城东郊金龙寺，为寺内的一座戏楼，因金龙寺毁于天火，民国二十年（1931）迁建于现荆州市中山公园内东北隅，并被改建为阁楼，但总体仍保留着戏楼形式。

阁内供奉关羽拜读《春秋》塑像，故名春秋阁。阁宇建在高大厚实的台阶之上，三面环水，绿树掩映。阁基为条石砌筑。正面置有横向石梯两道。阁平面呈矩形，通高13米，其中台高5.45米，阁分上下两层，上为阁、下为室。

上层面阔三间，明间面阔5米，次间面阔2.5米，进深两间，均为4.2米。阁顶为单檐歇山琉璃顶，主体木结构，方形石柱支撑，底部为六层黑色祥云装饰高柱础，上刻有凤凰、牡丹、鹿等吉祥浮雕。

前额中置'春秋阁'三个大字，正中两檐柱上悬挂一幅咏叹关羽的楹联：'绍尼山大一统心传遗憾三分缺汉鼎；为守土留两间正气声灵万古濯荆江。'每个转角处施双昂五踩斗拱两架，前檐下遍施斗拱，其上雕有华丽精致的镀金龙头、凤首和祥云图案。斗拱连同额枋均按旧制拼装，结构严密。

上层台基的石栏杆上则雕有黑色的花虫、走兽等图案，朴素却不失细腻。

English 英文

Chunqiu Pavilion is located in Zhongshan Park, Shashi District, Jingzhou City, built in the 11th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1806), originally located at Jinlong Temple in the eastern suburb of Jingzhou City, serving as a theater tower in the temple; because Jinlong Temple was destroyed by natural fire, in the 20th year of the Republic (1931) it was relocated and built at the northeast corner inside the current Zhongshan Park of Jingzhou City, and was converted into a pavilion, but overall it still retains the theater tower form. Inside the pavilion is enshrined a statue of Guan Yu reading the 'Spring and Autumn Annals,' hence the name Chunqiu (Spring and Autumn) Pavilion. The pavilion is built on a tall and solid platform, surrounded by water on three sides, shaded by green trees. The pavilion base is built with strip stones. On the front there are two horizontal stone staircases. The pavilion has a rectangular plan, with a total height of 13 meters, of which the platform is 5.45 meters high; the pavilion is divided into upper and lower two stories, with the upper being the pavilion and the lower being rooms. The upper floor is three bays wide, with the central bay 5 meters wide and the secondary bays 2.5 meters wide, two bays deep, both 4.2 meters. The pavilion top is a single-eave hip-and-gable glazed roof, with a main wooden structure supported by square stone columns; the bottom has six layers of black auspicious-cloud decorated high column bases, carved with auspicious reliefs such as phoenixes, peonies, and deer. In the middle of the front forehead is placed the three large characters 'Chunqiu Pavilion'; on the two central eave columns hangs a couplet chanting Guan Yu: 'Inheriting the unified teaching of Nishan, regretting that the three kingdoms lack the Han tripod; leaving the righteous spirit of two spaces for defending the land, its soul cleanses the Jingjiang River for eternity.' At each corner, two ang five-step bracket sets are applied; under the front eave, bracket sets are applied everywhere, above which are carved gorgeous and exquisite gilded dragon heads, phoenix heads, and auspicious cloud patterns. The bracket sets together with the architraves are all assembled according to the old system, with a strict structure. On the stone railings of the upper platform base are carved black patterns of flowers, insects, and beasts, simple yet not lacking in delicacy.

220. 沙市民居

Vernacular Dwellings in Shashi
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清末
地址 Address
荆州市沙市区胜利街等
类型 Type
民居建筑
看点 Highlights
洋式与传统结合的建筑风貌胜利街九十铺邓氏住宅恒春大药房
中文 Chinese

'天下口，要汉口，天下市，算沙市。'明清时期，沙市凭借其便利的漕运已成为湖北仅次于汉口的繁华商会。随着清末沙市的进一步开埠，其街市也进一步繁荣和开放。如《沙市志略校由》载：'沙市其为楚都外港，当随之而兴。

且荆襄为旧日西南各省人都通商，沙市正其枢纽。'《竹枝词》'偶咽沙头市，玲珑竹岸窗'，知其繁盛，在唐时已然矣……青石大街、刘家场、丝线街，赤帝宫街等，全市精华，荟萃于斯。

'又如《沙市志记》载：'……至清光绪二十一年中日《马关条约》，开沙市、苏州、杭州为商埠后，此处更见兴盛耳。'胜利街、崇文街（俗称'丝线街'）、中山路是当时最为繁华的街市。

明清时期，得胜街沿街商铺密集，故名'九十铺'或'九十埠'，荆州沦陷时曾名兴亚街，光复后改为中正一、二、三街，1949年后改现名，现为荆州市传统历史文化保护街区。胜利街西起管家牌，东至青龙观，长约1.8公里，青石路面。

街两侧为密集的传统民居，建于晚清的邓氏住宅、恒春懋大药房等都在此地。其中，较典型的是清光绪二十七年（1901）满汉旗后裔邓氏迁至沙市九十埠兴建的大宅，构造、格局、装修、雕饰均非常讲究。

沙市中山路类似汉口中山路以及广州、天津等地的一些街道，它们处于中国建筑承上启下、中西交错、新老并存、相互影响的阶段，具有独特的历史价值和建筑艺术价值。中山大马路和原青石大街、拖船埠、三府街、刘家场一起，作为商埠城市的骨架，出现了不少中西合璧的洋行、领事馆、商铺、民居、会馆。

中山路沿街商铺的设计吸取了不少洋式店面形式，临街建筑一般3-4层，大多横三段，竖三段划分。有的采用西方古典凹拱式门窗线脚，有的采用西方方柱子或壁柱。柱子上多用横向窗脚按功能划分墙体，正面开间檐部有折线或曲线状的山墙装饰。

在建材上，较早采用了铁件、油漆、水泥、玻璃等新兴建材，同时，我国民间常用的建材如布瓦、薄砖、杉松木料等也得到了广泛应用。当时的金融商业建筑中，较为典型的则有同震银楼、老天宝银楼、老丹凤银楼、老万年银楼、聚兴城、徐万源布庄等。

English 英文

'The mouth under heaven, count Hankou; the market under heaven, count Shashi.' During the Ming and Qing, Shashi, relying on its convenient water transport, had become a prosperous commercial city in Hubei second only to Hankou. With the further opening of Shashi as a treaty port at the end of the Qing, its streets and markets further prospered and opened up. As recorded in the 'Collation of Shashi Local Records': 'Shashi as the outer port of the Chu capital, should prosper accordingly. Moreover, Jingxiang was the hub for merchants from all southwestern provinces in the old days, and Shashi was exactly its pivot.' The 'Bamboo Branch Ci' says 'Occasionally passing the Shatou market, exquisite bamboo shore windows,' showing that its prosperity already existed in the Tang... Qingshi Street, Liujiachang, Sixian Street, Chidigong Street, etc., the essence of the whole city, gathered here.' Another example from the 'Records of Shashi': '...After the Treaty of Shimonoseki between China and Japan in the 21st year of Guangxu, Qing, opened Shashi, Suzhou, and Hangzhou as treaty ports, this place became even more prosperous.' Shengli Street, Chongwen Street (commonly called 'Sixian Street'), and Zhongshan Road were the most prosperous streets at that time. During the Ming and Qing, Desheng Street had dense shops along the street, hence the name 'Ninety Shops' or 'Ninety Ports'; during the Japanese occupation of Jingzhou it was once named Xingya Street, after recovery it was changed to Zhongzheng First, Second, and Third Streets, and after 1949 changed to its current name; it is now a traditional historical and cultural protection block in Jingzhou City. Shengli Street starts from Guanjia Pai in the west and reaches Qinglong Temple in the east, about 1.8 km long, with bluestone pavement. On both sides of the street are dense traditional dwellings; the Deng family residence built in the late Qing and the Hengchunmao Pharmacy are all located here. Among them, the more typical one is the large mansion built by the Deng family, descendants of Manchu-Han bannermen, who moved to Shashi's Ninety Ports in the 27th year of Guangxu, Qing (1901); its construction, layout, decoration, and carvings are all very exquisite. Zhongshan Road in Shashi is similar to Zhongshan Road in Hankou and some streets in Guangzhou, Tianjin and other places; they are at a stage where Chinese architecture connects the past and future, with Chinese and Western styles interlaced, old and new coexisting, and mutually influencing, having unique historical value and architectural artistic value. Zhongshan Main Road, together with the original Qingshi Street, Tuochuan Port, Sanfu Street, and Liujiachang, as the skeleton of the treaty port city, saw the emergence of many Chinese-Western combined foreign firms, consulates, shops, dwellings, and guildhalls. The design of shops along Zhongshan Road absorbed many Western-style storefront forms; the street-facing buildings are generally 3-4 stories, mostly divided horizontally into three sections and vertically into three sections. Some adopt Western classical concave arch door and window moldings, some adopt Western square columns or pilasters. On the columns, horizontal window feet are mostly used to divide the wall by function, with broken-line or curved gable decorations on the front eaves. In terms of building materials, emerging building materials such as iron parts, paint, cement, and glass were adopted relatively early; at the same time, commonly used Chinese folk building materials such as cloth tiles, thin bricks, and fir and pine wood were also widely used. Among the financial and commercial buildings of the time, the more typical ones include Tongzhen Silver Building, Laotianbao Silver Building, Laodanfeng Silver Building, Laowannian Silver Building, Juxingcheng, Xu Wanyuan Cloth Store, etc.

221. 沙市同震银楼

Tongzhen Silverware Shop of Shashi

看点 Highlights
仿汉口璇宫饭店建筑造型巴洛克风格圆拱顶828平方米U形回廊
中文 Chinese

清光绪十一年（1885），宁波商人童澄海出资兴建了同震银楼，该楼是当时沙市最大的金银首饰商铺，也是沙市较早的巴洛克风格圆拱顶建筑。其建筑面积为828平方米，正立面采用奉化产玉石砌筑，赭红色水泥砂浆抹面。

窗、门、阳台均有浮雕花饰。内部原为木屋架结构，按清代营造法式制作。双坡屋盖上置有玻璃天棚，'U'形回廊，有镂花直棂式推窗。三方围护体均为灌斗墙，因自重较重，恐地基下沉，施工时基础采用铁箍木桩，开沙市地基处理之先河。

民国二十三年（1934年）扩宽中山路时，按原样朝北后退5米重建，梁柱改为钢筋混凝土现浇。

English 英文

In the 11th year of Guangxu, Qing (1885), Ningbo merchant Tong Chenghai funded the construction of Tongzhen Silver Building; this building was the largest gold and silver jewelry shop in Shashi at that time, and also one of the earlier Baroque-style round-arch-top buildings in Shashi. Its building area is 828 square meters; the front facade is built with jade stone produced in Fenghua, plastered with ochre-red cement mortar. The windows, doors, and balconies all have relief floral decorations. The interior was originally a wooden roof frame structure, made according to Qing dynasty construction methods. On the double-slope roof there is a glass canopy, a 'U'-shaped corridor, and openwork straight-lattice push windows. The three-sided enclosing walls are all bucket-filled walls; due to heavy self-weight and fear of foundation settlement, iron-hooped wooden piles were used for the foundation during construction, pioneering foundation treatment in Shashi. When widening Zhongshan Road in the 23rd year of the Republic (1934), it was rebuilt 5 meters backward to the north according to the original appearance, and the beams and columns were changed to cast-in-place reinforced concrete.

1920年，汉阳帮老板洪发利兴建天宝银楼，1949年前为私人银楼，1949年后曾改作沙市百货公司纺织品商店。

English 英文

In 1920, Hanyang gang boss Hong Fali built Tianbao Silver Building; before 1949 it was a private silver building, and after 1949 it was converted into a textile goods store of the Shashi Department Store Company. This building imitated the architectural form of the Xuangong Hotel designed by Hankou Jingming Foreign Firm; it is a four-story reinforced concrete structure with a building area of 886 square meters; both ends of the facade protrude, and each floor in the center has a double-column circular balcony, with an exquisite shape. Originally there was a corner tower on each side of the top, and a reinforced concrete pavilion in the middle, all of which were damaged during the 'Cultural Revolution.'

The Episcopal Church of Shashi was built by the American church in 1900; the existing building is the residence of the president and preaching personnel, and was rented to Shashi Middle School as a dormitory in 1953. Laozheng Street and Vernacular Dwellings in Zhoulaozui
级别 Level
