戏楼形制彩绘纹饰益阳大鼓清乾隆十二年建清雍正年间
中文 Chinese

明清时期，随县北部一带称益阳县，这里毗邻河南，民间说书艺人吸收了当地的民间艺术'孝歌'，又受到北方鼓书风格的影响，创造出益阳大鼓这一独具特色的演唱方式。益阳大鼓说唱相间，唱词以七字句式、十字句式为主；唱腔以平腔为主，也有嘹子、雅腔、大悲等板式。

解河戏楼所在的新城镇是益阳大鼓的发源地之一，唱戏看戏之风浓厚，戏楼本身是益阳大鼓重要的表演场。随州花鼓剧团的编剧李永朝先生在20世纪80年代初，曾在戏楼的大梁上发现'此楼重建于清乾隆十二年'字样，表明戏楼初始的建造年代应不晚于清雍正年间。

彼时梁上还保存有曾来此演出的三十多个戏班名单的墨迹题字，今已不可考。戏楼坐落在石筑夯土台基之上，坐南朝北，分前...

English 英文

During the Ming and Qing, the northern area of Sui County was called Yiyang County, bordering Henan; folk storytellers absorbed the local folk art 'Xiao Ge' (Filial Piety Song) and were influenced by the northern drum-book style, creating Yiyang Drum, a unique singing style. Yiyang Drum alternates between singing and speaking, with lyrics mainly in seven-character and ten-character sentence patterns; the singing style is mainly plain tune, and also has styles such as Liaozi, Yaqiang, and Dabei. The Xincheng Town where Jiehe Theater is located is one of the birthplaces of Yiyang Drum, with a strong atmosphere of performing and watching operas, and the theater itself is an important performance venue for Yiyang Drum. Mr. Li Yongchao, a screenwriter of the Suizhou Huagu Opera Troupe, in the early 1980s, once found on the main beam of the theater the words 'This theater was rebuilt in the 12th year of Qianlong, Qing,' indicating that the initial construction date of the theater should be no later than the Yongzheng period of the Qing. At that time, the beam also preserved ink inscriptions of the names of more than thirty opera troupes that had come to perform here, which can no longer be verified today. The theater is located on a stone-built rammed-earth platform base, facing north from south, divided into front...

258. 岳氏祠

Yue's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
市级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
随县万和镇解河村
类型 Type
祭祀建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
木雕帝尧时期名臣伯夷万和镇岳氏于明末清初由孝感迁徙至此后殿面阔五间明间前额上雕刻暗八仙和福寿二字
中文 Chinese

岳氏先祖相传为帝尧时期的名臣伯夷，他掌管祭祀，为第一任太岳，其子孙遂以官为氏，称岳姓。万和镇岳氏于明末清初时由孝感迁徙至此，祠坐东北朝西南，现仅存后殿。后殿面阔五间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，抬梁式构架；

屋脊作三段跌落，正脊微弯，两端翘起。明间、次间有前廊，廊下在屋顶之下又做一层装饰性的卷棚顶，宽约2米，卷棚之下为装饰性的月梁板。明间前额上雕刻暗八仙和'福''寿'二字，在墙壁和屋顶之间的窗格亦有蝙蝠和团花图案装饰。

English 英文

The ancestor of the Yue family is legendarily said to be Boyi, a famous minister during the period of Emperor Yao; he was in charge of sacrifices and was the first Grand Yue, hence his descendants took the official title as their surname, called Yue. The Yue family of Wanhe Town migrated here from Xiaogan at the end of the Ming and beginning of the Qing; the ancestral hall faces southwest from northeast, and now only the rear hall remains. The rear hall is five bays wide, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof and a post-and-lintel frame; the roof ridge is made in three stepped drops, the main ridge slightly curved, with both ends upturned. The central and secondary bays have front porches; under the porch and below the roof, another decorative rolling-roof ceiling is made, about 2 meters wide, and below the rolling roof is a decorative moon-beam board. On the front lintel of the central bay, the Dark Eight Immortals and the characters 'Fu' (fortune) and 'Shou' (longevity) are carved; the window lattice between the walls and the roof is also decorated with bat and medallion flower patterns.

259. 杨氏祠

Yang's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
市级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
随县万和镇冷湾村北
类型 Type
祭祀建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
平面格局木构架明初由山西迁至麻城明末清初又由麻城迁至随县清嘉庆年间建解放战争时期曾为随北县委县政府所在地
中文 Chinese

万和镇杨氏祠明初由山西迁至麻城，明末清初又由麻城迁至随县。随县杨氏祠建于清嘉庆年间，祠堂坐北朝南，两进院落，有前、中、后堂和左右厢房。大门之上有两层砖砌檐，以砖雕和泥塑简易地模仿贴面牌楼。

各进堂屋均面宽五间，前堂为单面坡屋顶，中、后堂均为单檐硬山灰瓦顶；后堂与岳氏祠类似，明、次间前有檐廊，屋顶作三段跌落。解放战争时期，杨氏祠曾为随北县委县政府所在地，李先念等革命领导人曾在此工作。

English 英文

The Yang's Ancestral Hall of Wanhe Town migrated from Shanxi to Macheng at the beginning of the Ming, and from Macheng to Sui County at the end of the Ming and beginning of the Qing. The Yang's Ancestral Hall in Sui County was built during the Jiaqing period of the Qing; the ancestral hall faces south, with two courtyards, and has front, middle, and rear halls and left and right wing rooms. Above the main gate there are two layers of brick-built eaves, simply imitating a veneer paifang with brick carvings and clay sculptures. Each entry hall is five bays wide; the front hall has a single-slope roof, and the middle and rear halls both have single-eave gable gray-tile roofs; the rear hall is similar to Yue's Ancestral Hall, with eaves porches in front of the central and secondary bays, and the roof made in three stepped drops. During the Liberation War, Yang's Ancestral Hall was once the location of the Suibei County Party Committee and County Government, and revolutionary leaders such as Li Xiannian once worked here.

260. 徐店戏楼

Theater in Xudian
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
广水市余店镇徐店村
类型 Type
娱乐建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
戏楼形制纹饰细部始建于清嘉庆四年咸丰十年重修供奉火观音菩萨的火观庙平面呈凸字
中文 Chinese

徐店戏楼在徐店村的北端，始建于清嘉庆四年（1799），咸丰十年（1860）重修。据村中老人介绍，戏楼原属于供奉火观音菩萨的火观庙，由街坊集资兴建。抗日战争时期日军占领徐店，火观庙正殿被拆毁；'文革'时期，戏楼伸出的垛子和正梁上'二龙戏珠'的木雕被毁坏。

戏楼坐西朝东，平面呈'凸'字，分前后台。前台为单檐歇山灰瓦顶，四角立柱，正脊两端饰鸱尾，中置白色宝瓶，四戗脊各饰卧龙一条；后台面阔三间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶。整体造型和规模都与解河戏楼十分相近。戏楼前有斜坡场子地，可容千余人看戏。

当地人崇尚文雅，在劳作之余经常自编自演古今剧目。如今，逢正月初一、十五，或是重大节日、红白喜事，都会有各种剧目轮流上演，以汉剧、楚剧和豫剧为主，短则二三日，长则十天半月。

English 英文

Xudian Theater is at the northern end of Xudian Village, first built in the 4th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1799), and rebuilt in the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860). According to introductions by elderly villagers, the theater originally belonged to the Huoguan Temple dedicated to the Fire Guanyin Bodhisattva, built with funds raised by neighborhood residents. During the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, the Japanese army occupied Xudian, and the main hall of Huoguan Temple was demolished; during the 'Cultural Revolution' period, the protruding buttresses of the theater and the wood carving of 'Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl' on the main beam were destroyed. The theater faces east from west, with a plan in the shape of the character '凸' (convex), divided into front and back stages. The front stage has a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, with columns at the four corners; both ends of the main ridge are decorated with chiwei (owl-tail ornaments), with a white precious vase in the middle, and each of the four diagonal ridges is decorated with a reclining dragon; the back stage is three bays wide, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof. The overall shape and scale are very similar to Jiehe Theater. In front of the theater there is a sloped open space, capable of holding more than a thousand people to watch operas. Local people value elegance and refinement, and in their spare time from labor they often write and perform ancient and modern plays themselves. Today, on the first and fifteenth days of the first lunar month, or on major festivals, weddings and funerals, various plays are performed in rotation, mainly Han opera, Chu opera, and Yu opera, lasting from two or three days to ten days or half a month.

261. 千户冲民居

Vernacular Dwellings in Qianhuchong
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
广水市十里办事处千户冲村
类型 Type
民居
看点 Highlights
木雕石雕坐落在半山腰的一片绿荫之中四路院落一字排开杨姓千户清乾隆杨氏兄弟三人建
中文 Chinese

千户冲民居坐落在半山腰的一片绿荫之中，坐南朝北，四路院落一字排开，门前有一条与山脊平行的大田冲（方言，房前田地为'冲'，房后为'畈'）。据当地传说，这里曾经是一个杨姓千户（元代以来的一种官名）修建的宅院，因此名为千户冲；

在另一个更为具体的说法里，千户冲的建造者是晚清的杨氏兄弟三人。老二杨长青在广西做县官，身份最为显赫，因此他的房子在中间，左、右两侧分别是大哥和三弟的房子，整组宅院历时三年建成，每家各有两进院落。

后来，大哥一支人丁兴旺，便在左侧又增建一路，因为是小辈，院墙稍微矮些，且仅建造了一进较大的庭院。这四座宅院各有前后两进院落，每进正房五间，两侧有厢房相通，四家共八个庭院。位于中间的杨长青宅，大门为八字形，比另外三个方形大门宽阔、讲究、气派，体现出为官者身份的不同。

大门两侧各有一个角门，供佣人进出。门楣上有四个门簪，门前原有一对抱鼓石，2014年曾失窃，警方追回后一直没有装回...

English 英文

The vernacular dwellings of Qianhuchong are located in a patch of green shade on a mountainside, facing north from south, with four rows of courtyards lined up in a row; in front of the doors there is a large field chong (dialect: the field in front of the house is 'chong,' and behind the house is 'fan') parallel to the mountain ridge. According to local legend, this was once a residential compound built by a Yang-surname qianhu (a kind of official title since the Yuan Dynasty), hence named Qianhuchong; in another more specific account, the builders of Qianhuchong were three Yang brothers in the late Qing. The second brother, Yang Changqing, served as a county magistrate in Guangxi, with the most prominent status, hence his house is in the middle, and the left and right sides are respectively the houses of the eldest brother and the third brother; the entire group of residential compounds took three years to build, and each family has two courtyards. Later, the eldest brother's branch had a prosperous population, so another row was added on the left; because they were juniors, the courtyard walls were slightly lower, and only one larger courtyard was built. These four residential compounds each have front and rear two courtyards, with five bays of main rooms in each entry, and wing rooms on both sides connecting them; the four families have a total of eight courtyards. The Yang Changqing residence in the middle has an eight-character-shaped main gate, which is wider, more exquisite, and more imposing than the other three square main gates, reflecting the different status of an official. On both sides of the main gate there is a corner gate each, for servants to enter and exit. On the lintel there are four door pegs; in front of the door there was originally a pair of drum-shaped holding stones, which were stolen in 2014 and have not been reinstalled after being recovered by the police...

襄阳市

Xiangyang
67 处

262. 襄阳古隆中

Ancient Longzhong in Xiangyang
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区001县道隆中6号
类型 Type
纪念建筑
看点 Highlights
环境石雕建筑纪念性诸葛亮隐居之所三顾茅庐和隆中对隆中十景
中文 Chinese

大巴山脉分支——武当山向东南蜿蜒至襄州区、南漳县、谷城县三地交界处，汉水以南，形成一处群山环抱的小小山谷，'有山隆然中起'，这便是隆山——古隆中所在。《舆地志》又云：'隆中者，空中也。行其上空空然有声。'如罗贯中所描绘，其环境'山不高而秀雅；水不深而澄清；

地不广而平坦；林不大而茂密'。从大环境来看，襄阳据南北驿道的要冲，隆中虽地属山林，却并不闭塞。此处即相传一代名相诸葛亮出山之前，躬耕苦读的隐居之所，著名的'三顾茅庐'和'隆中对'的历史故事就发生于此，史籍和当代影视作品对这一段'凡三往，乃见'的故事有极为精彩的刻画。

因此古隆中又名诸葛亮故居、诸葛庙。诸葛亮出山后，此处空留草屋若干间，曾易为董姓所居，后随董家没落而衰。晋代有碑铭记述，唐代建有武侯庙，此后多有损毁、重建。至明中叶弘治年间，襄简王朱见淑沼其宅址建陵，并于故宅东侧山梁另建小祠以奉祀武侯，逐渐形成以三顾堂为中心的'隆中十景'（后扩展为十二景）。

此后，明嘉靖、万历和清康熙年间又多次重修，近代当代也多有维修和新建。

现存建筑多为清代所建，依山势错落、散布于约2平方公里的隆中山南麓，大都以诸葛亮当年的遗址而定名，主要建筑和胜迹有：'古隆中'牌坊、抱膝亭、武侯祠、三顾堂、草庐亭、野云庵（卧龙深处）、襄王陵、躬耕田、小虹桥、梁父岩、老龙洞、半月溪等，山中遍存石碑48通。

English 英文

A branch of the Daba Mountains — Wudang Mountain winds southeast to the junction of Xiangzhou District, Nanzhang County, and Gucheng County, south of the Han River, forming a small valley surrounded by mountains, 'with a mountain rising prominently in the middle,' this is Long Mountain — where Ancient Longzhong is located. The 'Yudi Zhi' (Geographical Records) also says: 'Longzhong means empty in the air; walking above it, one hears a hollow sound.' As depicted by Luo Guanzhong, its environment is 'the mountains are not high but elegant; the water is not deep but clear; the land is not broad but flat; the forest is not large but dense.' From the broader environment, Xiangyang occupies the strategic point of the north-south post road; although Longzhong belongs to mountain forests, it is not isolated. This place is legendarily the hermitage where Zhuge Liang, a generation of famous prime minister, farmed and studied hard before coming out of seclusion; the famous historical stories of 'Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage' and 'Longzhong Dialogue' took place here, and historical records and contemporary film and television works have extremely wonderful depictions of this story of 'went three times before being received.' Hence Ancient Longzhong is also called Zhuge Liang's Former Residence and Zhuge Temple. After Zhuge Liang came out of seclusion, only several thatched cottages remained here, which were once occupied by the Dong family, and later declined with the Dong family's downfall. In the Jin Dynasty there were stele inscriptions recording this; in the Tang a Wuhou Temple was built, and thereafter it was damaged and rebuilt many times. By the middle of the Ming, during the Hongzhi period, Prince Xiangjian Zhu Shianshu appropriated the site of his former residence to build a mausoleum, and built a small shrine on the mountain ridge east of the former residence to worship Wuhou, gradually forming the 'Ten Scenes of Longzhong' centered on the Sangu Hall (later expanded to Twelve Scenes). Thereafter, during the Jiajing and Wanli periods of the Ming and the Kangxi period of the Qing, it was repaired many times, and in modern and contemporary times there have also been many repairs and new constructions. The existing buildings were mostly built in the Qing, scattered along the mountain terrain on the southern foot of Long Mountain in an area of about 2 square kilometers, mostly named after the sites where Zhuge Liang once was; the main buildings and scenic spots include: the 'Ancient Longzhong' Paifang, Baoxi Pavilion, Wuhou Temple, Sangu Hall, Caolu Pavilion, Yeyun Nunnery (Wolong Deep Place), Xiangwang Mausoleum, Gonggeng Field, Xiaohong Bridge, Liangfu Rock, Laolong Cave, Banyue Stream, etc., with 48 stone steles preserved throughout the mountain.

263. 古隆中牌坊

Ancient Longzhong Paifang
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区古隆中景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑·石结构
看点 Highlights
古隆中标志性建筑清光绪十九年建四柱三间三楼青石仿木结构坊正中额枋雕刻古隆中三个大字柱上浮雕渔樵耕读
中文 Chinese

明代以前的'隆中十景'中并无古隆中石牌坊，牌坊建于清光绪十九年（1893，一说建于光绪十六年，1890）湖北提督、北宋程颢、程颐后人陈文树建，而后逐渐成为古隆中的标志性建筑。

牌坊坐西朝东，四柱三间三楼，青石仿木结构，中门宽2.7米，侧门宽1.94米，中楼高7.5米，次楼高5.56米，石柱上雕梁画栋，起角弯爪，单檐斗拱，带背座吻，古朴素雅。

坊正中额枋雕刻'古隆中'三个大字，背面为苏轼名言'三代下一人'，中枋额正、背面分别阴刻'澹泊明志，宁静致远'，石柱上分别阴刻杜甫《蜀相》诗'三顾频烦天下计，两朝开济老臣心'以及陈维周《咏怀古迹五首》诗'伯仲之间见伊吕，指挥若定失萧曹'。

柱周围浮雕中访贤故事，枋间多处浮雕渔樵耕读、琴棋书画、八仙过海、二龙戏珠、双凤朝日、鹿鹤同寿、麒麟送子、赤虎朋寿等浮雕，柱前后有抱鼓石共10个。

English 英文

Before the Ming, there was no Ancient Longzhong stone paifang in the 'Ten Scenes of Longzhong'; the paifang was built in the 19th year of Guangxu, Qing (1893, one says built in the 16th year of Guangxu, 1890) by Chen Wenshu, Hubei Military Commander and descendant of Northern Song Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi, and thereafter gradually became the landmark building of Ancient Longzhong. The paifang faces east from west, with four columns, three bays, and three stories, of bluestone imitating wood structure; the central gate is 2.7 meters wide, the side gates 1.94 meters wide, the central tower 7.5 meters high, the secondary towers 5.56 meters high; the stone columns are carved with beams and painted with pillars, with upturned corner claws, single-eave bracket sets, and ridge ornaments, simple and elegant. In the middle of the paifang, the额枋 is carved with the three large characters 'Ancient Longzhong'; on the back is Su Shi's famous saying 'One Man Below Three Generations'; the front and back of the central额枋 are respectively incised with 'Indifferent to Fame, One Clarifies the Mind; Tranquil and Peaceful, One Reaches Far'; on the stone columns are respectively incised with Du Fu's poem 'Prime Minister of Shu' — 'Three visits frequently troubled the plan for the world; two dynasties opened and sustained the old minister's heart' — and Chen Weizhou's poem 'Five Poems Chanting Ancient Sites' — 'Between brothers one sees Yi and Lü; with calm command one surpasses Xiao and Cao.' Around the columns are reliefs of stories of visiting sages; between the额枋 are many reliefs of fisherman, woodcutter, farmer, and scholar, lute, chess, calligraphy, and painting, Eight Immortals Crossing the Sea, Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl, Two Phoenixes Facing the Sun, Deer and Crane Sharing Longevity, Qilin Delivering a Child, Red Tiger and Friend Longevity, etc.; before and behind the columns there are a total of 10 drum-shaped holding stones.

264. 武侯祠

Wuhou Temple
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区古隆中景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
古隆中主要建筑始建于晋朝明嘉靖年间重建清乾隆二十一年重修中轴线上四进三层院台建筑殿内供奉诸葛亮铜像
中文 Chinese

武侯祠位于山腰，为古隆中的主要建筑，始建于晋朝，'历唐、宋、元皆知崇奉'，重建于明嘉靖年间，清乾隆二十一年（1756）重修。建筑群坐北朝南，依山就势，中轴线上四进三层院台建筑，有前殿、中殿、过殿和正殿。

除第三进院落过殿为卷棚式，其他均为单檐硬山。殿与殿之间设有廊庑，院墙围拢，院中植有古柏、枇杷树等。祠前石狮精美，狮座有奔马、舞凤、麒麟等浮雕，画面生动，具有极高的艺术水平。前殿面阔三间，硬山顶。

前檐设砖仿木结构四柱三间式楼，檐下施三层斗拱，额匾书楷书'汉诸葛丞相武侯祠'，明间石门框上书'冈枕南阳依旧田园淡泊，统开西蜀尚留遗像清高'对联，门前的圆鼓石上浮雕松鹤、凤凰图案，殿内供奉诸葛亮铜像。

正殿为砖木结构，面阔三间，供诸葛亮及其子诸葛瞻、孙诸葛尚坐像。正殿两侧有娘娘殿和三义殿。娘娘殿供奉黄月英，三义殿供奉刘、关、张塑像。正殿东侧有铜鼓台。

English 英文

Wuhou Temple is located on the mountainside and is the main building of Ancient Longzhong; it was first built in the Jin Dynasty, 'through the Tang, Song, and Yuan all knew to revere and worship it,' rebuilt during the Jiajing period of the Ming, and repaired in the 21st year of Qianlong, Qing (1756). The building complex faces south, following the mountain terrain, with four entries and three layers of courtyard buildings on the central axis, including the front hall, middle hall, passage hall, and main hall. Except for the passage hall of the third-entry courtyard which is of rolling-roof style, the others are all single-eave gable roofs. Between the halls there are corridors and side rooms, enclosed by courtyard walls, with ancient cypresses and loquat trees planted in the courtyard. The stone lions in front of the temple are exquisite, with reliefs of galloping horses, dancing phoenixes, and qilin on the lion bases, with vivid pictures and extremely high artistic level. The front hall is three bays wide, with a gable roof. The front eave is set with a brick-imitating-wood structure of four columns and three bays; under the eave are three layers of bracket sets; the inscribed plaque reads in regular script 'Han Prime Minister Zhuge Wuhou Temple'; on the stone door frame of the central bay is the couplet 'The ridge rests on Nanyang, still the fields are indifferent; the rule opens Western Shu, still the portrait remains lofty'; on the round drum stones in front of the door are reliefs of pine and crane, phoenix patterns, and the hall enshrines a bronze statue of Zhuge Liang. The main hall is of brick-wood structure, three bays wide, enshrining seated statues of Zhuge Liang and his son Zhuge Zhan and grandson Zhuge Shang. On both sides of the main hall there are the Niangniang Hall and Sanyi Hall. The Niangniang Hall enshrines Huang Yueying, and the Sanyi Hall enshrines statues of Liu, Guan, and Zhang. East of the main hall there is the Bronze Drum Platform.

265. 三顾堂

Sangu Hall (Hall of Three Visits)
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区古隆中景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
始建于明成化年间重建于清康熙五十八年光绪初年重修过厅面阔三间正殿面阔五间相传为刘关张三顾茅庐系马之处
中文 Chinese

武侯祠向西几十米为三顾堂，始建于明成化年间，重建于清康熙五十八年（1719），光绪初年重修。三顾堂主要由过厅、正殿和廊庑组成。

过厅面阔三间，进深三间，前接八字形山门影壁，正中悬挂'三顾堂'匾额，山门前有两株古柏，相传为刘、关、张三顾茅庐系马之处。正殿面阔五间，进深三间。均为单檐硬山灰瓦顶。

院内两厢碑廊墙上嵌有诸葛亮部分遗作石刻及历代诗文碑刻数十方。

English 英文

A few dozen meters west of Wuhou Temple is Sangu Hall, first built during the Chenghua period of the Ming, rebuilt in the 58th year of Kangxi, Qing (1719), and repaired in the early Guangxu period. Sangu Hall is mainly composed of a passage hall, main hall, and corridors. The passage hall is three bays wide and three bays deep, with an eight-character-shaped mountain gate screen wall in front; in the center hangs the 'Sangu Hall' inscribed plaque; in front of the mountain gate there are two ancient cypresses, legendarily the place where Liu, Guan, and Zhang tied their horses during the Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage. The main hall is five bays wide and three bays deep. Both are single-eave gable gray-tile roofs. On the walls of the two-side stele corridors in the courtyard are embedded stone carvings of part of Zhuge Liang's surviving works and dozens of stele inscriptions of poetry and prose from successive dynasties.

266. 躬耕田、躬耕亭

Gonggeng Field and Gonggeng Pavilion
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区古隆中景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑
看点 Highlights
相传为诸葛亮当年躬耕陇亩之地躬耕田边建有躬耕亭上题田园淡泊匾额亭中竖躬耕陇亩石碑躬耕田边上有溪溪上有桥名小虹桥
中文 Chinese

从三顾堂前沿山坡缓缓而下，可达躬耕田，位于乐山与隆中山之间，相传为诸葛亮当年躬耕陇亩之地。躬耕田边现建有躬耕亭，上题'田园淡泊'匾额，亭中竖'躬耕陇亩'石碑。躬耕田边上有溪，溪上有桥，名小虹桥，为诸葛亮隐居隆中时出入必经之桥，刘备二顾茅庐时在此桥上误把诸葛亮岳父黄承颜认作诸葛亮。

现今之小桥为1983年重修。

English 英文

Going slowly down the hillside from in front of Sangu Hall, one can reach Gonggeng Field, located between Le Mountain and Long Mountain; legendarily it was the place where Zhuge Liang farmed the fields in those years. Beside Gonggeng Field there is now built Gonggeng Pavilion, with the inscribed plaque 'Indifferent Fields and Gardens' on top; in the pavilion stands the stone stele 'Farming the Fields.' Beside Gonggeng Field there is a stream, and over the stream there is a bridge named Xiaohong Bridge, which was the bridge Zhuge Liang had to pass when going in and out during his seclusion in Longzhong; when Liu Bei made the second visit to the thatched cottage, on this bridge he mistook Zhuge Liang's father-in-law Huang Chengyan for Zhuge Liang. The current small bridge was rebuilt in 1983.

267. 抱膝亭

Baoxi Pavilion (Hugging-Knees Pavilion)
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区古隆中景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
建于清康熙五十八年重建于光绪十八年六角三重檐攒尖顶底边长3.55米通高12米亭前立圆首跌座石碑一通
中文 Chinese

抱膝亭与躬耕田遥遥相对，建于清康熙五十八年（1719），重建于光绪十八年（1892）。为六角三重檐攒尖顶，造型挺秀端庄。底边长3.55米、通高12米。亭内有木梯可登楼观景，二层设隔扇。门柱刻楷书对联一副。

亭前立圆首跌座石碑一通，阳面刻'抱膝处'，为清代书法家张裕钊所书。'抱膝亭'之名是来自诸葛亮在隆中躬耕之余休憩时抱膝长吟，抑或后人凭吊诸葛亮时抱膝长吟，已无从可考。

English 英文

Baoxi Pavilion faces Gonggeng Field from afar; it was built in the 58th year of Kangxi, Qing (1719), and rebuilt in the 18th year of Guangxu (1892). It is a hexagonal three-eave pyramidal roof, with an elegant and dignified shape. The base side length is 3.55 meters, and the total height is 12 meters. Inside the pavilion there is a wooden ladder to climb the tower for viewing, and the second story is fitted with lattice doors. On the door columns is carved a pair of regular-script couplets. In front of the pavilion stands a stone stele with a round top and stepped base; the front face is carved with 'Place of Hugging Knees,' written by the Qing calligrapher Zhang Yuzhao. The name 'Baoxi Pavilion' comes from whether Zhuge Liang hugged his knees and chanted long when resting after farming in Longzhong, or later generations hugged their knees and chanted long when commemorating Zhuge Liang; this can no longer be verified.

268. 草庐亭、草庐碑

Caolu Pavilion and Caolu Stele
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区古隆中景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
位于三顾堂背后距抱膝亭50米相传亭所在即为草庐遗址亭内供有诸葛亮年轻时塑像清康熙五十九年始建清嘉庆十六年重建明嘉靖十九年立龙首龟座石碑一座
中文 Chinese

草庐亭位于三顾堂背后，距抱膝亭50米，依山向谷，环境幽静，相传亭所在即为草庐遗址，亭内供有诸葛亮年轻时塑像，故又名幼像亭。亭为清康熙五十九年（1720）始建，清嘉庆十六年（1811）重建，六角重檐攒尖顶，砖木结构。

额题'草庐遗址'，下分鼎，石翻阴云八阵图，出自修建草庐亭的郧襄观察使赵宏恩所写《隆中武侯草庐诗》。草庐亭下有明嘉靖十九年（1540）立龙首龟座石碑一座，正面刻'草庐'，相传为明代唐寅手笔。背面刻'龙卧处'三字。

English 英文

Caolu Pavilion is located behind Sangu Hall, 50 meters from Baoxi Pavilion, facing the valley against the mountain, with a quiet environment; legendarily the place where the pavilion stands is the site of the thatched cottage, and inside the pavilion is enshrined a statue of Zhuge Liang in his youth, hence also called Young Statue Pavilion. The pavilion was first built in the 59th year of Kangxi, Qing (1720), and rebuilt in the 16th year of Jiaqing (1811); it is a hexagonal double-eave pyramidal roof, of brick-wood structure. The额 is inscribed 'Site of the Thatched Cottage'; below it is divided into tripods, with stone-carved negative cloud Eight-Formation Diagram, from the 'Poem on the Thatched Cottage of Wuhou in Longzhong' written by Zhao Hongen, the Yunxiang Observer who built Caolu Pavilion. Below Caolu Pavilion there is a stone stele with a dragon head and turtle base erected in the 19th year of Jiajing, Ming (1540); the front face is carved with 'Thatched Cottage,' legendarily written by Tang Yin of the Ming. The back face is carved with the three characters 'Place Where the Dragon Rests.'

269. 野云庵/卧龙深处

Yeyun Nunnery / Wolong Deep Place
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区古隆中景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
隆中胜景中最高处为后人按想象所建诸葛亮交友聚会之卧室重建于清雍正七年乾隆时卧龙深处改为野云庵有两进院落
中文 Chinese

'卧龙深处'又名'隆中草庐''野云庵'，在草庐北百米处半山腰，也是隆中胜景中最高处，为后人按想象所建诸葛亮交友聚会之卧室，重建于清雍正七年（1729），乾隆时'卧龙深处'改为'野云庵'。现有两进院落，有前堂、正房及厢房。

前堂、正房均面阔三间，进深三间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶。

English 英文

'Wolong Deep Place' is also called 'Longzhong Thatched Cottage' and 'Yeyun Nunnery'; it is on the mountainside a hundred meters north of the thatched cottage, and is also the highest point among the scenic spots of Longzhong; it is a bedroom built by later generations according to imagination for Zhuge Liang to make friends and gather, rebuilt in the 7th year of Yongzheng, Qing (1729), and during Qianlong 'Wolong Deep Place' was changed to 'Yeyun Nunnery.' Now there are two courtyards, with a front hall, main rooms, and wing rooms. The front hall and main rooms are all three bays wide and three bays deep, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs.

270. 襄阳城墙

City Wall of Xiangyang
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明代
地址 Address
汉水南岸，襄阳市滨江大道与襄阳北街交汇处
类型 Type
古城墙·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
城墙整体格局瓮城形制始建于汉宋代改为砖城明洪武初年于旧址重筑新城周长7311米高10.84米我国南方古城池中最大的护城河
中文 Chinese

襄阳城位于汉水南岸，三面环水，一面靠山，是一座山清水秀、景色宜人的古城。古时由于地处水陆要冲，交通方便，春秋时便设楚国之北津戍，东汉末为荆州牧治所，是历代兵家必争之地。襄阳城墙始建于汉，原为土城，宋代改为砖城，并筑瓮城。

屡遭破坏，至元末，城垣已大部被毁。明洪武初年于旧址重筑新城，洪武、正德、嘉靖、隆庆和清顺治以后各代均有重修、扩建。现存的襄阳城墙仍可体现明初旧制，是我国保存较为完好的明代城墙。

城墙平面近方形，周长7311米，高10.84米，宽11—14米，周长7322米，北以汉水为濠，东、西、南有宽约180—250米、深约4—8米的护城河，河与北边的汉水相接。

形成我国南方古城池中最大的护城河。古城城墙每座城门设有瓮城或子城，城四隅设有角台，城墙沿线分设敌台或烽火台，城垣上设垛堞4210个，炮台29个。城墙四周原有'阳春''文昌''西成''拱宸''震华''临汉'六座城门，现存临汉门城楼、拱宸门瓮城。

现存城墙以北城垣最完整，清代重修的临汉门城楼仍矗立城头，重檐九脊，北临汉水，南望岘山。

English 英文

Xiangyang City is located on the south bank of the Han River, surrounded by water on three sides and backed by mountains on one side; it is an ancient city with beautiful mountains and clear waters and pleasant scenery. In ancient times, because it was located at the strategic point of land and water transportation with convenient交通, in the Spring and Autumn period the northern garrison of Chu State was established here, and at the end of the Eastern Han it was the seat of the Governor of Jingzhou; it was a place contested by military forces throughout the dynasties. The Xiangyang City Wall was first built in the Han, originally an earthen city; in the Song it was changed to a brick city, and an urn city was built. It was repeatedly damaged, and by the end of the Yuan, most of the city wall had been destroyed. In the early Hongwu period of the Ming, a new city was rebuilt on the old site; during Hongwu, Zhengde, Jiajing, Longqing, and after Shunzhi of the Qing, successive dynasties all repaired and expanded it. The existing Xiangyang City Wall can still reflect the old system of the early Ming, and is a relatively well-preserved Ming city wall in China. The city wall plane is nearly square, with a perimeter of 7311 meters, a height of 10.84 meters, and a width of 11–14 meters; the perimeter is 7322 meters, with the Han River as the moat to the north, and a moat about 180–250 meters wide and 4–8 meters deep to the east, west, and south; the river connects with the Han River to the north, forming the largest moat among ancient cities in southern China. Each gate of the ancient city wall is equipped with an urn city or sub-city; at the four corners of the city there are corner platforms; along the city wall there are enemy platforms or beacon towers; on the city wall there are 4210 crenellations and 29 artillery platforms. Around the city wall there were originally six city gates: 'Yangchun,' 'Wenchang,' 'Xicheng,' 'Gongchen,' 'Zhenhua,' and 'Linhan'; now the Linhan Gate tower and Gongchen Gate urn city remain. The existing city wall is most complete on the north side; the Linhan Gate tower, rebuilt in the Qing, still stands on the city head, with double eaves and nine ridges, facing the Han River to the north and looking toward Xian Mountain to the south.

Linhan Gate tower, also called Small North Gate tower. 274. 夫人城

Furen City (Lady's City)
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
东晋、明代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区襄阳城西北角
类型 Type
古城墙·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
城西北角筑有子城夫人城为东晋太元三年筑梁州刺史朱序的母亲韩夫人率众所筑明代初年及以后多次扩建平面呈长方形稍向外突出东与襄阳城墙相连墙上嵌石匾镌夫人城三字
中文 Chinese

城西北角筑有子城'夫人城'，为东晋太元三年（378）中郎将、梁州刺史朱序的母亲韩夫人率众所筑，明代初年及以后多次扩建。平面呈长方形，稍向外突出，东与襄阳城墙相连。

南、西、北墙分别长21.7米、29.2米、19.2米，高约11米，厚约18米，内以土夯筑，外砌大城。北墙上嵌石匾，镌'夫人城'三字，下嵌碑数通，刻有'襄郡益民胜迹夫人城为最'等字样。

English 英文

At the northwest corner of the city, a sub-city 'Furen City' (Lady's City) was built; it was built in the 3rd year of Taiyuan, Eastern Jin (378), led by Lady Han, the mother of Zhu Xu, General of the Household and Inspector of Liangzhou, and was expanded many times in the early Ming and thereafter. The plane is rectangular, slightly protruding outward, and connected to the Xiangyang City Wall on the east. The south, west, and north walls are respectively 21.7 meters, 29.2 meters, and 19.2 meters long, about 11 meters high and about 18 meters thick; the interior is rammed with earth, and the exterior is built with large bricks. On the north wall is embedded a stone plaque engraved with the three characters 'Furen City'; below it are embedded several steles, engraved with words such as 'Among the scenic spots benefiting the people of Xiangyang Commandery, Furen City is the foremost.'

Zhongxuan Tower

类型 Type
纪念建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
为纪念东汉末年著名才子王粲在襄阳作登楼赋所建明代王世贞曾作仲宣楼记王粲字仲宣建安七子之一
中文 Chinese

仲宣楼在襄阳城内东南角，为纪念东汉末年著名才子王粲在襄阳作《登楼赋》所建。明代王世贞曾作《仲宣楼记》。王粲（177—217），字仲宣，山阳高平（今山东邹县）人，'建安七子'之一，以博闻多识、文思敏捷著称。

建安十三年（208），王粲随曹操南下，寓居襄阳多年，在此写下著名的《登楼赋》，抒发思乡之情和建功立业之志。仲宣楼即为纪念他而建，历代屡有兴废，现存建筑为当代重建。

English 英文

Zhongxuan Tower is at the southeast corner inside Xiangyang City, built to commemorate Wang Can, a famous talented scholar at the end of the Eastern Han, who wrote the 'Rhapsody on Climbing a Tower' in Xiangyang. In the Ming, Wang Shizhen once wrote 'Record of Zhongxuan Tower.' Wang Can (177–217), courtesy name Zhongxuan, was a native of Gaoping, Shanyang (present-day Zou County, Shandong), one of the 'Seven Scholars of Jian'an,' known for his extensive knowledge and quick literary mind. In the 13th year of Jian'an (208), Wang Can followed Cao Cao southward and lived in Xiangyang for many years, where he wrote the famous 'Rhapsody on Climbing a Tower,' expressing his longing for his hometown and his ambition to achieve merit and establish a career. Zhongxuan Tower was built to commemorate him; it experienced repeated rises and falls throughout the dynasties, and the existing building was rebuilt in contemporary times.

276. 襄阳王府绿影壁

Green Screen Wall of Prince Xiang's Mansion
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄城区曲径巷8号
类型 Type
居住建筑·仿木结构
看点 Highlights
石雕我国现存四大影壁之一因全用青绿色石料雕刻砌筑而成故名明正统五年始建襄王府坐北朝南明末被张献忠焚毁仅存照壁长26.2米厚1.6米高7.6米
中文 Chinese

襄阳王府绿影壁位于今襄樊襄城区南街，也是襄王府遗址所在。

据相关文献记载，襄王府坐北朝南，由第一代襄宪王朱瞻墡始建于明正统五年（1440）前后，先后历八代九王，至明末农民起义军领袖李自成占领王府后，曾在此称帝，改襄阳为襄京，建立'大顺'政权，之后不久，王府被张献忠率农民起义军焚毁，仅存照壁，即今天所见的绿影壁。

绿影壁是我国现存四大影壁之一，因全用青绿色石料雕刻砌筑而成，故名。影壁坐北朝南，为四柱三间仿木结构石壁，长26.2米，厚1.6米，高7.6米，须弥座，庑殿瓦顶。绿矾石壁心，汉白玉石镶边。

其壁顶、柱枋、框架、须弥座用榫卯相接。影壁明间略高于左右次间，明间壁心高浮雕巨幅'二龙戏珠'图，左右次间壁心各浮雕巨龙腾云图。四周边框雕姿态各异的小龙99条。两面山壁心分别雕刻山水、卷云图案，柱、枋及瓦当施龙纹浮雕。

其纹饰精美，神态动人，雕刻技巧融圆、浮、平雕于一体，粗犷豪放，浑厚古朴，具有较高的艺术价值。

English 英文

The Green Screen Wall of Prince Xiang's Mansion is located on South Street, Xiangcheng District, present-day Xiangfan, and is also the site of the former Prince Xiang's Mansion. According to relevant documents, Prince Xiang's Mansion faced south and was first built around the 5th year of Zhengtong, Ming (1440), by the first Prince Xiangxian Zhu Zhanshan; it successively went through eight generations and nine princes; by the end of the Ming, after Li Zicheng, leader of the peasant uprising army, occupied the mansion, he once proclaimed himself emperor here, changed Xiangyang to Xiangjing, and established the 'Dashun' regime; shortly thereafter, the mansion was burned down by Zhang Xianzhong leading the peasant uprising army, leaving only the screen wall, i.e., the Green Screen Wall seen today. The Green Screen Wall is one of the four existing great screen walls in China; it is named because it is entirely carved and built with blue-green stone materials. The screen wall faces south, and is a four-column three-bay stone wall imitating wood structure, 26.2 meters long, 1.6 meters thick, and 7.6 meters high, with a sumeru base and a hip-and-gable tile roof. The wall heart is of green vitriol stone, edged with white marble. Its wall top, columns and lintels, frame, and sumeru base are connected by mortise and tenon. The central bay of the screen wall is slightly higher than the left and right secondary bays; the wall heart of the central bay has a high-relief giant 'Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl' picture, and the wall hearts of the left and right secondary bays each have a relief of a giant dragon soaring in clouds. The surrounding frame is carved with 99 small dragons in various postures. The two gable wall hearts are respectively carved with landscape and scrolling cloud patterns; the columns, lintels, and tile ends are applied with dragon-pattern reliefs. Its ornamentation is exquisite, with touching expressions; the carving technique integrates round, relief, and flat carving into one, rough and bold, vigorous and simple, with relatively high artistic value.

277. 广德寺多宝塔

Duobao Pagoda in Guangde Temple
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄阳城西13公里处
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
石佛石雕艺术塔之形态广德寺原名云居寺始建于唐代贞观年间鄂西著名的古刹寺院三面环山一面可远眺汉水明成化年间由隆中迁此多宝佛塔保存完好
中文 Chinese

多宝佛塔所在的广德寺原名云居寺，始建于唐代贞观年间，是鄂西著名的古刹。寺院三面环山，一面可远眺汉水，是一处'地接隆中鹫岭千峰云叠嶂，塔悬江汉虎溪一派水环流'的幽美佳境。寺内古木参天，殿宇林立，气势宏伟壮丽，被誉为'历朝之胜迹，襄阳一大观'。

该寺现位于襄阳城西约13公里处，隆中东麓，是湖北佛教历史上著名的十方丛林，始建于唐贞观年间，明成化年间由隆中迁此，因宪宗御笔亲赐'广德禅林'，改名广德寺，明末时遭兵燹，仅多宝佛塔保存完好。清康熙、乾隆、嘉庆、道光、咸丰各代均有重修。

广德寺坐北朝南，南北长约250米、东西宽约180米，原有规模较大，共有房屋127间，占地面积约4.5万平方米。格局方正，有整齐的护寺河，除东山门外，别处无法进入寺院。

寺院中轴对称布局，现存山门、藏经阁、方丈室、东西客堂及多宝佛塔等，1992年维修并重修山门、天王殿。藏经楼面阔、进深三间；方丈室、知客堂各为一小三合院，主室面阔、进深三间，左、右厢房均面阔、进深一间；

东、西客堂均面阔三间、进深三间。建筑均单檐硬山灰瓦顶，穿斗或抬梁式构架，前壁设隔扇，有檐廊。寺外残存部分护寺壕沟，残宽1米、深1米—2.5米左右。寺内古木参天，寺外碧水环绕，环境优雅宜人。

寺中有古银杏树一株，周长4人合抱，高约35米。明嘉靖皇帝赐以'大将军'封号，清朝康熙皇帝赐封为'护法尊'，后清乾隆皇帝又加封为'感应大将军'，在树旁有碑刻记其事，古银杏树千年不衰，枝叶茂盛。

English 英文

The Guangde Temple where the Duobao (Many Treasures) Buddha Pagoda is located was originally called Yunju Temple, first built during the Zhenguan period of the Tang, and is a famous ancient temple in western Hubei. The temple is surrounded by mountains on three sides, with one side offering a distant view of the Han River; it is a beautiful and serene place described as 'the land connects Longzhong, with eagle ridges and a thousand peaks of clouds piled up; the tower hangs over Jianghan, with tiger stream and a school of water circulating.' Inside the temple, ancient trees tower to the sky, halls and pavilions stand in rows, with a magnificent and grand momentum, praised as 'a scenic spot of successive dynasties, a grand sight of Xiangyang.' The temple is now located about 13 km west of Xiangyang City, at the eastern foot of Longzhong; it is a famous ten-direction Buddhist monastery in the Buddhist history of Hubei, first built during the Zhenguan period of the Tang, moved here from Longzhong during the Chenghua period of the Ming, and because Emperor Xianzong personally bestowed the imperial writing 'Guangde Chanlin' (Guangde Buddhist Grove), it was renamed Guangde Temple; at the end of the Ming it suffered from war, and only the Duobao Buddha Pagoda was preserved intact. During the Kangxi, Qianlong, Jiaqing, Daoguang, and Xianfeng periods of the Qing, it was repaired in each generation. Guangde Temple faces south, about 250 meters long from north to south and about 180 meters wide from east to west; it originally had a relatively large scale, with a total of 127 rooms and an area of about 45,000 square meters. The layout is square, with a neat temple-protecting river; except for the East Mountain Gate, there is no other way to enter the temple. The temple has a centrally symmetric layout; the existing buildings include the mountain gate, scripture library, abbot's room, east and west guest halls, and the Duobao Buddha Pagoda, etc.; in 1992 it was maintained and the mountain gate and Heavenly King Hall were rebuilt. The scripture library is three bays wide and three bays deep; the abbot's room and guest reception room are each a small three-sided courtyard, with the main room three bays wide and three bays deep, and the left and right wing rooms each one bay wide and one bay deep; the east and west guest halls are each three bays wide and three bays deep. The buildings all have single-eave gable gray-tile roofs, with column-and-tie or post-and-lintel frames; the front walls are fitted with lattice doors and windows, with eaves porches. Outside the temple, part of the temple-protecting ditch remains, with a remaining width of about 1 meter and a depth of about 1–2.5 meters. Inside the temple, ancient trees tower to the sky; outside the temple, blue water surrounds it, with an elegant and pleasant environment. In the temple there is an ancient ginkgo tree, with a circumference requiring four people to embrace, and a height of about 35 meters. Emperor Jiajing of the Ming bestowed on it the title 'Great General'; Emperor Kangxi of the Qing bestowed on it the title 'Dharma-Protecting Venerable'; later Emperor Qianlong of the Qing additionally bestowed on it the title 'Inductive Great General'; beside the tree there is a stele inscription recording this matter; the ancient ginkgo tree has not declined for a thousand years, with lush branches and leaves.

278. 习家池

Xi Family's Private Garden
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清
地址 Address
襄阳城南约五公里的凤凰山（又名白马山）南麓
类型 Type
园林建筑
看点 Highlights
选址环境一处集宅邸和花园于一体的园林始建于东汉建武元年至三十二年为我国现存最早的私家园林东汉建武元年襄阳侯习郁在岘南山麓修建宅院习郁晚年还居襄阳对习家池进行了大规模扩建与修缮唐代名人孟浩然、皮日休、李白、杜甫等曾神游习家池
中文 Chinese

习家池位于襄樊市城南岘山南麓，是一处集宅邸和花园于一体的园林。始建于东汉建武元年至三十二年（25—56），为我国现存最早的私家园林。

东汉建武元年，襄阳侯习郁在岘南山麓修建宅院，至三十二年，习郁效仿春秋末越国大夫范蠡养鱼法，在侧院内开凿长60步，宽40步的池塘，引入白马泉水，并在池中建钓鱼台，台上筑亭阁，'虹梁飞架，云堤高扶'，池水净洁如镜，水质甘甜，时为名仕的襄阳侯习郁将其命名为'习家池'。

西晋永嘉五年至建兴四年（311—316），'竹林七贤'之一山涛之子——镇南将军山简镇守襄阳，其号高阳酒徒，常在习家池游玩饮酒，乐而忘返，不醉不归，因而习家池当时又称'高阳池馆'。唐代孟浩然感叹：'当昔襄阳雄盛时，山公常醉习家池。

'皮日休也曾言：'竹屏风下登山屐，十宿高阳忘却回。'东晋时期，习郁后裔著名史学家习凿齿在习家池读书立著，撰有《汉晋春秋》。习凿齿晚年还居襄阳，对习家池进行了大规模扩建与修缮。从此，习家池名声大振。

唐代名人孟浩然、皮日休、李白、杜甫等曾神游习家池，并留下大量的诗文和墨宝，令其成为全国名胜。唐末，习家池毁于战乱。南宋嘉定元年至宝庆三年（1208—1227），制帅属官尹焕在习家池遗址发现《习池诗》石碑，决定重修习家池，筑堂二十八楹，匾额'习池'；

筑寝舍二十八楹，匾额'怀晋'；堂舍外引泉凿池，水上架桥，周边筑围墙，建高门，匾额'习池馆'。宋元之际，习家池再次遭到毁坏。明正德十二年（1517），荆南兵巡道聂贤见习家池荒废，决定主持修缮，在池上筑坛形石台，周围砌石栏，并修长渠，渠上架桥，石台上建一亭，匾额'凤泉'。

嘉靖初年，习家池建筑残损，水塘荒废。嘉靖二十五年（1546），副使江汇重修方塘，整修亭台，并立杜祠，祭祀习凿齿、杜甫。之后，习家池遭遇兵燹，再次遭到毁坏。

明正德十二年（1517），荆南兵巡道聂贤见习家池荒废，决定主持修缮，在池上筑坛形石台，周围砌石栏，并修长渠，渠上架桥，石台上建一亭，匾额'凤泉'。嘉靖初年，习家池建筑残损，水塘荒废。嘉靖二十五年（1546），副使江汇重修方塘，整修亭台，并立杜祠，祭祀习凿齿、杜甫。

之后，习家池遭遇兵燹，再次遭到毁坏。清康熙七年（1668），总戎杨来嘉对习家池进行重建，亭台耸峙，楼榭参差，桃柳亚塘，芙蓉蔽水，重现了昔日园林美景。乾隆年间，习家池水淹没，仅存半池。乾隆五十八年（1793），守道王公奉再度修缮池馆及祠庙，供奉释迦、习郁、山简。

道光六年（1826），太守周凯游于池上，见习家池残破不堪，仅剩古屋三间，且已半废，他对习家池进行修缮和扩建，用作灌溉民田的蓄水池，在池东、西设二石流，以控制启闭。修建后的水池面积为3亩，'深七尺'，在池上建有亭子和石桥，修葺亭台榭馆；

同时将高阳池馆改为刁氏四贤祠，祠内供奉习郁、习珍、习凿齿和山简。同治五年（1866），习家池再次重建。

English 英文

Xi Family's Private Garden is located at the southern foot of Xian Mountain south of Xiangfan City; it is a garden integrating a residence and a garden. It was first built from the 1st to the 32nd year of Jianwu, Eastern Han (25–56), and is the earliest existing private garden in China. In the 1st year of Jianwu, Eastern Han, Xi Yu, Marquis of Xiangyang, built a residence at the southern foot of Xian Mountain; by the 32nd year, Xi Yu, imitating the fish-farming method of Fan Li, a grandee of Yue State at the end of the Spring and Autumn period, dug a pond 60 paces long and 40 paces wide in the side courtyard, introduced White Horse Spring water, and built a fishing platform in the pond, with pavilions and towers on the platform, 'rainbow beams flying across, cloud embankments high supporting'; the pond water was as clean as a mirror, with sweet water quality, and Xi Yu, Marquis of Xiangyang, who was then a famous scholar, named it 'Xi Family's Pond.' From the 5th year of Yongjia to the 4th year of Jianxing, Western Jin (311–316), Shan Jian, son of Shan Tao — one of the 'Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove' — and General Who Guards the South, guarded Xiangyang; his hao was Gaoyang Wine Drinker, and he often played and drank at Xi Family's Pond, enjoying himself so much that he forgot to return, not leaving until drunk; hence Xi Family's Pond was also called 'Gaoyang Pond Lodge' at that time. In the Tang, Meng Haoran sighed: 'In the past when Xiangyang was prosperous and powerful, Lord Shan often got drunk at Xi Family's Pond.' Pi Rixiu also said: 'Under the bamboo screen wind, mountain-climbing clogs; ten nights at Gaoyang, forgetting to return.' During the Eastern Jin, Xi Zaochi, a famous historian and descendant of Xi Yu, studied and wrote at Xi Family's Pond, authoring 'Chronicles of Han and Jin.' In his later years, Xi Zaochi returned to live in Xiangyang and carried out large-scale expansion and repair of Xi Family's Pond. From then on, Xi Family's Pond became greatly famous. In the Tang, famous figures such as Meng Haoran, Pi Rixiu, Li Bai, and Du Fu once visited Xi Family's Pond and left a large amount of poetry, prose, and calligraphy treasures, making it a national scenic spot. At the end of the Tang, Xi Family's Pond was destroyed by war. From the 1st year of Jiading to the 3rd year of Baoqing, Southern Song (1208–1227), Yin Huan, a subordinate official of the military commander, discovered the 'Xi Pond Poetry' stone stele at the site of Xi Family's Pond and decided to rebuild Xi Family's Pond, building 28 bays of halls with the plaque 'Xi Pond'; building 28 bays of bedrooms with the plaque 'Huai Jin' (Cherishing Jin); outside the halls and bedrooms, introducing springs and digging ponds, building bridges over the water, surrounding with walls, building a high gate with the plaque 'Xi Pond Lodge.' Between Song and Yuan, Xi Family's Pond was destroyed again. In the 12th year of Zhengde, Ming (1517), Nie Xian, Patrol Inspector of Southern Jing, saw Xi Family's Pond abandoned and decided to preside over its repair, building an altar-shaped stone platform on the pond, surrounding it with stone railings, and building a long canal with a bridge over it, and a pavilion on the stone platform with the plaque 'Fengquan' (Phoenix Spring). In the early Jiajing period, the buildings of Xi Family's Pond were damaged and the pond was abandoned. In the 25th year of Jiajing (1546), Vice Commissioner Jiang Hui rebuilt the square pond, repaired the pavilions and terraces, and established the Du Shrine to worship Xi Zaochi and Du Fu. Thereafter, Xi Family's Pond suffered from war and was destroyed again. In the 7th year of Kangxi, Qing (1668), Military Commander Yang Laijia rebuilt Xi Family's Pond, with pavilions and terraces towering, towers and pavilions irregular, peach and willow trees by the pond, hibiscus covering the water, reproducing the former garden beauty. During the Qianlong period, Xi Family's Pond was submerged, leaving only half a pond. In the 58th year of Qianlong (1793), Circuit Intendant Wang Gongfeng again repaired the pond lodge and shrines, enshrining Sakyamuni, Xi Yu, and Shan Jian. In the 6th year of Daoguang (1826), Prefect Zhou Kai toured by the pond and saw Xi Family's Pond in ruins, with only three old rooms remaining and already half abandoned; he repaired and expanded Xi Family's Pond, using it as a reservoir for irrigating civilian fields, setting two stone sluices at the east and west of the pond to control opening and closing. After construction, the pond area was 3 mu, 'seven chi deep'; pavilions and stone bridges were built on the pond, and pavilions, terraces, and lodges were repaired; at the same time, the Gaoyang Pond Lodge was changed to the Diao Family Four Sages Shrine, enshrining Xi Yu, Xi Zhen, Xi Zaochi, and Shan Jian. In the 5th year of Tongzhi (1866), Xi Family's Pond was rebuilt again.

The Jianzhu Pond is 7.45 meters long and 8.75 meters wide, with an octagonal plane, and spring water gushes inside the pond; the Bangui Pond has a semicircular plane with a diameter of 13.9 meters, in a simple and ancient form.

Xi Pond has an area of about 1700 square meters, with the longest east-west dimension of about 90 meters and the widest north-south dimension of about 58 meters, with a water depth of 2 meters. The pond is built with rough stones, and lotus flowers and fish are raised inside the pond.

中文 Chinese

习家池原有大量的碑刻和题记，因年代久远，大部分已散失，现仅存《重建高阳池馆碑记》石碑和《修习家池》石碑。《重建高阳池馆碑记》碑刻于康熙七年（1668）。青石质，方座。高1.68米、宽0.57米、厚0.18米。

碑文楷书12行，满行25字，记重建习家池事。另从周边搜集4通石碑，或记修缮、重记修缮、重建习家池事，或记维护习家池周边环境事。

Xi Family's Pond originally had a large number of stele carvings and inscriptions; due to the long age, most have been scattered and lost; now only the 'Record of the Reconstruction of Gaoyang Pond Lodge' stone stele and the 'Repair of Xi Family's Pond' stone stele remain. The 'Record of the Reconstruction of Gaoyang Pond Lodge' stele was carved in the 7th year of Kangxi (1668). It is of bluestone quality, with a square base. It is 1.68 meters high, 0.57 meters wide, and 0.18 meters thick. The stele inscription is in regular script, 12 lines, with 25 characters per full line, recording the reconstruction of Xi Family's Pond. In addition, 4 stone steles were collected from the surrounding area, either recording repairs, re-recording repairs and reconstruction of Xi Family's Pond, or recording the maintenance of the environment around Xi Family's Pond.

中文 Chinese

English 英文

Xiangyang Watchtower is located at No.102 South Street, Xiangcheng District; it was first built during the Chenghua period of the Ming; during the Jiajing period, a copper clepsydra was installed inside, and it was reinstalled during Wanli, hence also called 'Clepsydra Platform.' It was destroyed at the end of the Ming, rebuilt in the 5th year of Yongzheng, Qing (1727), and majorly repaired in the 3rd year of Guangxu (1877) and the 13th year of the Republic (1924). The tower body faces east from west, located on a brick-stone platform base 40 meters long, 16 meters wide, and 5.4 meters high. It is five bays wide, 18.9 meters, and three bays deep, 10.56 meters. It has a double-eave hip gray-tile roof, a post-and-lintel frame, and lattice doors and windows on the front and rear walls.

建筑形制建筑形制始建于唐代明洪武元年、清顺治十三年、乾隆十七年重修现仅存大殿面阔五间21.2米进深三间8.7米单檐歇山灰瓦顶两山穿斗式构架中部抬梁式构架
中文 Chinese

铁佛寺大殿位于襄城区檀溪路襄樊职业技术学院内，始建于唐代，明洪武元年（1368）、清顺治十三年（1656）乾隆十七年（1752）重修。现仅存大殿，面阔五间21.2米，进深三间8.7米。

English 英文

The Main Hall of Tiefo Temple is located inside Xiangfan Vocational and Technical College on Tanxi Road, Xiangcheng District; it was first built in the Tang, and repaired in the 1st year of Hongwu, Ming (1368), the 13th year of Shunzhi, Qing (1656), and the 17th year of Qianlong (1752). Now only the main hall remains, five bays wide, 21.2 meters, and three bays deep, 8.7 meters. It has a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, is a nanmu wood building, with column-and-tie frames on the two gable sides and a post-and-lintel frame in the middle. The front wall is fitted with lattice doors and windows, and the other three sides are enclosed by brick walls.

286. 襄樊码头

Xiangfan Dock
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty

中文 Chinese

襄樊码头均位于汉江汉阳、樊城古城段，大多为直立式码头，下部有石坪台，有的上部为斜坡、台阶式码头，沿江堤有石驳岸，上堤进城有石台阶。这些码头多为客货两用码头。岸线长者400余米，短者仅10余米，宽窄不一，在3—30米之间；

泊位多少不一，但最多不超过10个，停泊吨位均为300吨以下。有的驳岸条石上钻孔栓系锚绳。现均因汉江崔家营大坝蓄水被淹没。

现存码头分为18个，包括公馆门码头、罗家码头、檀溪码头、梯子口码头、官码头、火星观码头、千福码头、大码头、龙子口码头、中州码头、公馆门码头、回龙寺码头、兴武街、小北门码头、官厅码头、铁庄码头、大北门码头等。

English 英文

Xiangfan Docks are all located in the Hanyang and Fancheng ancient city sections of the Han River; most are vertical docks, with stone platform bases at the lower part, and some have sloped or stepped docks at the upper part; along the river embankment there are stone revetments, and stone steps lead up the embankment into the city. These docks are mostly passenger-cargo dual-use docks. The longer shorelines are more than 400 meters, the shorter ones only more than 10 meters, with varying widths between 3 and 30 meters; the number of berths varies, but no more than 10 at most, and the停泊 tonnage is all below 300 tons. Some revetment strip stones have drilled holes for tying anchor ropes. Now they are all submerged due to the impoundment of the Cuijiaying Dam on the Han River. The existing docks are divided into 18, including Gongguan Gate Dock, Luo Family Dock, Tanxi Dock, Tizikou Dock, Official Dock, Huoxingguan Dock, Qianfu Dock, Great Dock, Longzikou Dock, Zhongzhou Dock, Gongguan Gate Dock, Huilong Temple Dock, Xingwu Street, Small North Gate Dock, Guanting Dock, Tiezhuang Dock, Great North Gate Dock, etc.

中文 Chinese

公馆门码头，据记载建于道光二十五年（1845），现位于樊城区米公街道办事处友谊街社区沿江大道与朝阳路交叉口南端，处汉江北岸。该码头为直立式码头，上有梯形磴礓18级，下为曲尺形坪台，长16米、宽7.25米。

台东西各有两组磴礓，至台下面形成一等腰梯形驳岸。驳岸正中嵌石匾，阴刻楷书'民不能忘'四字。

English 英文

Gongguan Gate Dock, according to records, was built in the 25th year of Daoguang (1845); it is now located at the south end of the intersection of Yanjiang Avenue and Chaoyang Road, Youyi Street Community, Migong Subdistrict Office, Fancheng District, on the north bank of the Han River. This dock is a vertical dock, with 18 trapezoidal steps at the top and a carpenter's-square-shaped platform at the bottom, 16 meters long and 7.25 meters wide. On the east and west of the platform there are two groups of steps each, forming an isosceles trapezoidal revetment below the platform. In the middle of the revetment is embedded a stone plaque, incised in regular script with the four characters 'The People Cannot Forget.'

中文 Chinese

大北门码头位于襄城区昭明街道办事处荆州北街社区大北门北端，处汉江南岸。该码头主要为过人码头，坪台长100米、宽30米，有泊位2个。

现在直立式伸出的条石上仍可见到停船时栓系缆绳的孔洞，直径约10厘米，大部分孔洞的外部被拉断。大北门瓮城东北角立石碑1通，青石质，抹角，高1.45米、宽0.52米、厚0.13米，表面剥蚀较严重。

English 英文

Great North Gate Dock is located at the north end of Great North Gate, Jingzhou North Street Community, Zhaoming Subdistrict Office, Xiangcheng District, on the south bank of the Han River. This dock is mainly a pedestrian dock, with a platform 100 meters long and 30 meters wide, with 2 berths. Now on the vertically protruding strip stones, holes for tying mooring ropes when stopping boats can still be seen, about 10 cm in diameter, and the exterior of most holes has been pulled off. At the northeast corner of the Great North Gate urn city stands one stone stele, of bluestone quality, with chamfered corners, 1.45 meters high, 0.52 meters wide, and 0.13 meters thick, with severe surface erosion. The stele inscription is in incised script, divided into upper and lower parts; the upper part is horizontally written 'Xiangfan Ferry Regulations,' 5 lines, with 6 characters per full line, recording the maximum limit for people and loading boats; the lower part is written on the right 'Matters Needing Attention,' 6 lines, with 11 characters per full line, the content unclear.

289. 襄阳学宫大成殿

Dacheng Hall of Xiangyang Government-run School
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄城区积仓街襄阳五中实验中学内
类型 Type
教育建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
平面格局建筑形制始建年代不详唐代时位于城外北宋庆历五年迁至城内明代五次重修崇祯末年毁于战火清顺治年间、康熙十二年重建后不断扩修现仅存大成殿建于道光二年面阔五间17.8米
中文 Chinese

襄阳学宫大成殿位于襄城区积仓街中段北侧，襄阳五中实验中学内。始建年代不详，唐代时位于城外，北宋庆历五年（1045）迁至城内，明代五次重修，崇祯末年毁于战火。清顺治年间、康熙十二年（1673）重建，后不断扩修。

现仅存大成殿，建于道光二年（1822）。面阔五间17.8米，进深三间11米。重檐歇山琉璃瓦顶，中部抬梁式构架，两山穿斗式构架。前壁设隔扇，有檐廊。

殿坐落于月台上，月台正面铺二龙戏珠石雕板，是生员们拜孔子的地方。殿前方约80米处有泮池，呈半圆形，上架一小拱桥，俗称'状元桥'。

English 英文

The Dacheng Hall of Xiangyang Government-run School is located on the north side of the middle section of Jicang Street, Xiangcheng District, inside Xiangyang No.5 Middle School Experimental Middle School. The initial construction date is unknown; in the Tang it was located outside the city, and in the 5th year of Qingli, Northern Song (1045) it was moved inside the city; it was repaired five times in the Ming, and destroyed by war at the end of Chongzhen. It was rebuilt during the Shunzhi period of the Qing and in the 12th year of Kangxi (1673), and continuously expanded and repaired thereafter. Now only the Dacheng Hall remains, built in the 2nd year of Daoguang (1822). It is five bays wide, 17.8 meters, and three bays deep, 11 meters. It has a double-eave hip-and-gable glazed tile roof, with a post-and-lintel frame in the middle and column-and-tie frames on the two gable sides. The front wall is fitted with lattice doors and windows, with an eaves porch. The hall is located on a platform; the front of the platform is paved with a stone carving board of two dragons playing with a pearl, which is the place where students worshipped Confucius. About 80 meters in front of the hall there is a Pan Pond, semicircular in shape, with a small arch bridge over it, commonly called 'Zhuangyuan Bridge' (Top Scholar Bridge).

290. 米公祠

Mi's Memorial Hall
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
襄阳市樊城区沿江大道2号
类型 Type
纪念建筑
看点 Highlights
匾额石刻又名米家庵是纪念北宋著名书法家米芾的祠堂现存清代重修的拜殿、宝晋殿及重修米氏故里、米氏宗谱宗规和摹刻米芾等宋代大书法家的书碑帖45通米芾字元章号鹿门居士襄阳漫士祠始建于元末明代被毁清康熙二十二年重建并摹刻碑碣30余通整个祠堂坐北朝南占地面积约3.2平方米中轴对称布局有三进院落
中文 Chinese

米公祠位于樊城区米公街道办事处沿江大道与米公路交汇处西北，又名米家庵，是纪念北宋著名书法家米芾的祠堂。现存清代重修的拜殿、宝晋殿及重修米氏故里、米氏宗谱宗规和摹刻米芾等宋代大书法家的书碑帖45通。

米芾（1051—1107），字元章，号'鹿门居士''襄阳漫士'，世称'米襄阳'，山西太原人，官至礼部员外郎。祠始建于元末，明代被毁，清康熙二十二年（1683）重建，并摹刻碑碣30余通。

整个祠堂坐北朝南，占地面积约3.2平方米，中轴对称布局，有三进院落。

中轴主题建筑包括拜殿、碑廊、宝晋斋、仰高堂等，建筑中珍藏有米芾及宋四大家的大量墨迹和石刻，拜殿、宝晋斋内悬挂的匾额、楹联琳琅满目，有'颠不可及''妙不得笔''与孟鹿门号两襄阳书传千古，共苏黄蔡称四巨子颠压三人'等题词，是后人对米芾书法及人物性格的高度评价。

中轴两侧为东、西石苑，苑内亭、台、榭、廊高低错落，参差有致，游鱼满塘。廊壁陈列着米芾、苏轼、黄庭坚、蔡襄等书法家的石刻100多块，以及当代著名书法家为米公祠留下的墨迹石刻30多块。

清光绪元年（1875），文渊阁大学士、襄阳人单懋谦为祠堂题写了'米公祠'门额。

English 英文

Mi's Memorial Hall is located northwest of the intersection of Yanjiang Avenue and Migong Road, Migong Subdistrict Office, Fancheng District; it is also called Mi Family Nunnery, and is a memorial hall for Mi Fu, a famous calligrapher of the Northern Song. The existing buildings include the Qing-rebuilt Worship Hall, Baojin Hall, and the rebuilt Mi Family Native Place, Mi Family Genealogy and Clan Rules, as well as 45 carved stone steles and calligraphy copies of great Song calligraphers such as Mi Fu. Mi Fu (1051–1107), courtesy name Yuanzhang, hao 'Lumen Jushi' (Lumen Recluse) and 'Xiangyang Manshi' (Xiangyang Wanderer), commonly called 'Mi Xiangyang,' was a native of Taiyuan, Shanxi, and served as a yuanwailang (vice director) of the Ministry of Rites. The memorial hall was first built at the end of the Yuan, destroyed in the Ming, and rebuilt in the 22nd year of Kangxi, Qing (1683), with more than 30 steles carved and copied. The entire memorial hall faces south, covering an area of about 3.2 square meters, with a centrally symmetric layout and three courtyards. The main buildings on the central axis include the Worship Hall, stele corridors, Baojin Studio, and Yanggao Hall, etc.; the buildings珍藏 a large number of ink traces and stone carvings of Mi Fu and the Four Great Calligraphers of the Song; the plaques and couplets hanging in the Worship Hall and Baojin Studio are dazzling, with inscriptions such as 'Dian (Eccentric) Unattainable,' 'Wonderful Beyond the Brush,' and 'Together with Meng Lumen, called Two Xiangyangs, calligraphy passed down through a thousand years; together with Su, Huang, and Cai, called Four Giants, eccentricity overwhelms the Three,' which are high evaluations by later generations of Mi Fu's calligraphy and character. On both sides of the central axis are the East and West Stone Gardens; in the gardens, pavilions, terraces, open pavilions, and corridors are scattered at different heights, well-proportioned, with fish filling the ponds. On the corridor walls are displayed more than 100 stone carvings by calligraphers such as Mi Fu, Su Shi, Huang Tingjian, and Cai Xiang, as well as more than 30 ink-trace stone carvings left by contemporary famous calligraphers for Mi's Memorial Hall. In the 1st year of Guangxu, Qing (1875), Shan Maoqian, a Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and a native of Xiangyang, wrote the gate plaque 'Mi's Memorial Hall' for the ancestral hall.

291. 水星台

Shuixing Shrine (Water Star Platform)
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
樊城区水星台街道办事处定中门西200米
类型 Type
市政建筑
看点 Highlights
高台殿内梁架因在城基上筑台建庙祭祀水星而得名始建于东晋明嘉靖十九年重修清雍正十三年题匾水星台乾隆四年至光绪十年又有5次扩建整修水星台实际上是火警瞭望台古时轮流兵役值日巡逻全城的火情樊城的制高点坐北朝南长约30米
中文 Chinese

水星台建于清代，现位于樊城区定中门街道办事处水星台巷北端。因在城基上筑台建庙祭祀水星而得名。始建于东晋，据内保存的乾隆四年（1739）碑记：水星台'晋郭璞建，以镇樊城水灾'。

明嘉靖十九年（1540）重修，清雍正十三年（1735）题匾'水星台'，乾隆四年至光绪十年（1884）又有5次扩建整修。水星台实际上是火警瞭望台，清《樊城街市要图》中展示了水星台的位置与地势，以及城内的防火水系。

古时轮流兵役值日，巡逻全城的火情，见哪里有火警号角声，遂快马加鞭报告官府，兵丁们立刻赶赴火场。扑灭火灾后，樊城的三盛皮坊、聚盛号、何恒丰、曾盛兴记、永茂号、隆生号、王茂记等商户，都要前来慰问道谢。水星台自建成至20世纪70年代一直是樊城的制高点。

抗日战争时期是敌我双方争夺的要地，北墙和北端墙上仍残留许多枪战的痕迹。水星台四合式建筑，坐北朝南，长约30米，宽22.4米。建筑坐落在8米高的砖石围砌夯土台基上，沿台阶而上，大门檐下石匾竖写着'水星台'匾额，额枋饰有莲花、游龙。

台边两侧有两条悬空的龙头螭首，每逢大雨过后，台内积水从龙口喷出，形成一道道彩虹霞光。环顾水星台城墙，西墙中有南宋'宜''邵'和'官'字的文字砖，台之北杂树繁茂，台之东存有瞭望窗、城墙上还留有战争遗留下的弹孔。主体建筑坐北朝南，并排三套院，中轴线上有前殿和后殿。

中院前、后殿为勾连搭式，均面阔三间9.85米，进深三间，分别为8.92米、9.32米，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，两山穿斗式构架，中部抬梁式构架；

东西院分前后厢房，均面阔三间8.22米，进深二间，分别为7.61米、8米，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，两山抬梁式构架，中部穿斗式构架。

前殿面阔三间，进深三间，硬山灰瓦屋面。正面建有牌楼，四柱三间，中部设门，门额嵌石匾，上书'水星台'三字。殿中部为抬梁式木构架、两山穿斗式构架，墙壁上嵌有明、清有关水星台的石雕碑刻数通。

如明嘉靖十九年（1540）所立的'汉江记会'碑刻，汉白玉质，高1.98米，宽1.03米，记重修水星台事；清光绪十年（1884）的'福缘善庆'碑3通，均青石质，楷书碑文；

嘉庆二十一年（1816）题'装塑神像功德铭'碑，青石质，楷书碑文，记载捐款人姓名。文楷文书，文18行980字，记载重修水星台事。殿内供奉救火祖师——真武大帝，明清时人们把它称为'镇火水神'。

后殿硬山式，面阔三间，进深三间，灰瓦屋面，中部抬梁、两山穿斗式构架。厢房连接前、后殿两侧，硬山灰瓦屋顶，面阔三间，进深两间，两山抬梁式、中部穿斗式构架。

English 英文

Shuixing Shrine was built in the Qing, now located at the north end of Shuixingtai Lane, Dingzhong Gate Subdistrict Office, Fancheng District. It is named because a platform was built on the city foundation and a temple was built to worship the Water Star. It was first built in the Eastern Jin; according to the stele record of the 4th year of Qianlong (1739) preserved inside: Shuixing Shrine was 'built by Guo Pu of the Jin to suppress floods in Fancheng.' It was repaired in the 19th year of Jiajing, Ming (1540), and in the 13th year of Yongzheng, Qing (1735) the plaque 'Shuixing Shrine' was inscribed; from the 4th year of Qianlong to the 10th year of Guangxu (1884), there were another 5 expansions and repairs. Shuixing Shrine is actually a fire lookout tower; the Qing 'Key Map of Fancheng Streets and Markets' shows the location and terrain of Shuixing Shrine, as well as the fire-prevention water system inside the city. In ancient times, rotating soldiers were on duty, patrolling the whole city for fire; wherever there was a fire alarm horn sound, they would gallop to report to the authorities, and soldiers would immediately rush to the fire scene. After extinguishing the fire, merchants in Fancheng such as Sansheng Leather Workshop, Jusheng Hao, He Hengfeng, Zeng Shengxing Ji, Yongmao Hao, Longsheng Hao, and Wang Mao Ji would all come to express gratitude. From its completion to the 1970s, Shuixing Shrine was always the highest point in Fancheng. During the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, it was a strategic point contested by both the enemy and ourselves; traces of gunfights still remain on the north wall and the north-end wall. Shuixing Shrine is a courtyard-style building, facing south, about 30 meters long and 22.4 meters wide. The building is located on an 8-meter-high brick-stone-enclosed rammed-earth platform base; going up the steps, under the eaves of the main gate, a stone plaque vertically writes 'Shuixing Shrine,' and the额枋 is decorated with lotus and swimming dragons. On both sides of the platform edge there are two suspended dragon-head chi (hornless dragon) heads; after every heavy rain, the accumulated water inside the platform sprays out from the dragon mouths, forming rainbow-colored rays. Looking around the city wall of Shuixing Shrine, the west wall contains character bricks of 'Yi,' 'Shao,' and 'Guan' from the Southern Song; miscellaneous trees flourish north of the platform; east of the platform there are lookout windows, and bullet holes left by war still remain on the city wall. The main building faces south, with three sets of courtyards side by side; on the central axis there are a front hall and a rear hall. The front and rear halls of the central courtyard are of interlocking-eave style, both three bays wide, 9.85 meters, and three bays deep, respectively 8.92 meters and 9.32 meters, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs, column-and-tie frames on the two gable sides, and post-and-lintel frames in the middle; the east and west courtyards are divided into front and rear wing rooms, both three bays wide, 8.22 meters, and two bays deep, respectively 7.61 meters and 8 meters, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs, post-and-lintel frames on the two gable sides, and column-and-tie frames in the middle. The front hall is three bays wide and three bays deep, with a gable gray-tile roof. On the front there is a paifang, four columns and three bays, with a door in the middle; the door lintel is embedded with a stone plaque, inscribed with the three characters 'Shuixing Shrine.' The middle of the hall has a post-and-lintel wood frame and column-and-tie frames on the two gable sides; several Ming and Qing stone carvings and steles related to Shuixing Shrine are embedded in the walls. For example, the 'Hanjiang Ji Hui' stele erected in the 19th year of Jiajing, Ming (1540), of white marble, 1.98 meters high and 1.03 meters wide, records the repair of Shuixing Shrine; the 3 'Fuyuan Shanqing' (Blessing and Kindness) steles of the 10th year of Guangxu, Qing (1884), all of bluestone, with regular-script inscriptions; the 'Merit Inscription for Installing and Sculpting Divine Statues' stele of the 21st year of Jiaqing (1816), of bluestone, with regular-script inscription, recording the names of donors. The text is in regular script, 18 lines and 980 characters, recording the repair of Shuixing Shrine. Inside the hall is enshrined the Patriarch of Firefighting — Zhenwu Great Emperor; in the Ming and Qing, people called it the 'Fire-Suppressing Water God.' The rear hall is of gable style, three bays wide and three bays deep, with a gray-tile roof, with a post-and-lintel frame in the middle and column-and-tie frames on the two gable sides. The wing rooms connect the front and rear sides of the halls, with gable gray-tile roofs, three bays wide and two bays deep, with post-and-lintel frames on the two gable sides and column-and-tie frames in the middle.

抚州会馆为清代江西临川商贾设在樊城沿江中路陈老巷口的工行帮机构，今位于樊城区中山后街陈老巷口。建筑坐北朝南，占地面积约2000平方米，原先占地面积很大，建筑十分壮观。中轴对称布局，现存有戏楼、正殿及后殿。

The building faces south, covering an area of about 2000 square meters; originally it covered a large area, and the building was very spectacular. With a centrally symmetric layout, the existing buildings include a theater tower, main hall, and rear hall. The theater tower is a two-story wood structure with four columns and five paifangs, built on a base 13.6 meters long and ... wide

293. 樊城山陕会馆、黄州会馆、樊城小江西会馆

Shanxi-Shaanxi, Huangzhou, and Xiao Jiangxi Guild Halls in Fancheng
级别 Level

清代

襄阳市樊城区
类型 Type
商业与手工业建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
樊城三大会馆山陕会馆黄州会馆小江西会馆清代商业建筑会馆建筑
中文 Chinese

樊城作为明清时期汉水流域重要的商业码头，吸引了全国各地的商人在此设立会馆。其中山陕会馆、黄州会馆和小江西会馆是保存较为完整的三座代表性会馆建筑，分别由山西陕西商人、黄州商人和江西商人集资修建，体现了清代樊城商业的繁荣和不同地域商帮的文化特色。

English 英文

As an important commercial dock in the Han River basin during the Ming and Qing, Fancheng attracted merchants from all over the country to establish guild halls here. Among them, the Shanxi-Shaanxi Guild Hall, Huangzhou Guild Hall, and Xiao Jiangxi Guild Hall are three relatively well-preserved representative guild hall buildings, respectively built with funds raised by Shanxi-Shaanxi merchants, Huangzhou merchants, and Jiangxi merchants, reflecting the prosperity of commerce in Fancheng during the Qing and the cultural characteristics of different regional merchant groups.

294. 山陕会馆

Shanxi-Shaanxi Guild Hall in Fancheng
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
樊城区定中门街办瓷器街
类型 Type
商业与手工业建筑·石木结构
看点 Highlights
石雕斗拱又名山陕庙始建于清康熙五十二年由当时在襄樊的山西和陕西籍人士筹资修建乾隆三十九年兴建了祭祀天地水的三官庙嘉庆六年又重修了山门及戏楼增建了花园和荷花池这座神庙与会馆结合的建筑群有阁楼堂室100余间规模之大居樊城会馆之首是樊城曾经作为繁华商埠的历史缩影
中文 Chinese

山陕会馆，又名山陕庙，始建于清康熙五十二年（1713），由当时在襄樊的山西和陕西籍人士筹资修建，乾隆三十九年（1774）兴建了祭祀天、地、水的三官庙，嘉庆六年（1801）又重修了山门及戏楼，增建了花园和荷花池。

这座神庙与会馆结合的建筑群，有阁楼堂室100余间，规模之大，居樊城会馆之首，是樊城曾经作为繁华商埠的历史缩影。

嘉庆六年（1801）、道光年间又有重修、扩修，今位于襄阳樊城区，也是全国山陕会馆中装饰最精美、保存最完好的，是襄阳地区会馆建筑的代表，具有重要的历史价值。

会馆建筑坐西朝东，三进两院，占地面积约4000平方米，中轴对称布局，有石牌楼门楼、戏楼、钟鼓楼、拜殿和正殿；会馆山门外有一对造型生动的石狮，雄狮弄球，雌狮抚幼，相视而望；

石牌楼门仅存左、右八字形照壁，高12米，以绿色琉璃构件镶嵌，绘有人物、花草图案，正中为盘龙翔凤云纹浮雕，通体翠绿，华丽精美，在红墙的衬映下显得富丽堂皇；

进入院内是一宽阔庭院，戏楼已毁，只见钟、鼓亭分立两侧，均建在边长2.2米、高4米的砖砌台基上，台基厚重敦实，古朴典雅，楼台平面为四边形，单檐歇山绿琉璃瓦屋面，檐下施如意斗拱，密密麻麻，层层叠叠，托起上翘的飞檐，显得轻巧灵活；

钟楼均为歇山顶，檐部施如意斗拱，建于边长2.2米、高4米的砖砌台基上；

两殿均面阔三间16.6米，分别进深14.2米、13.4米，单檐硬山琉璃瓦顶，抬梁式构架。正殿抬梁式木构架，殿内檐柱为四角方石柱，其他柱为木柱。

殿内供关公神像，左有关平手捧金印，右有周仓手持青龙偃月大刀，站立其旁，造型生动，高大威武，令人望而生畏，肃穆起敬；

殿内另存《创建铁山庙碑记》《樊镇西庙创建三官殿碑记》《山陕会馆重修山门西乐楼碑序》等石碑，均圭首方座，通高2.2米，宽0.92米，厚0.21米，楷书碑文，17行1000字左右，记捐资重建会馆事，分别刻于康熙五十二年（1713）、乾隆三十九年（1774）、嘉庆六年（1801）。

民国中期，社会动荡，生意萧条，山陕客商不断离樊城返乡，仅有小部分在樊城定居。山陕会馆也就逐渐衰落下来。正殿西南侧原有配殿十余间，内供神态各异的站立彩绘泥塑神像数十尊。可惜的是1951年襄樊市二中扩建时，配殿及其塑像均被拆除。

English 英文

Shanxi-Shaanxi Guild Hall, also called Shanxi-Shaanxi Temple, was first built in the 52nd year of Kangxi, Qing (1713), with funds raised by people of Shanxi and Shaanxi origin then in Xiangfan; in the 39th year of Qianlong (1774), the Sanguan Temple for worshiping Heaven, Earth, and Water was built; in the 6th year of Jiaqing (1801), the mountain gate and theater tower were repaired again, and a garden and lotus pond were added. This building complex combining a temple and a guild hall had more than 100 rooms of attics, towers, halls, and chambers; its scale was the largest among the guild halls in Fancheng, and it is a historical epitome of Fancheng once being a prosperous commercial port. In the 6th year of Jiaqing (1801) and during the Daoguang period, there were further repairs and expansions; today it is located in Fancheng District, Xiangyang, and is also the most exquisitely decorated and best-preserved among the Shanxi-Shaanxi guild halls nationwide; it is a representative of guild hall architecture in the Xiangyang area, with important historical value. The guild hall building faces east from west, with three entries and two courtyards, covering an area of about 4000 square meters, with a centrally symmetric layout, including a stone paifang gate tower, theater tower, bell and drum towers, worship hall, and main hall; outside the mountain gate of the guild hall there is a pair of vividly shaped stone lions, the male lion playing with a ball and the female lion caressing a cub, looking at each other; only the left and right eight-character-shaped screen walls of the stone paifang gate remain, 12 meters high, inlaid with green glazed components, painted with figures, flowers, and plants patterns, with a coiled dragon and soaring phoenix cloud-pattern relief in the center, entirely emerald green, gorgeous and exquisite, appearing magnificent and resplendent against the red walls; entering the courtyard is a wide courtyard; the theater tower has been destroyed, only the bell and drum pavilions stand separately on both sides, both built on brick platform bases with a side length of 2.2 meters and a height of 4 meters; the platform bases are heavy and solid, simple and elegant; the tower plane is quadrilateral, with a single-eave hip-and-gable green glazed tile roof; under the eaves are applied ruyi (as-you-wish) bracket sets, dense and layered, propping up the upturned flying eaves, appearing light and flexible; the bell towers are all hip-and-gable roofs, with ruyi bracket sets on the eaves, built on brick platform bases with a side length of 2.2 meters and a height of 4 meters; both halls are three bays wide, 16.6 meters, with depths of 14.2 meters and 13.4 meters respectively, with single-eave gable glazed tile roofs and post-and-lintel frames. The main hall has a post-and-lintel wood frame; the eave columns inside the hall are four-corner square stone columns, and the other columns are wooden. Inside the hall is enshrined the statue of Guan Gong; on the left, Guan Ping holds a golden seal in both hands; on the right, Zhou Cang holds a Green Dragon Crescent Moon Broadsword, standing beside it, with a vivid shape, tall and mighty, making one feel awe-inspiring and respectful; inside the hall there are also stone steles such as 'Record of the Creation of Tieshan Temple,' 'Record of the Creation of the Three Halls in the West Temple of Fanzhen,' and 'Preface to the Stele of the Rebuilding of the Mountain Gate and West Music Tower of the Shanxi-Shaanxi Guild Hall,' all with圭首 (scepter-head) tops and square bases, with a total height of 2.2 meters, a width of 0.92 meters, and a thickness of 0.21 meters; the inscriptions are in regular script, 17 lines and about 1000 characters, recording the matter of donating funds to rebuild the guild hall, respectively carved in the 52nd year of Kangxi (1713), the 39th year of Qianlong (1774), and the 6th year of Jiaqing (1801). In the mid-Republic period, social turmoil and business depression caused Shanxi-Shaanxi merchants to continuously leave Fancheng and return to their hometowns, with only a small part settling in Fancheng. The Shanxi-Shaanxi Guild Hall thus gradually declined. Southwest of the main hall there were originally more than ten side halls, enshrining dozens of standing painted clay statues with various expressions. Unfortunately, when Xiangfan No.2 Middle School was expanded in 1951, the side halls and their statues were all demolished.

中文 Chinese

黄州会馆又名黄州书院，位于定中门街与马街，始建年代不详，同治八年（1869）重建。坐北朝南，占地面积约950平方米。两进四合院式布局，有戏楼、正殿、后殿。

戏楼仅存下部，面阔三间12.4米，分别进深三间11.5米、10.6米，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，砖木结构，两山为穿斗式构架，中部为抬梁式构架，封火山墙，前壁设隔扇。

English 英文

Huangzhou Guild Hall, also called Huangzhou Academy, is located at Dingzhong Gate Street and Majie; the initial construction date is unknown, and it was rebuilt in the 8th year of Tongzhi (1869). It faces south, covering an area of about 950 square meters. It has a two-entry courtyard layout, with a theater tower, main hall, and rear hall. Only the lower part of the theater tower remains; it is three bays wide, 12.4 meters, with depths of three bays respectively 11.5 meters and 10.6 meters, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, of brick-wood structure, with column-and-tie frames on the two gable sides and a post-and-lintel frame in the middle, fire-sealing gable walls, and lattice doors and windows on the front wall. Various wood carvings are applied under the eaves.

296. 樊城小江西会馆

Xiao Jiangxi Guild Hall in Fancheng
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
樊城区中山前街曾家巷口212号
类型 Type
商业与手工业建筑
看点 Highlights
会馆呈长方形四合院式布局共七进院落抗日战争期间至解放前前三进由江西富商杨牧顺经营药铺后四进由江西富商何仁顺囤积粮食建筑院墙高8米院深80米各房屋结构相同硬山式二层楼面阔三间穿斗式构架每两进院落中间是天井每天井并建有天沟和漏筒
中文 Chinese

会馆呈长方形四合院式布局，共七进院落，抗日战争期间至解放前，前三进由江西富商杨牧顺经营药铺，后四进由江西富商何仁顺囤积粮食。建筑院墙高8米，院深80米，各房屋结构相同，硬山式二层楼，面阔三间，穿斗式构架。

每两进院落中间是天井，每天井并建有天沟和漏筒，雨水由漏筒排入窨井。江西会馆供奉的许真君，原名许逊，为晋代治水名家和著名的道教师。他生于南昌，博通经史术和天文地理学说。26岁跟随西安吴猛学道，42岁任四川旌阳县令。十年后回归故里南昌一带解决洪水之患。

其治水故事，至今广为江西人传诵。许逊最后选定南昌城西逍遥山的桐园为隐居修道之地，成为道教'净明忠孝'派的创始人。为表彰他的功德，东晋朝廷将其任职的旌阳改为德阳，乡人在其桐园故宅建立了许仙祠（西山万寿宫的前身），将他逝世之日定为升仙日后。

后许仙祠后来被宋徽宗改名为'玉隆万寿宫'，江西人在全国和世界各地修建的江西会馆即万寿宫，一律供奉许逊。

English 英文

The guild hall has a rectangular courtyard layout, with a total of seven courtyards; from the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression to before liberation, the first three courtyards were used by wealthy Jiangxi merchant Yang Mushun to operate a pharmacy, and the last four courtyards were used by wealthy Jiangxi merchant He Renshun to hoard grain. The building courtyard walls are 8 meters high, and the courtyard depth is 80 meters; each house has the same structure, a gable-style two-story building, three bays wide, with a column-and-tie frame. Between every two courtyards there is a courtyard (tianjing); each courtyard is built with a roof gutter and a drain pipe, and rainwater is discharged through the drain pipe into a sewer. The Xu Zhenjun (True Lord Xu) enshrined in the Jiangxi Guild Hall, originally named Xu Xun, was a famous flood-control expert and renowned Taoist master of the Jin Dynasty. He was born in Nanchang, well-versed in classics, history, arts, astronomy, and geography. At 26 he followed Wu Meng of Xi'an to study Taoism, and at 42 he served as the magistrate of Jingyang County in Sichuan. Ten years later he returned to his hometown around Nanchang to solve the flood disaster. His flood-control stories are still widely recited by Jiangxi people today. Xu Xun finally chose Tongyuan on Xiaoyao Mountain west of Nanchang City as a place to live in seclusion and cultivate Taoism, becoming the founder of the 'Jingming Zhongxiao' (Pure Brightness, Loyalty, and Filial Piety) sect of Taoism. To commend his merits and virtues, the Eastern Jin court changed Jingyang, where he served, to Deyang; villagers built the Xu Xian Shrine (predecessor of the Xishan Wanshou Palace) at his former Tongyuan residence, and designated the day of his death as the Ascension-to-Immortality Day. Later, the Xu Xian Shrine was renamed 'Yulong Wanshou Palace' by Emperor Huizong of Song; the Jiangxi guild halls built by Jiangxi people across the country and around the world are Wanshou Palaces, all enshrining Xu Xun.

Site of City Wall of Fancheng
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位

樊城区米公路至东风路间，大庆路南侧
类型 Type

看点 Highlights
城门形制樊城城址始建年代不详最早见于记载是在东汉从今樊城外围发现的众多遗址、墓葬看其发展也是在东汉后南宋末被毁明嘉靖三十九年重修砖城清道光八年、咸丰十年增修平面近椭圆形东西约3500米南北约1500米周长7500米城墙高5-6米
中文 Chinese

樊城城址始建年代不详，最早见于记载是在东汉，从今樊城外围发现的众多遗址、墓葬看，其发展也是在东汉后，南宋末被毁，明嘉靖三十九年（1560）重修砖城，清道光八年（1828）、咸丰十年（1860）增修。

平面近椭圆形，东西约3500米，南北约1500米，周长7500米。城墙高5—6米，顶宽5米左右。有'迎汉''朝觐''朝圣''定中''屏襄''汇通''迎旭'七座城门，门上建有城楼。城外有护城河遗迹。

1973年后逐步被推平，仅存'定中''屏襄'门及火星观城墙。火星观段城墙于1999年底修建沿江大道时被拆。

English 英文

The initial construction date of the Fancheng city site is unknown; the earliest record is in the Eastern Han; judging from the numerous sites and tombs discovered around present-day Fancheng, its development was also after the Eastern Han; it was destroyed at the end of the Southern Song, the brick city was rebuilt in the 39th year of Jiajing, Ming (1560), and additional repairs were made in the 8th year of Daoguang, Qing (1828) and the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860). The plane is nearly elliptical, about 3500 meters east-west and about 1500 meters north-south, with a perimeter of 7500 meters. The city wall is 5–6 meters high and about 5 meters wide at the top. There were seven city gates: 'Yinghan,' 'Chaojin,' 'Chaosheng,' 'Dingzhong,' 'Pingxiang,' 'Huitong,' and 'Yingxu,' with gate towers built on the gates. Outside the city there are remains of a moat. After 1973 it was gradually leveled, leaving only the 'Dingzhong' and 'Pingxiang' gates and the Huoxingguan section of the city wall. The Huoxingguan section of the city wall was demolished when Yanjiang Avenue was built at the end of 1999.

Dingzhong Gate is located on the west side of the middle section of Dingzhong Street; it was the north gate of ancient Fancheng, a brick arch gate, 4.4 meters wide, 10.2 meters deep, and 4.04 meters high. The lower shoulder is built with strip stones, 1.3 meters high. The upper body is built with strip bricks, among which there are dozens of incised character bricks such as 'City Work of the 12th Year of Tongzhi' and 'City Work of the 5th Year of Guangxu.' The remaining city walls on both sides are about 15 meters long and about 5 meters high.

中文 Chinese

屏襄门位于解放路与东风路交汇处西北侧，为古樊城东北门。砖石券门，下部条石砌筑，上部条砖叠砌至顶，双层券顶，前部券顶较高。门洞宽4米、深12.2米、前部高3.4米，过道条石铺地。门洞北侧两壁有防水闸槽及门横梁。

English 英文

Pingxiang Gate is located on the northwest side of the intersection of Jiefang Road and Dongfeng Road; it was the northeast gate of ancient Fancheng. It is a brick-stone arch gate, with the lower part built of strip stones and the upper part built of stacked strip bricks to the top, with a double-layer arch top, and the front arch top is higher. The gate opening is 4 meters wide, 12.2 meters deep, and 3.4 meters high at the front; the passageway is paved with strip stones. On the two walls on the north side of the gate opening there are waterproof gate slots and gate beams. The remaining walls on the east and west sides are respectively about 3.6 meters and 8.6 meters long, with top widths of 3.6 meters and 3.1 meters, and heights of 4.7 meters and 4 meters. The lower shoulder is built with strip stones, gradually thickening northward, and the upper part is built with stacked strip bricks.

301. 鹿门寺

Lumen Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
宋、明、清代
地址 Address
襄阳城南约15公里处东津镇鹿门山
类型 Type
宗教建筑
看点 Highlights
选址环境寺院格局位于襄阳市城东南15公里的东津镇境内津镇有鹿门山原名苏岭山据记载东汉光武帝与近臣习郁都曾梦见苏岭山神光武帝命令习郁在山上立祠庙因道口两边刻有石鹿百姓称之为鹿门庙并以庙名山鹿门寺东汉建武年间由襄阳侯习郁始建西晋改名为万寿禅寺魏晋南北朝时期香火不衰
中文 Chinese

鹿门寺位于襄阳市城东南15公里的东津镇境内。津镇有鹿门山，原名苏岭山。据记载，东汉光武帝与近臣习郁都曾梦见苏岭山神，光武帝命令习郁在山上立祠庙，因道口两边刻有石鹿，百姓称之为鹿门庙，并以庙名山。

鹿门寺东汉建武年间（26—56）由襄阳侯习郁始建，西晋改名为万寿禅寺，魏晋南北朝时期，香火不衰，成为全国的佛教圣地。唐朝复名鹿门寺，唐代名僧处贞、丹霞、宋法灯禅师均主持过鹿门寺。

明朝景泰年间（1450—1456），在此建'三高祠'（庞统、孟浩然、皮日休）并供其像，以示纪念。明末毁于火，清初以来，屡有修废。该寺庙依山势而建，环山临水，山涧幽深，林木苍翠，初建时规模宏大，历代名僧常来此主持佛事，北宋政和年间最为兴盛，极盛时有房屋约500余间。

历史上诸多名人曾在此隐居，如汉末名士庞德公不受刺史刘表数次宴请，携家登鹿门山采药；唐代诗人孟浩然宦场失意幽居鹿门山，吟咏山水自得其趣；晚唐文学家皮日休也曾幽栖鹿门。因此世称'鹿门高士傲帝王'。现存鹿门寺院、三高祠、八角井、庞公制药洞、望江亭等。

English 英文

Lumen Temple is located in Dongjin Town, 15 km southeast of Xiangyang City. In Dongjin Town there is Lumen Mountain, originally named Suling Mountain. According to records, Emperor Guangwu of the Eastern Han and his close minister Xi Yu both dreamed of the god of Suling Mountain; Emperor Guangwu ordered Xi Yu to build a shrine on the mountain; because stone deer were carved on both sides of the road entrance, common people called it Lumen (Deer Gate) Temple, and named the mountain after the temple. Lumen Temple was first built by Xi Yu, Marquis of Xiangyang, during the Jianwu period of the Eastern Han (26–56); in the Western Jin it was renamed Wanshou Chan Temple; during the Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties, incense continued unabated, and it became a Buddhist holy land nationwide. In the Tang it was renamed Lumen Temple; famous Tang monks such as Chuzhen, Danxia, and Song Fadeng Chan Master all presided over Lumen Temple. During the Jingtai period of the Ming (1450–1456), the 'Sangao (Three Highs) Shrine' (for Pang Tong, Meng Haoran, and Pi Rixiu) was built here and their statues were enshrined for commemoration. It was destroyed by fire at the end of the Ming, and since the early Qing it has been repeatedly repaired and abandoned. The temple is built along the mountain terrain, surrounded by mountains and facing water, with deep mountain ravines and lush forests; when first built it was large in scale, and famous monks of successive dynasties often came here to preside over Buddhist affairs; it was most prosperous during the Zhenghe period of the Northern Song, with about 500 rooms at its peak. Many famous people in history lived in seclusion here, such as Pang Degong, a famous scholar at the end of the Han, who refused several banquets by Inspector Liu Biao and took his family to climb Lumen Mountain to gather herbs; Meng Haoran, a Tang poet, frustrated in officialdom, lived in seclusion at Lumen Mountain, chanting mountains and waters and enjoying himself; Pi Rixiu, a late Tang litterateur, also once lived in seclusion at Lumen. Hence the world says 'Lumen's lofty scholars disdain emperors.' The existing buildings include Lumen Temple compound, Sangao Shrine, Octagonal Well, Lord Pang's Medicine-Making Cave, and Wangjiang (River-Viewing) Pavilion, etc.

302. 鹿门书院

Lumen Academy
级别 Level

襄阳市襄州区鹿门寺景区内
