鹿门寺主体建筑坐北朝南占地面积约3000平方米四合院式布局有山门、前殿、后殿及左右偏殿山门为四柱三间牌楼式前殿面阔三间进深一间单檐硬山灰瓦顶抬梁式构架后殿面阔三间进深三间重檐歇山灰筒瓦顶抬梁式构架还有鹿门寺碑廊
中文 Chinese

鹿门寺主体建筑坐北朝南，占地面积约3000平方米。四合院式布局，有山门、前殿、后殿及左右偏殿。山门为四柱三间牌楼式；

前殿面阔三间、进深一间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，抬梁式构架；后殿面阔三间，进深三间，重檐歇山灰筒瓦顶，抬梁式构架。

还有鹿门寺碑廊，为廊式庭院式建筑布局，碑刻环绕于廊墙上，重要的碑刻有：宋《故襄阳鹿门第二代法灯禅师塔记》，明《鹿门万寿禅寺重修记》《新建三高祠记》，清《重修鹿门三高祠记》《鹿门息波禅师伏虎谒》《望古遥集》等。

English 英文

The main building of Lumen Temple faces south, covering an area of about 3000 square meters. It has a courtyard layout, with a mountain gate, front hall, rear hall, and left and right side halls. The mountain gate is a four-column three-bay paifang style; the front hall is three bays wide and one bay deep, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof and a post-and-lintel frame; the rear hall is three bays wide and three bays deep, with a double-eave hip-and-gable gray tube-tile roof and a post-and-lintel frame. There is also the Lumen Temple stele corridor, with a corridor-style courtyard building layout; stele carvings surround the corridor walls. Important stele carvings include: the Song 'Record of the Pagoda of the Second-Generation Fadeng Chan Master of Former Xiangyang Lumen,' the Ming 'Record of the Reconstruction of Lumen Wanshou Chan Temple' and 'Record of the Newly Built Sangao Shrine,' and the Qing 'Record of the Reconstruction of Lumen Sangao Shrine,' 'Tiger-Subduing Visit by Chan Master Xibo of Lumen,' and 'Looking at Ancient Times from Afar,' etc.

303. 三高祠

Sangao Shrine (Shrine of Three Highs)
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄州区鹿门寺景区内
类型 Type
纪念建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
三高祠面阔三间进深三间重檐歇山灰筒瓦顶抬梁式构架前壁设隔扇槛窗内塑庞德公、孟浩然、皮日休像
中文 Chinese

三高祠面阔三间，进深三间，重檐歇山灰筒瓦顶，抬梁式构架，前壁设隔扇槛窗。内塑庞德公、孟浩然、皮日休像。

English 英文

Sangao Shrine is three bays wide and three bays deep, with a double-eave hip-and-gable gray tube-tile roof and a post-and-lintel frame; the front wall is fitted with lattice doors and windows. Inside are enshrined statues of Pang Degong, Meng Haoran, and Pi Rixiu.

304. 鹿门寺碑刻

Stele Carvings of Lumen Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
宋、明代
地址 Address
襄阳市襄州区鹿门寺景区内

看点 Highlights
宋故襄阳鹿门第二代禅师塔记碑刻于建炎元年青石质高0.75米宽0.45米厚0.1米碑文楷书21行275字记第二代禅师到鹿门寺重振禅院事重修鹿门三高祠记碑刻于万历四十一年青石质圆首方座通高2.2米
中文 Chinese

宋《故襄阳鹿门第二代禅师塔记》碑刻于建炎元年（1127）。青石质。高0.75米、宽0.45米、厚0.1米。碑文楷书，21行275字，记第二代禅师到鹿门寺重振禅院事。

《重修鹿门三高祠记》碑刻于万历四十一年（1613）。青石质，圆首，方座。通高2.2米、宽0.9米、厚0.22米。额篆'重修三高祠记'，碑文楷书，19行750字，记重修三高祠事。

English 英文

The Song 'Record of the Pagoda of the Second-Generation Chan Master of Former Xiangyang Lumen' stele was carved in the 1st year of Jianyan (1127). It is of bluestone quality, 0.75 meters high, 0.45 meters wide, and 0.1 meter thick. The stele inscription is in regular script, 21 lines and 275 characters, recording the matter of the second-generation Chan Master going to Lumen Temple to revive the Chan monastery. The 'Record of the Reconstruction of Lumen Sangao Shrine' stele was carved in the 41st year of Wanli (1613). It is of bluestone quality, with a round top and square base. It is 2.2 meters high, 0.9 meters wide, and 0.22 meters thick. The额 is inscribed in seal script 'Record of the Reconstruction of Sangao Shrine'; the stele inscription is in regular script, 19 lines and 750 characters, recording the matter of reconstructing Sangao Shrine.

305. 光化黉学

Guanghua Hongxue Academy
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
老河口市老县城村
类型 Type
教育建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
黉学是古代的学校为尊孔儒师们宣教化育贤才善民俗的讲学之所据光化县志记载光化黉学始建于宋熙宁年间宋元符三年重修明万历元年迁至现址之后多次重修清光绪十三年最后一次大修光化黉学占地50余亩坐北朝南原有规模较大包括石碑坊、状元桥、棂星门、泮池、大成门（又称过殿）、大成殿、名宦乡贤祠、明伦堂、射圃厅等
中文 Chinese

黉学是古代的学校，为尊孔儒师们'宣教化、育贤才、善民俗'的讲学之所。据《光化县志》记载，光化黉学始建于宋熙宁年间，宋元符三年（1100）重修，明万历元年（1573）迁至现址，之后多次重修，清光绪十三年（187）最后一次大修。

光化黉学占地50余亩，坐北朝南，原有规模较大，包括石碑坊、状元桥、棂星门、泮池、大成门（又称过殿）、大成殿、名宦乡贤祠、明伦堂、射圃厅等，中轴对称布局。现仅存大成门和明伦堂，约80米长的青石板路连接两座建筑。

大成殿俗称'九架九檩朝王殿'，面阔五间22.6米，进深三间9.5米，硬山顶砖木结构，抬梁式构架，前部卷棚顶。

明伦堂分前、后二堂，前堂面阔三间14.7米、后堂面阔四间11.8米，进深三间分别为9.8米、7.2米；

中部抬梁式、两侧穿斗式构架，勾连搭式屋顶，硬山顶砖木结构。

English 英文

Hongxue (Academy) was an ancient school, a place for Confucian teachers to 'propagate education, nurture talents, and improve folk customs.' According to the 'Guanghua County Annals,' Guanghua Hongxue Academy was first built during the Xining period of the Song, rebuilt in the 3rd year of Yuanfu, Song (1100), moved to the current site in the 1st year of Wanli, Ming (1573), and repaired many times thereafter, with the last major repair in the 13th year of Guangxu, Qing (1887). Guanghua Hongxue Academy covers more than 50 mu, faces south, and originally had a large scale, including a stone paifang, Zhuangyuan (Top Scholar) Bridge, Lingxing Gate, Pan Pond, Dacheng Gate (also called Passage Hall), Dacheng Hall, Minghuan and Xiangxian Shrines, Minglun Hall, and Shepu (Archery) Hall, etc., with a centrally symmetric layout. Now only the Dacheng Gate and Minglun Hall remain, connected by an about 80-meter-long bluestone road. The Dacheng Hall is commonly called the 'Nine-Frame Nine-Purlin King-Audience Hall'; it is five bays wide, 22.6 meters, and three bays deep, 9.5 meters, with a gable roof, brick-wood structure, post-and-lintel frame, and a rolling-roof ceiling at the front. The Minglun Hall is divided into front and rear halls; the front hall is three bays wide, 14.7 meters, and the rear hall is four bays wide, 11.8 meters, with three bays deep respectively 9.8 meters and 7.2 meters; the middle has a post-and-lintel frame and the two sides have column-and-tie frames, with an interlocking-eave roof and a gable roof, brick-wood structure.

306. 秦家老屋

Qin Family's Old House
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
老河口市南街社区秦川楼道子22号
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
四合院平面布局据秦家后人秦喜辉老人口述老屋始建于清道光四年为祖上自陕西搬至老河口市经商时所建老屋为典型北方四合院坐东南朝西北平面近方形外墙青砖到顶侧面开门建筑面阔五间南房与两侧厢房为一层
中文 Chinese

据秦家后人秦喜辉老人口述，老屋始建于清道光四年（1824），为祖上自陕西搬至老河口市经商时所建。老屋为典型北方四合院，坐东南朝西北，平面近方形，外墙青砖到顶，侧面开门，建筑面阔五间，南房与两侧厢房为一层，正房为两层，皆硬山屋顶，砖木混合结构。

正房北侧设梯，可至二层。如今房子的二层基本闲置，只有一层仍有人居住。西侧厢房和正房的立面已经换成了现代的砖墙。

English 英文

According to the oral account of Qin Xihui, an elderly descendant of the Qin family, the old house was first built in the 4th year of Daoguang, Qing (1824), built when the ancestors moved from Shaanxi to Laohekou City to do business. The old house is a typical northern courtyard, facing northwest from southeast, with a nearly square plane; the exterior walls are blue brick to the top, with doors on the side; the building is five bays wide; the south room and the two side wing rooms are one story, and the main room is two stories, all with gable roofs, of brick-wood mixed structure. A staircase is set on the north side of the main room, leading to the second story. Now the second story of the house is basically idle, and only the first story is still inhabited. The facades of the west wing room and the main room have been replaced with modern brick walls.

307. 太平街民居

Vernacular Dwellings on Taiping Street
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
老河口市太平街
类型 Type
居住建筑
看点 Highlights
老街格局封火山墙老河口地处汉水中游东岸扼川陕咽喉控鄂西北及川陕豫水陆交通接壤地区之孔道历来为四省物资集散地商业繁盛手工业尤为发达在宋代时老河口已有兴起的迹象景佑五年任乾德县令的欧阳修写道其民尤富太平街位于老河口市区的西北部东接两仪街
中文 Chinese

老河口地处汉水中游东岸，扼川陕咽喉，控鄂西北及川、陕、豫水陆交通接壤地区之孔道，历来为'四省物资集散地'，商业繁盛，手工业尤为发达，在宋代时老河口已有兴起的迹象，景佑五年（1038）任乾德县令的欧阳修写道'其民尤富'（《尚书屯田员外郎李君墓表》），还有其他资料加以佐证：'襄阳路属邑光化，其山川土地既盛且沃，居民繁庶是异。

'（薛简：《朱县尹政绩铭并序》）这都表明宋代的乾德县已经倚仗水运优势具备了初步的发展规模。

明清时候老河口有码头21处：万福、望江楼、小码头、上大码头、龙王庙码头、均邦码头、太平码头、公议码头、湖南码头、新街码头、湿码头、米邦码头、下大码头、汉南码头、朝佛街码头、新码头、'洋油栈'码头、正兴街码头、老新街码头、大街码头、路家巷码头、干码头。基本上达到了老河口码头历史上最鼎盛的状态。

清雍正三年（1725），泾阳孟琅执政光邑，老河口人烟密集（约3万人），商贾咸集，烟火万家。至光绪年间，城区内已有知名商店1200余家，外商数十家，主要经营桐油、药材、布匹、食盐等主要品种，交易金额白银5000万两。

城内街道70余条，各码头经常停泊船只达六七千只，人口近8万。辛亥革命前后，老河口依然有20个码头，商业特别发达，被称为'银钱窝'。那时老河口水陆交通之便，是货物集散转运要地，历史上素有'小汉口'之称。

太平街位于老河口市区的西北部，东接两仪街，南邻乐盛街，是一条有着两百多年历史的老街。路呈东西向，全长196米，宽6.6米，占地面积2.14万平方米，是老河口市区内现存比较完好的一条古居民老街。

沿街南北两侧共有38家商行，各商行的建筑风格基本一致，现存的建筑保存较好，马头墙错落有致。街内的房屋大多是明末清初的古民宅。其建筑融合了北方四合院和徽派民居的风格，黑铺板门，粉墙黛瓦，尖檐微翘，三进连的烽火墙既有防火功能，又彰显商家气派。

现存的太平街民居古建筑众多，如建于清代的李家烟馆，位于光华街办两仪街288号，面阔七间，两层硬山顶砖石结构，前壁八根方砖柱家砖墙土顶，下层三门圆拱券，四窗及上层七窗弧券形檐。

又如李记杂货铺，1914年建，位于光华街办太平街45号，原为两层欧式砖木结构四合院建筑，现存临街店铺三间，前壁四根罗马式方柱间青砖墙体，拱形窗。

English 英文

Laohekou is located on the east bank of the middle reaches of the Han River, guarding the throat of Sichuan and Shaanxi, controlling the passage of the water and land transportation junction area of northwest Hubei and Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Henan; it has historically been a 'material distribution center for four provinces,' with prosperous commerce and especially developed handicrafts. In the Song Dynasty, Laohekou already showed signs of rise; in the 5th year of Jingyou (1038), Ouyang Xiu, who served as the magistrate of Qiande County, wrote 'its people are especially wealthy' ('Epitaph of Mr. Li, Vice Director of the Bureau of Agriculture'), and other materials corroborate: 'Guanghua, a county under Xiangyang Road, has both prosperous and fertile mountains and land, and a dense and abundant population unlike others.' (Xue Jian: 'Inscription and Preface on the Political Achievements of Magistrate Zhu') This all indicates that Qiande County in the Song already had a preliminary development scale relying on its water transport advantages. During the Ming and Qing, Laohekou had 21 docks: Wanfu, Wangjiang Tower, Small Dock, Upper Great Dock, Dragon King Temple Dock, Junbang Dock, Taiping Dock, Gongyi Dock, Hunan Dock, New Street Dock, Wet Dock, Mibang Dock, Lower Great Dock, Hannan Dock, Chaofo Street Dock, New Dock, 'Foreign Oil Depot' Dock, Zhengxing Street Dock, Old New Street Dock, Great Street Dock, Lujia Lane Dock, and Dry Dock. It basically reached the most prosperous state in the history of Laohekou docks. In the 3rd year of Yongzheng, Qing (1725), Meng Lang from Jingyang governed Guangyi, and Laohekou had a dense population (about 30,000), with merchants gathering and ten thousand households. By the Guangxu period, there were already more than 1200 well-known shops in the urban area, with dozens of foreign merchants, mainly operating tung oil, medicinal materials, cloth, salt, and other main varieties, with a transaction amount of 50 million taels of silver. There were more than 70 streets in the city, and each dock often had six to seven thousand boats moored, with a population of nearly 80,000. Around the Xinhai Revolution, Laohekou still had 20 docks, with especially developed commerce, and was called a 'silver money nest.' At that time, Laohekou, with its convenient water and land transportation, was an important place for cargo distribution and transshipment, and historically known as 'Little Hankou.' Taiping Street is located in the northwest of the urban area of Laohekou, connecting Liangyi Street to the east and adjacent to Lesheng Street to the south; it is an old street with a history of more than two hundred years. The road runs east-west, with a total length of 196 meters and a width of 6.6 meters, covering an area of 21,400 square meters; it is a relatively well-preserved old residential street in the urban area of Laohekou. There are 38 commercial firms on both the north and south sides along the street, and the architectural styles of each firm are basically the same; the existing buildings are well-preserved, with horse-head walls scattered in an orderly manner. Most of the houses in the street are ancient residences from the late Ming and early Qing. Their architecture integrates the styles of northern courtyards and Huizhou vernacular dwellings, with black plank doors, white walls and black tiles, slightly upturned pointed eaves, and the three-entry connected beacon walls have both fire-prevention functions and demonstrate the grandeur of merchants. There are many ancient buildings of vernacular dwellings on Taiping Street; for example, the Li Family Opium Den built in the Qing, located at No.288 Liangyi Street, Guanghua Subdistrict Office, is seven bays wide, a two-story gable-roof brick-stone structure, with eight square brick columns on the front wall between brick walls and earthen tops, three round arch doors on the lower floor, and four windows and seven windows on the upper floor with arched eaves. Another example is Li Ji Grocery Store, built in 1914, located at No.45 Taiping Street, Guanghua Subdistrict Office; originally a two-story European-style brick-wood courtyard building, now three street-facing shops remain, with blue brick walls between four Roman-style square columns on the front wall and arched windows.

308. 清真寺

Mosque in Laohekou
级别 Level
市级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
老河口市北京路街道办事处两仪街南段
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
建筑形制据老河口市志记载伊斯兰教传入老河口市约在清初最早的两座清真寺均建于清咸丰之前一处位于花城门内称为上寺另一处位于魏家院（现新马路东段）称为下寺清咸丰三年回民集资购买魏家井（现两仪街）东段地皮修建了这座具有徽派建筑风格的清真寺历经战乱幸得保存至今而上寺于抗战时期撤除清真寺占地面积约800平方米
中文 Chinese

据《老河口市志》记载，伊斯兰教传入老河口市约在清初，最早的两座清真寺均建于清咸丰之前。一处位于花城门内，称为上寺；另一处位于魏家院（现新马路东段），称为下寺。

清咸丰三年（1853）回民集资购买魏家井（现两仪街）东段地皮，修建了这座具有徽派建筑风格的清真寺，历经战乱，幸得保存至今。而上寺于'抗战'时期撤除。

清真寺占地面积约800平方米，主体建筑面积600平方米，砖木结构，由山门、厢房、邦克楼、浴室、过殿、大殿等组成。

1941年，时任参谋总长兼军训部长的白崇禧（中国回教救国协会理事长）为老河口清真寺题词'兴教建国'，此匾现悬挂大殿正门上方。2006年重新修建后，仅山门保持旧貌。

English 英文

According to the 'Laohekou City Annals,' Islam was introduced to Laohekou City around the early Qing, and the earliest two mosques were both built before the Xianfeng period of the Qing. One was located inside Huacheng Gate, called the Upper Mosque; the other was located at Weijiayuan (now the east section of Xinma Road), called the Lower Mosque. In the 3rd year of Xianfeng, Qing (1853), Hui people raised funds to purchase the land in the east section of Weijiajing (now Liangyi Street) and built this mosque with Huizhou architectural style; through wars, it fortunately has been preserved to this day. The Upper Mosque was demolished during the 'War of Resistance' period. The mosque covers an area of about 800 square meters, with a main building area of 600 square meters, of brick-wood structure, composed of a mountain gate, wing rooms, minaret, bathhouse, passage hall, main hall, etc. In 1941, Bai Chongxi (Chairman of the Chinese Islamic Salvation Association), then Chief of the General Staff and Minister of Military Training, inscribed 'Promote Religion, Build the Nation' for the Laohekou Mosque; this plaque is now hung above the main entrance of the main hall. After being rebuilt in 2006, only the mountain gate retains its old appearance.

309. 黉学大殿

Great Hall of Hongxue Academy
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
枣阳城区内大南街东侧市粮食局院内
类型 Type
教育建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
木雕黉学大殿又称至圣殿系清代祭祀建筑位于枣阳城区内大南街东侧市粮食局院内此处曾为明清乡试之地始建于元至正三年清嘉庆年间重修坐北朝南原占地面积约7300平方米三进四合院式沿中轴线布局有棂星门、至圣殿、崇圣祠及明伦堂、节孝祠、忠义祠等
中文 Chinese

黉学大殿又称至圣殿，系清代祭祀建筑，位于枣阳城区内大南街东侧市粮食局院内。此处曾为明清乡试之地，始建于元至正三年（1343），清嘉庆年间重修。坐北朝南，原占地面积约7300平方米。

三进四合院式，沿中轴线布局，有棂星门、至圣殿、崇圣祠及明伦堂、节孝祠、忠义祠等，大部分建筑在抗日战争时被日军炸毁。现存至圣殿，面阔五间26米，进深三间13米。

单檐歇山琉璃瓦顶，两山穿斗式构架，中部抬梁式构架。

English 英文

The Great Hall of Hongxue Academy, also called the Holy Temple, is a Qing sacrificial building, located inside the Municipal Grain Bureau, east side of Danan Street, Zaoyang City. This place was once the site of the Ming and Qing provincial examinations; it was first built in the 3rd year of Zhizheng, Yuan (1343), and repaired during the Jiaqing period of the Qing. It faces south, originally covering an area of about 7300 square meters. It is a three-entry courtyard style, laid out along the central axis, with a Lingxing Gate, Holy Temple, Chongsheng Shrine, Minglun Hall, Jiexiao Shrine, Zhongyi Shrine, etc.; most of the buildings were blown up by the Japanese army during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. The existing Holy Temple is five bays wide, 26 meters, and three bays deep, 13 meters. It has a single-eave hip-and-gable glazed tile roof, with column-and-tie frames on the two gable sides and a post-and-lintel frame in the middle.

310. 白水寺

Baishui Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清、民国
地址 Address
枣阳市吴店镇白水村白水路
类型 Type
宗教建筑
看点 Highlights
碑刻环境白水寺原名白水禅林始建于元至正三年系乡人为祀汉光武帝刘秀而建后经多次修葺该寺地处枣阳市狮子山上雄踞山巅庄重古朴寺院坐北朝南呈东西向长方形分布东西长约250米
中文 Chinese

白水寺原名白水禅林，始建于元至正三年（1343），系乡人为祀汉光武帝刘秀而建，后经多次修葺。该寺地处枣阳市狮子山上，雄踞山巅，庄重古朴。寺院坐北朝南，呈东西向长方形分布，东西长约250米、南北宽约150米。

原有刘秀殿、佛爷殿、大雄宝殿、娘娘殿，罗汉殿等八组建筑，现存大雄宝殿、佛爷殿、刘秀殿及娘娘殿正殿，均为砖木结构，或硬山或悬山或卷棚顶，有石碑2通，其余僧舍多属清代后期增建。

整座寺庙殿堂古朴典雅，雕塑精美，寺内外遍布古树，门前石阶壮观，洋溢着浓郁的梵宇气息。佛爷殿、刘秀殿均为四合院式布局，有前殿、正殿及偏殿。

前殿分别面阔五、三间16.43米、10.95米，进深三间7.1米、5.2米，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，抬梁式构架；

正殿分别面阔三、五间13.57米、17.83米，进深四、三间14米、6.65米，各为单檐悬、硬山灰瓦顶，抬梁式构架；

左、右偏殿均面阔两间6.6米、4.5米，进深一间3.1米、2.25米，分别为卷棚、单檐硬山灰瓦顶，穿斗式构架。

娘娘殿正殿面阔五间16.52米，进深三间7米。重檐悬山灰瓦顶，抬梁式构架。白水寺内所存2通石碑均刻于民国三十年（1941）。青石质，碑文楷书，记整修白水寺事。

碑一，'白水重光'碑，立于刘秀殿正殿前，方座，通高2.4米、宽0.8米、厚0.18米，碑阳额题'万古千秋'中竖刻'白水重光'，字径0.44米×0.38米，碑阴刻《重修白水寺序》，11行约800字；

碑二，无题碑，横匾式，嵌于娘娘殿前壁，宽0.8米、高0.6米，文9行144字。

English 英文

Baishui Temple, originally called Baishui Chanlin (White Water Buddhist Grove), was first built in the 3rd year of Zhizheng, Yuan (1343), built by villagers to worship Emperor Guangwu of Han Liu Xiu, and repaired many times thereafter. The temple is located on Lion Mountain in Zaoyang City, towering on the mountain top, solemn and simple. The temple faces south, distributed in an east-west rectangular shape, about 250 meters long east-west and about 150 meters wide north-south. It originally had eight groups of buildings such as Liu Xiu Hall, Buddha Hall, Mahavira Hall, Niangniang (Goddess) Hall, and Luohan (Arhat) Hall; the existing buildings include the Mahavira Hall, Buddha Hall, Liu Xiu Hall, and the main hall of Niangniang Hall, all of brick-wood structure, with either gable,悬山 (overhanging gable), or rolling-roof tops, with 2 stone steles; the rest of the monk's quarters mostly belong to additions in the late Qing. The entire temple halls are simple and elegant, with exquisite sculptures; ancient trees are spread inside and outside the temple, and the stone steps in front of the gate are spectacular, permeated with a strong Buddhist temple atmosphere. The Buddha Hall and Liu Xiu Hall both have a courtyard layout, with a front hall, main hall, and side halls. The front halls are respectively five and three bays wide, 16.43 meters and 10.95 meters, three bays deep, 7.1 meters and 5.2 meters, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs and post-and-lintel frames; the main halls are respectively three and five bays wide, 13.57 meters and 17.83 meters, four and three bays deep, 14 meters and 6.65 meters, each with single-eave overhanging gable and gable gray-tile roofs and post-and-lintel frames; the left and right side halls are both two bays wide, 6.6 meters and 4.5 meters, one bay deep, 3.1 meters and 2.25 meters, respectively with rolling-roof and single-eave gable gray-tile roofs and column-and-tie frames. The main hall of Niangniang Hall is five bays wide, 16.52 meters, and three bays deep, 7 meters. It has a double-eave overhanging gable gray-tile roof and a post-and-lintel frame. The 2 stone steles preserved in Baishui Temple were both carved in the 30th year of the Republic (1941). They are of bluestone quality, with regular-script inscriptions, recording the repair of Baishui Temple. Stele 1, the 'White Water Re-lighted' stele, stands in front of the main hall of Liu Xiu Hall, with a square base, a total height of 2.4 meters, a width of 0.8 meters, and a thickness of 0.18 meters; the front of the stele has the额 title 'Eternity Through the Ages,' with 'White Water Re-lighted' vertically carved in the middle, with a character size of 0.44 m × 0.38 m; the back of the stele is carved with 'Preface to the Reconstruction of Baishui Temple,' 11 lines and about 800 characters; Stele 2, an untitled stele, in horizontal plaque style, embedded in the front wall of Niangniang Hall, 0.8 meters wide and 0.6 meters high, with 9 lines and 144 characters.

311. 邱家前湾民居群

Vernacular Dwellings in Qiujia Qianwan
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清、民国
地址 Address
枣阳市新市镇邱家前湾村
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
村落格局寨墙形制邱家前湾民居群位于枣阳市新市镇邱家前湾村明景泰泰年间至清朝康熙、乾隆年间建成邱家前湾自然村处一道山冈的南坡面积约7.2万平方米建筑群依山就势建造有两横七纵巷道互为相通进出非常方便村落前是一个人工挖掘的大水塘
中文 Chinese

邱家前湾民居群位于枣阳市新市镇邱家前湾村，明景泰泰年间至清朝康熙、乾隆年间建成。邱家前湾自然村，处一道山冈的南坡。面积约7.2万平方米。建筑群依山就势建造，有两横七纵巷道，互为相通，进出非常方便。

村落前是一个人工挖掘的大水塘，面积约1800平方米，水深约1米，做储备消防用。民居群依山就势，步步升高，高低错落有致，巷道家家连通，排水明暗相通，集于主水道，最终通向村前的水塘。

村落现存11栋较完整民居，四合院式布局，多数有三进院落，建筑多面阔三间，少量面阔五间，硬山顶砖木结构，少量有两层。每家一个四合院，开门方向不一，小院子内种有柿子树、枣树，门厅前的汉白玉石凳上刻有龙、竹等花形，墙壁是青砖砌成的。

正厅由两层小阁楼组成，房顶的瓦片上都印有精美的'寿'字。清嘉庆年间为防白莲教起义，清廷采取坚壁清野政策，要求村村建寨抵御白匪，邱家前湾便在村落的外围筑起了坚实的寨墙，开有四门，其上设有炮楼、寨墙。炮楼共有6个。

现东大门外小小南边靠着一块石碑，白石质地，上面刻着'圆恩嘉奖'，记载着邱母节俭持家的生平事迹，为民国时期的碑刻。

English 英文

The vernacular dwellings in Qiujia Qianwan are located in Qiujia Qianwan Village, Xinshi Town, Zaoyang City, built from the Jingtai period of the Ming to the Kangxi and Qianlong periods of the Qing. Qiujia Qianwan natural village is located on the southern slope of a hill ridge, covering an area of about 72,000 square meters. The building complex is built according to the mountain terrain, with two horizontal and seven vertical alleys, interconnected, making entry and exit very convenient. In front of the village is an artificially dug large pond, with an area of about 1800 square meters and a water depth of about 1 meter, used for reserve fire protection. The dwelling group follows the mountain terrain, rising step by step, with高低错落 in an orderly manner; the alleys connect every household, and the drainage is connected both openly and covertly, converging into the main water channel and finally leading to the pond in front of the village. The village now preserves 11 relatively complete dwellings, with a courtyard layout, most having three courtyards; the buildings are mostly three bays wide, a few five bays wide, with gable roofs and brick-wood structures, a few having two stories. Each household has one courtyard, with different door-opening directions; persimmon trees and jujube trees are planted in the small courtyards; the white marble stone benches in front of the gate halls are carved with patterns such as dragons and bamboo, and the walls are built of blue bricks. The main hall consists of two small attics, and the tiles on the roof are all printed with exquisite 'Shou' (longevity) characters. During the Jiaqing period of the Qing, to prevent the White Lotus Rebellion, the Qing court adopted a policy of strengthening the walls and clearing the fields, requiring every village to build a fortress to resist the White Bandits; Qiujia Qianwan then built a solid fortress wall around the periphery of the village, with four gates opened, and watchtowers and fortress walls on top. There are a total of 6 watchtowers. Now outside the east gate, leaning against the south side, there is a stone stele of white stone quality, engraved with 'Yu'en Jiajiang' (Graceful Reward), recording the life story of Mrs. Qiu's thrifty household management, and it is a stele from the Republican period.

312. 钱岗陕山会馆

Shaanxi-Shanxi Guild Hall in Qiangang

斗拱木雕钱岗陕山会馆位于钱岗乡钱岗街始建年代不详清乾隆年间重建建筑坐北朝南占地面积225平方米四合院式布局有前、后殿及偏房现存后殿及西偏房后殿面阔三间9.7米进深一间6米
中文 Chinese

钱岗陕山会馆位于钱岗乡钱岗街，始建年代不详，清乾隆年间重建。建筑坐北朝南，占地面积225平方米。四合院式布局，有前、后殿及偏房。现存后殿及西偏房。

后殿面阔三间9.7米，进深一间6米，厢房面阔三间9米，进深一间6米，后殿屋檐高出厢房，偏房面阔五间，均为单檐硬山灰瓦顶，抬梁式构架。

English 英文

The Shaanxi-Shanxi Guild Hall in Qiangang is located on Qiangang Street, Qiangang Township; the initial construction date is unknown, and it was rebuilt during the Qianlong period of the Qing. The building faces south, covering an area of 225 square meters. It has a courtyard layout, with front and rear halls and side rooms. The existing buildings include the rear hall and west side room. The rear hall is three bays wide, 9.7 meters, and one bay deep, 6 meters; the wing room is three bays wide, 9 meters, and one bay deep, 6 meters; the eaves of the rear hall are higher than those of the wing room; the side room is five bays wide, all with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs and post-and-lintel frames.

313. 郭营祠堂

Guo's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
枣阳市新市镇钱岗村
类型 Type
礼制建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
木雕碑刻郭营祠堂位于枣阳市鹿头镇郭营村处枣北低岗地坐北朝南平面呈长方形三合院布局通面阔17.1米通进深20米硬山顶砖木结构重檐式门楼门楼后为过屋
中文 Chinese

郭营祠堂位于枣阳市鹿头镇郭营村，处枣北低岗地。坐北朝南，平面呈长方形，三合院布局。通面阔17.1米，通进深20米。硬山顶砖木结构。

重檐式门楼，门楼后为过屋，面阔一间3.54米，进深一间1.98米，后两角各有一柱，前部直接架在院墙上，两面坡式瓦顶。

两侧为厢房，均面阔三间10.9米，进深一间5.68米，前有走廊，中部抬梁式构架，两侧砖墙直接承搁梁架。

正堂面阔五间17.1米，进深三间8.07米，两侧靠山墙为穿斗式，中部抬梁式构架。大殿前有檐廊，月梁是一组木雕，内容有缠枝牡丹、喜鹊登梅等。

正堂山墙檐廊壁嵌石碑2通，一为'郭氏家族十条公议规则'，一为修建郭营祠堂经过，均刻于清光绪十六年（1891）。

English 英文

Guo's Ancestral Hall is located in Guoying Village, Lutou Town, Zaoyang City, in the low hill area of northern Zaoyang. It faces south, with a rectangular plane and a three-sided courtyard layout. The total width is 17.1 meters and the total depth is 20 meters. It has a gable roof and brick-wood structure. The double-eave gate tower is followed by a passage house, one bay wide, 3.54 meters, and one bay deep, 1.98 meters; there is a column at each of the two rear corners, and the front part is directly framed on the courtyard wall, with a two-slope tile roof. On both sides are wing rooms, each three bays wide, 10.9 meters, and one bay deep, 5.68 meters, with a corridor in front, a post-and-lintel frame in the middle, and brick walls on both sides directly supporting the beam frames. The main hall is five bays wide, 17.1 meters, and three bays deep, 8.07 meters; the two sides against the gable walls are of column-and-tie style, and the middle has a post-and-lintel frame. In front of the main hall there is an eaves porch; the moon beam is a set of wood carvings, with contents such as interlocking peonies and magpies climbing plum blossoms. On the wall of the eaves porch of the gable wall of the main hall, 2 stone steles are embedded; one is 'Ten Public Discussion Rules of the Guo Family,' and the other is the process of building Guo's Ancestral Hall, both carved in the 16th year of Guangxu, Qing (1891).

314. 无量台

Wuliang Hall (Beamless Hall)
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
枣阳吴店镇陈湾村
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
无梁之结构形式无量台又名无量祖师殿位于枣阳市吴店镇陈湾村庙坡自然村西始建于明代清乾隆年间扩建相传原为东汉光武帝刘秀起兵所筑点将台后人为纪念刘秀建庙供奉后成为道教场所更名无量祖师殿建筑主体所在的土台系人为筑成略呈圆形中间高四周低
中文 Chinese

无量台，又名无量祖师殿，位于枣阳市吴店镇陈湾村庙坡自然村西，始建于明代，清乾隆年间扩建，相传原为东汉光武帝刘秀起兵所筑点将台，后人为纪念刘秀建庙供奉，后成为道教场所，更名无量祖师殿。

建筑主体所在的土台系人为筑成，略呈圆形，中间高四周低，直径约100米，现最高处约5米。

原有建筑坐北朝南，基本呈中轴线对称布局，有殿门、前殿、无梁亭、正殿、偏殿等建筑，无量台为平面方形全砖攒尖顶亭式结构，无栋无梁，长6.2米，宽5.82米，顶高10米，内祀刘秀，无量台后及东西各有三间正殿、偏殿，正殿供奉道教祖师。

台南10米建有前殿，东西有厢房，前部为殿门。除前殿外所有建筑均于1966年被毁。

前殿硬山顶砖木结构，面阔三间11.6米，进深三间8.35米，脊高5.2米。两侧为穿斗式，中间为抬梁式构架，两侧山墙顶部前后各出墀头。

明间前部缩进2.1米，中部开门，两侧呈'八'字墙，次间前壁中部开窗。原供奉关羽及关平、周仓，现塑像不存，建筑破损亦较为严重。前殿东侧残存1通石碑，残长0.8米、宽0.52米、厚0.15米，碑文因剥蚀严重不清。

English 英文

Wuliang Hall, also called Wuliang (Beamless) Patriarch Hall, is located west of Miaopo natural village, Chenwan Village, Wudian Town, Zaoyang City; it was first built in the Ming and expanded during the Qianlong period of the Qing. Legend has it that it was originally a general-appointing platform built by Emperor Guangwu of Han Liu Xiu when he raised troops; later generations built a temple to worship Liu Xiu in commemoration, and it later became a Taoist site, renamed Wuliang Patriarch Hall. The earthen platform where the main building is located was artificially built, slightly circular, high in the middle and low around, with a diameter of about 100 meters, and the highest point now is about 5 meters. The original buildings faced south, basically in a centrally symmetric layout, including a temple gate, front hall, beamless pavilion, main hall, and side halls; Wuliang Hall is a square-plan all-brick pyramidal-roof pavilion-style structure, without purlins or beams, 6.2 meters long, 5.82 meters wide, and 10 meters high at the top, enshrining Liu Xiu inside; behind Wuliang Hall and to the east and west there are respectively three bays of main hall and side hall, with the main hall enshrining the Taoist patriarch. 10 meters south of the platform, a front hall was built, with wing rooms on the east and west, and the front part is the temple gate. All buildings except the front hall were destroyed in 1966. The front hall has a gable roof and brick-wood structure, three bays wide, 11.6 meters, three bays deep, 8.35 meters, with a ridge height of 5.2 meters. The two sides are of column-and-tie style, and the middle has a post-and-lintel frame; the top of the gable walls on both sides has chi (projecting gable tops) at the front and rear. The front part of the central bay is recessed by 2.1 meters, with a door in the middle, and the two sides form an 'eight'-shaped wall; the front wall of the secondary bays has windows in the middle. It originally enshrined Guan Yu, Guan Ping, and Zhou Cang; now the statues no longer exist, and the building is also relatively severely damaged. On the east side of the front hall, 1 stone stele remains, with a remaining length of 0.8 meters, a width of 0.52 meters, and a thickness of 0.15 meters; the inscription is unclear due to severe erosion.

315. 徐庶祠

Memorial Hall of Xu Shu
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
南漳县城关镇徐庶路10-1号
类型 Type
礼制建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
平面格局徐庶祠位于南漳县城关镇徐庶路又名单公祠、徐庶庙徐庶字元直河南颍川人汉初平中客居荆州向刘备推荐诸葛亮后从曹操官至右中郎将、御史中丞祠始建于清嘉庆元年1949年后多次维修建筑坐北朝南
中文 Chinese

徐庶祠位于南漳县城关镇徐庶路，又名单公祠、徐庶庙。徐庶（？—232），字元直，河南颍川人，汉初平（190—193）中客居荆州，向刘备推荐诸葛亮于此，后从曹操，官至右中郎将、御史中丞。祠始建于清嘉庆元年（1796），1949年后多次维修。

建筑坐北朝南，由门楼、前厅、后殿及过廊组成两进小院。门楼四柱三开间单檐硬山楼阁式，明间升高置大门。两次间立面墙上分书'虎啸''龙吟'行体大字。门前有嘉庆十七年（1812）所竖'汉徐庶故里'碑。

前厅、后殿均为面阔三间、进深二间的硬山顶建筑，后殿殿内有徐庶塑像。现辟为南漳县博物馆。

English 英文

Xu Shu Memorial Hall is located on Xushu Road, Chengguan Town, Nanzhang County, also called Shan Gong Shrine or Xu Shu Temple. Xu Shu (?–232), courtesy name Yuanzhi, was a native of Yingchuan, Henan; during the Chuping period of the Han (190–193), he sojourned in Jingzhou and recommended Zhuge Liang to Liu Bei here; later he followed Cao Cao, serving as Right General of the Household and Censor-in-Chief. The shrine was first built in the 1st year of Jiaqing, Qing (1796), and repaired many times after 1949. The building faces south, consisting of a gate tower, front hall, rear hall, and passage corridor, forming two small courtyards. The gate tower is a four-column three-bay single-eave gable pavilion style, with the central bay raised to place the main gate. On the facade walls of the two secondary bays, the running-script large characters 'Hu Xiao' (Tiger Roars) and 'Long Yin' (Dragon Chants) are written separately. In front of the gate stands the 'Former Residence of Han Xu Shu' stele erected in the 17th year of Jiaqing (1812). The front hall and rear hall are both gable-roof buildings three bays wide and two bays deep; inside the rear hall there is a statue of Xu Shu. It is now opened as the Nanzhang County Museum.

316. 板桥民居/冯氏民居

Vernacular Dwellings in Banqiao / Feng's Residence
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
南漳县板桥镇冯家湾村
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
砖雕木雕平面格局板桥民居又名冯哲夫民居、冯公干民居位于南漳板桥镇冯家湾村是一处庄园式建筑始建于明朝崇祯年间原为陶姓人家所有后被冯姓家族购得曾是辛亥革命国民临时政府内务部长、国务总监冯开浚（字哲夫）的住所建筑坐北朝南依山就势
中文 Chinese

板桥民居，又名冯哲夫民居、冯公干民居，位于南漳板桥镇冯家湾村。是一处庄园式建筑，始建于明朝崇祯年间，原为陶姓人家所有，后被冯姓家族购得，曾是辛亥革命国民临时政府内务部长、国务总监冯开浚（字哲夫）的住所。建筑坐北朝南，依山就势，左环右抱，前低后高。

整个建筑群规模宏大，南北进深较浅，南面设置空场及石砌围堰，形成了背山面水的理想格局。建筑群为三路两进四合院式中心对称布局，主要房屋共5栋，大小房间105间，均为单檐硬山灰瓦顶。中路采用正面开门的形式，左右两路对称采用正面开门、山墙收头的形式。

每路院落均分正门、中门、侧门，由大门进入一进院落，后又分两个中门分别进入第二进院落，侧门则与其他院落相连，形成了三路九院落的基本格局。建筑自前向后依山势逐步抬高，有前堂、过厅、后堂及左右偏房。中路规模最大。

正门采用了凹入式石门楼的形式，结合门匾题字、檐口轩顶收口等手法进行重点处理。第一进为东西狭长的长方形院落，长约30米，进深仅7米，两个中门面对一进院落对称开门，这样形成了中厅并非正对正门的独特格局；

中厅比一进院落高出七级台阶，中门的处理同样是采用了石鼓、石坎的石门匾题字的形式；前堂通面阔七间29米，进深一间4.9米。

第二进院落为边长大约6米的方院，正堂也高出院落七级台阶，形成了三级台地，很自然地利用了地形高差，使空间变化比较丰富：正堂前为穿廊，设置侧门及与二楼联系的楼梯，两旁东西厢房对称布置，二楼采用独特的挑廊处理，不形成环廊，第二进被分割为左、右两个小天井院，过厅均面阔三间，均...

English 英文

Banqiao vernacular dwellings, also called Feng Zhefu Residence or Feng Gonggan Residence, are located in Fengjiawan Village, Banqiao Town, Nanzhang County. It is a manor-style building, first built during the Chongzhen period of the Ming, originally owned by the Tao family, later purchased by the Feng family, and was once the residence of Feng Kaijun (courtesy name Zhefu), Minister of the Interior and Chief Supervisor of State Affairs of the Provisional Government of the Republic of China during the Xinhai Revolution. The building faces south, following the mountain terrain, surrounded on left and right, low in front and high at the back. The entire building complex is large in scale, with a shallow north-south depth; an open field and a stone-built cofferdam are set on the south, forming an ideal pattern of backing the mountain and facing the water. The building complex has a three-row two-entry courtyard-style centrally symmetric layout, with a total of 5 main buildings and 105 rooms of various sizes, all with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs. The middle row adopts the form of opening doors on the front, and the left and right rows symmetrically adopt the form of opening doors on the front and closing the gable walls. Each row of courtyards is divided into a main gate, middle gate, and side gate; entering the first-entry courtyard through the main gate, it is then divided into two middle gates respectively entering the second-entry courtyard, and the side gates connect with other courtyards, forming the basic pattern of three rows and nine courtyards. The building gradually rises from front to back along the mountain terrain, with a front hall, passage hall, rear hall, and left and right side rooms. The middle row is the largest in scale. The main gate adopts the form of a recessed stone gate tower, combined with methods such as inscribed door plaques and eave cornice closure for key treatment. The first entry is an east-west long and narrow rectangular courtyard, about 30 meters long and only 7 meters deep; the two middle gates open symmetrically facing the first-entry courtyard, thus forming a unique pattern where the middle hall is not directly opposite the main gate; the middle hall is seven steps higher than the first-entry courtyard, and the treatment of the middle gate also adopts the form of stone drums and stone sills with inscribed stone door plaques; the front hall has a total width of seven bays, 29 meters, and one bay deep, 4.9 meters. The second-entry courtyard is a square courtyard with a side length of about 6 meters; the main hall is also seven steps higher than the courtyard, forming three terraces, naturally utilizing the terrain height difference to make the spatial changes relatively rich: in front of the main hall is a passage corridor, with side gates and stairs connecting to the second floor; the east and west wing rooms on both sides are symmetrically arranged; the second floor adopts a unique挑廊 (projecting corridor) treatment, not forming a surrounding corridor; the second entry is divided into left and right two small courtyard (tianjing) courtyards, and the passage halls are all three bays wide, all...

选址环境水镜庄又名白马洞始建于清乾隆七年光绪十三年、十六年、三十二年、民国二十五年增修、扩建依山势而建坐南朝北占地面积约3000平方米水镜庄位于南漳县城南0.5公里处北临蛮河南靠玉溪山依山面水
中文 Chinese

水镜庄又名白马洞，始建于清乾隆七年（1742），光绪十三年（1887）、十六年（1890）、三十二年（1906）、民国二十五年（1936）增修、扩建。依山势而建，坐南朝北，占地面积约3000平方米。

水镜庄位于南漳县城南0.5公里处。北临蛮河，南靠玉溪山，依山面水，风光绮丽。庄前的蛮河弯弯如带，飘飘东去；庄后的玉溪山山势陡峭，林木繁茂，雄伟壮观。东汉末年司马徽曾在此隐居，因他又称水镜先生，山庄也因此而称水镜庄。

庄前立有石碑，上书'汉水镜栖隐处'，为清乾隆七年（1742年）南漳知县徐彦所书。石碑左侧为荐贤堂，两进平房，中隔小院，每进三间，建筑庄重古朴，占地约300平方米。

山之北麓横陈数块如刀削之石壁，西起永丰渠首，东至螃蟹眼旁，全长1200米，有'三里石壁长廊'之称。最大石壁高50米，长280米，巍峨壮观，形似赤壁。壁中有巨洞，传说昔有白马出洞，故名白马洞。

洞高8米，宽10米，深30米，可容百人。洞中建有水镜祠。左侧有一幽暗小洞，高2米，宽1米，内有深潭，用砖石堵塞。庄后有两小径通白马洞。

一条沿头天门上山，出荐贤堂南行，过石拱小桥，行数步，登14级台阶，进头天门，再攀登43级台阶至二天门。沿石壁向西凿有横道，全长42米。外侧筑有城墙，有城垛25个。出横道下几级石阶，迎面即是会仙门。过会仙门上十几步石阶，左折即入白马洞。

另一山径在头天门之西，是倚山而上的土路，要经过水镜祠门楼。门楼横...

English 英文

Shuijing Residence, also called White Horse Cave, was first built in the 7th year of Qianlong, Qing (1742), and was additionally repaired and expanded in the 13th year of Guangxu (1887), 16th year (1890), 32nd year (1906), and 25th year of the Republic (1936). Built along the mountain terrain, it faces north from south, covering an area of about 3000 square meters. Shuijing Residence is located 0.5 km south of Nanzhang County seat. It faces the Man River to the north and backs onto Yuxi Mountain to the south, leaning against the mountain and facing the water, with beautiful scenery. The Man River in front of the residence winds like a belt, floating eastward; the Yuxi Mountain behind the residence has steep terrain and lush forests, magnificent and spectacular. At the end of the Eastern Han, Sima Hui once lived in seclusion here; because he was also called Mr. Shuijing (Water Mirror), the mountain villa was hence called Shuijing Residence. In front of the residence stands a stone stele, inscribed with 'Place Where Han Shuijing Lived in Seclusion,' written by Xu Yan, Magistrate of Nanzhang in the 7th year of Qianlong, Qing (1742). To the left of the stone stele is the Jianxian (Recommending Sages) Hall, two entries of bungalows, separated by a small courtyard, three bays per entry; the building is solemn and simple, covering about 300 square meters. On the northern foot of the mountain, several knife-cut stone walls lie horizontally, starting from the head of Yongfeng Canal in the west to the side of Pangxie Eye in the east, with a total length of 1200 meters, known as the 'Three-Li Stone Wall Corridor.' The largest stone wall is 50 meters high and 280 meters long, towering and spectacular, shaped like Red Cliff. In the middle of the wall there is a giant cave; legend has it that in the past a white horse came out of the cave, hence named White Horse Cave. The cave is 8 meters high, 10 meters wide, and 30 meters deep, capable of holding a hundred people. Inside the cave is built the Shuijing Shrine. On the left side there is a dark small cave, 2 meters high and 1 meter wide, with a deep pool inside, blocked with bricks and stones. Behind the residence there are two small paths leading to White Horse Cave. One goes up the mountain along the First Heavenly Gate: going south from the Jianxian Hall, crossing a small stone arch bridge, walking a few steps, climbing 14 steps, entering the First Heavenly Gate, then climbing 43 steps to the Second Heavenly Gate. Along the stone wall to the west, a horizontal path is chiseled, with a total length of 42 meters. On the outer side, a city wall is built, with 25 crenellations. Leaving the horizontal path and going down a few stone steps, facing you is the Huixian (Meeting Immortals) Gate. Passing through the Huixian Gate and going up more than ten stone steps, turning left, you enter White Horse Cave. The other mountain path is west of the First Heavenly Gate, a dirt road going up the mountain, passing through the gate tower of Shuijing Shrine. The gate tower horizontally...

中文 Chinese

东巩民居包括田家湾民居、蔡家棚民居等，位于东巩镇口泉村，四周群山围绕，有着原始的自然风光，民居保存良好。田家湾民居建于清代，建筑为三路两进四合院，各路均面阔三间，除正屋单层，余两层为硬山顶砖木结构。

English 英文

Donggong vernacular dwellings include Tianjiawan dwellings, Caijiapeng dwellings, etc., located in Kouquan Village, Donggong Town, surrounded by mountains on all sides, with primitive natural scenery, and the dwellings are well-preserved. Tianjiawan dwellings were built in the Qing; the building is a three-row two-entry courtyard, each row three bays wide; except for the main house which is single-story, the rest are two-story gable-roof brick-wood structures. Caijiapeng dwellings were also built in the Qing; the building is a two-entry courtyard, three bays wide, a two-story gable-roof brick-wood structure. After a hundred years of baptism, although the interior is somewhat dilapidated, it still gives people a sense of solemnity and majesty.

Ganxi vernacular dwellings, also called Manyun dwellings, are located in Ganxi Village, Xunjian Town; the old street consists of Upper Street and Lower Street, running east-west; the dwellings on both sides of the street are built facing each other north and south, with a bluestone-paved street in the middle. There are more than 20 dwellings in total, generally courtyards, two or three entries, with gable roofs and brick-wood structures, many also having the nature of shops. One of them, facing south, covers an area of 182 square meters. It has a courtyard layout, with a front hall, left and right wing rooms, and a main room. They all have single-eave gable gray-tile roofs and post-and-lintel frames. The foundation of the main room is 1.06 meters higher than that of the front hall.

都家巷民居也是南漳古民居的代表，位于巡检镇甘溪乡，两山环抱之间有溪，截为水库，沿水库两边各分布两组规模不大的建筑群，装饰精美，用材粗大，其中尤以位于小溪北面的王氏民居较为典型。

Dujiaxiang vernacular dwellings are also representative of ancient dwellings in Nanzhang; they are located in Ganxi Township, Xunjian Town, with a stream between the embrace of two mountains, dammed into a reservoir; along both sides of the reservoir, two groups of not-large-scale building complexes are distributed respectively, with exquisite decoration and thick and large materials; among them, the Wang's residence located north of the small stream is particularly typical. Wang's Residence No.1 is located north of Dujiaxiang Village, covering about 544 square meters; the existing middle and right road courtyards have a relatively large scale, with a front hall, main room, and left and right wing rooms; a partition remains in the middle of the front hall, retaining the side-door form. The overall architectural form is a single-eave gable gray-tile roof; the entrance adopts an external eight-character gate tower; the wall tops at both ends of the gate tower are covered with gray-tile flying eaves, with dynamic and smooth lines; the stone carvings on the stone door, stone drums, stone sills, and stone frames of the main gate are rich and exquisite.

English 英文

The Jiamazhai Paper Mill is located in Fengjiawan Village, Banqiao Town, built in the Qing; it has three trough rooms, with an overhanging gable roof and earth-wood structure, 2 rotting material pools, and 1 water diversion channel. There is 1 oil-press workshop and 16 paper-making workshops. Among them, the layout and structure of the oil-press workshop are similar to those of residential shops. The paper-making workshops are all located in the mountainous area of Nanzhang, beside rivers, generally composed of trough rooms, rotting material pools, water diversion channels, trough pools, water wheels, etc. The trough rooms basically have overhanging gable roofs; some have stone-built walls with rammed-earth (gan-dalei) style walls; some have walls built with flagstones or block stones. The beam frames are directly supported on the walls, with small tile roofs. Some also have tools such as mills and pestles.

Yanshan Watch Tower is also called Sifangping Watch Tower. It is a one-entry courtyard overhanging-gable tower-style watch tower building; a five-story watch tower was built in the northeast corner by the rammed-earth (gan-dalei) method; the watch tower has four stories above ground and one basement; on the four walls above the ground of the watch tower, square holes of various sizes are set, used for lookout and shooting. The watch tower and the surrounding three residences form a mutual corner, connected into one piece, becoming a private residential building complex integrating defense and residential functions. 中文 Chinese

板桥乡公所旧址位于南漳县板桥镇新集村，处于一弯月形山脚中部。始建于1921年，系民国时期重要史迹及代表性建筑。原为当地乡绅冯伯元居所。

20世纪30年代，其子冯达夫担任板桥乡乡长后，为抵御'匪患'侵袭，在原居所基础上加盖左右和南北对称的三间二层围屋，并在乡公所西南角建造了碉楼。建筑坐北朝南，依山势而建，平面呈横长方形，自南向北渐高沿十字线成对称布局。

面阔20米、通进深23.5米。其四面围合成一个整体，中部形成一个天井院，上层内侧有回廊相通。均为两层硬山顶土木结构，穿斗与抬梁相结合梁架，墙体采用干打垒方式构成。共有大小房间49间。

西南角干打垒式建造有一座五层方形碉楼，高14米。

English 英文

The Historic Site of Banqiao Township Office is located in Xinji Village, Banqiao Town, Nanzhang County, in the middle of a crescent-shaped mountain foot. It was first built in 1921 and is an important historical site and representative building of the Republican period. It was originally the residence of local gentry Feng Boyuan. In the 1930s, after his son Feng Dafu served as the township head of Banqiao Township, to resist the invasion of 'banditry,' three two-story surrounding houses symmetric on left-right and north-south were added on the basis of the original residence, and a watch tower was built at the southwest corner of the township office. The building faces south, built along the mountain terrain, with a horizontal rectangular plane, gradually rising from south to north and symmetrically laid out along the cross line. It is 20 meters wide and 23.5 meters deep in total. Its four sides enclose into a whole, forming a courtyard (tianjing) in the middle, with corridors connecting on the inner side of the upper floor. They are all two-story gable-roof earth-wood structures, with beam frames combining column-and-tie and post-and-lintel styles, and walls constructed by the rammed-earth (gan-dalei) method. There are a total of 49 rooms of various sizes. At the southwest corner, a five-story square watch tower was built by the rammed-earth method, 14 meters high.

中文 Chinese

承恩寺始建于隋大业年间（605—618），位于谷城县茨河镇五朵山北麓，背靠狮子岩，面对五朵山，峰岗拱卫，清泉流淌，茂林修竹，景色幽奇，为风水形胜绝佳之地，相传为隋炀帝的公主隐居疗疾之地。

该寺原名宝严寺，唐改名广德寺，宋、元屡毁屡建，明永乐二十一年（1423）重修，天顺年间，明英宗朱祁镇为报答叔父襄王朱瞻培对自己复辟的帮助，改广德寺为'大承恩寺'，再次对该寺进行修缮，承恩寺因此而得名。嘉靖四十二年（1563）再次重修，清代多次整修。

承恩寺坐北朝南，占地面积1237平方米。整体建筑依山叠起，中轴对称布局，前低后高。沿中轴线...

English 英文

Cheng'en Temple was first built during the Daye period of the Sui (605–618), located at the northern foot of Wuduo Mountain, Cihe Town, Gucheng County, backing onto Lion Rock and facing Wuduo Mountain, with peaks and hills guarding, clear springs flowing, dense forests and tall bamboos, and a secluded and wonderful scenery; it is an excellent place of fengshui scenic beauty, legendarily the place where the princess of Emperor Yang of Sui lived in seclusion to treat illness. The temple was originally named Baoyan Temple, renamed Guangde Temple in the Tang, repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt in the Song and Yuan, repaired in the 21st year of Yongle, Ming (1423); during the Tianshun period, Emperor Yingzong of Ming Zhu Qizhen, to repay his uncle Prince Xiang Zhu Zhanpei for his help in his restoration, changed Guangde Temple to 'Da Cheng'en Temple' (Great Temple of Receiving Grace), and repaired the temple again; Cheng'en Temple thus got its name. It was repaired again in the 42nd year of Jiajing (1563), and repaired many times in the Qing. Cheng'en Temple faces south, covering an area of 1237 square meters. The overall building rises in layers along the mountain, with a centrally symmetric layout, low in front and high at the back. Along the central axis...

325. 三神殿

Hall of Three Gods
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
谷城县城关镇中码头街
类型 Type

看点 Highlights
平面格局三神殿始建于明末清初原址为一座道观因年久失修道观被毁当地回民商贾出资在道观基础上修建三神殿以供奉财神、水神和雷神清道光二十三年、二十七年、民国二十五年维修三神殿所在地面临南河背靠汉江历史上是水陆码头要冲历来商贾云集
中文 Chinese

三神殿始建于明末清初，原址为一座道观，因年久失修，道观被毁，当地回民商贾出资在道观基础上修建三神殿，以供奉财神、水神和雷神。清道光二十三年（1843）、二十七年（1847）、民国二十五年（1936）维修。

三神殿所在地面临南河，背靠汉江，历史上是水陆码头要冲，历来商贾云集，物流繁忙，车水马龙，不同行业的人都要供奉各自尊崇的神灵，因此有了三神同居一庙的奇特形式。同时，三神殿还具有回民会馆的性质。在清代，这里一直是各省回民的聚集之地。

辛亥革命时，海风山的部队攻破谷城后，司令部亦设于此。建筑坐北朝南，占地面积约2400平方米。三进四合院式布局，有门楼、前殿、中殿、后殿及厢房。山门和戏楼连在一起，戏楼为单檐歇山屋面。

戏楼屋面后坡与山门屋面后坡相连，形成'丁'字形整体。戏楼基本保存完好。中殿为硬山式屋面，砖木结构，面阔三间，进深三间，建筑正中供奉三神，左为雷神，中为水神，右为财神。

后殿为两层硬山式建筑，砖木结构，面阔三间，进深三间，建在高台之上，底层明...

English 英文

The Hall of Three Gods was first built at the end of the Ming and beginning of the Qing; its original site was a Taoist temple, which was destroyed due to long-term disrepair; local Hui merchants funded the construction of the Hall of Three Gods on the basis of the Taoist temple to enshrine the God of Wealth, God of Water, and God of Thunder. It was repaired in the 23rd year of Daoguang, Qing (1843), the 27th year (1847), and the 25th year of the Republic (1936). The place where the Hall of Three Gods is located faces the Nan River and backs onto the Han River; historically it was a strategic point of land and water docks, always gathering merchants, with busy logistics and heavy traffic; people of different trades all had to enshrine their respective revered gods, hence the peculiar form of three gods dwelling together in one temple. At the same time, the Hall of Three Gods also had the nature of a Hui guild hall. In the Qing, this was always a gathering place for Hui people from all provinces. During the Xinhai Revolution, after Haifengshan's troops captured Gucheng, the headquarters was also set up here. The building faces south, covering an area of about 2400 square meters. It has a three-entry courtyard layout, with a gate tower, front hall, middle hall, rear hall, and wing rooms. The mountain gate and theater tower are connected together; the theater tower has a single-eave hip-and-gable roof. The rear slope of the theater tower roof is connected with the rear slope of the mountain gate roof, forming a 'T'-shaped whole. The theater tower is basically well-preserved. The middle hall has a gable roof, of brick-wood structure, three bays wide and three bays deep; in the center of the building are enshrined the three gods, with the God of Thunder on the left, God of Water in the middle, and God of Wealth on the right. The rear hall is a two-story gable building, of brick-wood structure, three bays wide and three bays deep, built on a high platform; the ground floor central bay...

326. 谷城老街古建筑群

Ancient Building Complex on the Old Street of Gucheng
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清、民国
地址 Address
谷城县城关镇老街、中码头街
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
老街格局谷城老街明清古建筑群始建于明代初年形成于明代中叶兴盛于明末清初鼎盛于清代和民国明洪武二年谷城知县方文俊创建谷城土城时城东南靠河边之地已形成街道并已建成南河码头明成化年间南河码头已建成上码头、中码头和下码头老街的七街一巷（老街、五发街、五福街、中码头街、米粮街、新街、三神殿巷子）已经完全形成并成为谷城经济文化中心和名闻荆楚的鄂西北最大的商品集散地之一谷城老街街道呈四横三纵布局
中文 Chinese

谷城老街明清古建筑群始建于明代初年，形成于明代中叶，兴盛于明末清初，鼎盛于清代和民国。明洪武二年（1369）谷城知县方文俊创建谷城土城时，城东南靠河边之地已形成街道，并已建成南河码头。

明成化年间（1465—1487）南河码头已建成上码头、中码头和下码头，老街的七街一巷（老街、五发街、五福街、中码头街、米粮街、新街、三神殿巷子）已经完全形成，并成为谷城经济文化中心和名闻荆楚的鄂西北最大的商品集散地之一。

谷城老街街道呈四横三纵布局，占地面积1.2平方公里，现存古建筑共214座（三进41座、二进173座）。古建筑所有房屋面向街道。整体建筑仍然保持明清古建筑的风貌，整个建筑群以徽派风格（天井院、马头墙、白墙黑瓦）为主，兼有北方特征。

建筑布局前店后寝，沿街为二层房，下层经营，二层主要用于储存货物或外来客商临时住宿。门面房是由前后正屋和两边单坡厢房组成的2—3个不等的天井院。店铺之间由硬山墙紧密相接，有利于邻里交往；

七街、一巷、六条道子相互连接，每条街道都由多进宅院组成，每座宅院都由街巷贯通。沿街店铺，硬山重檐，青砖灰瓦，木铺板门。建筑用色以黑为主调，门面铺板、梁上垫板、门窗梁柱，均着黑漆。

English 英文

The Ming and Qing ancient building complex on Gucheng Old Street was first built in the early Ming, formed in the mid-Ming, flourished at the end of the Ming and beginning of the Qing, and reached its peak in the Qing and Republican periods. In the 2nd year of Hongwu, Ming (1369), when Fang Wenjun, Magistrate of Gucheng, built the earthen city of Gucheng, the land southeast of the city by the river had already formed streets, and the Nan River dock had already been built. During the Chenghua period of the Ming (1465–1487), the Nan River dock had built the Upper Dock, Middle Dock, and Lower Dock; the seven streets and one lane of the old street (Old Street, Wufa Street, Wufu Street, Zhongmatou Street, Miliang Street, Xin Street, Sandian Lane) had been completely formed, and became the economic and cultural center of Gucheng and one of the largest commodity distribution centers in northwest Hubei, famous throughout Jingchu. The streets of Gucheng Old Street have a four-horizontal-three-vertical layout, covering an area of 1.2 square kilometers; the existing ancient buildings total 214 (41 with three entries, 173 with two entries). All houses of the ancient buildings face the street. The overall architecture still maintains the style of Ming and Qing ancient buildings; the entire building complex is mainly in the Huizhou style (courtyard (tianjing) yards, horse-head walls, white walls and black tiles), with northern characteristics. The building layout is shop in front and residence behind; along the street are two-story houses, with the lower floor for business and the second floor mainly for storing goods or temporary accommodation for visiting merchants. The front shops are 2–3不等 courtyard (tianjing) yards composed of front and rear main rooms and single-slope wing rooms on both sides. Shops are closely connected by gable walls, facilitating neighborhood interaction; the seven streets, one lane, and six alleys are interconnected; each street is composed of multi-entry residences, and each residence is贯通 by streets and alleys. Street-facing shops have gable double eaves, blue bricks and gray tiles, and wooden plank doors. The building color scheme is mainly black; the front shop planks, beam backing boards, doors, windows, beams, and columns are all painted black lacquer.

327. 万寿宫

Wanshou Hall
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
谷城县盛镇后街
类型 Type
商业与手工业建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
建筑形制万寿宫位于盛镇后街又名江西会馆始建于道光元年一说乾隆癸卯年始建清道光元年重修光绪二十七年十月重修民国时期重修坐西南朝东北占地面积1385平方米四合院式布局现存正殿和戏楼
中文 Chinese

万寿宫位于盛镇后街，又名江西会馆。始建于道光元年（1821），一说乾隆癸卯年（1783）始建，清道光元年（1821）重修，光绪二十七年（1901）十月重修，民国时期重修。

坐西南朝东北，占地面积1385平方米，四合院式布局。现存正殿和戏楼。戏楼面阔五间21.7米，通进深16.8米，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，穿斗式构架，分上下两层，现左侧已坍塌；

正殿面阔三间14.7米，进深三间10.7米，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，两侧为穿斗式梁架，中部为抬梁式。前壁为隔扇，三间各开一门。

前有一宽3.6米的走廊，立廊柱两根，其上端以斗拱支撑檐枋。所用木柱围径1.04米，下垫直径1.3米的石础。部分建筑用砖上模印'江西'二字。

English 英文

Wanshou Hall is located on Back Street, Sheng Town, also called Jiangxi Guild Hall. It was first built in the 1st year of Daoguang (1821), one says first built in the Gui-Mao year of Qianlong (1783); it was repaired in the 1st year of Daoguang, Qing (1821), in October of the 27th year of Guangxu (1901), and during the Republican period. It faces northeast from southwest, covering an area of 1385 square meters, with a courtyard layout. The existing buildings include the main hall and theater tower. The theater tower is five bays wide, 21.7 meters, with a total depth of 16.8 meters, a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, and a column-and-tie frame, divided into upper and lower two stories; now the left side has collapsed; the main hall is three bays wide, 14.7 meters, and three bays deep, 10.7 meters, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, column-and-tie beam frames on both sides, and a post-and-lintel frame in the middle. The front wall is lattice doors and windows, with one door opened in each of the three bays. In front there is a corridor 3.6 meters wide, with two porch columns, whose upper ends support the eave lintel with bracket sets. The wooden columns used have a circumference of 1.04 meters, with stone plinths 1.3 meters in diameter underneath. Some building bricks are molded with the two characters 'Jiangxi'.

328. 吴氏庄园

Wu's Mansion
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
保康县歇马镇白竹村石磐岭
类型 Type
居住建筑
看点 Highlights
石雕木雕壁画吴氏庄园又称吴德峰故居吴德峰1949年后任武汉市首任市长建筑始建于晚清时期祖屋庄园位于海拔1100米的一个坡地上为晚清鄂西北典型的庄园式建筑其结构、雕花门窗、石质窗格、石阶、防火墙、壁画等都具有非常独特的民居风格大量的壁画、石刻、木雕现仍依稀可见建筑背倚山体坐西朝东
中文 Chinese

吴氏庄园又称吴德峰故居。吴德峰，1949年后任武汉市首任市长。建筑始建于晚清时期，祖屋庄园位于海拔1100米的一个坡地上，为晚清鄂西北典型的庄园式建筑。

其结构、雕花门窗、石质窗格、石阶、防火墙、壁画等都具有非常独特的民居风格，大量的壁画、石刻、木雕现仍依稀可见。建筑背倚山体，坐西朝东，整组建筑占地面积3500平方米，建筑面积1320平方米。

建筑有两进院落，前进大天井三合院，面阔十间，后并列三个小四合院，中路四合面阔三间。除正屋单层外余两层硬山顶砖木结构。

庄园外观古朴典雅，装饰重点主要在正厅前后檐轩廊和木构件雕刻、彩绘，以及正堂高耸的五花山墙，被朴素的青瓦屋面衬托出几分华丽的风采。建筑主屋系徽派风格，次房以半坡覆顶，院落里有依地而盘的一整块山石，引人注目。整个庄园构思精巧，布局浑然一体。

除起居生活空间，戏台、私塾、药铺、粮仓等一应俱全。正堂、山墙、雕花窗棂、板壁、磉蹬、石壁、壁画和廊柱等保存完好，是保康现存规模较大、保存最为完整的民居之一。建筑的匾额由三块木板拼合而成，长185厘米，宽85厘米。

右端自上而下题写着'大总统题褒'5字；主题匾文为'志洁行芳'，为黑漆浮雕，字迹清晰，保存完整；木匾左端，从右到左自上而下为跋文'保康节妇吴陈氏'，落款日期为'中华民国五年四月'，其正上方还刻有'荣典之玺'，约14厘米见方。

据考证，此匾为民国大总统袁世凯为吴元泽儿媳陈氏（长子吴世特妻子，18岁病故）题写，当时悬挂在武昌吴家（时从武昌蛇山到黄土坡即今首义路均为吴家房产），1938年武汉沦陷前夕由吴元钧继室龚敬勤（1948年在保康病故）带回保康祖宅。

English 英文

Wu's Mansion is also called the Former Residence of Wu Defeng. Wu Defeng served as the first mayor of Wuhan after 1949. The building was first built in the late Qing period; the ancestral mansion is located on a slope at an altitude of 1100 meters, and is a typical manor-style building of northwest Hubei in the late Qing. Its structure, carved doors and windows, stone window grilles, stone steps, fire walls, murals, etc., all have a very unique vernacular dwelling style; a large number of murals, stone carvings, and wood carvings are still faintly visible today. The building backs onto the mountain body, faces east from west, and the entire building complex covers an area of 3500 square meters, with a building area of 1320 square meters. The building has two courtyards; the front entry is a large courtyard (tianjing) three-sided courtyard, ten bays wide; behind it are three small courtyards arranged side by side, with the middle-road courtyard three bays wide. Except for the main house which is single-story, the rest are two-story gable-roof brick-wood structures. The exterior of the mansion is simple and elegant; the decorative focus is mainly on the front and rear eaves porches of the main hall, the carving and painting of wooden components, and the towering five-flower gable wall of the main hall, which is set off by the simple blue-tile roof to show a bit of gorgeous style. The main house of the building is in the Huizhou style, and the secondary houses are covered with half-slope roofs; in the courtyard there is a whole block of mountain stone coiled according to the terrain, eye-catching. The entire mansion is exquisitely conceived, with an integrated layout. In addition to living spaces, there is a theater stage, private school, pharmacy, granary, etc., all available. The main hall, gable walls, carved window lattice, plank walls, plinths, stone walls, murals, and porch columns are well-preserved, and it is one of the larger-scale and best-preserved vernacular dwellings existing in Baokang. The inscribed plaque of the building is composed of three wooden boards joined together, 185 cm long and 85 cm wide. At the right end, from top to bottom, are inscribed the 5 characters 'Bestowed and Praised by the Great President'; the main plaque text is 'Zhi Jie Xing Fang' (Pure Will and Virtuous Conduct), in black lacquer relief, with clear characters and complete preservation; at the left end of the wooden plaque, from right to left and top to bottom, is the postscript 'Baokang Chaste Widow Wu Chenshi', with the date 'April of the 5th Year of the Republic of China'; directly above it is also carved the 'Seal of Honorary Edicts', about 14 cm square. According to research, this plaque was inscribed by Yuan Shikai, President of the Republic, for Chen Shi, daughter-in-law of Wu Yuanze (wife of eldest son Wu Shite, died of illness at 18); it was then hung at the Wu family in Wuchang (at that time, from Snake Mountain to Huangtupo, i.e., present-day Shouyi Road, were all Wu family properties); on the eve of the fall of Wuhan in 1938, it was brought back to the Baokang ancestral residence by Gong Jingqin, the second wife of Wu Yuanjun (died of illness in Baokang in 1948).

Yichang

329. 黄陵庙

Huangling Shrine
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位

宗教建筑·砖石、砖木结构
看点 Highlights
禹王殿楠木柱木雕黄牛峡是西陵峡的四峡之一江水翻滚不息波涛汹涌两岸山势高耸粗犷多变黄陵庙就坐落在黄牛峡南岸的黄牛山上黄陵庙的历史非常悠久相传是春秋时期为纪念神助大禹开峡治水而修建的寺中保存的黄牛庙记石碑也很有可能是三国时诸葛亮重建庙宇时所镌刻的
中文 Chinese

黄牛峡是西陵峡的'四峡'之一，江水翻滚不息，波涛汹涌，两岸山势高耸，粗犷多变，黄陵庙就坐落在黄牛峡南岸的黄牛山上。

黄陵庙的历史非常悠久，相传是春秋时期为纪念神助大禹开峡治水而修建的，而寺中保存的《黄牛庙记》石碑，也很有可能是三国时诸葛亮重建庙宇时所镌刻的：'……古传所载，黄牛助禹开江治水，九载而功成，信不诬也，惜乎庙貌废去，使人太息……仆复而兴之，再建其庙号，目之曰黄牛庙。

'唐大中元年（847）复建时改名为黄牛祠。欧阳修任夷陵县令时，不信神牛触石之说，只信禹王开山之功，因而改黄牛祠为黄陵庙，还为此写下一首《黄牛祠》：'……峡山侵天起青嶂，崖崩路绝无由上。黄牛不下江头饮，行人惟向舟中望。

'此后黄陵庙多次重修，清同治九年（1870）曾遭遇过一次特大洪水，山门冲毁，现存建筑多在此之后修建。整座庙宇坐南朝北，环以围墙，主轴线上有山门、禹王殿、祖师殿，祖师殿现仅存遗址，左侧轴线上依次排列武侯祠和长生殿，院墙以外右侧还新建了一座九龙榭。

山门于清光绪十二年（1886）重建，为砖木结构单檐硬山灰瓦顶，正中高耸起一道四柱三间牌楼，饰以黑白为主的彩画，显得庄严、凝重，黑色竖匾上嵌隶书'老黄陵庙'四个鎏金大字。

各道额枋上均有精美的镂空石雕，正中上方为双龙戏珠，下方是八仙祝寿，两侧还有各种祥瑞图案。牌坊和主体建筑屋脊两段都饰有高高翘起的鸱尾，与背后黄牛岭起伏的山势相映成趣。

山门外有石阶三十三步又十八级，分别寓意'三十三重天'和'十八层地狱'，两旁还有一对通高近3米的镇水神兽石雕。

禹王殿是庙中最重要的建筑，面阔和进深均为五开间，平面接近正方形，重檐歇山屋顶，黄色琉璃瓦屋面，全部36根柱子均用楠木，显示出极高的规格。柱子原为黑色，现已被翻新为红色，明间金柱上盘有金龙，前后檐柱上端均置有五彩鳌鱼木雕。

殿内梁额下方还可看到最后一次重修时的题字，有'大清光绪十七年'和红色'钦命'等字样。大殿正面的两块匾额各有来历。下檐悬挂的一块褐底金字'玄功万古'匾，是明崇祯年间惠王朱常润手书，匾额四周饰以一圈二龙戏珠，表明题写者尊贵的身份；

上檐悬挂的褐底绿字'砥定江澜'匾，字体较为清秀，是清乾隆时期的公主爱新觉罗·琪格题写的。殿内供奉一尊6米高的大禹像。禹王殿的西侧是武侯祠，始建于唐代，原本紧挨在禹王殿的左侧，1983年修缮时移到现在的位置。

现存建筑重建于清光绪十二年（1886），是一座三开间的小殿，单檐硬山灰瓦屋顶，正面有前廊，木隔扇装修，掩映在丛丛绿荫中。武侯祠之后是长生殿，青砖灰瓦，古朴雅致的风格与黄陵庙内其他建筑的华丽精致迥然不同。长生殿最早为覃家老屋。

根据《覃氏族谱》的记载，黄牛岭覃氏于明代从四川搬到夷陵，以打鱼为生，族中一户富裕人家认为黄陵庙的形势为'九龙捧圣'，是块风水宝地，便买下这块地建起祖屋。老屋面阔三间，青砖砌筑，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，马头封火山墙，明间两侧也升起马头墙，同时墙面后退，形成入口。

室内的房间按中轴对称布局，有前厅、后堂，后堂分上下两层。覃氏族人认为，这座老屋同时也是覃氏最早的祠堂，后来的一段时间里，老屋被用作黄陵庙中的普舍堂和积善堂。

English 英文

Huangniu (Yellow Ox) Gorge is one of the 'Four Gorges' of Xiling Gorge; the river water rolls ceaselessly, with surging waves; the mountains on both banks tower high, rugged and varied; Huangling Shrine sits on Huangniu Mountain on the south bank of Huangniu Gorge. The history of Huangling Shrine is very long; legend has it that it was built in the Spring and Autumn period to commemorate the divine help to Yu the Great in opening the gorge and controlling floods; the 'Record of Huangniu Temple' stone stele preserved in the temple was also very likely carved when Zhuge Liang of the Three Kingdoms rebuilt the temple: '...According to ancient legends, the yellow ox helped Yu open the river and control floods, succeeding in nine years; this is truly not false. Unfortunately, the temple appearance was abandoned, making one sigh... I restored and revived it, rebuilt its temple name, calling it Huangniu Temple.' When rebuilt in the 1st year of Dazhong, Tang (847), it was renamed Huangniu Shrine. When Ouyang Xiu served as the magistrate of Yiling, he did not believe the legend of the divine ox touching the rocks, but only believed in Yu the Great's merit of opening the mountains; hence he changed Huangniu Shrine to Huangling Shrine, and also wrote a poem 'Huangniu Shrine' for this: '...The gorge mountains rise against the sky with green peaks, cliffs collapse and roads are cut off with no way up. The yellow ox does not come down to drink at the river head; travelers only look toward it from their boats.' Thereafter Huangling Shrine was repaired many times; in the 9th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1870), it once encountered an extraordinary flood, and the mountain gate was washed away; most of the existing buildings were constructed after this. The entire temple faces north from south, surrounded by walls; on the main axis there are the mountain gate, Yu King Hall, and Patriarch Hall; the Patriarch Hall now only remains as a site; on the left axis, Wuhou Shrine and Changsheng Hall are arranged in sequence; outside the wall on the right side, a Nine-Dragon Pavilion was also newly built. The mountain gate was rebuilt in the 12th year of Guangxu, Qing (1886); it is a brick-wood structure single-eave gable gray-tile roof, with a four-column three-bay paifang towering in the center, decorated with paintings mainly in black and white, appearing solemn and dignified; on the black vertical plaque are inlaid the four gilded characters 'Old Huangling Shrine' in clerical script. On each额枋 there are exquisite openwork stone carvings; above the center is two dragons playing with a pearl, below is the Eight Immortals celebrating longevity, and on both sides there are various auspicious patterns. Both ends of the ridges of the paifang and the main building are decorated with high-upward chiwei (owl-tail ornaments), echoing the undulating terrain of Huangniu Ridge behind. Outside the mountain gate there are 33 stone steps plus 18 more, respectively symbolizing the 'Thirty-Three Heavens' and the 'Eighteen Levels of Hell'; on both sides there is also a pair of water-subduing mythical beast stone carvings with a total height of nearly 3 meters. The Yu King Hall is the most important building in the temple; both its width and depth are five bays, with a plane nearly square, a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, and a yellow glazed tile roof; all 36 columns are made of nanmu wood, showing an extremely high specification. The columns were originally black and have now been refurbished to red; on the golden columns of the central bay, golden dragons are coiled; at the upper ends of the front and rear eave columns, colorful giant fish wood carvings are placed. Below the beams and额枋 inside the hall, inscriptions from the last repair can still be seen, with words such as '17th year of Guangxu, Qing' and red 'Imperial Order.' The two plaques on the front of the main hall each have their origins. The brown-background gold-character 'Xuan Gong Wan Gu' (Profound Merit Through the Ages) plaque hanging under the lower eave was handwritten by Zhu Changrun, Prince Hui, during the Chongzhen period of the Ming; the plaque is decorated with a circle of two dragons playing with a pearl around it, indicating the noble status of the inscriber; the brown-background green-character 'Di Ding Jiang Lan' (Stabilizing the River Waves) plaque hanging on the upper eave has a more delicate font, and was inscribed by Aisin Gioro Qige, a princess of the Qianlong period of the Qing. Inside the hall is enshrined a 6-meter-high statue of Yu the Great. West of the Yu King Hall is Wuhou Shrine, first built in the Tang, originally紧挨着 on the left side of the Yu King Hall, and moved to its current position during repairs in 1983. The existing building was rebuilt in the 12th year of Guangxu, Qing (1886); it is a small three-bay hall with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, a front porch on the front, and wooden lattice doors and windows, nestled in clusters of green shade. Behind Wuhou Shrine is Changsheng Hall, with blue bricks and gray tiles; its simple and elegant style is quite different from the gorgeous and exquisite other buildings in Huangling Shrine. Changsheng Hall was originally the Qin Family Old House. According to the records of the 'Qin Family Genealogy,' the Qin family of Huangniu Ridge moved from Sichuan to Yiling in the Ming, making a living by fishing; a wealthy household in the clan believed that the terrain of Huangling Shrine was 'Nine Dragons Holding the Sage,' a fengshui treasure land, so they bought this land and built an ancestral house. The old house is three bays wide, built with blue bricks, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof and horse-head fire-sealing gable walls; horse-head walls also rise on both sides of the central bay, while the wall recedes to form an entrance. The indoor rooms are laid out symmetrically along the central axis, with a front hall and rear hall; the rear hall is divided into upper and lower two stories. The Qin clan believes that this old house was also the earliest ancestral hall of the Qin family; for a period later, the old house was used as the Pushe Hall and Jishan Hall in Huangling Shrine.

330. 杨家湾老屋

Old House in Yangjiawan
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
夷陵区三斗坪镇东岳庙村
类型 Type
民居建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
青砖灰瓦结构考究杨家湾老屋又名黎永志老屋始建于清乾隆五十二年老屋的创始者名为黎大镜他曾远渡日本留学回乡后从事水上运输服务行业逐渐累积了财富先后三处建房他的次子黎永志继承了这座杨家湾老屋又将老屋向两边扩建使现存建筑面积达到1300平方米
中文 Chinese

杨家湾老屋又名黎永志老屋，始建于清乾隆五十二年（1787）。老屋的创始者名为黎大镜，他曾远渡日本留学，回乡后从事水上运输服务行业，逐渐累积了财富，先后三处建房；他的次子黎永志继承了这座杨家湾老屋，又将老屋向两边扩建，使现存建筑面积达到1300平方米。

'抗战'时期，老屋曾是抗日部队三十军的长江上游江防总指挥部所在地。杨家湾老屋为横长方形布局，进深两进，横连十一屋，共有七个天井。青砖砌筑外墙，明间及主要厅堂有较为考究的木质屋架，其他房屋则以墙体支撑屋面，硬山灰瓦顶。每屋两侧都有马头墙。

门前屋后绿树环抱，婆娑叶影投映在干净的墙面上，让人觉得清新雅致。

English 英文

The Old House in Yangjiawan is also called Li Yongzhi Old House, first built in the 52nd year of Qianlong, Qing (1787). The founder of the old house was named Li Dajing; he once traveled far to study in Japan, and after returning home engaged in the water transportation service industry, gradually accumulating wealth and building houses at three places successively; his second son Li Yongzhi inherited this Yangjiawan Old House and expanded it to both sides, making the existing building area reach 1300 square meters. During the 'War of Resistance' period, the old house was once the location of the General Headquarters of River Defense in the Upper Yangtze of the 30th Army of the anti-Japanese forces. The Old House in Yangjiawan has a horizontal rectangular layout, with two entries in depth and eleven houses connected horizontally, with a total of seven courtyards (tianjing). The exterior walls are built with blue bricks; the central bay and main halls have more exquisite wooden roof trusses, while other houses use walls to support the roof, with gable gray-tile roofs. Each house has horse-head walls on both sides. Green trees surround the front and back of the house, and the dancing leaf shadows are cast on the clean walls, making people feel fresh and elegant.

Vernacular Dwellings in Nanbian

保存完好纹样细致夷陵区黄花乡南边村深处有两栋保存较好、规模较大的清代古民居分别名为宝和和老号两栋老屋相距不到200米这两座老屋都是当地易氏的故居始建于清嘉庆六年据易氏族谱记载易氏先祖由山西太原移至峡州（今宜昌）后为避乱又于清朝迁入深山峡谷的南边
中文 Chinese

夷陵区黄花乡南边村深处，有两栋保存较好、规模较大的清代古民居，分别名为'宝和'和'老号'，两栋老屋相距不到200米。这两座老屋都是当地易氏的故居，始建于清嘉庆六年（1801）。

据《易氏族谱》记载，易氏先祖由山西太原移至峡州（今宜昌），后为避乱，又于清朝迁入深山峡谷的南边。此后，族中的忠祚公支脉读书致仕，通过科举起家，又开办钱庄、放高利贷、开设酒坊商店，并编纂了《易氏族谱》12卷，今天南边民居的主人便是这一支的后人。

'宝和'清末建成，主人名为易起芬，占地面积...

English 英文

Deep in Nanbian Village, Huanghua Township, Yiling District, there are two well-preserved and relatively large-scale Qing ancient vernacular dwellings, respectively named 'Baohe' (Treasure Harmony) and 'Lao Hao' (Old Name); the two old houses are less than 200 meters apart. Both old houses are the former residences of the local Yi family, first built in the 6th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1801). According to the records of the 'Yi Family Genealogy,' the ancestors of the Yi family moved from Taiyuan, Shanxi to Xiazhou (present-day Yichang), and later, to avoid chaos, moved to Nanbian in the deep mountain gorges during the Qing. Thereafter, the Zhongzuo Gong branch of the clan studied to become officials, rose through the imperial examinations, and also opened money shops, lent high-interest loans, opened wine workshops and shops, and compiled 12 volumes of the 'Yi Family Genealogy'; today's owners of the Nanbian dwellings are descendants of this branch. 332. 望家祠堂

Wang's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
夷陵区太平溪镇高峡大道60号
类型 Type
祭祀建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
整体布局望家祠堂原址在太平溪镇伍厢庙村2000年配合三峡工程建设迁至现址望是一个历史悠久的姓氏其始祖可以追溯到周朝的齐太公吕尚即封神榜中大名鼎鼎的姜子牙望家祠堂占地面积约300平方米一进二层中间为天井前厅后堂两侧有厢房前厅为穿斗式木构架
中文 Chinese

望家祠堂原址在太平溪镇伍厢庙村，2000年配合三峡工程建设迁至现址。'望'是一个历史悠久的姓氏，其始祖可以追溯到周朝的齐太公吕尚，即《封神榜》中大名鼎鼎的姜子牙。

望家祠堂占地面积约300平方米，一进二层，中间为天井，前厅后堂，两侧有厢房。前厅为穿斗式木构架，后堂为抬梁式木构架，二楼天井四周有回廊，正如民间俗语所说'走马转阁楼，下雨不湿鞋'。

青砖外墙，灰瓦屋面，封火山墙，正门高起的墙面做成简单的牌楼式样，屋檐下有一圈彩画装饰。

English 英文

The original site of Wang's Ancestral Hall was in Wuxiangmiao Village, Taipingxi Town; in 2000, it was moved to the current site in coordination with the Three Gorges Project construction. 'Wang' is a surname with a long history; its first ancestor can be traced back to Lü Shang, Duke Tai of Qi in the Zhou Dynasty, i.e., the famous Jiang Ziya in 'Investiture of the Gods.' Wang's Ancestral Hall covers an area of about 300 square meters, with one entry and two stories, a courtyard (tianjing) in the middle, front hall and rear hall, and wing rooms on both sides. The front hall has a column-and-tie wooden frame, and the rear hall has a post-and-lintel wooden frame; around the courtyard on the second floor there are corridors, just as the folk saying goes, 'galloping horses turn the attic, no wet shoes in rain.' Blue brick exterior walls, gray tile roof, fire-sealing gable walls; the high wall at the main gate is made into a simple paifang style, with a circle of painted decoration under the eaves.

333. 圆通寺

Yuantong Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明代
地址 Address
夷陵区分乡镇界岭村
类型 Type
宗教建筑·石、木结构
看点 Highlights
石雕木构架圆通寺始建于元朝亦名院庄寺据清代东湖县志记载院庄寺在院庄铺伏牛山旧名圆通刹元建明洪武初乡人谭仲华施有常住地国朝康熙四年僧笔峰重修圆通寺现仅存山门和大殿
中文 Chinese

圆通寺始建于元朝，亦名院庄寺，据清代《东湖县志》记载：'院庄寺在院庄铺伏牛山，旧名圆通刹，元建。明洪武初，乡人谭仲华施有常住地，国朝康熙四年僧笔峰重修。'圆通寺现仅存山门和大殿，坐北朝南，虽然保存状况不佳，但可以看出这里曾经是一座规模宏大的佛刹。

山门和大殿均为五间单檐悬山屋顶，外观朴素，但木结构用材讲究，做工规整，构架制作精细。山门正面匾额上书'圆通禅林'四字，正殿脊檩下方还能看到清楚的'大清光绪五年三月初三'题记。

最有意思的是两座建筑中保存的石雕构件，如山门的门框上雕刻凤凰、喜鹊、梅花等图案，并使用了三种不同的浮雕技法，类似于《营造法式》中的剔地凸起、压地隐起和减地平钑。而大殿的八角形柱础每面都雕刻不同的图案，非常富有民间趣味。

English 英文

Yuantong Temple was first built in the Yuan Dynasty, also called Yuanzhuang Temple; according to the records of the 'Donghu County Annals' of the Qing: 'Yuanzhuang Temple is at Funiu Mountain, Yuanzhuang Pu, formerly named Yuantong Cha, built in the Yuan. At the beginning of Hongwu, Ming, local Tan Zhonghua donated permanent land; in the 4th year of Kangxi of the current dynasty, monk Bifeng rebuilt it.' Yuantong Temple now only retains the mountain gate and main hall, facing south; although the preservation condition is poor, it can be seen that this was once a large-scale Buddhist temple. Both the mountain gate and main hall have five-bay single-eave overhanging gable roofs, with a simple exterior, but the wooden structure uses refined materials, with regular workmanship and exquisite frame construction. On the front plaque of the mountain gate are written the four characters 'Yuantong Chan Lin' (Yuantong Buddhist Forest); below the ridge purlin of the main hall, a clear inscription '3rd day of the 3rd month, 5th year of Guangxu, Qing' can still be seen. The most interesting are the stone carving components preserved in the two buildings, such as the door frame of the mountain gate carved with patterns of phoenixes, magpies, plum blossoms, etc., using three different relief techniques, similar to the 'ti-di tu-qi' (raised carving), 'ya-di yin-qi' (subtle relief), and 'jian-di ping-ji' (flat carving) in the 'Yingzao Fashi' (State Building Standards). The octagonal column plinths of the main hall are carved with different patterns on each face, very rich in folk charm.

334. 宜昌近代建筑

Modern Architecture in Yichang

近代

看点 Highlights
1876年中英烟台条约辟宜昌为通商口岸开埠后的宜昌舟楫往来美孚、亚细亚、德士古等煤油公司纷纷建立了专用码头1877年4月1日宜昌海关设立英国人任税务司此后英国、德国和日本相继在宜昌设立领事馆中华民国三年宜昌成立商埠工程局市区向南郊扩展修建了通惠路（今解放路）、中山路、云集路、陶朱路（今陶珠路）等新型街道
中文 Chinese

1876年，《中英烟台条约》辟宜昌为通商口岸，开埠后的宜昌，舟楫往来，美孚、亚细亚、德士古等煤油公司纷纷建立了专用码头。

1877年4月1日，宜昌海关设立，英国人任税务司，此后英国、德国和日本相继在宜昌设立领事馆。

中华民国三年（1914），宜昌成立商埠工程局，市区向南郊扩展，修建了通惠路（今解放路）、中山路、云集路、陶朱路（今陶珠路）等新型街道，近代城市初具规模。

宜昌近代建筑主要分布在沿江的云集路、红星路一带，现存数量不多，但类型十分丰富，包括宜昌海关公署，教堂，英国领事馆，海军俱乐部，以及亚细亚火油公司的办公楼、住宅，太古轮船公司办公楼，海鸥百货商店等。

English 英文

In 1876, the 'Sino-British Chefoo Convention' opened Yichang as a trading port; after the opening, Yichang saw boats coming and going, and kerosene companies such as Mobil, Asiatic Petroleum, and Texaco successively built dedicated docks. On April 1, 1877, the Yichang Customs was established, with a British person serving as the tax commissioner; thereafter, Britain, Germany, and Japan successively established consulates in Yichang. In the 3rd year of the Republic of China (1914), Yichang established the Commercial Port Engineering Bureau; the urban area expanded to the southern suburbs, and new-type streets such as Tonghui Road (present-day Jiefang Road), Zhongshan Road, Yunji Road, and Taozhu Road (present-day Taozhu Road) were built, and the modern city began to take shape. Modern architecture in Yichang is mainly distributed along the river in the Yunji Road and Hongxing Road area; the existing number is not large, but the types are very rich, including the Yichang Customs Office, churches, the British Consulate, the Navy Club, as well as the office building and residence of the Asiatic Petroleum Company, the office building of the China Navigation Company, the Seagull Department Store, etc.

335. 英国领事馆

British Consulate in Yichang
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
1892年
地址 Address
伍家岗区红星路42号
类型 Type
公共建筑·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
红瓦顶拱券外廊红星路原名怀远路是长江边一条热闹的商业街宜昌开埠后宜昌商会取怀远以德中怀远二字为这条街道命名新中国成立后宜昌市政府选址红星路按照当时的惯例在地图上画一颗红星来标注党政机关随着搬来的机关部门不断增多地图上的红星也越来越多
中文 Chinese

红星路原名怀远路，是长江边一条热闹的商业街。宜昌开埠后，宜昌商会取'怀远以德'中'怀远'二字为这条街道命名。新中国成立后，宜昌市政府选址红星路。按照当时的惯例，在地图上画一颗红星来标注党政机关；

随着搬来的机关部门不断增多，地图上的红星也越来越多，于是怀远路更名为红星路。宜昌英国领事馆开设于1877年，最初设立在英国金河号军舰上，后迁至怀远路东侧（现址），光绪十八年（1892）建成现存办公楼。

领事馆占地约300平方米，为二层砖木混合结构，方形平面，正面设拱券外廊，顶部三角山花上饰'1892'字样。红瓦坡屋顶组合，错落有致。室内大厅设有壁炉，原有四个烟囱伸出屋顶。

这座见证了宜昌被侵略历史的建筑，2008年在一片争议中被用作酒楼，原本米色的外墙也被刷成红色。经过业主、市民、专家和文化局各方面的沟通交流，外墙最终恢复了原貌，而酒店也得以继续运营，经过这件事，文物建筑的保护和开发利用的规范更加深入人心。

English 英文

Hongxing Road was originally named Huaiyuan Road, a lively commercial street by the Yangtze River. After Yichang was opened as a port, the Yichang Chamber of Commerce named this street after the two characters 'Huaiyuan' from 'huai yuan yi de' (cherishing the distant with virtue). After the founding of New China, the Yichang Municipal Government chose Hongxing Road as its site. According to the convention at the time, a red star was drawn on the map to mark party and government organs; as more and more organs moved in, there were more and more red stars on the map, so Huaiyuan Road was renamed Hongxing Road. The British Consulate in Yichang was established in 1877, initially set up on the British warship HMS Kinsha, and later moved to the east side of Huaiyuan Road (the current site); the existing office building was completed in the 18th year of Guangxu (1892). The consulate covers an area of about 300 square meters, a two-story brick-wood mixed structure with a square plan, arched exterior corridors on the front, and the triangular gable at the top decorated with the characters '1892.' The red-tile sloped roof combination is well-proportioned. The indoor hall has a fireplace, and originally four chimneys protruded from the roof. This building, which witnessed the history of Yichang being invaded, was used as a restaurant amid controversy in 2008, and the originally beige exterior wall was also painted red. Through communication and exchange among the owner, citizens, experts, and the Cultural Bureau, the exterior wall was finally restored to its original appearance, and the hotel could continue to operate; through this incident, the norms for the protection and development of cultural heritage buildings became more deeply rooted in people's hearts.

336. 亚细亚火油公司

Asiatic Petroleum Company in Yichang
级别 Level
市级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
1912年

西陵区云集路29号
