魁星楼又名魁星阁为六角三层楼阁紧接着文昌祠右桂香殿右侧有侧门可直至现已拆除相传恩施有个魁星殿半截戳到天里头曾是登高俯瞰城风貌的最佳场所
中文 Chinese

魁星楼又名魁星阁，为六角三层楼阁，紧接着文昌祠右，桂香殿右侧有侧门可直至，现已拆除。相传'恩施有个魁星殿，半截戳到天里头'，曾是登高俯瞰城风貌的最佳场所。

English 英文

Kuixing Tower, also called Kuixing Pavilion, is a hexagonal three-story pavilion, immediately to the right of Wenchang Shrine; there is a side door on the right side of Guixiang Hall that leads directly to it, now demolished. Legend has it that 'Enshi has a Kuixing Hall, half of it pokes into the sky'; it was once the best place to climb high and overlook the city's scenery.

357. 城隍庙

City God Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
恩施市鳌脊山
类型 Type
宗教建筑
看点 Highlights
文昌祠下为城隍庙位于鳌脊山腰入口为南北对峙两门楼2层歇山顶砖木结构入院后顺山势上行正殿立于前单层硬山灰瓦顶殿前有双狮镇门傲居左右右手边立一柱石碑正面书太守文公公德政碑北面落阁郡士民公立字样
中文 Chinese

文昌祠下为城隍庙，位于鳌脊山腰，入口为南北对峙两门楼，2层歇山顶砖木结构。

入院后顺山势上行，正殿立于前，单层硬山灰瓦顶，殿前有双狮镇门，傲居左右，右手边立一柱石碑，正面'书太守文公公德政碑'，北面落'阁郡士民公立'字样，文庙两侧观有数排三层居民楼，风貌不佳。

English 英文

Below Wenchang Shrine is the City God Temple, located on the slope of Aoji Mountain; the entrance is two gate towers facing each other north-south, a two-story hip-and-gable roof brick-wood structure. After entering the courtyard, one goes up along the mountain terrain; the main hall stands in front, a single-story gable gray-tile roof; in front of the hall there are two stone lions guarding the gate, standing proudly on the left and right; on the right side stands a stone stele, with the front inscribed 'Virtuous Governance Stele of Prefect Wen Gong' and the north side inscribed 'Erected by the scholars and people of the prefecture'; on both sides of the Confucian Temple there are several rows of three-story residential buildings, with poor scenery.

358. 连珠塔

Lianzhu Pagoda
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
恩施市六角亭老城东门清江东岸
类型 Type
古塔·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
雕环境连珠塔位于五峰山主峰龙首山顶此山五峰并峙有珠玉相连之称塔因山而得名坐东向西与恩施古城武圣宫、文昌祠遥相呼应成三足鼎立之势古塔依托山高之势跨清江与恩施城构成良好的对景效果登至塔顶
中文 Chinese

连珠塔位于五峰山主峰龙首山顶，此山五峰并峙，有'珠玉相连'之称，塔因山而得名，坐东向西，与恩施古城武圣宫、文昌祠遥相呼应，成三足鼎立之势。古塔依托山高之势，跨清江与恩施城构成良好的对景效果，登至塔顶，可俯瞰整个恩施山城风光。

清吴式敏有诗赞曰：'秀挺五峰奎壁灿，灵钟三邑冕裳新。'连珠塔的修建历经数十年，清乾隆辛卯年（1771），施南府知府张应桃首倡建塔，未成功，至清道光十二年（1832）建成。道光十三年（1833）于塔前建石坊，周围建花墙、院门及斋堂等。

连珠塔为八角七层仿木结构楼阁式空心砖石，高34.8米，内有百余级石梯盘旋而上至塔顶。石砌须弥座塔基，一层上部及以上青砖砌筑，底层开拱形塔门，高约4米，门额嵌'连珠塔'石匾，门柱阴刻隶书对联：'七级庄严，人际风云瞻气象；五峰秀秉，天开图画助文明。

'二层以上除第五层设三门外均设四拱门，每层叠涩出檐，层檐微展，窗龛略收。每角设托塔力士，力士身着土家族服饰，敞胸露腹，肌体刚劲，气势威武，或蹲或站，双手或单手托塔，可见土家族人彪悍淳朴的强大气场。塔体石刻造工精细，雕刻有'鱼跃龙门图''威风祥麟图''五福（蝠）临门图'等多处生动纹饰。

塔刹由数枚大锡珠重叠而成，与塔身浑然一体，巍然壮观。塔前立'揽胜'石牌坊，牌坊高耸，前后各有石象、石狮一对，四兽雄踞，好不威严。塔四周衬以疏林。

English 英文

Lianzhu Pagoda is located on the top of Longshou (Dragon Head) Mountain, the main peak of Wufeng (Five Peaks) Mountain; this mountain has five peaks standing side by side, known as 'pearls and jade connected'; the pagoda is named after the mountain, facing west from east, echoing from afar with Wusheng Palace and Wenchang Shrine in the ancient Enshi city, forming a tripartite balance. The ancient pagoda, relying on the high mountain, forms a good opposite-scene effect with Enshi city across the Qing River; climbing to the top of the pagoda, one can overlook the entire scenery of the Enshi mountain city. Wu Shimin of the Qing praised it in a poem: 'Graceful and upright, the five peaks shine with literary stars; spiritually resonant, the three counties renew their official robes.' The construction of Lianzhu Pagoda took decades; in the Xin-Mao year of Qianlong, Qing (1771), Zhang Yingtiao, Prefect of Shinan Prefecture, first initiated the construction of the pagoda, but it was not successful; it was completed in the 12th year of Daoguang, Qing (1832). In the 13th year of Daoguang (1833), a stone paifang was built in front of the pagoda, with flower walls, courtyard gates, and vegetarian halls built around it. Lianzhu Pagoda is an octagonal seven-story imitated-wood-structure pavilion-style hollow brick-stone pagoda, 34.8 meters high, with more than a hundred stone steps spiraling up to the top. The base is a stone-built Xumi pedestal; the upper part of the first floor and above are built with blue bricks; the bottom floor opens an arched pagoda gate, about 4 meters high, with a stone plaque 'Lianzhu Ta' embedded in the lintel, and a clerical-script couplet carved in intaglio on the door pillars: 'Seven stories solemn, people meet wind and clouds and observe the aura; five peaks graceful, heaven opens paintings and aids civilization.' From the second floor upward, except for the fifth floor which has three gates, all have four arched gates; each floor has corbelled eaves, with the eaves slightly extending and the window niches slightly receding. At each corner there is a pagoda-supporting vajra warrior; the warriors wear Tujia costumes, with bare chests and bellies, strong bodies, and majestic momentum, either squatting or standing, supporting the pagoda with both hands or one hand, showing the powerful aura of the tough and simple Tujia people. The stone carvings on the pagoda body are exquisitely crafted, with many vivid decorative patterns such as 'Fish Leaping through the Dragon Gate,' 'Majestic Auspicious Qilin,' and 'Five Blessings at the Door.' The finial is formed by overlapping several large tin beads, integrated with the pagoda body, towering and magnificent. In front of the pagoda stands a 'Lansheng' (Gazing at Scenery) stone paifang, towering high, with a pair of stone elephants and stone lions in front and behind respectively; the four beasts stand dominantly, very majestic. The pagoda is surrounded by sparse forests.

359. 武圣宫

Emperor Guan's Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
恩施市城乡街104号
类型 Type
礼制建筑·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
戏楼形制走马转角楼形制又名关帝庙、开元寺是恩施古城中拜祀关羽、供奉武将的寺庙因土家族有尚武之风又受传统文化文拜孔子、武拜关公的影响武圣宫在城中很受重视武圣宫建于台地之上建筑坐北朝南东西窄而南砖木结构北长体量较大主体墙面呈白色
中文 Chinese

武圣宫又名关帝庙、开元寺，是恩施古城中拜祀关羽、供奉武将的寺庙。因土家族有尚武之风，又受传统文化'文拜孔子，武拜关公'的影响，武圣宫在城中很受重视。武圣宫建于台地之上，建筑坐北朝南，东西窄而南北长，体量较大，主体墙面呈白色，正面山门以砖红色为主，檐角飞扬。

建筑砖石墙体，两进四合院式布局，沿南北轴线依次是山门、戏楼及正殿，空间的秩序感较强。山门为牌坊式，前壁砖墙封檐，庙额刻'武圣宫'三字，东西两侧封火山墙，门前有上下两层台基，高数十米，衬托出山门的高大雄伟。

山门后檐突出，为二层戏楼，单檐歇山灰瓦顶，戏台平面呈'凸'字形，耳室分别位于两侧，利用正殿、戏楼和院墙来划分场地，构成了完整的戏剧观演空间。清朝武圣宫作为施南府操防营时，就有戏班子每逢农历五月十三关公生日时在此开唱，此时戏楼是庙宇不可分割的部分。

正殿面阔三间，进深三间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，抬梁式构架，大殿内供奉有关帝像，两侧马头墙层层跌落。

正殿左右两侧有回廊，为土家族特色建筑走马转角楼，二层栏杆式建筑，抬梁式构架，长约16米，宽约4米，可通向戏台。正殿和回廊的墙壁上还嵌有数十块石碑，记武圣宫沿革的历史沿革及历代维修情况。

English 英文

Wusheng Palace, also called Guandi Temple or Kaiyuan Temple, is a temple in the ancient Enshi city for worshipping Guan Yu and enshrining military generals. Because the Tujia people have a tradition of valuing martial arts, and under the influence of traditional culture 'civilian worship Confucius, military worship Guan Gong,' Wusheng Palace was highly valued in the city. Wusheng Palace was built on a terrace; the building faces south, narrow east-west and long north-south, with a large volume; the main wall surface is white, and the front mountain gate is mainly brick-red, with flying eave corners. The building has brick-stone walls, a two-entry courtyard layout, with the mountain gate, theater tower, and main hall in sequence along the north-south axis, with a strong sense of spatial order. The mountain gate is paifang-style, with the front wall brick-sealed eaves; the temple lintel is carved with the three characters 'Wusheng Gong'; on the east and west sides are fire-sealing gable walls; in front of the gate there are two levels of terraces, tens of meters high, setting off the tall and majestic mountain gate. The rear eave of the mountain gate protrudes, forming a two-story theater tower with a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof; the stage plane is 'convex'-shaped, with side rooms respectively located on both sides; the main hall, theater tower, and courtyard walls are used to divide the venue, forming a complete theatrical performance and viewing space. When Wusheng Palace served as the Cao Fang Camp of Shinan Prefecture in the Qing, theater troupes would perform here every year on the birthday of Guan Gong (the 13th day of the 5th lunar month); at this time the theater tower was an inseparable part of the temple. The main hall is three bays wide and three bays deep, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof and a post-and-lintel frame; inside the main hall is enshrined the statue of Guan Di; on both sides the horse-head walls descend in layers. On the left and right sides of the main hall there are corridors, which are Tujia characteristic buildings called 'zouma zhuanjiao lou' (galloping-horse corner-turning towers), two-story railing-style buildings with post-and-lintel frames, about 16 meters long and 4 meters wide, leading to the stage. Dozens of stone steles are also embedded in the walls of the main hall and corridors, recording the historical evolution and successive repairs of Wusheng Palace.

360. 滚龙坝古建筑群

Ancient Building Complex in Gunlongba
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
恩施市崔家坝镇滚龙坝村
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
多进天井与古墓群的虎头碑滚龙坝村坐落在山间平地四面环山古树参天因黄龙（尖龙河）、青龙（洋鱼沟）两条溪水从南北两侧如滚龙般奔流穿过山寨汇入天坑而得名滚龙坝是以土家大姓向氏家族居住的自然小村落是恩施古东大道要地以古建筑群、古墓葬闻名是中国第三批中国历史文化名村（2007）滚龙坝古建筑群由多进天井庭院和四合天井院落组成有别于当地其他土家族吊脚楼建筑
中文 Chinese

滚龙坝村坐落在山间平地，四面环山，古树参天，因'黄龙'（尖龙河）、'青龙'（洋鱼沟）两条溪水从南北两侧如滚龙般奔流穿过山寨，汇入天坑而得名。滚龙坝是以土家大姓向氏家族居住的自然小村落，是恩施古东大道要地，以古建筑群、古墓葬闻名，是中国第三批中国历史文化名村（2007）。

滚龙坝古建筑群由多进天井庭院和四合天井院落组成，有别于当地其他土家族吊脚楼建筑。

据《向氏宗源》记载，滚龙坝村为独姓向氏世居，先祖向大发为汉族人，崇祯七年（1635）因征战携家眷落户于此，后向氏族人与这里的土家族儿女繁衍，因而其建筑具有楚汉文化融合的特点。最早向氏同族兄弟间分家不分房，形成了三进、五进、七进，及五天井、十天井的中坪大型民居建筑楼群。

随着时间推移，村寨与外界联系增多，村落布局也从'聚族而居'的院落发展为独门独院，同时仍然保存有部分传统聚居院落。村内现存明清古建筑及有保护价值的近现代建筑群主要有3处，包括茅坎山古建筑群、中村古建筑群和石狮子屋。

主要是砖木结构的四合院式天井屋，四周以墙体围合'回'字形；有的两侧封火山墙，建筑窗扇、门扇等雕花精致，极有特色。

English 英文

Gunlongba Village is located on a flat land between mountains, surrounded by mountains on all sides, with towering ancient trees; it gets its name because two streams, 'Yellow Dragon' (Jianlong River) and 'Green Dragon' (Yangyugou), flow like rolling dragons from the north and south sides through the mountain village and converge into a sinkhole. Gunlongba is a natural small village inhabited by the Xiang family, a major Tujia surname; it was a strategic point on the ancient East Road of Enshi, famous for its ancient building complexes and ancient tombs, and is the third batch of Chinese Historical and Cultural Villages (2007). The Gunlongba Ancient Building Complex is composed of multi-entry courtyard (tianjing) yards and four-sided courtyard yards, different from other local Tujia stilted buildings. According to the records of 'Xiang Family Ancestral Origins,' Gunlongba Village is exclusively inhabited by the Xiang surname for generations; the ancestor Xiang Dafa was Han Chinese, and in the 7th year of Chongzhen (1635), due to military campaigns, he settled here with his family; later the Xiang clan multiplied with the Tujia people here, hence its buildings have the characteristic of fusion of Chu and Han cultures. At the earliest, the Xiang brothers of the same clan divided families but not houses, forming large residential building complexes of three, five, and seven entries, as well as five and ten courtyards (tianjing) in Zhongping. As time passed, the village had more contact with the outside world, and the village layout also developed from 'clan-living-together' courtyards to independent single courtyards, while still preserving some traditional clustered courtyards. The existing Ming and Qing ancient buildings and modern building complexes with protective value in the village mainly include 3 places: the Maokanshan Ancient Building Complex, Zhongcun Ancient Building Complex, and Stone Lion House. They are mainly brick-wood structure four-sided courtyard (tianjing) houses, surrounded by walls in a '回' (hui) shape; some have fire-sealing gable walls on both sides, and the building window sashes, door leaves, etc., are exquisitely carved, very distinctive.

361. 茅坎山建筑群

Maokanshan Building Complex
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明代
地址 Address
恩施市崔家坝镇滚龙坝村
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
茅坎山建筑群是明代向氏最早修建的房屋现仅存四房屋基一处保存较好的老屋位于茅坎山脚坪坝边沿由前三房、后三房、四侧房组成四合天井式砖木结构建筑虽建筑年代久远高耸的封火山墙气势磅礴依旧现房屋正墙面已粉刷一新
中文 Chinese

茅坎山建筑群是明代向氏最早修建的房屋，现仅存'四房屋基'，一处保存较好的老屋，位于茅坎山脚坪坝边沿，由前三房、后三房、四侧房组成四合天井式砖木结构建筑。虽建筑年代久远，高耸的封火山墙，气势磅礴依旧，现房屋正墙面已粉刷一新。

English 英文

The Maokanshan Building Complex was the earliest house built by the Xiang family in the Ming Dynasty; now only the 'Four-House Foundation' remains, a well-preserved old house located at the edge of the flatland at the foot of Maokan Mountain, composed of front three rooms, rear three rooms, and four side rooms forming a four-sided courtyard (tianjing) brick-wood structure building. Although the building is old, the towering fire-sealing gable walls still have a majestic momentum; the front wall of the house has now been freshly painted.

362. 中村建筑群

Zhongcun Building Complex
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
恩施市崔家坝镇滚龙坝村
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
中村建筑群建于清代多为坐西朝东为石门、前六房、后六房、八侧房、两天井、两边围屋组合的砖木结构建筑石门石柱础等雕刻精美现围屋、侧方多处已拆毁建筑保存状况令人担忧
中文 Chinese

中村建筑群建于清代，多为坐西朝东，为石门、前六房、后六房、八侧房、两天井、两边围屋组合的砖木结构建筑，石门石柱础等雕刻精美。现围屋、侧方多处已拆毁，建筑保存状况令人担忧。

English 英文

The Zhongcun Building Complex was built in the Qing Dynasty, mostly facing east from west; it is a brick-wood structure building composed of a stone gate, front six rooms, rear six rooms, eight side rooms, two courtyards (tianjing), and surrounding houses on both sides, with exquisite carvings on the stone gate and stone column plinths. Now many parts of the surrounding houses and side rooms have been demolished, and the preservation condition of the building is worrying.

363. 石狮子屋

Stone Lion House
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
恩施市崔家坝镇滚龙坝村
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
石狮子屋为三门九排多进砖木结构建筑分左中右三屋门前立清道光十八年石狮一对故而得名主屋为三进十房二天井右屋为七进十五房五天井左屋为五进十一房二天井左右两屋二进均为亭子屋三屋间有风火墙相隔但在一、二进间设有石门作为横向通道居住者来往走动可不出大屋
中文 Chinese

石狮子屋为三门九排，多进砖木结构建筑，分左中右三屋，门前立清道光十八年（1838）石狮一对，故而得名。主屋为三进十房二天井，右屋为七进十五房五天井，左屋为五进十一房二天井，左右两屋二进均为亭子屋。

三屋间有风火墙相隔，但在一、二进间设有石门作为横向通道，居住者来往走动可不出大屋。现房屋左屋前二进已毁，正面局部修葺新墙，整体保存较好。除上述三处主要建筑群，向若青屋、老学堂屋保存尚可。

向若青屋为单天井院落砖木结构建筑，由门楼、三间正屋，四间侧屋组成，两侧山墙矗立着高耸的马头墙。老学堂屋为砖木混合结构，硬山灰瓦顶，建筑二层出挑1米，是吊脚楼与汉族建筑风格相融合的演绎。

长街檐屋曾是滚龙坝古建筑群中规模最大屋场之一，由三石门、三进、前九房、后九房、八侧房、一抱厅、四天井、后花园等两头10多间围屋组合的砖木结构建筑。因呈长条形，故有长街檐之称，只可惜现已拆除。

茅坎山墓地又称祖坟岭，是滚龙坝向氏墓地主要分布地，共有数十座古墓葬，其中有四座墓碑为虎头碑，实属罕见。最早下葬的'明待封高祖大旺云峰向老大人之墓'时间可追溯到明末清初，对研究鄂西地区古墓葬具有重要的价值。

English 英文

The Stone Lion House has three gates and nine rows, a multi-entry brick-wood structure building, divided into left, middle, and right three houses; in front of the gate stand a pair of stone lions from the 18th year of Daoguang, Qing (1838), hence the name. The main house has three entries, ten rooms, and two courtyards (tianjing); the right house has seven entries, fifteen rooms, and five courtyards; the left house has five entries, eleven rooms, and two courtyards; the second entries of both the left and right houses are pavilion houses. The three houses are separated by fire walls, but between the first and second entries there are stone gates as horizontal passages, so residents can move back and forth without leaving the big house. Now the first two entries of the left house have been destroyed, and parts of the front have been repaired with new walls; the overall preservation is good. Besides the three main building complexes mentioned above, the Xiang Ruoqing House and Old School House are fairly well-preserved. The Xiang Ruoqing House is a single-courtyard brick-wood structure building, composed of a gate tower, three main rooms, and four side rooms, with towering horse-head walls standing on the gable walls on both sides. The Old School House is a brick-wood mixed structure with a gable gray-tile roof; the second story of the building overhangs by 1 meter, an interpretation of the fusion of stilted building and Han architectural styles. The Long Street Eave House was once one of the largest house complexes in the Gunlongba Ancient Building Complex, a brick-wood structure building composed of three stone gates, three entries, front nine rooms, rear nine rooms, eight side rooms, one embracing hall, four courtyards, back garden, and more than 10 surrounding houses at both ends. Because it is long and strip-shaped, it is called Long Street Eave; unfortunately it has now been demolished. The Maokanshan Cemetery, also called Ancestral Grave Ridge, is the main distribution area of the Xiang family tombs in Gunlongba, with dozens of ancient tombs, among which four tomb steles are tiger-head steles, truly rare. The earliest burial, the 'Tomb of the Late Elder Xiang Yunfeng, Great-Grandfather Dawa of the Ming,' dates back to the late Ming and early Qing, and has important value for studying ancient tombs in western Hubei.

364. 大水井古建筑群

Dashuijing Ancient Building Complex
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
利川市柏杨坝镇水井村、高仰村
类型 Type
居住建筑
看点 Highlights
木雕艺术民族风格大水井古建筑群为明、清时期土家族和汉族共同修建由李氏宗祠、李亮清庄园和高仰台李盖五旧宅三大建筑群落组成占地约2万平方米四周群山环抱风光旖旎相传大水井宗祠、庄园建筑群原为土家族人黄氏土司住宅及祖墓所在地清乾隆中期从湖南岳州西迁的李廷龙途经大水井图谋占据黄氏家产将城堡改建为李氏宗祠
中文 Chinese

大水井古建筑群为明、清时期土家族和汉族共同修建，由李氏宗祠、李亮清庄园和高仰台李盖五旧宅三大建筑群落组成，占地约2万平方米，四周群山环抱，风光旖旎。

相传大水井宗祠、庄园建筑群原为土家族人黄氏土司住宅及祖墓所在地，清乾隆中期，从湖南岳州西迁的李廷龙途经大水井，图谋占据黄氏家产，将城堡改建为李氏宗祠，落成于道光二十九年（1849）。

李氏后代官绅迭出，后在此基础上不断扩修屋宇，宗祠、庄园渐具规模，'土改'时期部分屋宇遭到破坏，现存较好的是李氏宗祠、李亮清庄园，分列东西，相距150米。

民国三十一年（1942）至三十七年（1948），在高仰台加建一座住宅，布局与庄园主体相仿，即李盖五旧宅。

大水井古建筑群作为土司的家宅而兴建，既有极具土家族特色的吊脚楼、绣花楼等传统建筑，又兼具西洋式建筑的装饰技艺，同时还融合了汉族民居风格，建筑群内有数十种雕花窗格，门窗、柱础上的雕刻也多达20余种，用料、做工十分讲究，是鄂西南地区目前规模最大、艺术价值极高的古建筑群。

李氏宗祠依山就势建于水井村罗汉山山阴，坐南朝北，占地面积约10万平方米，周遭群山峻岭，地势险峻，'北可望齐岳大山，南靠寒池高岭，东揽尖刀观古观，西控九雄关'。

宗祠规模险关，霸气威严，为宫殿式建筑，中轴对称布局，三路三进院落，前壁开左、中、右三门，中轴线上主体建筑为前殿、拜殿、祖宗殿，中路开大山门，山门顶是门楼式垛墙，中间匾额书'李氏宗祠'，左右两路为双厢式厢房，分别与前殿、祖宗殿相连。

三大殿形制相同，面积相仿，均面阔五间，进深三间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，砖木结构。拜殿是李氏家族祭祖的地方，陈列有木刻族规和家训，明间抬梁雕刻精美，殿两端山墙下各有一口水池，左名'廉泉井'，壁书一大'忍'字；

右名'让水池'，壁书一大'耐'字，喻示李氏家族的清廉礼让。祖宗殿为宗祠的正殿，檐下高悬'魁山堂'匾额。除三大殿外，宗祠内还有族长房、讲礼堂、账房、银库、守卫房等大小房屋60余间。

讲礼堂是当年李氏族长执行家法和审案的地方，内有一石构建——'过失桥'，是连接两边廊屋的过道，长3.81米，宽3.45米，厚0.27米，过去李氏族人若触犯族规需跪在过桥石上，听凭族长训斥与责罚。

宗祠四周均围以城墙，是宗祠的防御堡垒，正面一壁用巨大条石砌成保坎，左、右、后三方为依山势逐步升高的石墙堞垛，除正堡坎壁外，总长390余米，高约6米，厚约3米，全部用千斤以上花岗岩条石垒成，随山势蜿蜒。

城墙堞垛向外悬挑，依次布设56个射击孔，严密地封锁着进宗祠的通道，原有房廊遮风避雨，城墙的四角有望楼，常年有族人驻兵把守，现已毁。由宗祠东北角进入复道可见一口由高大围墙围住的水井，围墙由石块垒砌，正面刻有'大水井'三字，下七十二步台阶即可见水井。

实际上水井很小，原为本地的自然泉井，四季不涸，民国十九年（1930）前，川军贺国祥围攻李氏宗祠，因城池坚固，久攻不下，后围祠断水迫使族长李盖五投降，所以才有了后来的围井修墙，加强水源保护。

另在西南角和东北角山墙分别有望华门（生门）、承恩门（死门）两石门供出入，死门外不远处是一座悬崖，峭壁险峻，风景奇特，其上横跨一桥，名曰龙桥。龙桥河悬崖是李氏庄园处死家奴、盗贼之地，相传被宗族判死刑的人会被押解由生门至死门外龙桥，在桥上被推下摔死。

English 英文

The Dashuijing (Great Well) Ancient Building Complex was jointly built by the Tujia and Han people during the Ming and Qing periods; it consists of three major building complexes: the Li Family Ancestral Hall, Li Liangqing Manor, and the Former Residence of Li Gaiwu at Gaoyangtai, covering about 20,000 square meters, surrounded by mountains on all sides with beautiful scenery. Legend has it that the ancestral hall and manor building complex of Dashuijing was originally the residence and ancestral tomb site of the Tujia Huang chieftain; in the mid-Qianlong period of the Qing, Li Tinglong, who moved west from Yuezhou, Hunan, passed through Dashuijing, plotted to seize the Huang family property, and converted the castle into the Li Family Ancestral Hall, completed in the 29th year of Daoguang (1849). The Li family descendants produced many officials and gentry, and later continuously expanded and repaired houses on this basis; the ancestral hall and manor gradually took shape; during the 'Land Reform' period, some houses were damaged; the better-preserved ones are the Li Family Ancestral Hall and Li Liangqing Manor, arranged east and west, 150 meters apart. From the 31st year (1942) to the 37th year (1948) of the Republic, a residence was added at Gaoyangtai, with a layout similar to the main manor, namely the Former Residence of Li Gaiwu. The Dashuijing Ancient Building Complex was built as the family residence of a chieftain; it has both traditional buildings with strong Tujia characteristics such as stilted buildings and embroidery towers, as well as Western-style architectural decoration techniques, while also integrating Han residential styles; within the building complex there are dozens of types of carved window grilles, and the carvings on doors, windows, and column plinths also number more than 20 types, with very particular materials and workmanship; it is currently the largest and most artistically valuable ancient building complex in southwestern Hubei. The Li Family Ancestral Hall was built on the northern slope of Luohan Mountain in Shuijing Village according to the terrain, facing north from south, covering about 100,000 square meters; surrounded by steep mountains, with a precipitous terrain, 'north can see the Qiyue Great Mountain, south backs the Hanchi High Ridge, east embraces the Jiandaoguan Ancient Temple, west controls the Nine Heroic Passes.' The ancestral hall has a strategic and imposing scale, domineering and majestic; it is a palace-style building with a centrally symmetric layout, three roads and three-entry courtyards; the front wall opens left, middle, and right three gates; the main buildings on the central axis are the Front Hall, Worship Hall, and Ancestor Hall; the middle road opens a large mountain gate, the top of the mountain gate is a gate-tower-style parapet wall, with the middle plaque inscribed 'Li Family Ancestral Hall'; the left and right roads are double-wing side rooms, respectively connected to the Front Hall and Ancestor Hall. The three main halls have the same form and similar area, all five bays wide and three bays deep, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs and brick-wood structures. The Worship Hall is the place where the Li family worshipped ancestors, displaying wooden-engraved clan rules and family instructions; the raised beams in the central bay are exquisitely carved; under the gable walls at both ends of the hall there is a water pool each, the left named 'Lianquan Well' (Incorruptible Spring Well), with a large character 'Ren' (Endure) written on the wall; the right named 'Rangshui Pool' (Concession Water Pool), with a large character 'Nai' (Patience) written on the wall, symbolizing the integrity and courtesy of the Li family. The Ancestor Hall is the main hall of the ancestral hall, with a 'Kuishan Hall' plaque hanging high under the eaves. Besides the three main halls, there are more than 60 rooms of various sizes in the ancestral hall, such as the Clan Head Room, Lecture and Ritual Hall, Account Room, Silver Vault, and Guard Room. The Lecture and Ritual Hall was the place where the Li clan head enforced family rules and heard cases; inside there is a stone structure — the 'Fault Bridge,' a passage connecting the corridor houses on both sides, 3.81 meters long, 3.45 meters wide, and 0.27 meters thick; in the past, if a Li clan member violated clan rules, they would have to kneel on the bridge stone and listen to the clan head's reprimand and punishment. The ancestral hall is surrounded by city walls on all sides, serving as the defensive fortress of the ancestral hall; the front wall is built with huge dressed stones as a retaining wall; the left, right, and rear sides are stone wall parapets gradually rising according to the terrain; except for the front retaining wall, the total length is more than 390 meters, about 6 meters high and 3 meters thick, all built with granite dressed stones weighing more than a thousand jin, winding along the mountain terrain. The wall parapets overhang outward, with 56 shooting holes arranged in sequence, tightly blocking the passage into the ancestral hall; originally there were covered corridors for shelter from wind and rain; at the four corners of the wall there were watchtowers, with clan members stationed as guards year-round, now destroyed. Entering the covered passage from the northeast corner of the ancestral hall, one can see a well surrounded by a tall wall; the wall is built with stone blocks, with the three characters 'Da Shui Jing' (Great Well) carved on the front; descending seventy-two steps, one can see the well. In fact the well is very small, originally a local natural spring well, never drying up in all seasons; before the 19th year of the Republic (1930), the Sichuan army He Guoxiang besieged the Li Family Ancestral Hall; because the city was strong and could not be taken for a long time, they later surrounded the hall and cut off the water supply, forcing the clan head Li Gaiwu to surrender; hence the later wall-building around the well to strengthen water source protection. Additionally, at the southwest and northeast corner gable walls there are respectively the Wanghua Gate (Life Gate) and Cheng'en Gate (Death Gate) two stone gates for entry and exit; not far outside the Death Gate is a cliff, with steep and precipitous rock faces and peculiar scenery; a bridge spans across it, called the Dragon Bridge. The Dragon Bridge River cliff was the place where the Li Manor executed slaves and thieves; legend has it that those sentenced to death by the clan would be escorted from the Life Gate to the Dragon Bridge outside the Death Gate and pushed off the bridge to their death.

365. 李亮清庄园

Li Liangqing Manor
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代、民国
地址 Address
利川市柏杨坝镇水井村
类型 Type
居住建筑
看点 Highlights
中西合璧李亮清庄园位于宗祠北面相距约150米成犄角是一座规模宏大设计独特局部装饰带有西式风格的民居建筑修建于1924年占地4000多平方米整个庄园建筑鳞次栉比共有24个天井174间房屋
中文 Chinese

李亮清庄园位于宗祠北面，相距约150米，成犄角，是一座规模宏大、设计独特、局部装饰带有西式风格的民居建筑。修建于1924年，占地4000多平方米。

整个庄园建筑鳞次栉比，共有24个天井，174间房屋，房屋多为2—3层的楼房，层次分明，错落有致。西部为黄氏旧宅，始建于明朝，木构房屋，低矮古朴，民族特色浓郁；中、东部为清乾隆年间李氏扩建，砖木并用，阁楼高耸，中西合璧。

据介绍，庄园全部采用木骨架，没用一颗铁钉。庄园朝门偏离主体建筑中轴线45度，正对远处山坳，是吉利的屏山山势，满足了人们对风水的追求。门额上书'青莲美荫'四字，取李白自号'青莲居士'中的'青莲'之意，意攀李白为先祖，借以光耀门庭。

前院是主人颇费心思的地方，青石板铺就的院坝围以造型多变的石质坎墙，坎墙两侧逐级跌落，墙檐及线脚饰以彩绘。

与之相对的是一条横贯左右的西式柱廊，系西式拱门走廊，方柱上饰以雕花柱头，粗壮挺拔，雕凿精美，柱间为弧形廊檐，凸显欧式风格，左右两厢横楼则是两层土家吊脚楼，木刻雕花，古朴典雅。

院坝正对的即为庄园主体建筑，三进厅堂依地势逐级拔高，坐西北朝东南，砖木结构，中轴线上排布门楼、前厅、中厅和后殿，均以楼道相连接，形成众多天井。前厅两端又随地势建小院、小姐楼、绣花楼，且有通廊与后进宅院相连，外围建有长工屋和仓房等。

小姐楼高耸于后院东南角，阁楼高出其他屋面，为小姐活动之所，采用一柱六梁结构，建筑法式独特。西北角有一绣楼与小姐楼遥相呼应，楼阁高耸，檐角高翘。

English 英文

Li Liangqing Manor is located north of the ancestral hall, about 150 meters away, forming a strategic corner; it is a residential building of grand scale, unique design, and local decoration with Western-style elements. It was built in 1924, covering more than 4,000 square meters. The entire manor buildings are closely arranged, with a total of 24 courtyards (tianjing) and 174 rooms; the houses are mostly 2–3 story buildings, with distinct layers and well-proportioned arrangement. The western part is the Huang family old residence, first built in the Ming Dynasty, with wooden structures, low and simple, rich in ethnic characteristics; the central and eastern parts were expanded by the Li family during the Qianlong period of the Qing, using both brick and wood, with towering attics, combining Chinese and Western styles. According to reports, the entire manor uses wooden frames, without a single iron nail. The manor gate deviates 45 degrees from the central axis of the main building, directly facing a distant mountain col, an auspicious screen-mountain terrain, satisfying people's pursuit of fengshui. On the door lintel are written the four characters 'Qinglian Meiyin' (Beautiful Shade of Green Lotus), taking the 'Green Lotus' from Li Bai's self-styled 'Qinglian Jushi' (Green Lotus Scholar), meaning to claim Li Bai as an ancestor to glorify the family. The front courtyard is a place where the owner put much thought; the courtyard paved with bluestone slabs is surrounded by stone retaining walls of varied shapes, with both sides of the retaining wall descending in steps, and the wall eaves and moldings decorated with paintings. Opposite to it is a Western-style colonnade spanning left and right, a Western-style arched corridor, with square columns decorated with carved capitals, sturdy and upright, exquisitely carved, with arched eaves between columns, highlighting the European style; the horizontal buildings on the left and right wings are two-story Tujia stilted buildings, with wood carvings, simple and elegant. Directly opposite the courtyard is the main building of the manor; the three-entry halls rise step by step according to the terrain, facing southeast from northwest, of brick-wood structure; on the central axis are arranged the gate tower, front hall, middle hall, and rear hall, all connected by corridors, forming numerous courtyards. At both ends of the front hall, small courtyards, young lady towers, and embroidery towers are built according to the terrain, with covered passages connecting to the rear courtyards; outside there are hired-hand houses and granaries, etc. The young lady tower stands high at the southeast corner of the rear courtyard, with its attic higher than other roofs, serving as the activity place for young ladies; it adopts a one-column six-beam structure, with a unique architectural method. In the northwest corner there is an embroidery tower echoing the young lady tower from afar, with the tower towering and eave corners high upturned.

366. 李盖五旧宅

Former Residence of Li Gaiwu
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
民国
地址 Address
利川市柏杨坝镇高仰村
类型 Type
居住建筑
看点 Highlights
中西合璧李盖五旧宅位于庄园东北距庄园约4公里原址为葡萄瓮宅址取高山仰止之意命名高仰台建筑中西合璧两进四院占地3000余平方米建筑面积2000余平方米有房屋40多间造型结构与李亮清庄园相仿
中文 Chinese

李盖五旧宅位于庄园东北，距庄园约4公里，原址为葡萄瓮，宅址取'高山仰止'之意，命名'高仰台'。建筑中西合璧，两进四院，占地3000余平方米，建筑面积2000余平方米，有房屋40多间，造型结构与李亮清庄园相仿，保存较好。

笔者到访时正维修中，尚未开放参观。整个庄园建筑飞檐翘角，精雕细琢，鬼斧神工，其匠心工艺丝毫不亚于与之遥相对应的李家宗祠和李亮清庄园，不仅从点上增加了该建筑群的密度，而且从左右两边进一步烘托出李氏宗祠的中心高度。

建筑的建造模式基本仿照成都文殊院，风格类似南方汉族的祠堂，但天井院落的位置、结构、大小等方面又在别于其他汉族地区的四合院天井，具有明显的土家族建筑特色，是土家族'吊脚楼'建筑与中国传统四合院相结合的典范，兼具土家族与汉族民居的风格。

建筑群建造工艺精湛，在设计中还运用了西方古典主义的建筑手法，是中西合璧的一座艺术瑰宝。

English 英文

The Former Residence of Li Gaiwu is located northeast of the manor, about 4 km from the manor; the original site was Putao Weng (Grape Jar); the residence site takes the meaning of 'looking up to a high mountain' and is named 'Gaoyangtai' (High Admiration Terrace). The building combines Chinese and Western styles, with two entries and four courtyards, covering more than 3,000 square meters, with a building area of more than 2,000 square meters and more than 40 rooms; its shape and structure are similar to Li Liangqing Manor, and it is well-preserved. When the author visited, it was under repair and not yet open for visits. The entire manor building has flying eaves and upturned corners, exquisitely carved, with supernatural craftsmanship; its ingenious craftsmanship is in no way inferior to the Li Family Ancestral Hall and Li Liangqing Manor that echo it from afar; it not only increases the density of the building complex at points, but also further sets off the central height of the Li Family Ancestral Hall from the left and right sides. The construction mode of the building basically imitates Wenshu Monastery in Chengdu, with a style similar to southern Han ancestral halls; however, in terms of the position, structure, and size of the courtyard (tianjing), it differs from the four-sided courtyard of other Han areas, with obvious Tujia architectural characteristics; it is a model of the combination of Tujia 'stilted building' architecture and traditional Chinese four-sided courtyards, combining both Tujia and Han residential styles. The building complex has exquisite construction craftsmanship, and also uses Western classical architectural techniques in its design; it is an artistic treasure combining Chinese and Western styles.

367. 鱼木寨

Yumu Stockaded Village
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明代
地址 Address
利川市谋道镇鱼木村
类型 Type
民居建筑
看点 Highlights
选址遗址环境鱼木寨又名鱼目寨、舆木寨土家族人村寨位于鄂渝边界处始建于明洪武二年（1369）清嘉庆年间重建至清雍正十三年（1735）一直为土司军事要塞山寨孤悬山崖顶端寨上村庄海拔1150米
中文 Chinese

鱼木寨，又名鱼目寨、舆木寨，土家族人村寨，位于鄂渝边界处，始建于明洪武二年（1369），清嘉庆年间重建，至清雍正十三年（1735）一直为土司军事要塞。

山寨孤悬山崖顶端，寨上村庄海拔1150米，四周悬崖峭壁，沟壑纵横，几乎与外界隔绝，唯寨西南有一处石板古道与外界相通。清同治五年（1866）增修《万县志》载：'鱼木寨山高峻，四周壁立，广约十里，形如鼗鼓，以鼓柄入寨门，其径险仄。

'有说法认为山寨三面环山，形如一柄渔鼓，得名鱼木寨。也有传说明代此寨名为成家寨，属龙阳洞谭土司管辖，后石柱土司图谋此地，出兵围困，断其水源，久攻不下。数月之后，谭土司派人从寨东的岩洞口向下抛掷活鱼，有的鱼就落在了马土司帐前的树枝上。

马土司感叹攻克此寨，犹如缘木求鱼，因此得名'鱼木寨'。不过也有说法认为守寨的是马土司，攻寨的是谭土司。抛开历史真相不论，正是因为有天堑之势，鱼木寨形成守卫的天然屏障，才使得这里免遭战火涂炭。鱼木寨现为一个居民五六百人的自然村，土家族、苗族和汉族人民共同居住。

寨顶平坦略呈椭圆，南北长约2公里，东西宽约1公里。进入鱼木寨一般有寨门楼、三阳关、亮梯子3条通道，南边寨门楼最方便，公路修好后开车可抵达。另两条进寨道路全以条石铺砌，石级陡窄，建于绝壁之上，人来往需手脚并用，堪称天险。

手扒岩是鱼木寨北面的通道，为古人上寨要径，过了手扒岩，就是三阳关。台阶凿于悬崖上，共32级石梯，形如新月，步距约0.5米。在一排仅可踏足的石梯旁，凿有数处方形孔穴，据说孔内曾安有石柱，石柱上牵有铁链，上下攀爬时可做扶手，因此俗称'手扒岩'。

亮梯子建于寨东绝壁之上，更奇更险，直上直下共28级石板，每级条石长约1.5米、宽约0.4米，一头半插在岩壁中，一半悬空。攀登此路犹如踏在一条垂直的旋梯上，向下望一眼也会胆战心惊。寨门楼位于山寨入口，为保山寨安全，横跨于通向山寨的狭路之上，两侧与山脊绝壁取齐。

坐北朝南，分前后两部分，上下两层四间，平面呈梯形，前宽后窄。前楼面阔一间，进深一间，以规整条石铺就，上端稍有收分，下层中间开门，门额正楷阴刻'鱼木寨'三字，其上设炮台，留有两排共9个射击孔，以利作战。

除营建寨楼外，还在寨楼东、西两侧的山崖下各由石条垒筑一段石寨墙，单从今天残存的片段来看，也足见'一夫当关，万夫莫开'之势。

此外，三阳关、樟凤坪和福堰塘3处岩石上还各建卡门一座，现樟凤坪卡门已被拆除，其余2座保存较好，特别是三阳关卡门，门上古木葱郁，两侧巨石巍峨，真可谓'人在卡内不知卡前有路，人行山外不知崖内藏关'。

鱼木寨现存少数穿斗式木构建筑，最具代表性的是大湾下老房子向氏老屋，又名'六吉堂'，是鱼木寨木构房屋中最大的建筑。始建于清末，建成于民国九年（1920），坐西朝东，占地约1000余平方米，四合院式布局，主体建筑面阔五间，进深三间。

正堂高耸，堂前有可作为戏楼的抱厦，高出院坝1.5米，与前厅相对。戏台为单层，平面呈'凸'字形，正中有石质台阶4级，左右两侧雕饰山水人物。前廊石阶壁左右各嵌石刻一通，正楷阴刻《南阳柴夫子训子格言》，中心院坝用规整石板铺砌，两侧设有看楼。

寨内石碑石墓规模宏大且工艺精湛，虽部分已在'文革'中移除，现仍存清代碑墓10座，碑高一般都在5米以上，墓葬十分豪华。石碑多为牌楼式，也有塔式、牌坊式、圆顶式、平卧式等，石雕题材丰富，雕饰细腻生动。

English 英文

Yumu (Fish-Wood) Stockaded Village, also called Yumu Village or Yumu Village, is a Tujia ethnic village located at the border of Hubei and Chongqing; it was first built in the 2nd year of Hongwu, Ming (1369), rebuilt during the Jiaqing period of the Qing, and remained a chieftain military fortress until the 13th year of Yongzheng, Qing (1735). The mountain village hangs alone at the top of a cliff; the village on the stockade is at an altitude of 1150 meters, surrounded by steep cliffs and crisscrossed gullies, almost isolated from the outside world; only in the southwest of the stockade is there an ancient stone road connecting with the outside. The 'Wan County Annals' revised in the 5th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1866), records: 'Yumu Stockade has high and steep mountains, with cliffs standing on all sides, about ten li wide, shaped like a pellet drum, with the drum handle entering the stockade gate, and the path is dangerous and narrow.' Some say the stockade is surrounded by mountains on three sides, shaped like a fishing drum, hence the name Yumu Stockade. There is also a legend that in the Ming this stockade was named Chengjia Stockade, under the jurisdiction of Tusi Tan of Longyang Cave; later Tusi of Shizhu plotted to take this place, sent troops to besiege it, cut off its water source, but could not take it for a long time. After several months, Tusi Tan sent people to throw live fish down from the cave entrance east of the stockade, and some fish landed on the branches in front of Tusi Ma's tent. Tusi Ma sighed that conquering this stockade was like climbing a tree to catch fish, hence the name 'Yumu Stockade' (Fish-Wood Stockade). However, some say the one defending the stockade was Tusi Ma and the one attacking was Tusi Tan. Leaving aside the historical truth, it is precisely because of the natural barrier that Yumu Stockade formed a natural defensive barrier, sparing it from the ravages of war. Yumu Stockade is now a natural village with five to six hundred residents, where Tujia, Miao, and Han people live together. The top of the stockade is flat and slightly elliptical, about 2 km long from north to south and 1 km wide from east to west. There are generally 3 passages into Yumu Stockade: the Stockade Gate Tower, Sanyang Pass, and Liang Ladder; the south Stockade Gate Tower is the most convenient, and after the road was built, one can arrive by car. The other two entry roads are all paved with dressed stones, with steep and narrow stone steps built on precipices; people going back and forth need to use both hands and feet, which can be called a natural danger. Shoupa Rock (Hand-Climbing Rock) is the passage on the north side of Yumu Stockade, an important path for ancient people to climb the stockade; after passing Shoupa Rock, one reaches Sanyang Pass. The steps are chiseled on the cliff, with a total of 32 stone ladders, shaped like a crescent moon, with a step distance of about 0.5 meters. Beside a row of stone ladders that can only be stepped on, several square holes are chiseled; it is said that stone columns were once installed in the holes, with iron chains attached to the columns, serving as handrails when climbing up and down, hence commonly called 'Shoupa Rock' (Hand-Climbing Rock). The Liang Ladder (Bright Ladder) is built on the cliff east of the stockade, even more peculiar and dangerous; straight up and down there are 28 stone slabs, each dressed stone about 1.5 meters long and 0.4 meters wide, with one end half inserted in the rock wall and half suspended. Climbing this path is like stepping on a vertical spiral staircase; even a glance downward would make one tremble with fear. The Stockade Gate Tower is located at the entrance of the mountain village; to ensure the safety of the stockade, it spans across the narrow road leading to the stockade, with both sides aligned with the ridge cliffs. Facing south from north, it is divided into front and rear parts, with two stories and four rooms, with a trapezoidal plane, wide in front and narrow in back. The front building is one bay wide and one bay deep, paved with regular dressed stones, with a slight tapering at the upper end; a door opens in the middle of the lower floor, with the three characters 'Yumu Zhai' carved in regular script intaglio on the lintel; above it is a gun platform, with two rows of 9 shooting holes in total for combat. Besides building the stockade tower, stone stockade walls were also built with dressed stones under the cliffs on the east and west sides of the stockade tower; judging from the surviving fragments today, one can see the momentum of 'one man guarding the pass, ten thousand cannot pass.' In addition, a check gate was built on each of the 3 rocks at Sanyang Pass, Zhangfengping, and Fuyantang; now the Zhangfengping check gate has been demolished, and the other 2 are well-preserved; especially the Sanyang Pass check gate, with ancient trees lush on the gate and giant rocks towering on both sides, it can truly be said that 'people inside the check gate do not know there is a road before it, and people outside the mountain do not know there is a pass hidden in the cliff.' Yumu Stockade now has a few column-and-tie wooden buildings; the most representative is the Xiang family old house at Dawanxia, also called 'Liuji Tang' (Six Auspicious Hall), the largest wooden building in Yumu Stockade. It was first built at the end of the Qing and completed in the 9th year of the Republic (1920), facing east from west, covering about 1,000 square meters, with a four-sided courtyard layout; the main building is five bays wide and three bays deep. The main hall is towering; in front of the hall there is a front porch that can serve as a theater tower, 1.5 meters higher than the courtyard, opposite the front hall. The stage is single-story, with a 'convex'-shaped plane, with 4 stone steps in the center, and landscapes and figures carved on both left and right sides. On the left and right of the front porch stone step wall, a stone carving is embedded respectively, with the 'Admonitions of Master Chai of Nanyang to His Son' carved in regular script intaglio; the central courtyard is paved with regular stone slabs, with viewing towers on both sides. The stone steles and stone tombs in the stockade are large in scale and exquisite in craftsmanship; although some were removed during the 'Cultural Revolution,' 10 Qing stele-tombs still exist, with steles generally over 5 meters high, and the tombs are very luxurious. Most stone steles are of the paifang (memorial arch) style, but there are also tower-style, paifang-style, dome-style, and horizontal-style ones; the stone carving themes are rich, and the carvings are delicate and vivid.

368. 石龙寺

Shilong Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明代
地址 Address
利川市团堡镇北侧的石龙山上
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
石雕利川团堡镇北侧有一小山团而不圆名团凸山又叫石龙山山上有一古寺内有石龙名曰石龙寺石龙寺始建于明洪武初年为酉阳土司冉如龙家庙清代历经数次重修做过佛寺
中文 Chinese

利川团堡镇北侧有一小山，团而不圆，名团凸山，又叫石龙山，山上有一古寺，内有石龙，名曰'石龙寺'。石龙寺始建于明洪武初年，为酉阳土司冉如龙家庙，清代历经数次重修，做过佛寺、设过义学；民国二十六年（1937）再次扩建，寺前增建碉楼，寺后建厅堂；

1949年后，先后为粮食仓库，后为团堡乡党校。

石龙寺为殿堂式庙宇建筑，坐北朝南，殿高10余米，建筑面积约2000平方米，砖木结构，四进三院布局，中轴线上有山门、正殿、大佛殿及后殿，两侧有厢房，因大佛殿前天井里有卧石，形似卧龙而得名。

寺内现存大小碑刻20多块，记述石龙寺的兴衰始末，碑刻年代上起乾隆，下至光绪，内容涉及当地政治、经济、法律、社会、结构、宗教、教育诸多方面，尤其是对于冉氏一家记载详细。石龙寺山门为单檐歇山灰瓦顶，两侧环以一圈白墙灰瓦的院墙，略高于山门。

笔者到访时正值盛夏，院外绿植青翠，林木茂盛，自然变得一股子清凉。一进山门，四周为砖墙砌体，正殿内木构架穿枋联结，木柱粗厚扎实，木枋浮雕精美，楼台廊庑相互映衬。大佛殿面阔五间，进深四间，是寺的第二殿，也叫练功殿，相传是石龙寺佛家弟子习武练功的地方。

English 英文

North of Tuanbao Town, Lichuan City, there is a small mountain, round but not circular, named Tuantuo Mountain, also called Shilong (Stone Dragon) Mountain; on the mountain there is an ancient temple, with a stone dragon inside, called 'Shilong Temple.' Shilong Temple was first built in the early Hongwu period of the Ming, serving as the family temple of Ran Rulong, Tusi of Youyang; it underwent several repairs in the Qing, serving as a Buddhist temple and a free school; in the 26th year of the Republic (1937), it was expanded again, with a watchtower added in front of the temple and a hall built behind the temple; after 1949, it successively served as a grain warehouse and later as the Party School of Tuanbao Township. Shilong Temple is a hall-style temple building, facing south, with halls over 10 meters high and a building area of about 2,000 square meters, of brick-wood structure, with a four-entry three-courtyard layout; on the central axis there are the mountain gate, main hall, Great Buddha Hall, and rear hall, with wing rooms on both sides; it gets its name because there is a lying stone in the courtyard (tianjing) in front of the Great Buddha Hall, shaped like a crouching dragon. More than 20 stone steles of various sizes remain in the temple, recording the rise and fall of Shilong Temple; the stele dates range from Qianlong to Guangxu, covering local politics, economy, law, society, structure, religion, education, and many other aspects, especially with detailed records of the Ran family. The mountain gate of Shilong Temple has a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, surrounded by a circle of white-walled gray-tile courtyard walls, slightly higher than the mountain gate. When the author visited, it was midsummer; outside the courtyard the green plants were lush and the trees were dense, naturally bringing a sense of coolness. Upon entering the mountain gate, the surroundings are brick-wall masonry; in the main hall, the wooden frame is connected by through-tenons, with thick and solid wooden columns, exquisite reliefs on wooden beams, and towers, terraces, and corridors setting each other off. The Great Buddha Hall is five bays wide and four bays deep, the second hall of the temple, also called the Training Hall; legend has it that it was the place where Buddhist disciples of Shilong Temple practiced martial arts. 369. 如膏书院

Rugao Academy
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
利川市南坪乡南坪镇，南坪小学校内
类型 Type
教育建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
石雕藻井如膏书院是利川置县后最早的义学之一始建于清乾隆五十八年南坪巡检王霖兴建清嘉庆三年被焚历时三年重建光绪十八年改书院为学堂1949年后改为小学现今位于南坪乡南坪小学校内围有防护栅栏保护较好
中文 Chinese

如膏书院是利川置县后最早的义学之一，始建于清乾隆五十八年（1793），南坪巡检王霖兴建，清嘉庆三年(1798)被焚，历时三年重建，光绪十八年（1892）改书院为学堂，1949年后改为小学。

现今位于南坪乡南坪小学校内，围有防护栅栏，保护较好。建筑坐北朝南，中轴对称布局，共三进两厢，现两厢已毁（新建右厢房），仅存前楼、正厅和后殿。

前楼名为魁星楼，砖木结构，山门呈拱形，白石灰抹墙面，面阔五间，进深两间，明、次间为硬山灰瓦顶，稍间为单层悬山顶。

入山门至过厅，其上为二层三间戏楼，略高出厢房屋顶1.5米，戏台两侧设木梯，与一层相通，可供上下。戏楼前为一院坝，内植两柱直径粗大的桂花树，现一株枝叶繁茂，一枝丫枯萎，略发几枝新芽。

正厅为大成殿，悬山灰瓦顶，面阔、进深各三间，均约15米，抬梁式木构架，殿内16根木柱，柱基石雕刻差较大。山墙内壁及庭院内散存数通碑刻，均为正楷阴刻，碑文较为系统地记述了南坪地方建书院、改学校的始末缘由。

正厅后起一阁楼与后殿相连，阁楼室内顶棚有八卦藻井，藻井下神龛前立有一块汉白玉分石心，蟠龙石雕龙头昂然向上，气势轩昂，四周密布祥云图饰，造型生动。阁楼两侧左右对称布置两天井，凸显了大成殿的宽敞明亮。

后殿为悬山灰瓦，面阔三间，进深二间，靠正殿楼阁处设舞台。现书院四周围绿树掩映，环境清幽，果真是一处读书的好去处。

书院东侧500米处有一座楼阁式七级石塔，名凌云塔，又名文笔塔，是如膏书院的风水塔，与其余两处古塔合称为'利川三塔'。

English 英文

Rugao Academy was one of the earliest free schools after Lichuan was established as a county; it was first built in the 58th year of Qianlong, Qing (1793), built by Wang Lin, Nanping Inspector; it was burned in the 3rd year of Jiaqing (1798) and rebuilt over three years; in the 18th year of Guangxu (1892), the academy was changed to a school; after 1949, it was changed to a primary school. It is now located inside Nanping Primary School, Nanping Township, surrounded by protective fences, well-preserved. The building faces south, with a centrally symmetric layout, three entries and two wings; now both wings have been destroyed (a new right wing has been built), only the front tower, main hall, and rear hall remain. The front tower is named Kuixing Tower, of brick-wood structure; the mountain gate is arched, with white lime plastered walls, five bays wide and two bays deep; the central and secondary bays have gable gray-tile roofs, while the side bays have single-story overhanging gable roofs. Entering the mountain gate to the passage hall, above it is a two-story three-bay theater tower, slightly 1.5 meters higher than the wing roof; wooden ladders are set on both sides of the stage, connected to the first floor for going up and down. In front of the theater tower is a courtyard, with two osmanthus trees of large diameter planted inside; now one has lush branches and leaves, while one branch has withered, slightly sprouting a few new buds. The main hall is the Dacheng Hall, with an overhanging gable gray-tile roof, three bays wide and three bays deep, both about 15 meters, with a post-and-lintel wooden frame; there are 16 wooden columns in the hall, with relatively large differences in the carving of the column base stones. Several steles are scattered on the inner walls of the gable walls and in the courtyard, all in regular script intaglio; the inscriptions systematically record the whole story of building the academy and changing it to a school in Nanping. Behind the main hall, an attic is built connected to the rear hall; the indoor ceiling of the attic has a Bagua (Eight Trigrams) caisson; in front of the shrine under the caisson stands a white marble heart-shaped stone, with a coiling-dragon stone carving with the dragon head raised upward, imposing and dignified, surrounded by dense auspicious cloud decorations, vivid in shape. On both left and right sides of the attic, two courtyards (tianjing) are symmetrically arranged, highlighting the spaciousness and brightness of the Dacheng Hall. The rear hall has an overhanging gable gray-tile roof, three bays wide and two bays deep, with a stage set near the main hall attic. Now the academy is surrounded by green trees, with a quiet and elegant environment, truly a good place for reading. 500 meters east of the academy there is a pavilion-style seven-story stone pagoda named Lingyun Pagoda, also called Wenbi Pagoda, which is the fengshui pagoda of Rugao Academy, and together with the other two ancient pagodas is called the 'Three Pagodas of Lichuan.'

370. 三元堂

Sanyuan Taoist Temple
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
利川市忠路镇八圣乡木坝河南岸
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
选址环境整体格局由利彭公路下车路边矗立着湖北省文物保护单位所立的三元堂碑志顺着垂直公路的一段不足50米的水泥铺路向山坳走一眼便可看见主体建筑为黄色的三元堂三元堂基址位于背山面水的龙穴之地堂前约100米处有郁江水流过木坝河大桥如长虹飞跨其上形成开阔的视域堂后群山起伏远处寨公、寨母两峰并置
中文 Chinese

由利彭公路下车，路边矗立着湖北省文物保护单位所立的'三元堂'碑志，顺着垂直公路的一段不足50米的水泥铺路向山坳走，一眼便可看见主体建筑为黄色的三元堂。三元堂基址位于背山面水的'龙穴'之地，堂前约100米处有郁江水流过，木坝河大桥如长虹飞跨其上，形成开阔的视域；

堂后群山起伏，远处寨公、寨母两峰并置，极富层次感与景深；四周古木苍翠，风景秀美，道观掩映于这样的大环境中更显清雅幽静。三元堂为清代道教宫观，道家以天、地、水为三元，故称三元堂。旧时，观内道众长期义渡木坝河两岸过往百姓，广行善事，也被称为善堂。

始建年代不详，据光绪年间《利川县志》推断，该观始建年代最迟在清光绪八年（1882），现存主体建筑为光绪二十七年（1901）在原址基础上扩建而成。

道观坐北朝南，依地势逐进升高呈阶梯式分布，砖木结构，共两进厢一阁，中轴线建筑有门厅、正殿及玉皇阁，为土家族祠庙'二厅一阁'的典型做法，两侧分布厢房等附属建筑，周围建有围墙。

建筑主体呈明黄色，色彩艳丽，屋顶歇山与悬山共存，屋面高低起伏，错落有致，正因为建筑巧妙的布局，使得道...

English 英文

Getting off at the Lipeng Highway, by the roadside stands the 'Sanyuan Tang' stele erected by the Hubei Provincial Cultural Heritage Protection Unit; walking along a cement road of less than 50 meters perpendicular to the highway toward the mountain col, one can at a glance see the Sanyuan Tang with its main building in yellow. The site of Sanyuan Tang is located at a 'dragon lair' place backing onto mountains and facing water; about 100 meters in front of the hall, the Yu River flows by, and the Muba River Bridge spans across it like a long rainbow, forming an open field of view; behind the hall, mountains rise and fall, and in the distance the two peaks of Zaigong and Zhaimu stand side by side, rich in layering and depth; surrounded by lush ancient trees and beautiful scenery, the Taoist temple is even more elegant and quiet set in such a grand environment. Sanyuan Tang is a Qing Dynasty Taoist temple; Taoists take Heaven, Earth, and Water as the Three Primes (Sanyuan), hence the name Sanyuan Tang. In old times, the Taoist priests in the temple long provided free ferry service for people crossing the Muba River on both banks, doing good deeds widely, hence it was also called the Good Deeds Hall. The founding date is unknown; according to the 'Lichuan County Annals' of the Guangxu period, it is inferred that the temple was founded no later than the 8th year of Guangxu, Qing (1882); the existing main building was expanded on the original site in the 27th year of Guangxu (1901). The Taoist temple faces south, rising step by step according to the terrain in a terraced distribution, of brick-wood structure, with two entries, wings, and one pavilion; the buildings on the central axis include the entrance hall, main hall, and Yuhuang (Jade Emperor) Pavilion, a typical practice of Tujia ancestral temples 'two halls and one pavilion'; on both sides are distributed auxiliary buildings such as wing rooms, surrounded by a wall. The main building is bright yellow, with bright colors; the roofs coexist hip-and-gable and overhanging gable styles, with the roof surfaces rising and falling, well-proportioned; precisely because of the clever layout of the building, the Taoist...

371. 花梨岭天主堂

Hualiling Catholic Church
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
利川市凉雾乡花梨村
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖、石、木结构
看点 Highlights
男、女堂分设之格局教堂位于花梨村10组四周群山环抱古木成群环境极其幽静始建年代不详初建成时曾有英国、法国、荷兰、比利时等国的传教士在此传教现为旧貌重修占地约10余公顷建筑面积3000余平方米分男堂、女堂两部分
中文 Chinese

教堂位于花梨村10组，四周群山环抱，古木成群，环境极其幽静。始建年代不详，初建成时，曾有英国、法国、荷兰、比利时等国的传教士在此传教，现为旧貌重修。占地约10余公顷，建筑面积3000余平方米，分男堂、女堂两部分。

教堂入口为一标示性的五拱券山门，蓝灰瓷砖贴面，其后一片翠植，过山门径直往前便来到女堂，分两部分，前为育婴堂，单檐悬山灰瓦顶，三开间二层小楼，屋内有展示花梨岭天主教简介的各类图文资料。

据传'育婴堂'名为收养婴孩，实际上'常有剖腹剖心之惨'，'活焚育婴为医用'，后被'义民'焚烧，发生了震惊一时的'花梨岭教案'，光绪二十六年（1900），'大府迫于西人之挟，不得不重惩吾民，以弥衅而修睦'，光绪皇帝亲笔题匾'敕建天主教堂'赔款重建，于清光绪三十二年（1906）建成。

女堂后为修道院，坐东朝西，木构四合院建筑，平面呈矩形，面宽约70余米，进深约25米，内有天井，四周有石砌围墙，圈地约3000平方米。

出女堂门前石铺地登九十九石梯可见男堂山门，入山门还有两道院门，院门与三面建筑围合一天井院落，建筑为白墙灰瓦顶，正堂为二层楼，左面建筑为一楼一阁，悬山瓦顶，檐口与正屋二楼窗台齐平；

右面建筑为礼拜堂，一层高跨结构，穹隆顶，檐口与正屋檐口平齐，立面方形砖柱对称排列，窗明瓦亮，朴素大方。教堂两角建碉楼，据说是用来做了望台，四周均有用青石凿成的内大外小的望孔，防卫严谨。男女礼拜堂内均设祭台、置桌椅、挂圣像，整个经堂宽敞气派、庄严肃穆。

女院经堂正前为一圆穹顶舞台，男教堂则为尖三角形吊顶，正前方十字架上面是一幅《最后的晚餐》画作，其上是一块书有'万王之王'的黑匾，左边的展览室还陈列了展品。

English 英文

The church is located in Group 10, Huali Village, surrounded by mountains on all sides, with clusters of ancient trees and an extremely quiet environment. The founding date is unknown; when first built, missionaries from Britain, France, the Netherlands, Belgium and other countries preached here; it has now been restored to its original appearance. It covers about 10 hectares, with a building area of more than 3,000 square meters, divided into male and female halls. The church entrance is a symbolic five-arched mountain gate, faced with blue-gray tiles, followed by a patch of green vegetation; passing through the mountain gate and going straight forward, one arrives at the female hall, divided into two parts; the front is the Foundling Home, a single-eave overhanging gable gray-tile roof, a three-bay two-story small building, with various graphic and textual materials displaying an introduction to Hualiling Catholicism inside. Legend has it that the 'Foundling Home,' named for adopting infants, in fact 'often had the tragedy of cutting open abdomens and hearts,' and 'burning infants alive for medical use'; later it was burned by 'righteous people,' causing the 'Hualiling Church Case' that shocked the time. In the 26th year of Guangxu (1900), 'the high officials, forced by the Westerners, had to severely punish our people to quell the dispute and maintain peace'; Emperor Guangxu personally inscribed a plaque 'Imperially Built Catholic Church' and paid compensation for reconstruction, completed in the 32nd year of Guangxu, Qing (1906). Behind the female hall is the monastery, facing west from east, a wooden four-sided courtyard building, with a rectangular plane, about 70 meters wide and 25 meters deep, with a courtyard (tianjing) inside, surrounded by stone walls, enclosing about 3,000 square meters. Exiting the front stone pavement of the female hall and climbing ninety-nine stone steps, one can see the male hall mountain gate; entering the mountain gate there are two more courtyard gates; the courtyard gates and the three-sided buildings enclose a courtyard, with white walls and gray-tile roofs; the main hall is a two-story building; the left building is one story with one pavilion, with an overhanging gable tile roof, and the eaves are level with the second-floor window sill of the main house; the right building is the chapel, a one-story high-span structure with a dome, and the eaves are level with the eaves of the main hall; on the facade, square brick columns are symmetrically arranged, with bright windows and tiles, simple and elegant. At both corners of the church, watchtowers were built, said to be used as observation platforms; on all sides there are observation holes chiseled from bluestone, large inside and small outside, with strict defense. Both male and female chapels have altars, tables and chairs, and hanging holy images; the entire chapel is spacious, imposing, solemn and dignified. Directly in front of the female chapel is a domed stage; the male church has a pointed triangular ceiling; above the cross in front is a painting of 'The Last Supper,' above which is a black plaque inscribed 'King of Kings'; the exhibition room on the left also displays exhibits.

Three Pagodas in Lichuan
