看点 Highlights
五云楼九曲黄河墙太子坡净乐国太子15岁入山修炼紫气元君化老妇用铁杵磨针点化永乐十二年始建嘉靖年间扩建清康熙乾隆4次重修1.6万平方米105间九曲黄河墙五云楼4层
中文 Chinese

俗称'太子坡'，是传说中净乐国太子15岁入武当山修炼时最初居住的地方。后来太子意志不坚，私自下山，在回家的路上遇到紫气元君幻化而成的老妇，用铁杵磨针点化，复又上山修炼，这组建筑因而得名复真观。

始建于明永乐十二年（1414），嘉靖年间扩建，清康熙、乾隆年间4次重修。建筑群依山势展开，占地面积约1.6万平方米，有宫门、九曲黄河墙、龙虎殿、祖师殿、斗姆楼、藏经阁、皇经堂和五云楼等，共105间。

其中，走进宫门后夹道随山势曲折，两侧的九曲黄河墙高低起伏，不见首尾，使人感到神秘而威严。而高达4层的五云楼则是武当山最高的建筑，室内一根立柱上穿插交叠十二根梁，被誉为'一柱十二梁'。

English 英文

Commonly called 'Taizi Slope' (Crown Prince Slope), it is the place where, according to legend, the crown prince of the Jingle Kingdom first lived when he entered Wudang Mountain to cultivate at the age of 15. Later, the crown prince's will was not firm and he secretly went down the mountain; on his way home, he met an old woman transformed by Ziyuan Zhenjun, who enlightened him by grinding an iron pestle into a needle, so he returned to the mountain to cultivate, hence this building group is named Fuzhen (Returning to Truth) Temple. It was first built in the 12th year of Yongle, Ming (1414), expanded during the Jiajing period, and rebuilt 4 times during the Kangxi and Qianlong periods of the Qing. The building group unfolds along the mountain terrain, covering about 16,000 square meters, with 105 rooms including the palace gate, Nine-Bend Yellow River Wall, Dragon-Tiger Hall, Patriarch Hall, Doumu Tower, Scripture Pavilion, Huangjing Hall, and Wuyun (Five Clouds) Tower. Among them, after entering the palace gate, the夹道 winds along the mountain terrain, and the Nine-Bend Yellow River Walls on both sides rise and fall, with neither beginning nor end visible, making people feel mysterious and solemn. The four-story Wuyun Tower is the tallest building on Wudang Mountain; inside, twelve beams are interlaced on one column, hailed as 'one column with twelve beams.'

436. 治世玄岳牌坊

Zhishixuanyue Memorial Archway
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清
地址 Address
武当山镇东6公里
类型 Type
标志建筑·石结构
看点 Highlights
明代石雕玄岳门古均州城至武当山的官道与朝山进香的神道相接之处嘉靖三十一年始建清乾隆二十年修缮四柱三间五楼仿木式样石牌坊通高近12米柱高6米巨大的碌墩石柱顶架龙门枋明间嵌巨大横匾两面均镌刻嘉靖皇帝所题治世玄岳四个大字
中文 Chinese

'治世玄岳'牌坊，俗称玄岳门，位于古均州城至武当山的官道与朝山进香的神道相接之处，进入此门，便由人间进入仙山范围。始建于明嘉靖三十一年（1552），清乾隆二十年（1755）修缮。

坐西朝东，四柱三间五楼仿木式样石牌坊，通高近12米。其中柱高6米有余，下有巨大的碌墩石。柱顶架龙门枋，明间嵌一块巨大的横匾，两面均镌刻嘉靖皇帝所题'治世玄岳'四个大字。

石匾之上为又一道额枋，额枋上置六攒七踩斗拱，上承屋顶，屋脊上有鸱吻、宝瓶等装饰。两侧的次间、尽间分为两层，按照云板、额枋、斗拱、屋顶的顺序，依次架设。

整个石坊的雕刻装饰异常华美，虽然匾额、斗拱等使用了皇家才能使用的规制，但雕刻题材却一反官式建筑中常见的龙凤狮子，而是鳌鱼、蟠龙、仙鹤、云水、水浪、如意、卷草和神仙人物图案，使得整个牌坊充满了神仙之气。

线刻、浮雕、圆雕和透雕等技法使用娴熟，是明代石雕中的上乘佳作。治世玄岳石坊是明世宗嘉靖皇帝大修武当山的代表建筑，表达了嘉靖以道教治理天下的愿望。

世宗崇信道教，在位时又多次逢凶化吉，为报答真武大帝的庇佑，按照明成祖的做法，成立了专门的指挥机构。施工之时恰逢郧阳、襄阳连年灾荒，朝廷转而以工代赈，不仅招募了大量廉价劳动力，节约了大批资金，也救济了灾民。

工程历时1年零4个月，除了修建石坊，还维修了八宫和其所辖庙观的屋面，更换琉璃瓦，重做油漆彩绘，修补宫墙、台基、沟渠和神道、石桥等，并新增5座琉璃建筑。

English 英文

The 'Zhishi Xuanyue' (Governing the World, Mysterious Mountain) Archway, commonly called Xuanyue Gate, is located at the junction of the official road from ancient Junzhou city to Wudang Mountain and the sacred path for pilgrimages to the mountain; entering this gate, one moves from the human world into the scope of the immortal mountain. It was first built in the 31st year of Jiajing, Ming (1552), and repaired in the 20th year of Qianlong, Qing (1755). Facing east from west, it is a four-column three-bay five-story imitation-wood-style stone archway, with a total height of nearly 12 meters. The columns are more than 6 meters high, with huge lu-dun stones below. On top of the columns, longmen (dragon-gate) lintels are placed; in the central bay, a huge horizontal plaque is embedded, with the four large characters 'Zhishi Xuanyue' inscribed by the Jiajing Emperor on both sides. Above the stone plaque is another architrave; on the architrave, six sets of seven-step bracket sets are placed, supporting the roof; on the ridge there are decorations such as chiwen (dragon-like roof ornaments) and treasure vases. The secondary and end bays on both sides are divided into two stories, erected in sequence according to the order of cloud boards, architraves, bracket sets, and roofs. The carved decoration of the entire stone archway is extraordinarily gorgeous; although the plaque and bracket sets use regulations that only the imperial family could use, the carving themes, contrary to the dragon, phoenix, and lion commonly seen in official-style buildings, are patterns of mythical fish, coiling dragons, cranes, cloud-water, water waves, ruyi (auspicious), scrolling grass, and immortal figures, making the entire archway full of immortal atmosphere. Techniques such as line carving, relief carving, round carving, and openwork carving are used skillfully, making it a superior masterpiece of Ming stone carving. The Zhishi Xuanyue Stone Archway is a representative building of the Jiajing Emperor Shizong of Ming's large-scale renovation of Wudang Mountain, expressing Jiajing desire to govern the world through Taoism. Shizong believed in Taoism, and during his reign he repeatedly escaped danger; to repay the protection of the Great Emperor Zhenwu, following the practice of Emperor Chengzu of Ming, he established a special command organization. At the time of construction, it coincided with successive years of famine in Yunyang and Xiangyang; the court instead used work as relief, not only recruiting a large amount of cheap labor and saving a great deal of funds, but also relieving the disaster victims. The project lasted 1 year and 4 months; in addition to building the stone archway, it also repaired the roofs of the eight palaces and their subordinate temples, replaced glazed tiles, redid paint and colored drawings, repaired palace walls, pedestals, ditches, sacred paths, and stone bridges, and added 5 new glazed buildings.

437. 琼台中观

Qiongtai Taoist Temple (Middle)
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
元、明、清
地址 Address
武当山金殿索道出口
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木、石结构
看点 Highlights
元代初年的石殿始建于元代明崇祯九年重修清咸丰六年大部分毁于火同治和光绪年间先后修复坐西南朝东北1.5万平方米大殿、北配房、石殿石碑十余通石殿高近4米单檐歇山顶殿内供奉石雕造像8尊
中文 Chinese

始建于元代，明崇祯九年（1636）重修，清咸丰六年（1856）大部分毁于火，同治和光绪年间先后修复。坐西南朝东北，占地面积约1.5万平方米，现存大殿、北配房、石殿等建筑，以及记载明清重修中观的石碑十余通。

其中最重要的建筑为元代初年的石殿，殿高近4米，单檐歇山顶，殿内供奉石雕造像8尊。琼台三观曾经规模宏大，建筑之间亭桥相连，上观名为白玉龟台，中观叫紫岳琼台，下观为玉乐霄台。现上观仅存遗址，下观残存大殿和配殿13间。

English 英文

It was first built in the Yuan Dynasty, rebuilt in the 9th year of Chongzhen, Ming (1636), mostly destroyed by fire in the 6th year of Xianfeng, Qing (1856), and successively restored during the Tongzhi and Guangxu periods. Facing northeast from southwest, it covers about 15,000 square meters; existing buildings include the main hall, north side room, and stone hall, as well as more than ten stone steles recording the Ming and Qing restorations of the middle temple. The most important building is the stone hall of the early Yuan Dynasty, nearly 4 meters high, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, enshrining 8 stone-carved statues inside. The three Qiongtai temples were once large in scale, with pavilions and bridges connecting the buildings; the upper temple was named White Jade Tortoise Terrace, the middle temple was called Purple Mystic Qiongtai, and the lower temple was Jade Music Cloud Terrace. Now only ruins remain of the upper temple, while the lower temple has 13 remaining rooms of the main hall and side halls.

438. 榔梅祠

Langmei Shrine
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清
地址 Address
武当山乌鸦岭
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木、石结构
看点 Highlights
历史故事榔梅是武当山独有的一种树李时珍本草纲目记载榔梅只出均州太和山徐霞客说榔梅开花时花色浮空映山绚丽榔梅的果实也是明代的贡品由武当山道士每年进献榔梅祠正是因道士刘希将榔梅果进皇宫上而建永乐十年1000平方米前殿、后殿和配殿后殿为1989年修复单檐歇山灰瓦顶
中文 Chinese

榔梅是武当山独有的一种树，李时珍《本草纲目》记载：'榔梅，只出均州太和山。'徐霞客则说榔梅开花时'花色浮空，映山绚丽'。而榔梅的果实也是明代的贡品，由武当山道士每年进献，据传，榔梅祠正是因道士刘希将榔梅果进皇宫上而建。

建于永乐十年（1412），占地面积1000平方米，有前殿、后殿和配殿，现存后殿为原物，其他建筑为1989年修复。后殿为单檐歇山灰瓦顶，四壁砖墙封砌，下有石雕须弥座。

正面开拱券门，门额上嵌'榔梅仙祠'石匾。不知为何，到清代时武当山的榔梅树便完全绝迹，如今仅有几棵，是明代武当山作为贵重的礼物赠予齐云山，当代又从齐云山引回，栽种在榔梅祠旁的。

English 英文

Langmei (plum-apricot) is a tree unique to Wudang Mountain; Li Shizhen 'Compendium of Materia Medica' records: 'Langmei only grows in Taihe Mountain, Junzhou.' Xu Xiake said that when langmei blooms, 'the flower color floats in the air, reflecting the mountain gorgeously.' The fruit of langmei was also a tribute in the Ming Dynasty, offered annually by Wudang Mountain Taoists; according to legend, Langmei Shrine was built precisely because the Taoist Liu Xi presented langmei fruit to the imperial palace. It was built in the 10th year of Yongle (1412), covering 1,000 square meters, with a front hall, rear hall, and side halls; the existing rear hall is original, and the other buildings were restored in 1989. The rear hall has a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, with brick walls sealing all four sides and a stone-carved xumizuo (Sumeru) pedestal below. On the front, an arched gate is opened, with a stone plaque 'Langmei Immortal Shrine' embedded on the lintel. For unknown reasons, by the Qing Dynasty the langmei trees on Wudang Mountain had completely disappeared; today there are only a few, which Wudang Mountain gave as a precious gift to Qiyun Mountain in the Ming Dynasty, and were brought back from Qiyun Mountain in contemporary times and planted beside Langmei Shrine.

439. 朝天宫

Chaotian Palace
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清
地址 Address
武当山欢喜坡
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木、石结构
看点 Highlights
人间与仙境的分界线始建于元代后屡建屡毁明永乐十年敕建玄帝殿、配殿等17间嘉靖年间扩建清代、民国多次修补山门、大殿、配殿建筑群顺应地势坐落在一组高耸的台基之上
中文 Chinese

始建于元代，后屡建屡毁，明永乐十年（1412）敕建玄帝殿、配殿等17间，嘉靖年间扩建，清代、民国多次修补。现有山门、大殿、配殿等建筑。建筑群顺应地势，坐落在一组高耸的台基之上，被认为是人间与仙境的分界线。

English 英文

It was first built in the Yuan Dynasty, later repeatedly built and destroyed; in the 10th year of Yongle, Ming (1412), 17 rooms including the Xuandi Hall and side halls were imperially built, expanded during the Jiajing period, and repaired many times during the Qing and Republican periods. Existing buildings include the mountain gate, main hall, and side halls. The building group conforms to the terrain, sitting on a group of towering pedestals, and is considered the dividing line between the human world and the immortal realm.

440. 一天门、二天门、三天门

Chaotian Palace (First, Second, Third Heaven Gates)
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
元、明、清
地址 Address
武当山欢喜坡至天柱峰
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖石结构
看点 Highlights
转折处三座天门砖石结构拱券门通高近7米单檐歇山顶须弥座檐下嵌石匾书写名称三座天门中各存有从明至民国的石碑若干通
中文 Chinese

这三座天门皆位于从朝天宫到太和宫的神道上，山势转折之处。始建于元代，明永乐年间重建，规制完全相同：砖石结构拱券门，通高近7米，单檐歇山顶，须弥座，檐下嵌石匾书写名称。

三座天门中各存有从明至民国的石碑若干通。

English 英文

These three Heaven Gates are all located on the sacred path from Chaotian Palace to Taihe Palace, at the turning points of the mountain terrain. They were first built in the Yuan Dynasty and rebuilt during the Yongle period of the Ming, with completely identical regulations: brick-stone structure arched gates, with a total height of nearly 7 meters, single-eave hip-and-gable roofs, xumizuo (Sumeru) pedestals, and stone plaques embedded under the eaves writing their names. In each of the three Heaven Gates, several stone steles from the Ming to the Republican period are preserved.

441. 饶氏庄园

Rao's Mansion
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
1921年
地址 Address
浪河镇黄龙村水田畈
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖木、石结构
看点 Highlights
碉楼巨大木雕精美武当峡谷第一漂景区附近未庄园主人饶志义18岁开始做盐运生意通过捐官拥有自己的军队正逢乱世偏远隐蔽的地方两进两路院落硬山灰瓦屋顶入口南侧四层的巨大碉楼
中文 Chinese

位于'武当峡谷第一漂'景区附近，当地人称清末庄园。庄园的主人饶志义（1887-1926，一说饶宗义、饶崇义），18岁便开始做盐运生意，并逐步积攒了大量的财产，后来又通过捐官，拥有了自己的军队。

乡里传说，饶志义在马背上行走10天，都不喝别人的水，不走别人的路。在修建这座庄园时，他考虑到正逢乱世，特意挑选了这样一个偏远隐蔽的地方，不易被发现且易守难攻，也使得庄园的建筑得以相对完好地保存到今天。整个建筑群坐西朝东，有两进两路院落，硬山灰瓦屋顶。

一眼望去最显眼的便是入口南侧四层的巨大碉楼，每面都有若干大小形状相同的孔洞，用于监视和狙击；最上层还有一个开放的外廊，周围环绕以木制栏杆，屋顶为四角攒尖顶。若大胆推测一些，在入口北侧，与现状位置对称的地方，也应该有一座一样的碉楼，这样庄园的格局才算完整。

继续向前来到大门，首先是一道栅门，打开栅门才是厚重的正门。门楼两侧是云形马头山墙，山墙上雕刻五只蝙蝠，寓意'五福临门'。大门背面上方还有一个小小的露台，作戏台太小无法攀登，若用于储藏，则裙板上雕饰之莲花、凤凰、牡丹、缠枝花纹又显得太过奢侈。

大门和二门之间是一个前院，向左可以通向碉楼，而走进垂花门式的二门，进入主院之后可以看到，这样精美的木雕在院中比比皆是。第一进厅屋中的斜撑采用了镂空雕刻的技法，曲线造型显得浑厚有力；

而主院中每一道梁枋上都刻满了人物故事，材料用名贵的黄杨木、银杏木等，题材则有八仙过海、十八相送、刘海砍樵、曹冲称象、孔子讲学等。这些珍贵的木雕在'文革'时被一位有心的老木匠用一种粗糙的皮纸糊起来，上面写上毛主席语录，因此才能完整地保存到今天。

从主院向左是下人居住的配院，建筑形制类似而无任何装饰，显示出等级的区别。院中还存有一对雕刻有小猴子的拴马桩，寓意'马上封侯'。主院的右边仅仅以简单的土墙围绕起来，院内有一两棵高大的植物。

据管理员介绍，这里曾经是庄园的花园，面积也比现在大一倍，因为解放初期农民扒院墙盖房而逐渐毁坏，后来为保护庄园才筑起这道院墙。据说为修建这座庄园，饶志义在汉口聘请设计师

English 英文

Located near the 'Wudang Gorge No. 1 Rafting' scenic area, locals call it the late Qing manor. The owner of the manor, Rao Zhiyi (1887–1926, some say Rao Zongyi, Rao Chongyi), started a salt transportation business at the age of 18 and gradually accumulated a large amount of property; later, through donating for an official position, he had his own army. Local legend says that when Rao Zhiyi traveled on horseback for 10 days, he would not drink others water or walk on others roads. When building this manor, considering that it was a chaotic era, he specially chose such a remote and hidden place, not easy to be discovered and easy to defend but difficult to attack, which also allowed the manor buildings to be relatively well-preserved to this day. The entire building complex faces east from west, with two entries and two routes of courtyards, and gable gray-tile roofs. At first glance, the most conspicuous is the huge four-story watchtower south of the entrance; each side has several holes of the same size and shape, used for surveillance and sniping; on the top floor there is also an open veranda, surrounded by wooden railings, with a four-corner pyramidal roof. If one boldly speculates, on the north side of the entrance, at a position symmetrical to the current situation, there should also be an identical watchtower, so that the layout of the manor would be complete. Continuing forward to the main gate, first there is a fence gate; opening the fence gate is the heavy main gate. On both sides of the gate tower are cloud-shaped horse-head gable walls, with five bats carved on the gable walls, meaning 'five blessings arriving at the door.' Above the back of the main gate there is also a small terrace; too small to climb as a stage, and if used for storage, the carved lotus, phoenix, peony, and scrolling flower patterns on the skirt boards seem too luxurious. Between the main gate and the second gate is a front courtyard, to the left leading to the watchtower; entering the second gate in the form of a chuihuamen (flower-hung gate), after entering the main courtyard one can see that such exquisite wood carvings are everywhere in the courtyard. The diagonal braces in the first entry hall use the openwork carving technique, with curvilinear shapes appearing vigorous and powerful; while every beam in the main courtyard is covered with figure stories, using precious materials such as boxwood and ginkgo wood, with themes such as the Eight Immortals Crossing the Sea, Eighteen Send-offs, Liu Hai Cutting Firewood, Cao Chong Weighing the Elephant, and Confucius Teaching. These precious wood carvings were pasted over with a rough tissue paper by a caring old carpenter during the Cultural Revolution, with Chairman Mao quotations written on it, thus they could be completely preserved to this day. To the left from the main courtyard is the auxiliary courtyard where servants lived, with similar architectural form but without any decoration, showing the difference in rank. In the courtyard there is also a pair of horse-tying posts carved with little monkeys, meaning 'immediately conferred as a marquis.' The right side of the main courtyard is merely surrounded by a simple earthen wall, with one or two tall plants in the courtyard. According to the administrator, this was once the garden of the manor, and its area was also twice as large as now; because farmers tore down the courtyard wall to build houses in the early days after liberation, it was gradually destroyed, and later this courtyard wall was built to protect the manor. It is said that to build this manor, Rao Zhiyi hired a designer in Hankou

442. 龙山宝塔

Longshan Pagoda
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清光绪三十二年（1907）建成
地址 Address
土台乡龙巢山，丹江口水库库区旁
类型 Type
古塔·砖结构
看点 Highlights
楼阁式风水塔又名文笔塔清光绪二十六年至三十二年砖砌筑楼阁式风水塔六角三层高约12米室内木楼梯登上顶层眺望丹江口水库、汉水与武当山相传为镇龙颈、免水患位于古均州城东南为振兴艺文名为文笔塔均州八景中今天唯一还能看到的龙山烟雨
中文 Chinese

又名文笔塔，建于清光绪二十六年（1900）至三十二年（1907），是一座砖砌筑楼阁式风水塔，六角三层，高约12米。通过室内的木楼梯可以登上顶层，眺望丹江口水库、汉水与武当山的湖光山色。

塔之得名，相传为镇龙颈、免水患，故名龙山塔；又说因位于古均州城东南，为振兴艺文，名为文笔塔。宝塔立于龙巢山之上，每天天色转阴之时，便能看到古'均州八景'中今天唯一还能看到的'龙山烟雨'。塔后不远处曾有玉皇庙和禹王庙，今已毁。

English 英文

Also called Wenbi (Writing Brush) Pagoda, built from the 26th year (1900) to the 32nd year (1907) of Guangxu, Qing, it is a brick-built pavilion-style fengshui pagoda, hexagonal with three stories, about 12 meters high. Through the indoor wooden staircase, one can climb to the top floor and overlook the lake and mountain scenery of the Danjiangkou Reservoir, Han River, and Wudang Mountain. The name of the pagoda, according to legend, is to suppress the dragon neck and avoid flood disasters, hence named Longshan (Dragon Mountain) Pagoda; another saying is that because it is located southeast of ancient Junzhou city, to revitalize literature and art, it is named Wenbi Pagoda. The pagoda stands on Longchao Mountain; every day when the sky turns overcast, one can see 'Longshan Misty Rain,' the only one of the ancient 'Eight Scenes of Junzhou' that can still be seen today. Not far behind the pagoda there were once the Jade Emperor Temple and Yu the Great Temple, now destroyed.

443. 大晟庵箭楼

Dasheng an Archery Tower
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清
地址 Address
关垭镇银洞山村庵前沟，一处废弃铁矿西北的山坡上
类型 Type
宗教建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
军事防御建筑大晟庵建筑群是武当古建筑群的组成部分原有山门、前殿、主殿、左右厢房和箭楼等现存左右厢房和箭楼其他建筑仅存基址厢房面阔三间高两层单檐硬山灰瓦顶二层有外廊和栏杆现作为居住建筑使用箭楼位于右侧厢房的后方在整个建筑群中位置最高
中文 Chinese

大晟庵建筑群是武当古建筑群的组成部分，原有山门、前殿、主殿、左右厢房和箭楼等组成，现存左右厢房和箭楼，其他建筑仅存基址。厢房面阔三间，高两层，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，二层有外廊和栏杆，现作为居住建筑使用。

箭楼位于右侧厢房的后方，在整个建筑群中位置最高。

与道家提倡的'道法自然、天人合一''修身养性、与世无争'等理念明显不同的是，箭楼是一座军事防御建筑，高四层，墙厚70厘米，各个墙面上不规则地分布着八个窗户和数十个箭孔，站在顶层则能轻松俯瞰周围数百平方米，显示出良好的防御功能。

箭楼顶部正中梁上有'大明正德元年立''大清乾隆九年重修'等墨书题记，以及红黑相间的太极图案。箭楼也是武当山境内首次在道教建筑群中修建的军事防御设施。

English 英文

The Dasheng Temple building complex is part of the Wudang ancient building complex; it originally consisted of a mountain gate, front hall, main hall, left and right wing rooms, and an archery tower, etc.; currently the left and right wing rooms and the archery tower remain, while only the foundations of other buildings survive. The wing rooms are three bays wide, two stories high, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs; the second floor has verandas and railings, and is now used as residential buildings. The archery tower is located behind the right wing room, at the highest position in the entire building complex. Obviously different from the concepts advocated by Taoism such as 'the Tao follows nature, heaven and humanity are one' and 'cultivating oneself and living in peace with the world,' the archery tower is a military defensive building, four stories high, with walls 70 centimeters thick; eight windows and dozens of arrow holes are irregularly distributed on each wall surface; standing on the top floor, one can easily overlook several hundred square meters around, showing good defensive function. On the central beam at the top of the archery tower, there are ink inscriptions such as 'Erected in the 1st year of Zhengde, Ming' and 'Rebuilt in the 9th year of Qianlong, Qing,' as well as red-and-black Taiji patterns. The archery tower is also the first military defensive facility built in a Taoist building complex within Wudang Mountain.

444. 上津古城

Shangjin Ancient City
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
明、清
地址 Address
上津镇西街
类型 Type
标志建筑·砖、石、木结构
看点 Highlights
五座城门石叠古城墙上津道唐代从首都长安向东南陆行至商州上津县在此改由汉江水路通往江南和岭南地区驿道偏僻、艰险、设备简陋安史之乱和唐末节度使反叛时期成为保障首都物资的重要道路上津的兴衰与全国军事政治形势的局势变化密切相关三国时期上津附近最早设平阳县南北朝时期先后为上洛郡、上津郡省级政区上州的治所隋代以后降为上津县
中文 Chinese

上津道是唐代从首都长安向东南，陆行至商州上津县（今上津镇），在此改由汉江水路通往江南和岭南地区的一条驿道。这条驿道偏僻、艰险，设备简陋，因此只有在中原战乱、主要驿道阻塞不通时才被开辟使用，故而在安史之乱和唐末节度使反叛的时期，成为保障首都物资的重要道路。

历史上，上津的兴衰与全国军事政治形势的局势变化密切相关。三国时期，上津附近最早设平阳县，南北朝时期先后为上洛郡、上津郡，并成为省级政区上州的治所；而从隋代以后又降为上津县，并一直保持到明代，到清康熙年间再降为上津堡。

这说明在分裂战乱时期，特别是南北对峙的政权以秦岭为界，汉江上游成为重要的争夺对象时，上津的军事地位便会凸显出来。上津在水陆交通方面的重要性，表现为从水路向西南可以通向安康、汉中，向东南通向襄阳、武汉，陆路向西北通往长安，东北通往洛阳。

唐中宗李显被贬为庐陵王前往均州（今丹江口市均县镇）时，便是在这里下马乘船，因此古城西门的码头也被称为'天子渡口'。据说，战时流民来到上津居住，会折一枝家乡的柳树带来以寄托思乡之情，久而久之，上津柳树成荫，也被称为柳州城。

今天的上津古城墙建于明嘉靖二年（1523），清嘉庆七年（1802）重修，2005年成为国家级文物保护单位之后，又经历了一次大规模的修葺。

城的平面是一个东西约30米、南北长约300米的狭长长方形，石垒墙基，砖砌城墙，高近7米，外有护城河。有五座城门，东为'向郧'，西为'通汉'，南为'达楚'，北为'接秦'，西南还有一座小西门以方便居民出入。

城中偏西有一条南北向的主街，西门至主街还有一条小街，另外在北门外还保留着一条石子路老街和两排旧时民居。在城外东北的小山丘上还有一座山陕会馆，也称为关帝庙，始建于清乾隆、嘉庆交际之时，现仅存正殿的一进天井院。

平面为三开间，单檐硬山灰瓦，第一进卷棚顶。殿内供奉关帝，是山陕商人祭祀关公、联谊乡情并从事商业活动的重要场所。

English 英文

The Shangjin Road was a post road in the Tang Dynasty from the capital Chang'an southeastward, traveling by land to Shangjin County of Shangzhou (today Shangjin Town), where it changed to the Han River waterway to reach the Jiangnan and Lingnan regions. This post road was remote, dangerous, and poorly equipped, so it was only opened and used when the Central Plains was in chaos and the main post roads were blocked; hence, during the An Lushan Rebellion and the period of jiedushi (military governor) rebellion at the end of the Tang, it became an important road for ensuring supplies to the capital. Historically, the rise and fall of Shangjin was closely related to changes in the national military and political situation. During the Three Kingdoms period, Pingyang County was first established near Shangjin; during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, it successively became Shangluo Commandery and Shangjin Commandery, and became the seat of the provincial-level administrative region Shangzhou; from the Sui Dynasty onward, it was downgraded to Shangjin County and remained so until the Ming Dynasty, and in the Kangxi period of the Qing it was further downgraded to Shangjin Fort. This shows that during periods of division and war, especially when the opposing regimes of the north and south took the Qinling Mountains as the boundary and the upper Han River became an important object of contention, the military position of Shangjin would become prominent. The importance of Shangjin in water and land transportation is manifested in that by waterway it can lead southwest to Ankang and Hanzhong, southeast to Xiangyang and Wuhan; by land route it leads northwest to Chang'an and northeast to Luoyang. When Li Xian, Emperor Zhongzong of Tang, was demoted to Prince of Luling and went to Junzhou (today Junxian Town, Danjiangkou City), he dismounted and boarded a boat here, hence the dock at the west gate of the ancient city is also called 'Son of Heaven Ferry.' It is said that when war refugees came to live in Shangjin, they would bring a willow branch from their hometown to express their homesickness; over time, Shangjin became shaded with willows and was also called Liuzhou (Willow City). The current Shangjin ancient city wall was built in the 2nd year of Jiajing, Ming (1523), rebuilt in the 7th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1802), and after becoming a national cultural heritage protection unit in 2005, it underwent another large-scale renovation. The plane of the city is a narrow rectangle about 30 meters east-west and 300 meters north-south, with stone-built wall foundations and brick-built city walls, nearly 7 meters high, with a moat outside. There are five city gates: the east is 'Xiangyun' (toward Yun), the west is 'Tonghan' (to Han), the south is 'Dachu' (to Chu), the north is 'Jieqin' (connecting Qin), and there is also a small west gate in the southwest for the convenience of residents entering and exiting. In the city, slightly west of center, there is a north-south main street; from the west gate to the main street there is also a small street; in addition, outside the north gate, an old cobblestone street and two rows of old residences are preserved. On a small hill northeast of the city, there is also a Shaanxi-Shanxi Guild Hall, also called the Guandi Temple, built at the turn of the Qianlong and Jiaqing periods of the Qing; now only one entry of the courtyard of the main hall remains. Its plane is three bays wide, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, and the first entry has a curved roof. Inside the hall, Guandi is enshrined; it was an important place for Shaanxi-Shanxi merchants to sacrifice to Guan Gong, fellowship with fellow townspeople, and engage in commercial activities.

中文 Chinese

从上津镇继续向前，沿着301省道继续行驶约45分钟，在道路北侧山脚下的地方，可以看到一座并不起眼的小塔。在边停车，沿着田间小路跨过一条清澈的小溪，穿过一片水稻田，就可以近距离地观察这座铁山寺塔了。

塔建于明代，原本是一座六角十三级的楼阁式实心砖塔，由于山谷中泥沙的淤积，目前露出地面的仅有五层半，高约10米，逐层收分。塔刹也已毁坏，

English 英文

Continuing forward from Shangjin Town, driving along Provincial Highway 301 for about 45 minutes, at the foot of the mountain on the north side of the road, one can see an inconspicuous small pagoda. Parking by the roadside, crossing a clear stream along a field path, and passing through a rice paddy, one can observe this Tieshan Temple Pagoda up close. The pagoda was built in the Ming Dynasty; it was originally a hexagonal thirteen-story pavilion-style solid brick pagoda. Due to sedimentation in the valley, currently only five and a half stories are exposed above the ground, about 10 meters high, tapering story by story. The pagoda finial has also been destroyed,

446. 甘氏宗祠

Gan's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
国家级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
中峰镇甘家岭村小学院内
类型 Type
礼制建筑·砖、石、木结构
看点 Highlights
规模大气势足十堰市规模最大保存也相对完整的宗祠之一主体建筑始建于乾隆十九年光绪十四年增修纪念清康熙年间族长甘继芳在与地方叛军的战斗中为国捐躯而兴建康熙十四年鄂西北守军响应吴三桂叛乱竹溪扼守陕、鄂之间成为叛军争夺的要点当时的知县曹席珍由于县城没有城墙率官民退守到城西30里的中峰寨
中文 Chinese

甘氏宗祠是十堰市规模最大，保存也相对完整的宗祠之一，主体建筑始建于乾隆十九年（1754），光绪十四年（1888）增修，是为了纪念清康熙年间族长甘继芳在与地方叛军的战斗中为国捐躯而兴建的。

康熙十四年（1675），鄂西北守军响应吴三桂叛乱，竹溪扼守陕、鄂之间，因而成为叛军争夺的要点。当时的知县曹席珍由于县城没有城墙，率官民退守到城西30里的中峰寨，与甘继芳合力抗敌。早先明末动乱时期，甘继芳便带领乡民抵御流寇的滋扰，在10余年间多次将其击退。

甘、曹二人在山中困守60天，敌人始终无法攻破。这时曹知县一个名为曹二的门役因为犯错受到责罚，便偷偷下山，与一个名叫'马蹶子'的叛军合伙，带领叛军从后山的绝壁攻入山寨，捉住了甘继芳和曹知县。甘继芳拒绝与叛军合作，慷慨赴死，年64岁；

而曹知县则辗转逃至京城，甘继芳的事迹也因而得以流传，清政府为了褒奖忠义之士，赐匾3块，准立宗祠。建筑坐南朝北，中路为两进殿堂，有一个天井院；东侧为民国三年（1914）增建的官厅。

整体由青砖砌筑，各个单体均为单檐硬山灰瓦顶。官厅面阔五间，屋脊两端上翘呈凹曲线，两侧山墙突出高起的墀头装饰；正中入口为高耸的三间仿木牌楼，中间匾额书'甘宗祠'，门前一对抱鼓石，两侧两扇雕花石窗。

English 英文

Gan's Ancestral Hall is one of the largest and relatively well-preserved ancestral halls in Shiyan City. The main building was first built in the 19th year of Qianlong, Qing (1754), and expanded in the 14th year of Guangxu (1888), built to commemorate the clan leader Gan Jifang who died for his country in battle against local rebel forces during the Kangxi period of the Qing. In the 14th year of Kangxi (1675), the garrison in northwestern Hubei responded to Wu Sangui rebellion; Zhuxi, guarding the pass between Shaanxi and Hubei, thus became a key point contested by the rebels. At that time, the county magistrate Cao Xizhen, because the county seat had no city wall, led officials and people to retreat to Zhongfeng Stockade 30 li west of the city, and joined forces with Gan Jifang to resist the enemy. Earlier, during the late Ming turmoil, Gan Jifang led villagers to resist the harassment of roving bandits, repelling them many times over more than 10 years. Gan and Cao were besieged in the mountain for 60 days, and the enemy was never able to break through. At this time, a servant of Magistrate Cao named Cao Er, because he had been punished for a mistake, secretly went down the mountain and partnered with a rebel named 'Majuzi,' leading the rebels to attack the stockade from the precipice at the back of the mountain, capturing Gan Jifang and Magistrate Cao. Gan Jifang refused to cooperate with the rebels and died heroically at the age of 64; while Magistrate Cao escaped to the capital after many twists and turns, and Gan Jifang deeds thus spread. The Qing government, to commend the loyal and righteous, bestowed 3 plaques and permitted the establishment of an ancestral hall. The building faces north from south, with the central route being two-entry halls and one courtyard; on the east side is the official hall added in the 3rd year of the Republic (1914). The whole is built of blue bricks, and each individual unit has a single-eave gable gray-tile roof. The official hall is five bays wide, with both ends of the ridge upturned in a concave curve, and the gable walls on both sides protrude with high chi tou (gable-end) decorations; the central entrance is a towering three-bay imitation-wood paifang, with the central plaque reading 'Gan Ancestral Hall,' a pair of drum-holding stones in front of the gate, and two carved stone windows on both sides.

447. 敖宗祠

Ao's Ancestral Hall

看点 Highlights
石雕砖雕木雕工艺精致十堰地区另一座典型的祠堂外观和平面布局与甘氏宗祠相似而规模较小中路两进殿堂和一个天井院左手有侧院各个单体山墙的形状也与甘氏宗祠一致进深较小侧院的云形山墙已经简化成了一段圆弧据族谱记载敖宗祠始建于明朝
中文 Chinese

敖宗祠是十堰地区另一座典型的祠堂，外观和平面布局与甘氏宗祠相似而规模较小，为中路两进殿堂和一个天井院，左手有侧院，各个单体山墙的形状也与甘氏宗祠一致，不过由于进深较小，侧院的云形山墙已经简化成了一段圆弧。

据族谱记载，敖宗祠始建于明朝，而现存建筑的修建年代应不早于清中期。祠堂石雕、砖雕、木雕工艺精致，特别是主人口的砖砌牌楼，四根盘龙石柱，大门上置竖匾，上书'敖宗祠'，石柱和匾额的四周都贴有各色瓷片。

但可惜的是建筑内部已损毁殆尽，正殿坍圮，仅残余外部一层空壳。

English 英文

Ao's Ancestral Hall is another typical ancestral hall in the Shiyan area; its appearance and plane layout are similar to Gan's Ancestral Hall but smaller in scale, with the central route being two-entry halls and one courtyard, a side courtyard on the left, and the shape of each individual gable wall also consistent with Gan's Ancestral Hall; however, due to the smaller depth, the cloud-shaped gable wall of the side courtyard has been simplified into a circular arc. According to the genealogy, Ao's Ancestral Hall was first built in the Ming Dynasty, and the construction date of the existing building should not be earlier than the mid-Qing. The stone carving, brick carving, and wood carving craftsmanship of the ancestral hall are exquisite, especially the brick paifang at the main entrance, with four dragon-coiled stone columns; a vertical plaque is placed above the main gate, inscribed with 'Ao Ancestral Hall,' and various colored porcelain pieces are pasted around the stone columns and plaque. Unfortunately, the interior of the building has been completely destroyed, the main hall has collapsed, and only an outer one-story empty shell remains.

Dacheng Hall of Temple of Confucius

竹山文庙始建于明洪武十三年（1380），毁于明末，清初重建，清道光二十一年（1841）修缮，现仅存大成殿。大殿坐北朝南，面宽五间，重檐歇山灰瓦顶，砖木结构，抬梁式构架，屋顶高耸。

English 英文

Zhushan Confucian Temple was first built in the 13th year of Hongwu, Ming (1380), destroyed in the late Ming, rebuilt in the early Qing, and repaired in the 21st year of Daoguang, Qing (1841); now only the Dacheng (Great Achievement) Hall remains. The main hall faces south, five bays wide, with a double-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, brick-wood structure, post-and-lintel frame, and a towering roof. It has exterior corridors on three sides, with lattice doors and windows on the front and square brick paving on the ground.

449. 上庸古建筑群

Ancient Building Complex in Shangyong
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
上庸镇潘口水电站水库旁
类型 Type
教育、文化、娱乐建筑·砖木、石结构
看点 Highlights
超大型民居组群包括三盛院和黄州会馆两组天井式四合院为配合潘口水电站的建设而分别从两处搬迁至此三盛院原先位于官渡河与泗河交汇的两河口一组有六路院落的超大型民居组群于清朝嘉庆末年完工有大小48个天井房屋千余间地跨竹山、竹溪两县因年久失修搬迁前便已所剩无几王氏家族经商积累财富后在家乡建造的豪宅
中文 Chinese

上庸古建筑群包括三盛院和黄州会馆两组天井式四合院，是为配合潘口水电站的建设而分别从两处搬迁至此的。

三盛院原先位于官渡河与泗河交汇的两河口，是一组有六路院落的超大型民居组群，于清朝嘉庆末年完工，有大小48个天井，房屋千余间，地跨竹山、竹溪两县，但因年久失修，搬迁前便已所剩无几。

这一建筑群是王氏家族经商积累财富后在家乡建造的豪宅，'三盛'三字由慈禧太后亲笔题写，既是家族的名号，也用作商号，寓意人盛、地盛、财盛。六路院落分为北路三进，南三路三进，坐西朝东，呈'王'字形扩展布局。三盛院现存部分是搬迁前保存状况较好的两进天井院，作为民俗博物馆使用。

建筑高两层，硬山灰瓦顶，檐下有一圈彩绘和彩塑装饰。各处门窗均有精美的石雕装饰，题材丰富、各不相同。大门上石匾书'紫气东来'四字；门楣浮雕人物生活场景，角部饰以历史人物，下侧为一对麒麟舞丝带、滚绣球；石门墩各个面上亦有花木、丝带、龙纹等雕刻装饰。

此外，大门右侧的外墙上还有一对雕刻极精致的葡萄缠枝纹镂

English 英文

The Shangyong Ancient Building Complex includes two groups of courtyard-style quadrangles: the Sansheng Courtyard and the Huangzhou Guild Hall, which were relocated here from two places respectively to配合 the construction of the Pankou Hydropower Station. The Sansheng Courtyard was originally located at Lianghekou, where the Guandu River and Si River meet; it is a super-large residential building group with six routes of courtyards, completed in the late Jiaqing period of the Qing, with 48 courtyards of various sizes and more than a thousand rooms, spanning both Zhushan and Zhuxi counties; but due to long-term neglect and disrepair, little remained before relocation. This building complex was a mansion built by the Wang family after accumulating wealth through business in their hometown; the three characters 'Sansheng' were personally inscribed by Empress Dowager Cixi, serving both as the family name and as a trade name, meaning prosperity of people, land, and wealth. The six routes of courtyards are divided into the north route with three entries and the south three routes with three entries, facing east from west, in an expanded layout shaped like the character 'Wang' (king). The existing part of Sansheng Courtyard is the two-entry courtyard that was in relatively good preservation before relocation, used as a folk custom museum. The building is two stories high, with a gable gray-tile roof and a ring of painted and colored sculpture decorations under the eaves. Doors and windows everywhere have exquisite stone carving decorations, with rich and varied themes. On the stone plaque above the main gate are written the four characters 'Purple Qi Comes from the East'; the door lintel has relief sculptures of figure life scenes, with historical figures decorating the corners, and below is a pair of kylins dancing with ribbons and rolling embroidered balls; each face of the stone door piers also has carvings of flowers and trees, ribbons, dragon patterns, etc. In addition, on the exterior wall to the right of the main gate, there is also a pair of exquisitely carved grape-vine pattern openwork

450. 高家花屋

Huawu Mansion of Gao Family
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清乾隆、嘉庆年间
地址 Address
竹坪乡解家沟村白马山
类型 Type
居住建筑·砖、石、木结构
看点 Highlights
隐居山涧屋宇气派相比于三盛院的名动一方高家花屋位于更加偏僻的鄂陕边界也正因地远难行得以相对完好地保存到今天这座前后有三进院落的大宅子坐北朝南背山临渊选址极佳大门正对远处的最高峰门高约12米两侧有八字墙
中文 Chinese

相比于三盛院的名动一方，高家花屋位于更加偏僻的鄂陕边界，也正因地远难行，得以相对完好地保存到今天。这座前后有三进院落的大宅子坐北朝南，背山临渊，选址极佳。

大门正对远处的最高峰，门高约12米，两侧有八字墙，门前是13级青石板台阶，如此气派的入口在一般的民居中很少见到，让人不禁联想到宏丽的宫殿或庙宇。

据当地老人讲，高家花屋原有房间57间，除正房、粮仓外，还有吊酒房、当铺、钱庄等商业用房十几间，逢年过节，方圆100多公里内都有人上这儿来典当、拆借，是一座名副其实的豪宅。

两百年之后，这些房屋中有48间幸存下来，而类似这样的花屋，户主高方在世时共建了9座，保存至今的是其中最豪华的一座。

房屋刚盖了一半，高方便去世了，他的后代子孙又用了20年时间终于完工，至今当地仍然有民谣唱道：'高家盖房，三十年散板……'从花屋放眼望去，四周全是灰灰的大山，这样一座超级四合院是怎样建起来的呢？

据说，高方与父亲高启元本要从武昌去西安，走到解家沟时人困马乏，看到草房，想到草房之内正是无雪之地，当即拆除草房安葬母亲，从此以后便财运不断。另一个传说是'豪赌兴家'，说高方做长工时虽然肯下力干活，却也因为食量大而被东家嫌弃，闲来无聊便去看赌博，结果逢赌必赢，堪称'赌王'。

不过，从花屋的建造过程来看，这些传说也仅仅是耸人听闻，能够不惜巨大的人力物力在如此偏远的地方，建造这样一座颇有归隐意味的豪宅，又能开设粮铺、杂货铺、当铺，可见高方应是一个家底殷实又善于经营的人。

English 英文

Compared with the fame of Sansheng Courtyard, Gao Family Huawu (Ornamental House) is located at the more remote Hubei-Shaanxi border, and precisely because it is far and difficult to reach, it has been relatively well-preserved to this day. This large mansion with three courtyards front and back faces south, with mountains at its back and an abyss in front, with an excellent site selection. The main gate faces directly the highest peak in the distance; the gate is about 12 meters high, with splayed walls on both sides, and in front of the gate are 13 blue stone slab steps; such an imposing entrance is rarely seen in ordinary residences, making one不禁 think of magnificent palaces or temples. According to local elders, Gao Family Huawu originally had 57 rooms; besides the main house and granary, there were also more than ten commercial rooms such as wine distillery, pawnshop, and money shop; during festivals, people from within a radius of more than 100 kilometers would come here to pawn and borrow, making it a veritable mansion. Two hundred years later, 48 of these rooms survived; and similar ornamental houses, when the owner Gao Fang was alive, he built a total of 9, and the one preserved to this day is the most luxurious among them. When the house was only half built, Gao Fang passed away, and his descendants spent another 20 years finally completing it; to this day, there is still a folk ballad locally singing: 'The Gao family builds a house, thirty years of scattered boards...' Looking out from the ornamental house, all around are gray mountains; how was such a super quadrangle built? It is said that Gao Fang and his father Gao Qiyuan were originally going from Wuchang to Xi'an; when they reached Xiejiagou, both man and horse were exhausted; seeing a thatched house and thinking that inside the thatched house was a snow-free place, they immediately demolished the thatched house to bury their mother, and from then on their wealth continued to grow. Another legend is 'getting rich through extravagant gambling,' saying that when Gao Fang worked as a hired laborer, although he was willing to work hard, he was also disliked by his employer because of his large appetite; when bored, he went to watch gambling, and as a result won every bet, worthy of being called the 'King of Gamblers.' However, from the construction process of the ornamental house, these legends are merely sensational; being able to spare no expense in manpower and material resources to build such a mansion with a sense of seclusion in such a remote place, and also being able to open grain shops, grocery stores, and pawnshops, shows that Gao Fang should have been a person with a solid family background and good at business.

451. 显圣殿

Xiansheng Hall
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
军店镇军马铺村军马河口
类型 Type
礼制建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
选址环境始建于乾隆十四年道光二年重修现存一座武圣宫和两侧配殿咸丰十年又在后山之巅增修金顶整个建筑群依山面水从山脚一侧的大门可以拾阶而上武圣宫为二层楼阁单檐歇山灰瓦屋顶屋角翘起戗脊上施以仙人走兽装饰
中文 Chinese

始建于乾隆十四年（1749），道光二年（1822）重修，现存一座武圣宫和两侧配殿，咸丰十年（1860）又在后山之巅增修金顶。整个建筑群依山面水，从山脚一侧的大门可以拾阶而上。

武圣宫为二层楼阁，单檐歇山灰瓦屋顶，屋角翘起，戗脊上施以仙人走兽装饰。两座配殿均为五间二层楼，有外廊，而大殿前方的一座为砖木混合结构，单檐硬山屋顶，而后方的则以木结构为主，重檐硬山屋顶。

'显圣'一名众说纷纭，从武圣宫来看，显圣者当为关羽；而一说修建此殿时鲁班曾显圣，一说东汉方士费长房在此显圣，而种种说法之事迹均难以考证。

English 英文

It was first built in the 14th year of Qianlong (1749), rebuilt in the 2nd year of Daoguang (1822); currently there is one Wusheng (Martial Sage) Palace and two side halls, and in the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), a Golden Summit was additionally built on the top of the back mountain. The entire building complex leans against the mountain and faces the water; from the gate on one side at the foot of the mountain, one can climb up the steps. The Wusheng Palace is a two-story pavilion, with a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, upturned roof corners, and immortal and animal decorations on the diagonal ridges. The two side halls are both five-bay two-story buildings with exterior corridors; the one in front of the main hall is of brick-wood mixed structure with a single-eave gable roof, while the one at the rear is mainly of wooden structure with a double-eave gable roof. The name 'Xiansheng' (Manifesting Sage) has various explanations; from the Wusheng Palace, the one who manifests sage should be Guan Yu; while one saying is that Lu Ban manifested sage when this hall was built, another saying is that the Eastern Han alchemist Fei Changfang manifested sage here, but the deeds of various sayings are all difficult to verify.

452. 彭家祠堂

Peng's Ancestral Hall
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
门古寺镇彭家湾村
类型 Type
礼制建筑·砖、石、木结构
看点 Highlights
木雕壁画建于清光绪二十九年落成后第三年在祠堂中开设族塾1920年改为彭家湾私立民族小学解放后改为彭家湾小学新四军曾在此祠堂中办公彭家祠堂外观朴素除了大门上方高耸起三间垂花柱式的牌楼和门前一对抱鼓石并无多余的雕刻或彩画装饰引人注目的是牌楼正中的匾额不书彭宗祠而是写着圣宗祠三字
中文 Chinese

建于清光绪二十九年（1903），落成后第三年在祠堂中开设族塾，1920年改为'彭家湾私立民族小学'，解放后改为彭家湾小学，新四军曾在此祠堂中办公。

彭家祠堂外观朴素，除了大门上方高耸起三间垂花柱式的牌楼和门前一对抱鼓石，并无多余的雕刻或彩画装饰。引人注目的是牌楼正中的匾额不书'彭宗祠'，而是写着'圣宗祠'三字。

据祠中的碑文记载，彭氏曾有一位先祖在科举考试中取得不错的名次，因而彭氏在修建祠堂时得到了光绪皇帝恩准，彭氏宗族进京赶考被封为府案，彭和忠考中县案。彭氏家族要建祠堂荣耀祖德，得到光绪皇帝恩准，并由皇帝亲笔书写'圣宗祠'镌于匾额之上。

祠堂在中轴线上为两进三天井院，门窗、梁柱上各有祥瑞动物的木雕，墙上还绘有二十四孝壁画，虽然遭到了一定的破坏，但保存相对完好，实属不易。

值得一提的是，祠中还有一块长4米，宽1.5米，厚4厘米的巨型木匾，匾上文字一直难以辨识，直到村民走访到曾在祠堂中教书的86岁退休教师张发祥，才破出文字的内容。

原来，彭氏退休教师张发祥，彭氏的母亲刘氏贤惠善良、教子有方，光绪皇帝派大学士李家驹书'淑德延年'赐赠，其中'淑'字因为是异体字，困扰了专家们多年。

English 英文

It was built in the 29th year of Guangxu, Qing (1903); three years after completion, a clan school was opened in the ancestral hall; in 1920 it was changed to 'Pengjiawan Private Ethnic Primary School'; after liberation it was changed to Pengjiawan Primary School; the New Fourth Army once worked in this ancestral hall. Peng's Ancestral Hall has a simple appearance; except for the towering three-bay hanging-column-style paifang above the main gate and a pair of drum-holding stones in front of the gate, there is no多余 carving or painted decoration. What is striking is that the plaque in the center of the paifang does not read 'Peng Ancestral Hall,' but writes the three characters 'Sheng Ancestral Hall.' According to the inscriptions in the hall, one of the Peng ancestors achieved a good ranking in the imperial examinations, so when the Peng family built the ancestral hall, they received the approval of Emperor Guangxu; the Peng clan went to the capital to take the exam and was enfeoffed as fu an (prefectural case), and Peng Hezhong passed the county case. The Peng family wanted to build an ancestral hall to glorify the ancestral virtue, received the approval of Emperor Guangxu, and the emperor personally wrote 'Sheng Ancestral Hall' to be engraved on the plaque. The ancestral hall, on the central axis, is two entries with three courtyards; on the doors, windows, beams, and columns there are wood carvings of auspicious animals, and the walls are also painted with the Twenty-four Filial Piety murals; although they have suffered some damage, they are relatively well-preserved, which is really not easy. It is worth mentioning that there is also a giant wooden plaque in the hall, 4 meters long, 1.5 meters wide, and 4 centimeters thick; the text on the plaque had always been difficult to identify, until the villagers visited the 86-year-old retired teacher Zhang Faxiang who once taught in the ancestral hall, and then the content of the text was deciphered. It turned out that the mother of the Peng family, Liu Shi, was virtuous and kind, and good at teaching children; Emperor Guangxu sent the grand secretary Li Jiaju to write 'Shu De Yan Nian' (Virtuous Virtue Prolongs Years) as a gift; among them, the character 'Shu' (virtuous), because it was a variant character, puzzled experts for many years.

453. 三闾书院

Sanlü Academy
级别 Level
省级重点文物保护单位
年代 Dynasty
清代
地址 Address
阳日镇阳日大道22号
类型 Type
教育建筑·砖木结构
看点 Highlights
大殿立柱为马桑树又名武昌书院、武昌庙始建于清道光十七年时任湖北省学政的孙为曾为其题送冬雪春晖匾额至今悬于大殿檐下书院坐北朝南占地曾达到一千余平方米建筑有门楼、大殿、东西耳房、东西厢房和斋房现仅存大殿大殿为单檐硬山灰瓦屋顶面阔和进深均为三开间正面有前廊
中文 Chinese

又名武昌书院、武昌庙，始建于清道光十七年（1837），时任湖北省学政的孙为曾为其题送'冬雪春晖'匾额，至今悬于大殿檐下。

书院坐北朝南，占地曾达到一千余平方米，建筑有门楼、大殿、东西耳房、东西厢房和斋房，现仅存大殿。

大殿为单檐硬山灰瓦屋顶，面阔和进深均为三开间，正面有前廊，抬梁式木结构，脊檩两段分别书写'三闾书院合众首士修建''大清道光丁酉年九月吉旦'。

屋脊有仙人走兽，山墙彩绘装饰，部分墙砖上还依稀可见'武昌'二字。据说大殿立柱为马桑树，而在鄂西一带，马桑树被认为是无法成材的树种，因此用这种木料修建大殿，寄托了客居此地的武昌人望子成材的心愿。

English 英文

Also called Wuchang Academy or Wuchang Temple, it was first built in the 17th year of Daoguang, Qing (1837); Sun Wei, then the education commissioner of Hubei Province, once presented it with a plaque inscribed 'Winter Snow and Spring Sunshine,' which still hangs under the eaves of the main hall today. The academy faces south, once covering more than a thousand square meters; the buildings included a gate tower, main hall, east and west side rooms, east and west wing rooms, and study rooms; now only the main hall remains. The main hall has a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, with both the width and depth being three bays, a front porch on the front, and a post-and-lintel wooden structure; the two sections of the ridge purlin are respectively inscribed with 'Sanlü Academy built by all the leading gentlemen' and 'Auspicious day of the 9th month of the Dingyou year of Daoguang, Qing.' The roof ridge has immortal and animal decorations, the gable walls have painted decorations, and on some wall bricks the two characters 'Wuchang' can still be faintly seen. It is said that the columns of the main hall are made of matang (coral) tree wood; in western Hubei, the matang tree is considered a tree species that cannot become useful timber, so using this kind of wood to build the main hall expressed the wish of the Wuchang people living here as guests for their children to become talented.

DORLING KINDERSLEY
